notes: On 4 October 2019, a female petitioner from Xi'an, Shaanxi who went to appeal in Beijing was arrested in Haizijiao Village in Daxing district (Beijing) by governmental personnel from Shaanxi and hired thugs. She was then brought back to Shaanxi by car. The next day, she was detained in a hotel next to the Bianfang Elementary School in Weicheng District, Xianyang City until 11 October 2019. She was not allowed to have contact with anyone during her detention.

On 30 April 2019, a man who had a disability in one of his legs died after being punched by a city administrator in Shangjie District, Zhengzhou City. The man resisted when the city administrators tried to stop him from setting up his fortune telling stall, when he fell to the ground when one of the administrators punched him.

In June 2019, two missionaries from Shandong Province were arrested in northern Xinjiang (coded as Urumqi), based on a tip-off to the police from a resident. When they were refused to sign a statement proclaiming that they would not engage in evangelism in the future, one of the missionaries were brutally beaten until he lost consciousness. They were ordered to return to Shandong the following day.

On 23 August 2019, a Taoist temple in Yongnian District (Handan City, Hebei Province) was demolished by the local government. More than 400 people government officials blocked the road to the temple on the day, and forcibly removed believers from the premises.

In September 2019, an ancient Buddhist temple in Jingzhou City, Hubei Province was demolished by the local public security and urban management departments, on the grounds that its registration certificate was false.

Between late September and early October 2019, two meeting places of Guangming House Church in Jixi City, Heilongjiang Province were seized, on the grounds that the church did not have a registration certificate.
In October 2019, a three-faced Bodhisattva statue outside a Buddhist temple in Tianheng town, Jimo District (Qingdao City, Shandong Province) was demolished by the local government.

On 19 October 2019, a Seventh-day Adventist house church in Neijiang City, Sichuan Province was raided by more than 200 people (including government officials and police officers). They ordered to have the electricity cut off, and took some valuables from the church. Two employees of the church were beaten up by four police officers. The two employees, the pastor and a preacher were taken to a detention house for interrogation.

Around 23 October 2019 (in the week after 19 October), a Seventh-day Adventist house church in Neijiang City, Sichuan Province was raided by more than 100 officials and police officers. They confiscated tables and chairs, audio equipment, and other properties of the church. They also threw copies of the Bible into a trash can outside the church. They subsequently welded the entrance to the church. Members of the church also recevied calls from government officials, threatening to withhold the salaries of their children and grandchildren if they did not renounce their faith.

On 31 October 2019, a Catholic church was demolished on orders from government officials in Guantao County (Handan City, Hebei Province). Two Catholics protested against the demolition, but were forcibly dragged out of the church.

On 2 November 2019, officials from the local government in Rencheng District, Jining City hired a construction team to remove religious signs and symbols from a women's mosque. The dome was also demolished, and the Chinese national flag was placed at the entrance.

On 17 November 2019, the Zunhua Muncipal Government forcibly demolished nine stupas in a Tibetan Buddhist temple in Zunhua County (Tangshan City, Hebei Province). This followed the previous incident on 14 November 2019 when the abbot of the temple was expelled, and parts of the temple were shut down.

On 9 December 2019, a Tibetan Buddhist temple was demolished by local authorities in Horqin (Tongliao City, Inner Mongolia). The police used pepper spray to disperse the crowd when hundreds of local herders tried to stop the demolition.

On 26 December 2019, a Christian Brother was at the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court in Wuhou District (Chengdu, Sichuan) for the trial of a reverend, when he was pushed down and attacked by a few plainclothes police. He was later taken away to the police station for questioning, on who is the leader of his church, and the reason for his appearance at the trial.

On 12 August 2019, an activist from Heyuan, Guangdong was taken away by the police from his home. Police did not specify the reason for the arrest when they were asked. His personal belongings such as phone, passport, bank cards and ID card were confiscated.

On 21 February 2020, an unreported number of people protested in front of a bank in Yichun City, Jiangxi Province, as they were unable to access their money due to funds being frozen as a result of the collapse of the bank.

On 26 February 2020, a citizen journalist was suspected to be taken away and held incommunicado by personnel from the Public Security Bureau in Wuhan City, Hubei Province. He had been in Wuhan reporting from the front line of the coronavirus outbreak, and was likely to be have been taken away by the authorities. He was livestreaming from his place of residence when there was a knock on his door, and his camera was abruptly cut off. This was part of an ongoing crackdown on people who had been reporting or sharing information about the coronavirus outbreak.

actor1: Police Forces of China (2012-) People's Armed Police
notes: On 14 January 2019, a church-run kindergarten in Xinglin District (Xiamen City, Fujian Province) was demolished by a large number of heavily armed police officers in anti-riot gear and personnel from the district's urban management bureau. It was reported that parents and teachers were blocked in their own homes, with each household guarded by 5 to 6 personnel to prevent them from going out during the demolition.

On 17 January 2019, five houses in Dongyangcun (Luoyang City, Henan Province) were forcibly demolished by a forced demolition team made up of more than 100 personnel (including representatives from the Urban and Rural Planning Bureau, public security, subdistrict office). The people whose houses were demolished believed that their properties were legal, and that the administrative agencies had no legal right to forcibly demolish them.

On 11 March 2019, more than a dozen officials stormed into the home of a believer of a Three-Self Church in Zhoukou City, Henan Province. They took away religious paintings and books from his home and burned them outside. The officials also ordered the family to get rid of the remaining religious items at home.

On 2 June 2019, four meeting venues of an All Sphere Church in Jianshui County (Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province) were raided by the police. Over 100 believers were taken away to the police stations for questioning. Bibles and hymnbooks were also confiscated from the venues. The houses of believers were raided, and believers were threatened by the police that they would be sentenced to prison should they continue practising their faith.

On 15 September 2019, more than 20 government officials raided and shut down a house church venue in Hebi City, Henan Province. This was part of a broader campaign to pressure house churches to join the state-run churches.

On 28 November 2019, local residents of Huazhou, Maoming, Guangdong took to the streets in Huazhou to demonstrate against a plan by authorities to build a crematorium in a neighbourhood. They held placards. Police dispersed the demonstrators with tear gas and some police used batons to beat up a civilian. Both sides engaged in physical clashes. Some demonstrators felt unwell and were hospitalised. The local party secretary announced on 1 December that the crematorium plan would be terminated.

As reported on 5 March 2020, between 101 and 1000 merchants demonstrated at a shopping mall in Shenyang City, Liaoning Province, demanding for a refund of rent for the months of February and March. This was due to sluggish business, which had been severely impacted by the coronavirus outbreak.

On 22 April 2019, almost 300 miners and migrant workers gathered at a park opposite to the Shanxi Provincial Petitioning Bureau in Xinghualing District (Taiyuan city, Shanxi) to demand for wage arrears, pension funds, production subsidies and unemployment funds delayed and owed by the state and state-owned enterprise Xishan Coal and Electricity Power. Negotiations were held between the protesters and government officials.

On 18 April 2019, as many as 100 taxi drivers went on strike and protested in Qixingguan district (Bijie, Guizhou) against the market saturation of illegally operating taxis, and drivers claiming to be part of veteran- or disability-focused taxi groups. Their office was vandalised in the past year amidst tension between the groups.
On 26 December 2019, as many as 100 workers protested in Qishan, Baoji, Shaanxi to demand more than 5 million RMB worth of wage arrears owed to more than 100 of them by a construction project.

On 21 May 2019, more than 300 teachers gathered at Jianyang's Letters and Calls Bureau in Jianyang County (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province) to demand for increase awards and 13 months worth of wage arrears owed to them by the schools.

On 9 April 2020, dozens of small shop owners demonstrated outside the Grand Ocean Department Store in Jianghan District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province), chanting slogans and calling for the landlord to waive rental fees for a year, or refund the lease. The demonstration was prompted by the poor business during the coronavirus outbreak, which had severely hit small shop owners at the department store. The demonstrators continued to protest and held a sit-in protest on 10 April 2020, holding placards during the demonstration. This was one of at least two reported demonstrations held by merchants on the same day across Wuhan City, calling for a waiver of rental fees.

On 4 March 2019, a supermarket worker and Early Rain Covenant Church member disappeared in Chengdu after public security officers took him away. He received intimidation visits at his house numerous times prior to his forced disappearance.

On 6 March 2019, officials from the Jinshui District Bureau of Religious Affairs sealed off Panshi Church in Erqi district (Zhengzhou, Henan) after claims about regulation violations, and forbade them from organising religious activities in the future. Slogans were removed, and electricity supply was cut off.

On 9 March 2019, a Shaanxi petitioner went incommunicado after he last informed a friend about being chased near his factory in Yanjiao town (Sanhe, Hebei) by the village chief and stability maintenance chief-of-staff of Ximing village, Chisha town, Chencang district of Baoji city. He was incommunicado for at least 11 days as of 20 Mar.

On 15 March 2019, a pig farmer and Early Rain Covenant Church member from Chengdu disappeared in Hangzhou after the police were seen visiting his rental apartment. His clothes and belongings were left behind, but his phone, laptop and the landlord's computer were missing.

On 21 March 2019, the former editor of Maoist website Red Reference - and now editor at a cultural organisation - was charged with 'inciting subservion of state power' by the Nanjing Ministry of State Security (Jiangsu), and placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL). The organisation was involved in the Jiashi workers unionization labour movement, and the Ministry was allegedly concerned with domestic non-government organisations that received funding from overseas. The editor usually worked in Nanjing, but also lived in Shanghai.

Around 20 March 2019 (in the week before 27 March 2019), almost a thousand family members of the deceased and the missing were sent to hotels in outlying counties and cities of Yancheng prefecture (Jiangsu) ahead of the government-organised memorial on the seventh day of an industrial explosion accident involving a chemical factory in Yancheng. It was an effort to 'maintain stability' and 'prevent them from congregating' after some family members had partaken in protests at county governments. At least one family was reported to have been arranged to stay in a hotel in Binhai district.

On 16 May 2019, a dissident was arrested and tortured by the police in Hefei City, Anhui Province during a 24-hour custodial interrogation. He suffered from hunger, fatigue, sleep deprivation, and being denied access to the toilet. He was interrogated about his involvement in the commemoration of the 30th anniversary of Tiananmen Square protests and his interviews by foreign reporters.

On 27 February 2019, the father and sister of a detained human rights lawyer were picked up by 3 officers from the Domestic Security Protection Bureau in Xingyang (Henan) and were held incommunicado at a hotel until 1 March 2019. The human rights lawyer had been detained for defending lawyers who were arrested as part of the '709 crackdown' and was scheduled to be released the following day; his father and sister were en route to receive him when they were picked up.

On 9 June 2019, around 150 fishers protested in the sea near Victoria Harbour (location coded as Admiralty, Central and Western District, Hong Kong) in support of the government's proposed extradition bill. They drove more than 20 ships displaying banners showing supportive messages of the bill.

On 2 March 2019, a human rights lawyer was taken away by two police officers and an officer from the Shijiazhuang Justice Bureau in Shijiazhaung City (Hebei) to undergo 'training' and was incommunicado for at least 6 days. A few days ago, he had started a petition to propose ammendments to the constitution that would stregthen civil rights that garnered almost 1000 signatures, and he had planned to submit it during the annual meeting of the CPPCC and NPC on 5 March 2019.

On 4 March 2019, the Luoyang People's Government arrested 13 protesters during the second day of their protest at the Railway Station Square and Wangcheng Park in Xigong District (Luoyang, Henan), and took 28 others back to Yiyang county. Since 3 Mar, more than 50 workers with pneumoconiosis had been protesting to urge the Yiyang County Government to promptly resolve their demands for medical treatment and financial compensation. Protesters 'strolled about' in t-shirts with slogans.

On 16 April 2019, at least 60 kindergarten teachers from three county-level districts - Xinfu district, Yuanping city and Wutai county - petitioned at the Xinzhou City Petitioning Bureau and the Education Bureau in Xinfu district (Xinzhou, Shanxi) to express concerns about their employment status. Those three districts - out of the 14 governed under Xinzhou - were the only districts that had not converted eligible kindergarten teachers into teachers under the public school system. They also demanded a raise in compensation fees.

On 3 March 2020, a supermarket employee was beaten by a large number of personnel from the urban management bureau in Jianghan District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province). It was reported that the supermarket employee was distributing groceries in a community during the coronavirus outbreak, as part of a collaboration between the residents of the community and the supermarket. This was one of a number of similar incidents reported of law enforcement personnel using violence while performing their duties during this period.

On 13 May 2019, more than 40 pneumoconiosis patients from Ziyang County of Shaanxi Province who had travelled to Luolong District (Luoyang City, Henan Province) to protest for their rights were arrested en masse by the police before they were able to start the protest. They were sent back to Ziyang County by the police on the following day.

Around 15 September 2019 (month of), a Catholic meeting venue in Poyang county (Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province) was ordered to cease religious activities because it was not part of the state-controlled Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association. Local officials threatened to revoke retirement pensions of elderly congregation members if another meeting were to be held. The church's cross, a painting of the Virgin Mary, and religious couplets were removed, and replaced with portraits of Xi Jinping and Mao Zedong.

On 28 November 2019, residents in Wenlou town (Huazhou, Maoming City, Guangdong Province) clashed with more than 1,000 police when they demonstrated against a local government plan to build a crematorium in the town. Villagers planned to bring a petition to the town government, but were stopped by the police. As the police tried to contain the villagers, they blocked roads with stones and woods and set fire to a police check point. Police beat demonstrators with batons and stones, fired tear gases, and used an armoured vehicle to clear the road. They also sealed off the village until the day after and arrested many young villagers to prevent them from escaping and reporting to the upper level of authority. Many people were injured and sent to hospitals, including elderly and children.

On 12 May 2020, 7 representatives from Pingxiang City petitioned at the Jiangxi Provincial Committee and Government Bureau for Letters and Calls in Donghu District (Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province), against an alleged misreporting by the Pingxiang municipal government, following a recently published announcement that it had settled and resolved 46 cases of petitions. It was reported that one of the representatives was taken away at the scene by an interceptor from the stability maintenance office.

Around 15 December 2019 (month of), 176 Christian headstones with crosses were demolished in Xiapu County (Ningde City, Fujian Province) by officials from the county government. It was reported that the land on which these headstones were resting on was later sold for ten times of the original price. This was part of a broader campaign to remove religious symbols from tombstones.

On 25 April 2019, nearly 100 private, substitute, and kindergarten teachers from cities and prefectures such as Zhaotong, Qujing, Kunming, and Red River gathered at the Provincial Party Committee and People's Government of Yunnan Province in Wuhua District (Kunming, Yunnan) to petition for their rights. Police forces stood by but did not intervene.

On 1 May 2019, between 130 and 500 pre-sale buyers of Pearl Horizon flats carrying white flags with slogans marched from the abandoned Polytex construction site in Areia Preta district to Government Headquarters in Nam Van district in Macao, urging the government to settle the long-running problem of the ill-fated residential project before the end of its term. A total of 120 police officers were present to maintain order, but they did not intervene in the protest.

On 1 May 2019, between 280 and 560 people took part in a march organised by the Macau Family Union Federation in Macao. They urged both the local government and the central government to meet their long-standing demand that their grown-up mainland-born children be allowed to move to Macao. The protesters started the demonstration in Triangle Garden, submitted their petition to an official at the Central People's Government Liaison Office in Macau in Zape and finished the march before submitting their petition to an official at Government Headquarters in Nam Van.

On 16 January 2019, two archaeologists were beaten by more than 10 urban management personnel at an excavation site in Sangshujiao, Hanjiang District (Yangzhou, Jiangsu). It was reported that the assault was prompted by grievances around the illegal construction of the archaeologists. The municipal government had reported that the officers involved had been detained and given a serious warning.

Around 15 October 2019 (month of), a Kazakh woman from Ulanbuqa village, Maralsu township of Emini county (Tarbagatay, Xinjiang) was questioned and beaten (most likely by authorities) after her husband's escape into Kazakhstan on 6 Oct, reportedly fainting from the assault. Her husband would succeed in obtaining political asylum in Kazakhstan.

On 27 May 2020, a Christian from Hubei was taken away from his residence in Fangshan District (Beijing) by 10 police and personnel from the Hubei representative office in Beijing. His wife stated that the police confirmed that he had been taken away by the public security bureau but his whereabouts remained unknown at the time of reporting on 28 May 2020. It was suspected that he might have been taken away ahead of the 31st anniversary of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Protests, as he had previously been involved in commemorative events for the Tiananmen Square Protests with his wife.

On 28 May 2020, a Christian from the Early Rain Covenant Church was assaulted in Chengdu City, Sichuan Province by the local police, subdistrict and community officers as he was preparing to move out to Caojiaxiang in another district of the city. Another Christian accompanying him was also beaten with the government personnel. The believer was evicted from his residence on 27 May 2020 in his hometown of Pingchang County after being administratively detained for 15 days. It was reported that this was part of a broader campaign by the authorities to evict believers of Early Rain Covenant Church from their jurisdiction and Chengdu.

On 1 December 2019, some residents of Huazhou, Maoming, Guangdong petitioned at the local government regarding the withdrawal of the plan by authorities to build a crematorium in a neighbourhood. They held a banner. During verbal confrontation with the protesters, the Public Security Officer of the local government stepped on a Chinese national flag.

On 14 March 2019, about 100 government officials and police officers, led by the Town Secretary, demolished a Three-Self church in Xianglushan town of Yiyang county (Luoyang, Henan). The church was state-approved with a property certificate, but authorities now claimed that it had 'violated building laws,' resulting in the joint operation led by the Yiyang County Government, State Land Management Bureau and Planning Bureau.

On 30 June 2019, a house church meeting venue in Nanchang's Wanli district was closed because it was unregistered, and the person in charge was taken away for questioning. Three other meeting venues in Nanchang were also shut down.

On 20 December 2019, a Protestant house church venue in Tai'erzhuang District (Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province) was raided by nine local government officials. During the raid, officials tore down religious paintings from the walls and burnt the paintings. This was part of a broader campaign to crack down on non-state-approved house churches.

On 6 March 2019, local government officials pried open the gate to a church in Erqi District (Zhengzhou City, Henan Province) and vandalized the venue. The officials also looted RMB 70,000 worth of church items, and sealed off the venue with barricade tape.

Around 13 June 2019, residents of Beidong village, under the jurisdiction of Bailingzhen in Xiushui county in Jiujiang, Jiangxi province protested over the burial reform that all bodies to be cremated, but were violently dispersed by the local police.

On 11 June 2019, more than 2000 people gathered at the cemetery in Quanfeng town, Xiushui county, Jiujiang in Jiangxi province to guard the grave of one deceased man whose family buried him on the same day secretly to avoid forced cremation by the government, after the government decided to dig up his remains.

In December 2019, numerous crosses were removed from a Three-Self church in Hegang City, Heilongjiang Province by the authorities. This was part of a broader campaign launched by the central government to remove crosses from churches across China.

On 26 September 2019, a Buddhist temple in Dawu County (Xiaogan City, Hubei Province) was razed to the ground by the local Religious Affairs Bureau. This was part of the ramped up efforts to crackdown on religious venues across Hubei Province ahead of the announcement of the central government's return inspections.

On 8 September 2019, a house church meeting venue in a village in Zhangwang Township (Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province) was raided by government officials. All future gatherings were banned for indefinite period due to the on-going 'riots' in Hong Kong. The officials threatened to dismiss the village's Party secretary and the village head if there was to be any future gatherings.

In July 2019, a statue of Lao-Tzu outside the Daoist Xuandu Temple in the Dagushan Scenic Area in Gushan town (Donggang City, Liaoning Province) were altered to look like a writer of one of the essential classical novels of Chinese literature as required by the city's Religious Affairs Bureau. The Bureau had sealed off the temple earlier in September 2018 in an attempt to demolish it, but only allowed to the temple to remain on the condition that Lao-Tzu statue would be altered.

On 5 August 2019, a Three-Self church in Hangkou town, Xiushui county (Jiujiang City, Jiangxi Province) was demolished by the local government on claims the land on which it stood was planned to be used for a new road. The order was issued on July 27, and the people in charge of the church tried to persuade the government to save the church. After that, they were held in the town hall and forced to sign an agreement to accept the demolition and relocation of the church. It was part of a broader campaign launched by the CCP to reduce the number of Three-Self Churches nationwide.

On 20 September 2019, a Sola Fide (Protestant) meeting venue in Chengdu City, Sichuan Province was shut down after a raid by police officers and officials from the Religious Affairs Bureau. They took down the ID information of all believers present, and threatened to detain and fine anyone who continued to gather.

On 12 May 2019, the Jinxiangtan Church in Xiangtan City, Hunan Province was shut down by the police. At least 15 other house churches were sealed off over the weekend. It was reported that it might be part of a national campaign by the authorities to silence dissent and religious individuals before the 30th anniversary of Tiananmen Square protests.

On 6 March 2019, local police raided six Buddhist statue factories in Zhuanlu Town (Baoding City, Hebei Province) and destroyed the casting kilns in one of the factories and smashed statue moulds in another factory. It was reported that the owners of these two factories incurred losses of ten of thousands of RMB. In the other four factories, Buddhist statues were confiscated. It was part of an extended campaign to crack down on Buddhist statues at the source, by cracking down on factories that produce the statues.

On 11 November 2019, law enforcement officers raided a Buddhist temple in Liangyuan District (Shangqiu City, Henan Province), and confiscated four pickup trucks worth of religious books. This was part of a broader effort to confiscate books by a prominent Buddhist monk, whose teachings have been banned by the CCP.

In November 2019, the cross and religious paintings were removed from a Protestant house church venue in Baishan (Boshan) Village, Qichun Town (Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province) by the authorities. Two people in charge of the church were also arrested later in the same month. This was part of a broader campaign to crack down on non-state-approved house churches.

On 6 September 2019, the Tianfu Temple in Xintan Town (Honghu City, Hubei Province) was demolished by government officials referring to the CCP's policy of banning all religions. The believers and the guards at the temple attempted to stop the demolition but were forcibly removed.

On 8 November 2019, a Three-Self church in Sanshu Town, Huaiyin District (Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province) was merged with two other Three-Self churches on orders of the government. The licence to hold religious activity at the venue had been cancelled by the authorities, and the believers were forced to congregate at a new venue that is six times smaller than the old venue. This was part of a broader campaign to reduce the number of churches.

On 4 January 2019, more than 10 law enforcement officers stormed into a Buddhist temple in Guangshui City (Suizhou City, Hubei Province) and smashed the statues inside the temple with sledgehammers. During the raid, they also threatened to arrest the person in charge if he interfered.

In August 2019, a house church meeting venue in Dachang Hui Autonomous County (Langfang City, Hebei Province) was shut down by the authorities, because it was not a member of the state-controlled Three-Self Churches. This was part of a broader campaign to force house churches to join the state-controlled Three-Self churches.

On 12 May 2019, the Fuzhou Reformed House Church in Gulou (Fuzhou City, Fujian Province) was shut down by the police for refusing to join the Three-Self Church. Over 20 police officers stormed into the meeting venue, dismissed all the believers and seized over 200 books, including Bibles and hymnbooks. The police also arrested the church's elders and a few co-workers. At least 15 other house churches were sealed off over the weekend. It was reported that it might be part of a national campaign by the authorities to silence dissent and religious individuals before the 30th anniversary of Tiananmen Square protests.

On 28 March 2019, government officials sealed off the Buddhist Fojing Temple in Jindegu township of Nanle county (Puyang, Henan) after burying religious statues that were previously erected. The temple did not manage to receive state approval despite repeated applications in the past three years.

On 15 January 2019, a Three-Self Church meeting venue housed in a relatively concealed basement of a residential building in Dapan Village, Zhongmu County (Zhengzhou City, Henan Province) was discovered and shut down by local authorities. The furnishings at the venue were also cleared out.

As reported on 15 April 2019, Islam-related and Arabic symbols were removed from an estimate of almost 150 Hui-owned stores across three streets in Chengde prefecture (Hebei), known for a high Hui Muslim population. This was done on orders from the United Front Work Department.

On 17 July 2019, a 10-meter-tall statue of Shakyamuni Buddha outside Longxing Temple in Mengjin county (Luoyang City, Henan Province) was demolished by government-hired workers. The complete demolition of the statue took two days. The act was taken according to the CCP's policy to remove outdoor religious statues nationwide.

On 5 May 2019, more than 20 workers hired by local government officials forcibly dismantled 6 round Islamic structures at the top of a residential building in an ethnic Hui community in Liangyuan District (Shangqiu City, Henan Province). It was part of the national five-year sinicization campaign targetting Muslims outside of Xinjiang.

On 7 July 2019, a Catholic church in Boye County, Baoding City (Hebei Province) was raided by over 30 police officers. Police emptied the church, took away the priest, and subsequently closed down the church. The priest was sent back to his hometown the next day.

On 15 July 2019, dozens of police stormed into a Three-self church in Foshan city, Guangdong province where more than 80 children were participating in a summer camp. Police recorded personal information of every child and took away the priest and 6 church workers. All were released on the same day. This is believed to be part of a crackdown on church influence on young people.

On 20 April 2019, a Three-Self Church in Lugou village, Yuecun town of Xinmi City (Zhengzhou City, Henan Province) was taken over by the government and repurposed into an activity centre. The village officials set up a stage and hung up the national flag inside the meeting venue.

On 13 June 2019, nearly 10,000 people gathered at the cemetery in Quanfeng town, Xiushui, Jiujiang in Jiangxi province to guard the grave of one deceased man whose family buried him on 11 June 2019, after learning that the government was planning to send over 400 police officers to subdue them. Many came from surrounding villages. Demonstrators displayed a banner to express their dissatisfaction with the government's implementation of the burial reform, which demanded to cremate all the deceased starting from 1 May 2019. The mayor of Quanfeng town threatened to cremate every deceased person for as long as he remained in office, provoking thousands of people to break down the gate to the town government, got inside, and tore up some documents in the office in demonstration. Attempting to bring the situation under control, local officials came to negotiate with the demonstrators. They apologized to the people and promised to allow burials, not to dig up graves or arrest people.
On 3 February 2019, the local government of Dianzhuangzhen, Luoyang, Henan blocked the entrance of a church in Dianzhuangzhen with two trucks to prevent church goers from entering the church.

On 22 July 2019, the police raided and shut down a house church meeting venue in Fuxing town (Arun banner, Hulunbuir region, Inner Mongolia) because it refused to join the state-controlled Three-Self Church. Six believers were arrested and fined. Two of them were detained for 10 days.

On 6 December 2019, 500 outdoor Arhat statues in a Buddhist temple in Yongcheng City (Shangqiu City, Henan Province) were ordered to be demolished to make way for a park and a stadium, despite receiving approval from the government to be built at the site over 30 years ago. The statues were then demolished on an unspecified date. This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CCP to crack down on religious activities.

On 19 June 2019, officials from the local Religious Affairs Bureau and police officers sealed off the Fule Church, a place of worship that was not part of the state-run Three-Self Church, in Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province. They broke into the church when a dozen members were listening to an audio sermon by a South Korean pastor. They confiscated 80,000 RMB (about $ 11,200) of donation money, some valuables, and more than 200 copies of religious literature, including the Bible because the church was not allowed to receive foreign donations according to Chinese law and the believers disobeyed the authority by refusing to join the Three-Self Church. The believers were taken to the local police station to sign statements promising not to attend worship services in the future.

On 14 April 2019, 33 Guanyin statues on the Guanyin Island, Zhanghe New Area (Jingmen City, Hubei Province) were demolished by the authorities to 'stop the commercialization of Buddhism and Taoism'. The demolition work lasted for half a month and was a part of the CCP's policy to destroy all outdoor religious statues in the country.

On 14 March 2020, a Three-Self church in Huoqiu County (Lu'an City, Anhui Province) was shut down by the county government. It was reported that the officials had initially ordered the church director to remove the cross, on the grounds that the cross would fall and injure people. They then forced the church to shut down after the church director refused to remove the cross.

On 16 March 2019, more than 30 government officials besieged a house church in Poyang County, Shangrao, Jiangxi province and robbed the church, confiscating things including piano, blankets, etc. They looked up the church's financial records and announced that the church would be closed because it was illegally built.

On 16 October 2019, police officers raided churches in Jiaozhou (Qingdao, Shandong) and arrested at least 23 Christians. The next day, 10 more Christians were arrested from churches in Licang during police raids. On 17 October 2019, police officers raided churches in Licang (Qingdao, Shandong) and arrested 10 Christians.

Some churches were burned down to the ground.

Around 24 November 2019 (as reported), a dozen cleaning workers from a company in Qingdao City, Shandong Province gathered to demand wage arrears owed by the company.

On 25 November 2019, at least 30 employees of the China Mobile Sichuan Branch gathered outside of the company office in Chengdu City, Sichuan Province, to protest against a financial product that was operated by the company and failed to pay their interests since the beginning of the month.
As reported on 6 August 2019, as many as 100 workers protested in Jinzhou, Liaoning to demand for wage arrears and unpaid social insurance owed to them by a chemical company for as many as 180 days.

Around 21 May 2020, at the start of the annual parliamentary sessions in China, the parents of a petitioner from Nanjing were taken away by government officials in Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province and detained in a black jail in Qixia District (Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province). After the petitioner tried several times to request for the release of his parents, he jumped off the Nanjing Yangtze Bridge.
On 5 September 2019, a petitioner from Wuhan, Hubei was abducted by 2 men dressed in black in Dongxihu (Wuhan, Hubei) and has been detained in a black jail since then.

On 3 June 2020, a man was summoned to the Guangyi Police Station in Liangxi District (Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province). He had since remained uncontactable for almost 24 hours at the time of reporting. It was reported that this was part of the intensified security measures ahead of the 31st anniversary of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Protests.

On 18 February 2020, during a dispute between a farmer and several police officers in Xiaogan CIty (Hubei) about village closure enforced by the local government, more than 10 villagers came to the scene and accused the police of abuse of power and holding up a gun during a non-violent dispute. The police reportedly fired into the sky to intimidate the villagers. The police officers were then driven out by the villagers.

On 21 June 2020, a petitioner went missing after making a phone call from the Haizijiao Police Station in Daxing District (Beijing). He had since remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 22 June 2020. It was reported that the petitioner had been petitioning for 17 years, and was recently in Beijing to petition during the annual parliamentary sessions.

Around 17 January 2019 (from 4 to 29 January 2019), a female petitioner being detained at the Fengdu County Detention Centre (Chongqing) was beaten up by prisoners multiple times. She sustained broken ribs and multiple injuries. She was originally supposed to be released on 4 Jan, but the police extended her detention period until 29 January 2019.

On 6 January 2020, a large group of teachers organized a sit-in protest from 9am to 9pm in front of the local government office building in Zixi County (Fuzhou, Jiangxi) to demand for the wage arrears owed to them.

On 28 February 2019, police officers broke into the respective homes of two petitioners - one female - in Caoba town of Yucheng district (Ya'an, Sichuan) in the middle of the night. The male petitioner was taken away without being given any reason for arrest, the female petitioner was incommunicado since the incident.

Around 28 February 2019 (a month before 31 March 2019), a dissident from Rongchang District (Rongchang, Chongqing) was taken away by the local police and detained in a mental hospital for about a month. He was released on 31 March 2019 and warned by the authorities not to post online again. This was one of many times that the dissident had been sent to a mental hospital for actively speaking out against the government.

On 13 February 2020, a number of epidemic prevention personnel went to a government building in Chongzhou City (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province) to demand for an explanation on the incident on 12 February 2020, where epidemic prevention personnel were assaulted by a man who claimed to have senior officials in his family. After failing to reach a conclusion, the personnel later brought the issue onto social media platforms to call for collective protection of their rights.

On 11 March 2019, a writer and well-known dissident from Hunan who was being detained at a hotel in Liuze Town (Shaoyang City, Hunan Province) was slapped and violently dragged through the elevator from the first to fifth floor by the Party Committee Deputy Secretary of Liuze Town. The deputy secretary hit the writer's head with a remote control and kicked his head. The writer retaliated by kicking the deputy secretary. The writer had originally been intercepted at Shaodong Railway Station, Shaoyang on 28 February 2019 and was taken away by four stability maintenance personnel led by a Liuze Town official.

On 19 May 2020, a female petitioner was beaten by the secretary of the local community, after being taken away to the community office in Xinwu District (Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province). It was reported that her mobile phone was taken away, and she vomited blood after being assaulted. She had since been placed under surveillance at her place of residence, which was guarded by 4 to 5 people. It was reported that she had been illegally detained and beaten for more than 400 days in total, for petitioning against the demolition of her house.

On 15 May 2020, a female citizen journalist was taken away from her rental house in Nanshixia Village, Gu'an County (Langfang City, Hebei Province) by the police. She was then handed over to the local government officials and detained in a hotel until the end of the annual parliamentary sessions. After the detention, she was repatriated to her rental house for treatment of her back pain.

On 29 September 2019, a female petitioner from Yiwu (Jinhua, Zhejiang) called the police after her motorbike was destroyed. Police came and did not arrest any of the personnel who were guarding the female petitioner. Rather, police arrested the petitioner and beat her up somewhere near the police station. She was then detained for 10 days.

On 4 February 2020, several residents of Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province were accused by epidemic prevention personnel of not reporting their return from Wuhan City (the epicentre of the coronavirus outbreak). The residents were reportedly pushed to the ground and violently beaten by the epidemic prevention personnel. This was one of a number of similar incidents reported of epidemic prevention personnel using violence while performing their duties.

On 1 May 2020, a female petitioner from Xinwu District in Jiangsu Province was beaten by two local government officials in Xinwu District (Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province). She was reportedly injured in the head and ear. It was reported that she had been illegally detained and beaten for more than 400 days in total, for petitioning against the demolition of her house.

On 18 September 2019, a female petitioner from Hubei was abducted by government officials in Chenzhou, Hunan and admitted to a mental hospital. The stability maintenance unit arranged 12 officials to keep an eye on her and to stop her from going out and meeting her family. The reason for locking her up was to prevent her from petitioning in Beijing during the National Day.

On 9 April 2019, a petitioner was taken away by Ya'an city government officials in Beijing for leading a group of people to petition in Beijing. He was subsequently detained in a police station in Ya'an city before being forcibly admitted into a mental hospital by authorities.

On 12 February 2020, following the assault on epidemic prevention personnel earlier in the day by a man on the grounds that one of his family members was a senior official, more than 100 epidemic prevention personnel and residents gathered at a police station in Longxing Town (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province) to demand a fair investigation and a disclosure of the identity of the police officer involved in the incident.

On 12 September 2019, a female petitioner from Fancheng, Xiangyang and her son petitioned at the Letters and Visits Bureau in Xiangcheng District (Xiangyang, Hubei) demanding to bring her son to a doctor. The neighbourhood committee secretary, along with 6 other men stormed into the Bureau and beat them up. The petitioner called the police but when they arrived, they refused to help her after finding out that she came to petition. They were hospitalised.

On 15 June 2019, residents of households or units subject to relocation due to building demolition took to the street in Zhushan (Jingdezhen, Jiangxi) to protest against the government's decision to demolish their households and transform the area. They claimed that the government fabricated the documents in order to target their households. Protesters held banners. The protest lasted until 18 June at the time of reporting.

Around 25 October 2019 (between 23 and 26 Oct), a petitioner being held at the Minhou detention centre in Fuzhou City (Fujian Province) was suspected to have been severely beaten in custody. His family was notified on 26 Oct that he was in a coma and had been hospitalised, leading them to suspect that he was assaulted after meeting with his lawyer on 23 October 2019. The petitioner was first taken away and detained by the police on 27 August 2019, and looked fine when he met his lawyer. The police stopped his family from examining his body in hospital. He died later in hospital on 6 November 2019.

On 30 June 2019, a petitioner was forcibly taken away from her home in Zibo, Shandong by police officers who refused to provide a reason for her arrest. This is likely part of a nationwide crackdown on petitioners and human rights defenders in anticipation of the anniversary of the CPC Founding Day, which falls on 1 July.

On 12 February 2020, a family of four were playing mahjong at home in Hubei when two police officers barged into their house, holding batons and hammers. During an argument, the police officer smashed the mahjong table with a hammer and almost hit one of the men with a baton, but was stopped by the other police officer. This was one of several reports of abuse by law enforcement officers while performing their duties for the prevention of the coronavirus outbreak.

On 14 February 2020, between 20 and 30 people were arrested by epidemic prevention personnel in Hubei Province for not wearing masks. They were tied together on a long string, with all of their hands tied to their back. It was reported that they were paraded on the streets as a form of punishment. This was one of several reports of abuse by law enforcement officers while performing their duties for the prevention of the coronavirus outbreak.

On 11 March 2020, more than 100 personnel from the local urban management bureau and excavators were dispatched to forcibly demolish houses in Zhaotong City, Yunnan Province. During the demolition, a large number of villagers broke through the epidemic prevention checkpoint to try and halt the demolition. A large number of urban management personnel violently pulled the villagers out of the cordoned area. 5 to 6 authorities reportedly beat up an old man, and some authorities used sticks to hit the bodies of villagers who rushed forward to help the old man. Some people were reportedly injured.

On 3 February 2019, a man ('founder' of un-recognised political party Zhongguo Minfudang) was cornered and assaulted by the police when he got ready to leave his residence in Jiangpu subdistrict of Pukou district (Nanjing, Jiangsu) for a haircut and bath ahead of the Spring Festival.

On 22 May 2020, a married couple was forcibly intercepted by a police officer, while they were waiting for the Beijing-bound train at Zhengzhou Railway Station in Erqi District (Zhengzhou City, Henan Province). A group of police officers and government personnel from the community and subdistrict offices appeared right after they were intercepted. They were then taken away to and detained at a hotel, likely to prevent them from travelling to Beijing to petition. This was part of the intensified security measures ahead of the annual parliamentary sessions scheduled to start on 21 May 2020 to prevent people from travelling to Beijing to petition.

On 14 January 2020, a lawyer from Shaanxi Province was held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location for allegedly endangering national security. He was taken away by Xi'an Public Security Bureau on 12 January 2020. He had previously participated in the defense of many human rights cases.

On 28 May 2020, a female street vendor was attacked by urban management officers in Banchang Town (Tongren City, Guizhou Province). It was reported that the urban management personnel were driving vendors off the streets when the female vendor got into an altercation with the officers. A officer then kicked the vendor onto the ground, before picking up a broom to continue beating the vendor. The vendor had since filed a claim with the urban management department, but was told that the officers acted in self-defence after she attacked the officers first.

On 29 July 2019, the ex-vice chairman of Wuhan Workers' Autonomous Federation was discovered to be missing in Chenzhou, Hunan and has been incommunicado for at least 2 days since. A few days prior to his disappearance, he had shown his friends a photo of him with the ex-premier of the PRC Li Peng on his phone and it is suspected that his disappearance is linked to this.

On 14 October 2019, a female petitioner was kidnapped by government interceptors near the National Bureau of Letters and Visits in Xicheng District (Beijing Municipality) and sent back to her home town in Hubei Province. She was beaten on the way.

On 22 September 2019, a petitioner was forcibly detained for 24 hours by the local police in Yubei District, Chongqing. She had planned to travel to Beijing to appeal for her petition against the illegal requisition of her land and demolition of her house by the government. During her detention, she sustained injuries to her ankles after being dragged by the handcuffs and shackles.
On 25 December 2019, hundreds of teachers at the top middle school in Zixi, Jiangxi demonstrated against the wage arrears owed to them.

On 6 November 2019, more than 10 construction workers employed by the government in Nantong City (Jiangsu Province) destroyed a house in Chongchuan District and beat the house owner and his mother when they tried to stop the workers. The house owner suffered multiple injuries on his body, and his mother was injured in her head and hospitalised.

On 9 March 2019, a petitioner from Chongqing was intercepted and placed under 'house arrest' on the 17th floor of Tianhe Hotel in Jinshui district (Zhengzhou, Henan). He had bought a train ticket to Hebi prefecture and was planning to visit Beijing. The incident was allegedly related to the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 7 March 2019, the government sent the last batch of about 10 protesters back to Zhiyang county during the fifth day of their protest at the Railway Station Square and Wangcheng Park in Xigong District (Luoyang, Henan). Since 3 Mar, workers with pneumoconiosis had been protesting to urge the Yiyang County Government to promptly resolve their demands for medical treatment and financial compensation. Protesters 'strolled about' in t-shirts with slogans.

On 20 October 2019, nearly 1,000 people gathered in front of the government offices in Changping District (Beijing Municipality) to protest against a government decision to demolish their houses in two villages within the district. The decision was published on 17 October and they were ordered to leave their houses by 18 October. They held boards and chanted slogans.

On 14 October 2019, a female petitioner was taken away by local authorities around the State Bureau of Letters and Calls in Dongcheng, Beijing and forcibly sent back to her hometown in Ezhou, Hubei province. Authorities violently beat her up during the journey. Back in Ezhou, she continued to be controlled by the authorities and was not allowed to seek treatment for her injuries. Officers threatened to send her to a mental hospital if she continued to cause trouble.

On 20 February 2020, more than a dozen workers went to the subdistrict office in Yanta District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to petition for their right to return to their factory. They reported that the government had issued a notice of the resumption of work and their company had called for employees to return to the factory. However, they had been blocked by epidemic prevention personnel from entering the factory or their dormitory upon arriving, who claimed that they had not received any notice for the resumption of work.

On 21 May 2020, a female petitioner was forcibly taken away from her uncle's home located 60 kilometres away from Zhangjiaguang City (Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province) by 8 to 9 police officers. She was dragged and beaten by several police officers and auxiliary police while being taken away to a car, causing many bruises on her body. She was later briefly detained in Chengbei subdistrict office, before she was taken back home for compulsory isolation for 14 days due to COVID-19, on the grounds that she had left Zhangjiaguang City.

On 16 February 2020, three people were playing mahjong at their own home, when several epidemic prevention personnel and police officers barged into their home in Xiaogan City, Hunan and smashed the mahjong table. Several police officers also surrounded the three people and beat them up. This was one of several reports of abuse by law enforcement officers while performing their duties for the prevention of the coronavirus outbreak.

On 15 March 2019, a petitioner from Matoupu town of Li county (Changde, Hunan) went incommunicado. His house was robbed by the deputy chief of the town and emptied after all of his possessions were taken.

On 10 March 2019, policemen from Shandong broke into the rental apartment of a woman from Hunan who was in search of a missing child after seeing an online post. She has been incommunicado since they took her away.

On 6 November 2019, 3 people went to the Fuzhou No. 1 Hospital in Taijiang District (Fuzhou City, Fujian Province) to protest against the death of their family member who allegedly died in the hospital due to the misconduct of the doctor and the hospital. The hospital's security personnel and employees threatened them before police arrived at the scene. The police tried to take away their banner and threatened them to leave.

On 15 April 2019, a petitioner was beaten up in a car at the public security bureau in Gu'an county of Langfang city, Hebei after interceptors escorted him back from his petitioning activities in Beijing, and arrested him. His family called the emergency hotline for help, but officials said emergency rooms were full and refused. Doctors at the Gu'an Renmin Hospital also refused to prescribe him painkillers when he was sent there the next day.

On 26 December 2019, a petitioner was intercepted by two police officers and illegally detained. The petitioner was visiting the Complaints Bureau of Wuhan City with his wife. No reason has been given for his detention.

As reported on 18 February 2019 by The Guardian, a Chinese surveillance company has been tracking the movements of at least 2.5 million residents in Xinjiang. The database contained the name, sex, ethnicity, ID number, birth date and employer of residents in Xinjiang and included 6.7m location points of 'trackers' that residents had passed in the past 24 hours.

On 11 June 2020, an owner of a flower shop was smashed in his head with a flower pot by an officer from the urban management bureau in Quyang County (Baoding City, Hebei Province). It was reported that the flower shop was operating illegally and occupying a road. While the owner and his wife were attempting to move their goods away, the urban management officers continued to seize their properties. The aggrieved owner shouted at the urban management personnel, before an officer picked up a flower pot and smashed it in the owner's head. His wife also sustained some abrasions in her leg during the scuffles. It was reported that the urban management personnel had been mobilised for law enforcement against merchants who were operating illegally on the roads, as part of the county government's campaign to beautify the appearance of the county.

On 8 June 2020, footballers and coaches from Liaoning Hongyun, and some parents of footballers demonstrated at the Liaoning Provincial Physical Education Bureau in Hunnan District (Shenyang City, Liaoning Province) against wage arrears owed to them by the football club. It was reported that the Bureau called the police who came to the scene to disperse the crowd. The team members had previously petitioned for the same issue on 25 May 2020 and was promised to be paid their wages within a week later. The football club had its registration revoked by the Chinese Football Association in May 2020 due to wage arrears.

On 18 April 2020, more than a dozen unidentified persons assaulted and took away the mobile phones of many reporters in Yuanyang County (Xinxiang City, Henan Province), where the reporters were conducting interviews at a cemetery. The assault took place after four children suffocated to death after being buried alive at an illegal construction site. ACcording to the county Publicity Department, family members of the children assaulted the reporters as they were not happy with the interviews. The mobile phones were returned to the reporters by the subdistrict office on 21 April 2020, with all contents related to the incident having been erased.

Around 24 June 2020 (as reported), China began building taxiways, aprons, hangars for military aircraft at the Tibet Linzhi Milin Airport in Mainling County (Nyingchi City, Tibet), close to the border with India. This followed the deadly clash between Indian and Chinese soldiers at the Line of Actual Control in Galwan Valley on 15 June 2020. According to the latest satellite images released, air defence missile positions were also built near the airport.

On 13 May 2020, at least 5 people of the Macau Family Reunion Federation petitioned outside the government headquarters in Macao (Macao Special Administrative Region), calling on the authorities to resolve the issue surrounding the reunification of families with overage children. The group stated that they had repeatedly petitioned to urge the authorities to resettle overage children in Macau as soon as possible but had not received any updates on the matter.
On 27 April 2020, the cross of a Christian church located on Suzhou Road in Luyang District (Hefei City, Anhui Province) was demolished by the authorities.

On 18 April 2020, the cross of a Catholic church in Ma'anshan City, Anhui Province was demolished by the community chairperson and several youths. They were informed by the county's United Front Work Department five days ago that the crosses from Christian and Catholic churches had to be demolished.

Around 3 April 2019 (in the 26 days before 16 April 2019), city officials from the Ministry of Land and Resources had demolished 5,911 Taoist Tudigong temples in Gaoyou city (Jiangsu) in the past 26 days (coded on April 3 due to aggregation). Officials claimed that the temples were constructed illegally, and carried out restoration and re-forestation projects on the lands reclaimed.

On 7 November 2019, more than 30 apartment owners gathered and kneeled on the ground in front of the government offices of Dingzhou City (Baoding City, Hebei Province) to demand government action in solving their problems regarding their residence. Police arrived and called 4 of them to the police office for disturbing public order. There was no further report on this event.
Around 25 January 2019 (as reported), employees of a gym gathered in front of the company located in Zhongshan District (Dalian, Liaoning) to demand for wage arrears.

On 31 March 2019, about 12 Tibetan families were evicted from their homes in resource-rich Gonjo County (Chamdo, Tibet) by police. The families, who were moved to Kongpo prefecture, had resisted orders to relocate from their ancestral land by Chinese authorities for months, despite promises that new land and housing would be provided for them.

Between 11 January and 13 January, nearly 100 villagers of the Sui minority ethnic group in Jichang Township, Duyun City demonstrated against the forced exhumation and cremation of bodies carried out by police. Demonstrators overturned police cars, smashed the cars with rocks, and threw stones at police, who retreated without arresting anyone or retaliating.

On 3 May 2020, 200 officials from the National Security and Religious Affairs Bureau raided a Protestant house church in Xinglin Residential District (Xiamen City, Fujian Province) and attempted to forcibly ban the believers from congregating. There was pushing and shoving between the officials and the believers, and during the scuffles, many believers were injured, including a believer who sustained slight fractures in his ribs. 9 believers were taken away by the officials for interrogation.

On 27 March 2020, thousands of residents and police officers from Hubei Province marched up the bridge over Yangtze River (which connects Hubei and Jiangxi Province) in Huangmei County (Huanggang City, Hubei Province) towards the checkpoint of Jiangxi Province, right after Jiangxi police refused to allow Hubei residents attempting to return to work to pass through the checkpoint. Officers and residents from both sides clashed, and some individuals supporting the Hubei police overturned a police car and destroyed other equipment belonging to the Jiangxi police officers. 5 Jiangxi police officers were reportedly injured. It was reported a group of migrant workers were allowed by the Jiangxi Province to pass, which sparked opposition from aggrieved residents from Hubei against what was perceived as the continued discrimination against them despite the lifting of travel restrictions imposed during the coronavirus outbreak.

During the last week of March 2019, an Uyghur businessman died at a local hospital in Xinjiang after being brought in from a re-education camp for medical treatment. The official cause of death was 'myocardial arrest,' but authorities refused to release his remains, and prepared his burial without allowing the involvement of family members.

On 20 August 2019, many people who showed support for an anti-rightist activist at a local court in Wuzhong District (Suzhou, Jiangsu) were driven away by the police, forbidding them to stay near the court and forcing them to a subway station.

Between 11 January and 13 January, nearly 100 villagers of the Sui minority ethnic group in Jichang Township, Duyun City demonstrated against the forced exhumation and cremation of bodies carried out by police. Demonstrators overturned police cars, smashed the cars with rocks, and threw stones at police, who retreated without arresting anyone or retaliating.
