notes: On 13 April 2019, about 300 residents gathered in Wangcheng district of Changsha, Hunan to oppose the state authorities' construction of a high-voltage power line tower near residential areas and schools. Police officers arrested more than ten people. Hundreds of police, special police and armed police were mobilised, and at least six buses full of special police and armed police were on standby nearby.

Between 11 January and 13 January, nearly 100 villagers of the Sui minority ethnic group in Jichang Township, Duyun City demonstrated against the forced exhumation and cremation of bodies carried out by police. Demonstrators overturned police cars, smashed the cars with rocks, and threw stones at police, who retreated without arresting anyone or retaliating.

On 19 September 2019, a Tibetan monk in the Ngaba county (also known as Aba county, Sichuan Province) was taken into custody by Chinese authorities and has been held incommunicado for at least 2 weeks. The arrest was likely related to his pro-Tibetan language post on wechat. His whereabout and the official reason for the arrest was not known.

On 3 September 2019, a family church at Taiyuan (Shanxi Province) was shut down by the police and the Xinghualing Religious Affairs office while it was hosting a gathering of around 200 people. It was reported that the closing down of the church was related to the upcoming National Day on 1 October. Meanwhile, events of church destructions had been reported in the past year across several provinces including Shandong, Henan, Anhui and Jiangxi.

On 24 September 2019, a leader of an evangelical church in Qiupo village, Tanghe county, Nanyang City (Henan Province) was taken away by the police and has not been heard from for at least a week thereafter. He had been ordered earlier by the government to demolish the church built on the commune land but he refused to do so. [location coded at Wolong]

On 14 March 2019, a man wielding two cleavers attacked 17 students outside a primary school in Tangshan City (Hebei) while they were waiting to be let in. The assailant, who was arrested at the scene, claimed that he had been 'forced to do so' by the former chief of the public security bureau. All the victims were hospitalised but none sustained life-threathening injuries.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2012-) People's Armed Police
notes: On 22 March 2019, about 700 villagers demonstrated at Sanhongqi Village, Beijiao Town in Shunde District (Foshan, Guangdong) in opposition to the selling off of their land at low prices by village officials. Demonstrators shouted slogans, carried banners, and got into clashes with riot police, who arrested about 60 of them.

On 12 May 2019, more than 100 bereaved parents who lost their children in the 2008 earthquake were beaten up by 200 police and government officers at the site of a collapsed high-school in Dujiangyan City (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province). The parents were attacked when they were hanging banners and placards for a quake memorial for victims. Several injured parents were sent to the hospital.

On 12 May 2019, protestant home churches were taken over by the authorities in Nanchang City of Jiangxi Province. In addition to three other cities, a total of more than 10 house churches were sealed off on the same day as part of a national campaign to crack down on home churches.

On 12 May 2019, protestant home churches were taken over by the authorities in Pidu District (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province). In addition to three other cities, a total of more than 10 house churches were sealed off on the same day as part of a national campaign to crack down on home churches.

On 12 May 2019, protestant home churches were taken over by the authorities in Xiamen city of Fujian Province. In addition to three other cities, a total of more than 10 house churches were sealed off on the same day as part of a national campaign to crack down on home churches.

On 1 May 2019, hundreds of protesters from the gaming sector participated in the International Workers' Day protest to demand better working conditions in front of the Macau government headquarters (Macau).

On 25 December 2019, a few thousand students and their parents gathered at the Shaoxing University Yuanpei College in Yuencheng District (Shaoxing, Zhejiang) to demonstratorte against the schools's decision to let the school be acquired by a real estate company in Shaoxing. Demonstrators shouted slogans and demanded a response from the school. In an attempt to stop the demonstration, the school closed the campus, disabled internet and deleted threads on Weibo. Demonstrators clashed with the security guards and some demonstrators broke through the cordon line to get to the Provincial Education Commission. Police officers and cars were also on standby at the scene.

As reported on 16 May 2019, the government authorities seized the land of as many as 40 Tibetan families in Chunga village, near Qabqa City (Hainan Tibetan Autonomous, Qinghai) in order to make way for airport construction.

On 14 November 2019, dozens of policemen and personnel from religious affairs bureau and fire department in Pukou District (Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province) demolished a Three-Self church in the district which served nearly 1,000 believers. They forcibly entered the church around 4pm and dragged out the people who were meeting inside. Some believers refused to leave and got beaten. It was reported that multiple officially approved churches in Nanjing city had received orders to demolish their churches and transfer their members to larger churches so that the government can administer more easily.

On 23 April 2019, over 100 Mongolian herders continued to petition and organized a sit-in outside government offices in Urad Middle Banner (Inner Mongolia), after a dozen of them were arrested the day before while petitioning for sheepfold subsidies and subsidies for inhabitants living near the border. They demanded for the immediate release of all arrested herders.

Around 23 April 2019 (as reported), a Christian church at an unspecified village in Hohhot (Inner Mongolia) was demolished during Easter on the grounds of being illegally constructed. There were reported clashes between several hundred worshippers and the police forces and demolition staff.

On 28 March 2019, a bomb was set off in the Shenyang Public Security Bureau Traffic Police Detachment Heping No.1 Brigade in Heping District (Shenyang, Liaoning). 2 police officers and 1 civilian were injured, while the suspect died at the scene. It is suspected that the suspect set off the bomb in retaliation to oppression by the authorities.
As reported on 18 July 2019, 3,600 more monks and nuns have been evicted from the Yachen Gar Tibetan Buddhist centre. This is a continuation of the expulsion since May 2019.

On 15 April 2019, a netizen was incommunicado after being detained by the Nantong prefecture police (Jiangsu). Officials searched his house the next day, but did not explain their allegations or reason for detention. The detainee was an online activist who often published articles, and petitioned for the list of victims in the '3.21' Xiangshui County Industrial Park explosion to be released.

From 10 to 11 April 2019, about 200 Catholics staged a silent sit-in protest at the Roman Catholic Diocese of Fengxiang County (Baoji, Shaanxi) to prevent up to 600 police officers and government personnel from demolishing their church. The protest lasted for more than 30 hours.

Around 5 May 2020 (as reported), a woman was forcibly taken away by government officials from her place of residence in Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province and admitted into a psychiatric hospital. This came six months after she had been release from the psychiatric hospital. It was unclear if she had been administered antipsychotic drugs after being admitted to the hospital this time around. She was previously forcibly admitted into a psychiatric hospital in 2018 for splashing ink on a portrait of Xi Jinping.

On 23 June 2019, tens of thousands of villagers marched in Mingtang Village (Yunfu, Guangdong) to oppose the construction of a garbage incineration power plant in the city. They also blocked highways and demanded the government to withdraw the project due to health concerns. The government withdrew the project on the same day.

On 17 April 2019, an independent writer was taken away by police at the Taining Buddhist Association in Fujian and his whereabouts were unknown thereafter. He had published a regular article on Taining Buddhism that accidentally linked to a personal blog on justice for the politically-sensitive death of his son.

As reported on 19 April 2019, Sichuan authorities had declared that no new residents will be allowed to reside or study at the state-backed, full-time religious institute Larung Gar Buddhist Academy in Laronggou, Luoruo town (Larung Gar) of Serthar county (Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan). Walls were built and checkpoints were set up.

As reported on 2 July 2019, the Chinese police pepper sprayed 3 human rights lawyers in Luoshan county in Xinyang city, Henan and took them away when they were visiting another human rights lawyer who was prosecuted as part of the '709 crackdown' and recently got released.

On 10 April 2019, about 200 Catholics staged a silent sit-in protest at the Roman Catholic Diocese of Fengxiang County (Baoji, Shaanxi) to prevent up to 600 police officers and government personnel from demolishing their church. The protest lasted for more than 30 hours.

On 11 June 2020, a church in Jimei District (Xiamen City, Fujian Province) was forcibly demolished by hundreds of police from the city's Public Security Bureau, Urban Management Bureau, firefighters and Religious Affairs Bureau. This followed a raid on the church by the police on 3 May 2020, where believers were arrested. Some believers reported that the church had been harassed by the authorities for refusing to join the state-run Three-Self church.

In May 2019, more than 500 Kazakh women from a local factory were secretly transferred by Chinese police from Ili Kazak Autonomous (Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region) to an unknown place during Ramadan.

On 16 April 2019, more than 200 herders protested outside a public security bureau in Inner Mongolia demanding that the authorities release an ethnic Mongolian herder-cum-author arrested for an earlier protest at Lake Dalainuur. One of the demonstrators was arrested by the police and detained for a couple of hours.

In April 2019, an Uyghur high school teacher from Kuqa County, Xinjiang was sent to a re-education camp in Kuqa County (Aksu, Xinjiang). It was reported that an unidentified official had confirmed that the teacher was detained in the re-education camp in the county, but did not specify the reasons for his detention.

On 21 June 2019, hundreds of villagers marched in Mingtang Village (Yunfu, Guangdong) to oppose the construction of a garbage incineration power plant in the city. They demanded the government to withdraw the project due to health concerns. Protesters marched every day until 23 June.

Around 23 April 2019 (as reported), a Christian church in Guojiaying village, Taohua township of Yuquan district (Hohhot, Inner Mongolia) was demolished by local authorities during Easter on the grounds of being illegally constructed and not registered with state authorities. Close to 100 worshippers surrounded the church to prevent the demolition, but they were dispersed by the police without reported injuries or violence. This was a part of an organized effort to 'Sinicise' all religions.

On 28 January 2020, thousands of people demonstrated in Xiapu County (Ningde City, Fujian Province) against the government's plan to build a quarantine site for the coronavirus near the residential area of the county. They blocked the road into the village, and threw wooden objects and other debris at the police.

On 10 May 2020, a large number of people held a protest march along Ping'an Road in Hongshan District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province), against the construction of substations in the residential area. They held banners and shouted slogans, expressing their concerns that the substation would be located only 27 metres away from the nearest residential building, and dozens of schools and training institutions in the vicinity. It was reported that during the demonstration, some people were blocked and pushed to the ground by the police.

On 20 November 2019, nearly 1,000 police and other government workers in Chuxiong City (Chuxiong Yi Autonomous, Yunnan City) set out to demolish the Mosque in the city that had lasted for nearly 80 years. They arrived in the morning, dragged out the people who were praying in the mosque, and managed to demolished the exterior wall, kitchen and toilet section of the estate. Some believers tried to stop the demolition. It was reported that many believers were beaten by government workers during the demolition, and a 80-year-old man was sent to the hospital for emergency treatment.

On 20 November 2019, more than 1000 police, government personnel and groups of unknown individuals surrounded a Mosque in Chuxiong City, Yunnan to demolish the mosque, without having agreed with the mosque management. They dragged Muslims who were praying outside of the mosque. In an hour, at least 35 Muslims brusquely entered the mosque and went to the top of the Islamic academic building. They threatened to jump off the building if the government demolish it. By that time, the kitchen and the walls of the mosque had already been demolished.

On 29 April 2019, 4 Tibetans gathered at an offering ceremony on a hill behind a monastery in Shiqu county, also named Sershul (Garze Tibetan Autonomous, Sichuan Province). A Tibetan shouted slogans calling for the release of the Panchen Lama and the reunion of the Panchen Lama and the Dalai Lama in Tibet. The police arrested the four people. A Tibetan who was physically disabled and unable to speak was released on the next day.

As reported on 1 August 2019, many male students from a Hebei University protested at a local police station in Handan, Hebei province to support a victim of sexual assault by a Pakistani male student. Under massive pressure, the police detained and later repatriated the Pakistani student.

On 13 April 2020, at least dozens of merchants held a protest march on Guanggu Pedestrian Street in Hongshan District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province, demanding for rent reductions. They held and chanted slogans during the demonstration, calling for the government to reduce rent for businesses. It was reported that arrests were made by the police during the demonstration. The demonstration was one of many demonstrations that had erupted across China since the easing of mobility restrictions in many of the provinces, where merchants and taxi drivers had taken to the streets calling for a reduction or waiver of rental fees, in support of their significantly reduced incomes during the coronavirus outbreak.

On 21 July 2019, at least 10 people participated in a demonstration in Lianzhou city, Qingyuan in Guangdong province against water pollution allegedly produced by a mining company as it carried out stealth mining. These rioters used sticks to break police cars. The city government had set up an investigation unit to look into this matter.

On 12 June 2020, more than 100 personnel from the Religious Affairs Bureau, Public Security Bureau and demolition workers raided a church in Zhengzhou City, Henan Province. They removed church properties, subdued believers and demolished the church. It was reported that one believer was beaten up by the officials during the demolition.
On 8 January 2020, employees of Xi'An Aircraft Industrial Design Co. Ltd (Xi'An, Shaanxi Province) demonstrated against pension funds owed to them by the company.

In the month of August 2019, five to six thousand dormitories were demolished at the Yachen Gar Tibetan Buddhist center in Baiyu/Palyul County (Garze Tibetan Autonomous, Sichuan Province) following a similar number of monks and nuns removed from the residents in May. Around 600 military personnel were deployed to monitor the inhabitants during the demolition. The demolition was said to be 'an unfolding political strategy' aimed at controlling the influence and growth of Tibetan Buddhist study and practice and dated back to early 2001.

On 22 April 2019, over 100 Mongolian herders petitioned at the government offices in Urad Middle Banner (Inner Mongolia). Police forces prevented the herders from getting into the building, and armed police and a government official were on the scene. Around a dozen protesters were arrested for the petition itself, 'thrown into SWAT vehicles,' as well as for seeking the assistance of other rights defenders. The petitioners were expressing discontent after the government promised sheepfold subsidies and subsidies for inhabitants living near the border, then failed to deliver.

On 18 March 2020, a villager was crushed to death by an excavator in Xiaqiao Village, Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province by government officials, after attempting to block the demolition of his village. It was reported that the villagers have been fighting against the forced demolition of their village for more than a month. After the incident, the officials dispatched a large number of police officers to seal off the area, while aggrieved villagers demonstrated and placed more than 80 wreaths at the site. 1 man killed.

On 8 June 2020, more than 100 officials from the Nanguan District's Religious Affairs Bureau, Public Security Bureau, and Land and Resources Bureau demolished a Three-Self church in Nanguan District (Changchun City, Jilin Province). Nearly 100 believers were guarding the church to prevent its demolition, and a large number of police officers were on guard with shields at the scene. A wheelchair-bound believer was reportedly pushed to the ground by a demolition staff.
On 28 September 2019, around 12-13 people gathered in Changsha (Hunan province). Some of them held banners to protest against the upcoming 1 October National Parade and were arrested the day after.

notes: On 16 December 2019, a large group of residents of Boyang Town, Maoming, Guangdong demonstrated in Boyang Town over plans to build a crematorium in their neighbourhood. The government agreed to suspend the plan to build the crematorium the day after.

On 9 March 2019, demonstrators marched in Sao Lazaro, Macau to protest against the recognition by the local government of the driving licenses from inland China. They demanded that the local government abolished the plan and to consult the public.

On 12 February 2019, a female petitioner from Zhou village, Huancheng town (Weishan, Jining, Shandong) was abducted from her home by people employed by the government and held in a nursing house in Weishan county. She was released on the 26 March 2019. It was part of a campaign by the local police to silence dissent during the annual meetings of Two Sessions.

On 15 March 2019, a worshipper of the Protestant Early Rain Covenant Church went incommunicado in Chengdu (Sichuan), and was reportedly last seen at Hangzhou East Station with undercover officers, his head shaved and his hands cuffed. Around 8 December 2019 (during the 10 days from 3 December 2019), a retired female worker was severely beaten up by police while being detained in Taiyuan, Shanxi. She was arrested on 3 Dec for sharing Hong Kong protest videos online and detained for 10 days.

On 12 June 2019, 24 mine workers protested at the Shaanxi provincial government in Xincheng District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to ask for help from the government to get back more than 300,000 RMB worth of wage arrears owed to them by a mining site in Yuyang, Yilin.

On 19 March 2020, 15 petitioners went to the Pingxiang Anyuan People's Court in Anyuan District (Pingxiang, Jiangxi Province) to file a lawsuit against the city's local newspaper including its president and responsible editors for publishing fake news. It was reported that on 29 March 2020, the petitioners received the ruling that the lawsuit had been rejected by the court. This was the second time that the same group of petitioners had filed a lawsuit against their local newspaper for the same reasons.

On 25 February 2019, dozens of people who had purchased houses off-plan from developers petitioned at the Xi'an Lianhu People's Government in Lianhu District (Xi'an, Shaanxi). Protesters urged the district government to pressure the developer to hand over the properties to buyers.

On 4 June 2019, more than 100 people protested at the Xi'an Public Security Bureau in Lianhu (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to demand the Bureau to strengthen its investigation into a loan case and to help them demand 1.67 billion RMB loan arrears owed to more than 34,000 people by an agricultural company.

On 8 November 2019, more than 40 residents from an estate in Shaanxi Province went to petition at the provincial government offices in Xincheng District, Xi'an City, because their purchased houses had been seized by the authorities following a court order, due to the unpaid debt owed by the estate developer to a third party.

On 22 April 2019, more than 20 petitioners gathered at the hall of Shaanxi People's Government in Xincheng district (Xi'an) to demand the government to stop 'diminishing their petitioning efforts' and responding with actions and attitudes such as 'refutation, deception, deceit, dispersion, beatings and arrests.' Around 20-30 police officers arrived to explain the regulations surrounding petitioning actions, and confiscated their protest armbands and placards. Three petitioners were handled in a rough manner with their arms twisted, and driven away by police car.

On 19 November 2019, more than 200 people gathered at the Shaanxi provincial government offices in Xincheng District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to demand government intervention in solving their disputes with some estate developing companies. These people all bought apartments in one residence area in Xi'an City and had been petitioning since 2012 because the estate developing companies failed to deliver apartments as promised.

On 12 April 2019, 41 contract workers petitioned at the Xi'an Letters and Calls Reception Centre in Beilin District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to urge the government to find out the whereabouts of their contractor who owed them wages and to make him pay up.

On 13 March 2019, 3 police officers broke into the home of a petitioner in Xuetian Village/Xuetiancun (Jingang Town, Zhangjiagang, Suzhou, Jiangsu), broke her things, and beat and pushed her until she wasn't able to get up from the floor or bend her waist. After the attack, hospital and police personnel refused to see to her and her assailants continued to monitor her.

On 3 April 2020, 15 petitioners from Pingxiang City (representing over 40 petitioners from the same city) petitioned at the Pingxiang Anyuan People's Court in Anyuan District (Pingxiang, Jiangxi Province) against the city's local newspaper including its president and responsible editors for publishing fake news. This was in response to the ruling received on 29 March 2020 that the previous petition had been rejected by the court.

On 20 May 2019, around 600 retrenched community, substitute, and kindergarten teachers from various cities in Shaanxi Province gathered at Shaanxi's Government Building in Xincheng District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to petition for a one-time economic compensation and higher living allowance.

On 3 March 2019, more than 50 workers with pneumoconiosis staged a protest at the Railway Station Square and Wangcheng Park in Xigong District (Luoyang, Henan) to urge the Yiyang County Government to promptly resolve their demands for medical treatment and financial compensation. Protesters 'strolled about' in t-shirts with slogans. It was reported that the protest lasted until 7 March 2019

On 12 April 2019, a female petitioner from Zhou village, Huancheng town (Weishan, Jining, Shandong) was abducted from her home by people employed by the government and held in a nursing house in Weishan county (Jining City, Shandong Province). She was released on the 1 May 2019. This is the second time she's been abducted since 12 February. It was part of a campaign by the local police to silence dissent before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation which held in Beijing on April 25-27.

On 1 March 2019, a petitioner from Dongfanghong Village, Yongshun, Hunan was kidnapped by police officers, village committee members, and the mayor of her village when the train she was on stopped at the Baoding railway station in Baoding City (Hebei). She was then sent in the direction of Hubei.

On 15 May 2019, more than 10 representatives of retired private enterprise employees petitioned to the Human Resources and Social Security Department in Gulou District (Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province). They demanded competitive pensions for retired private enterprise employees under the 'double track' pension system.

On 16 August 2019, more than 100 tenants who had pre-purchased homes but were not able to move in in time due to a delay in the completion of the construction project protested at Shaanxi provincial government in Xincheng, Xi'an city to demand that the government exercised its power to order the construction company to complete the building construction project as soon as possible.

On 17 March 2019, a female petitioner was beaten by her community office director and other employees when she was waiting to meet people from the Luyang District government offices (Hefei City, Anhui Province). She was forcibly taken back to her community. She reported the case to the Hefei police but the police refused to assist with the case. It was reported that the petitioner had appealed several times against the demolition of her house, where she was not resettled as promised.

Around 7 December 2019, an activist in Shanxi sent a message that he was held in a mental hospital by government security forces, where he was forced to delete all his Tweets from his Twitter account. He has since lost contact, and his Twitter account had been shut down on 12 December 2019.

On 10 June 2019, more than 100 people who had made the repayment for their apartments of a residential housing protested at the Shaanxi provincial government in Xincheng District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to demand the government handle the case where the residential project had ceased since July 2018. They wanted the government to protect their rights.

On 15 November 2019, more than 20 workers went to the Shaanxi provincial government offices in Xincheng District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to demand government intervention in collecting their wage arrears owed by a coal mine owner in the province. The government called the mine owner and his family to the office to negotiate on the same day. The wife of the mine owner assaulted one worker and got pushed to the floor. Police took the mine owner, his wife and the worker to the police office and instructed them for a few hours before releasing them.

On 27 May 2019, an unknown number of people protested at the Letters Bureau Reception Center in Beilin (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to petition the government to bear responsibility for supervisory negligence and take effective measures to force a real estate developer to refund the money to residents who bought their houses but did not receive the houses.

On 24 September 2019, a female citizen from Nanjing was knocked unconscious by government officials in Xuanwu, Nanjing and sent to a 'black jail' where she was deprived of any rights, including the right to watch TV, read, write, etc. She was released on 6 October 2019. Her home had been destroyed by the government in 2014 and she hass been seeking legal redress for this matter since.

On 19 April 2019, three petitioners from Yunxi County, Hubei Province were beaten up by private security personnel (who were reportedly paid by officials from the Letters and Calls Bureau in Yunxi County) at a deserted site dozens of miles away from Yunxi County. 2 female petitioners were reportedly covered in injuries. The petitioners were first taken away on 18 April 2019 by more than 20 private security personnel near the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng District (Beijing). After having their identity cards and mobile phones taken away, they were forcibly driven back to Yunxi County.

On 13 November 2019, more than 30 migrant workers from Guizhou and Hubei went to petition at Shaanxi Provincial Government Offices in Xincheng District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to ask for the government to intervene in getting back their wage arrears owed by a construction company in Xi'an.

On 10 May 2019, 600 to 700 residents from an estate in Shaanxi Province went to the Xi'an City petition offices in Beilin District to demand the government to take more actions against their estate developing company which had failed to issue the residents their property certificates for more than 6 years. They held national flags and banners outside the government offices. This was in response to the failure of the district government to provide a satisfactory answer on 9 May 2019 as promised.

On 20 May 2019, more than 300 residents protested and petitioned at the provincial government of Shaanxi in Xincheng District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to demand the government to reselect the location for the relocation of a thermo power station so it is farther away from densley populated residential areas.

On 28 August 2019, some migrant workers protested outside the Shaanxi provincial government in Xicheng, Xi'an, Shaanxi to request the government to intervene in a case regarding wage arrears owed to them by a gardening company in Hancheng city, Shaanxi. Workers waited outside the building for their issues to be addressed and spent their nights there. It was reported that the protest lasted until 30 August 2019.

On 25 April 2019, nearly 100 laid-off community, substitute, and kindergarten teachers from Zhaotong, Qujing, Kunming, Honghe and other cities petitioned to the Yunnan Provincial Party Committee in Xishan District (Kunming City, Yunnan Province) to demand fair pensions and social benefits according to their years of work.

On 28 May 2019, six art workers went missing in Nanjing (Jiangsu Province) during their exhibition tour. One of them had his home raided by the police on 29 May. Police told his wife that he was in detention due to potential charge of the 'crime of picking quarrels and provoking troubles', but there was no official decision issued. No further report on what happened during the period when they were missing.

On 24 February 2019, 44 members of the Early Rain Covenant Church, including women, children, and the elderly, were arrested by police while having Sunday church service in their homes in Chengdu (Sichuan). A couple was slapped by the police at the detention centre. 11 remained in detention, one of whom was beaten up the same day, another couldn't be located or contacted, and the others were released the same day.

On 22 April 2019, seven petitioners were intercepted by police officers who broke into their accommodation in Fangshan district (Beijing). They were transferred to the Shanghai Liaison Office, then sent to a Relief Service Centre 'black jail' near Beijing South Station in Fengtai and Dongcheng districts. They were escorted back to Shanghai sometime in between 22-24 April.

On 23 September 2019, an activist from Changsha, Hunan went missing in Changsha. He reported the day before that some National Security Force officials wanted to meet him due to the incident in which another activist from Hunan was found dead in a detention centre earlier. He then became unreachable on phone. He has been missing for four days by the time of reporting.

Around 1 October 2019 (during the 13 days from 24 September 2019), a citizen in Nanjing was held in the black jail for 13 days and severely beaten by government employees of the Xuanwu District (Nanjing, Jiangsu Province). She was knocked unconscious and taken to the 'black jail' on 24 Sep because of her previous pleading activities to get government compensations for her destroyed houses. She was eventually dropped on the side of a road near her home because the government staff feared that she might die from injuries.

On 31 October 2019, 7 people went to the Hefei General Trade Union in Shushan District (Hefei City, Anhui Province) to petition. 4 of them asked for better treatment for the workers who had to retire due to injuries at work. The other 3 complained that they had been treated unfairly by their local community office in an apartment distribution for workers at a state owned factory.

On 15 March 2019, a man was arrested by Chengdu police (Sichuan Province) and was held incommunicado until 5 July. He was released on 24 October 2019. His arrest was reportedly in connection with the shut down of Early Rain Covenant Church in Chengdu on 9 December 2018. He has worked extensively with American and Hong Kong organizations to collect information in relation to the treatment of prisoners and the death penalty in China.

On 16 November 2019, more than 20 workers went to the Shaanxi provincial government offices in Xincheng District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to demand government intervention in collecting their wage arrears owed by a coal mine owner in the province. Given that there was no solution achieved, these workers continued petitioning at the Shaanxi provincial government offices until the time of the report on 19 November 2019.

On 22 April 2019, as many as 300 miners-cum-migrant workers and manufacturing workers gathered at a park opposite the Shanxi Province Central Committee of the CPC in Yingze district (Taiyuan, Shanxi), and petitioned at various government buildings. They demanded answers to their retirement funds being cut, and labour-related compensations owed to them such as production subsidies and unemployment allowances.

On 22 April 2019, residents from an estate in Shaanxi Province went to the Yanta District government offices in Xi'an City to demand the government to take more actions against their estate developing company which had failed to issue the residents their property certificates for more than 6 years. The District government promised to respond by 10 May 2019.

On 15 July 2019, around 40 residents from Yuejiazhai in Yanta, Xi'an in Shaanxi province petitioned at the Shaanxi Provincial Party Committee of the CCP to demand that the Qujiang Management Committee returned 10 acres of land resold to Yuejiazhai, built facade houses as promised and resolved any related problems regarding settlement.
On 13 March 2019, a female villager at Zhangjiagang (Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province) was beaten by government employees when they tried to confiscate her family's contracted farm land.

On 8 January 2020, villagers from Huangyan Village, Beilin District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) collectively went to the Beilin District Government to petition against the resettlement and reconstruction plans of their villages.

Around 15 September 2019 (month of), a female petitioner from Zhou village, Huancheng town (Weishan, Jining, Shandong) was abducted from her home by people employed by the government and held in a nursing house in Huancheng town (Weishan county, Jining City, Shandong Province). She was still guarded by 8 people in the nursing house by the time of report on 14 November 2019. This is the third time she's been abducted since 12 February 2019 due to the upcoming 70th anniversary of Chinese National Day.

On 14 November 2019, hundreds of people gathered on streets near a residence area in Weiyang District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to demand government intervention in solving their disputes with the estate developing companies for that residence area. These people all bought apartments in that residence area and had been petitioning since 2012 because the companies failed to deliver apartments as promised.

On 26 February 2019, a petitioner from Wuxi who had his home demolished was petitioning at the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng when personnel from the Wuxi City government threw a hood over his head and kidnapped him back to Wuxi. On 4 March 2019, 20 private, substitute, and kindergearten teachers who had been dismissed petitioned at the Dali Bureau Of Education, in Dali County (Weinan, Shaanxi) to demand for pension, medical insurance, and financial compensation.

On 5 November 2019, more than 300 residents from an estate in Shaanxi Province went to the Xi'an City petition offices in Beilin District to demand the government to take more actions against their estate developing company which had failed to issue the residents their property certificates for more than 6 years and failed to maintain the management and services at the estate.

On 6 June 2019, more than 20 residents of Country Garden, Xi'an protested at the Shaanxi provincial government in Xincheng District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to demand the government to address the issue regarding a primary school in the district depriving the right to school of their children. Around 29 June 2020 (as reported), up to 100 migrant workers demonstrated in Shihe District (Xinyang City, Henan Province) against wage arrears owed to them by a construction project.

Four government officials from her hometown, Jiuhua Town (Rugao City, Jiangxi Province) arrived at the scene with another car and tried to bring her back to Jiangxi. She reported to the police. By the time of report on 29 November 2019, she was sent to a hospital in Beijing in the afternoon. The other petitioner went missing with the unidentified group. Her family later received a notice from the Huishan Branch of the Public Security Bureau that she had been detained for 10 days for violating surveillance residence regulations.
Around 30 November 2019 (end of month), the meeting venue of a Local Church in Sizhou town (Dexing City, Jiangxi Province) was sealed off and closed, after they refused to join the Three-Self Church.

Around 30 September 2019 (end of month), the statue of the Virgin Mary in a Catholic sanctuary in Tianjiajing Village, Linzhou City (Anyang City, Henan Province) was demolished on orders by the United Front Work Department and the Religious Affairs Bureau of Linzhou City. Its altar was also buried in a pit. This was part of the government's crackdown on Catholic pilgrimage sites against clergy members and congregations that refused to join the Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association.

Around 30 September 2019 (end of month), the local government demolished crosses and religious signs in 22 churches and meeting venues in Linhe District (Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region). This was part of a broader campaign to pressure house churches to join the state-run churches.

A few days later, officials confiscated the keys to the church and locked all its doors and windows.

On 14 January 2019, the founder of a human rights website 64tianwang.com was said to put to court in Mianyang, Sichuan. They were sent back to their respective cities by government deputies. Three petitioners from Chongqing were also abducted by police on their way to Mianyang. Six church members, including the pastor, were arrested and taken away for interrogation. The meeting venue has been shut down.

Around 31 March 2019 (end of month), a Three-Self Church in Jincheng City, Shanxi Province was demolished by local authorities. It was reported that the church was first designated for relocation as part of a redevelopment plan, but the construction of a new church never materialised.

It was reported that police officers threw out all the items stored in the church, and took away remains such as windows and bricks from the church to be sold for their own gains.

Around 16 August 2019 (middle of month), a Buddhist temple in Xisaishan District (Huangshi City, Hubei Province) was sealed off with bricks on government orders. This was part of the ramped up efforts by local authorities to demolish outdoor Buddhist religious statues and temples.

Around 30 November 2019 (end of month), a large open-air Buddha statue at a temple in Xiaonan District (Xiaogan City, Hubei Province) was demolished on orders by Hubei Province's religious affairs administration. This was part of the ramped up efforts by local authorities to demolish outdoor Buddhist religious statues and temples.

Around 31 March 2019 (end of month), a Protestant house church venue in Wuchang District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province) was raided by government officials and the police. This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CCP to crack down on religious activities.
Around 16 May 2019 (middle of month), a Sola Fide house church meeting venue in Chenzhou City (Hunan Province) was shut down by the authority for refusing to join the Three-Self Church.

Around 31 July 2019 (end of month), local authorities painted over a memorial stone at the Dafo Temple at Baijia town (Dianjiang county, Chongqing) which read 'Heaven-Sent Buddha Mountain'. The name of the temple at its entrance was also smeared over with cement. The act was taken in the context of a nationwide crackdown on outdoor religious statues initiated by Chinese central government.

Around 30 September 2019 (end of month), government personnel went to a Catholic church in Tianjiajing, Linzhou (Henan). They removed and buried the Our Lady's Altar in the church forcibly. A church-goer tried to stop them from advancing but was dragged away.
