Around 30 November 2019 (end of month), a Buddhist temple in Suizhou City, Hubei Province was demolished by government officials. It was reported that the temple's person-in-charge was held in a government building for four days and forced to sign a statement agreeing to the demolition of the temple. Government officials threatened to dismiss her son from public office if she refused to sign the statement. This was part of a broader campaign to crackdown on places of worship under the ongoing religious persecution strategy by the central government.

Around 16 July 2019 (middle of month), one Protestant house church in Sili town, Guixi city (Yingtan City, Jiangxi Province) was raided by the government, with the venue emptied and around 7,600 RMB (about $ 1,060) worth of property confiscated by the authorities because the church did not join state-controlled religious organisations. The person in charge of the church was threatened to be arrested if he continued holding religious meetings.

Around 30 September 2019 (end of month), the Bishop of Wenzhou Diocese in Wenzhou City (Zhejiang Province) was taken away by national security personnel sent by the Religious Affairs Bureau to be indoctrinated because of the upcoming 10th anniversary of the death of the former Bishop of Wenzhou on 4 October. Both of the bishops had been punished by the authorities because they refused to join the state-controlled Chinese Patriotic Catholic Church. He was allowed to go home on 8 October.

Around 1 May 2019 (beginning of month), government officials led more than 10 villagers to smash and destroy all of the Buddhist statues of Shiyu Temple in Zhangqiu (Jinan, Shandong). The remains of the statues were buried in dug-out pits. This is part of a plan to crackdown on temples and outdoor religious venues as local officials prepared for a visit by the central government.

Around 1 April 2019 (beginning of month), a Protestant house church meeting venue in Tangxia town in Rui'an County (Wenzhou City, Zhejiang Province) was demolished by the authorities because the land was claimed for the construction of an industrial development zone. It was reported that the authorities had been using the pretext that the land was needed in order to crack down on religious activities.

Around 15 April 2020 (middle of month), the crosses of all 33 Three-Self churches in Hanshan County (Ma'anshan City, Anhui Province) were removed by officials from the county's United Front Work Department and other government institutions. It was reported that the city authorities had been publicly criticised by the provincial government for not removing crosses quickly enough.

Around 30 April 2019 (end of month), two large statues of the Medicine Buddha and Nanhai Guanyin in Chinese Buddhism in the Yaowang Valley Scenic Spot in Beichuan county (Mianyang City, Sichuan Province) were demolished according to the orders from Sichuan provincial government to advance the CCP's nationwide campaign to eliminate all open-air religious symbols.

Around 15 June 2019 (month of), a 29-meter-tall Shakyamuni Buddha statue in Fengman District in Jilin City (Jilin Province) was destroyed with explosives [controlled explosion] because local authorities claimed that it was 'too tall'. The demolition was carried out with government officials present on site. The act was taken according to the CCP's policy to remove outdoor religious statues nationwide.

Around 1 September 2019 (beginning of month), the meeting venue of New Life Church in Hegang City (Heilongjiang Province) was shut down by the authorities, because it was not a member of the state-controlled Three-Self Churches. This was part of a broader campaign to force house churches to join the state-controlled Three-Self churches.

Around 30 September 2019 (end of month), two house church meeting venues in Jixi City (Heilongjiang Province) were shut down by the authorities because they were not members of the state-controlled Three-Self Churches. This was part of a broader campaign to force house churches to join the state-controlled Three-Self churches.

Around 15 November 2019 (middle of month), 34 bodhisattva statues in a Buddhist temple in Songjia Town, Zizhong County (Neijiang City, Sichuan Province) were demolished by the authorities. The authorities also sealed off an 8-metre-tall Buddha statue. It was reported that this was part of a broader campaign launched by the government of Neijiang City to shut down Buddhist and Taoist temples on a large scale since March 2019.

Around 15 November 2019 (middle of month), a Tibetan Buddhist temple in Yangqu County (Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province) was raided by government personnel. The government personnel confiscated Tibetan Buddhist scriptures and ceremonial scarfs during the raid. This was part of a broader campaign to prevent the spread of Tibetan Buddhism among Han Chinese.

Around 15 April 2020 (middle of month), the cross of a Three-Self church was demolished by the local government. A local believer reported that the government is planning to convert to church into an elderly activity centre. It was reported that Protestants in the county had been targeted likely due to their considerably large number of believers.

Around 30 April 2020 (end of month), a local Three-Self church in Shegeng Town (Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province) was emptied by government personnel led by the town mayor. The government personnel removed the church's podium, cross, and all other religious symbols. It was reported that Protestants in the county had been targeted likely due to the considerably large number of believers.

Around 15 April 2020 (middle of month), the cross and other religious symbols of a local church venue in Fenglingtou Town, Guangxin District (Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province) was forcibly removed by the local officials. It was reported that the officials also looted the church's donation money. This was part of the broader campaign aimed at forcing house churches to join the state-run churches.

Around 1 November 2019 (beginning of month), five meeting venues of the old Local Church in Zhengqiao Town, Leping City (Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province) were shut down by the authorities. All furniture, crosses, and other religious symbols were removed. This was part of a broader campaign launched by the town government to shut down all unlicensed church under the town's jurisdiction.

Around 16 October 2019 (middle of month), an outdoor Earth Store Bodhisattva statue of a Buddhist temple in Weichang County (Chengde City, Hebei Province) was dismembered and later removed by the authorities. It was reported that the government had repeatedly forced the temple's person-in-charge to remove the statue, claiming that this was part of a national campaign.

Around 1 May 2020 (beginning of month), four folk religion temples at a village in Hanshan district (Handan, Hebei) were either completely leveled to the ground with an excavator by local officials and had deity statues destroyed, or had their entrances blocked and icons removed. It was reported that the government of Hebei had been cracking down on folk religion temples in rural communities since April of the same year. By the end of July, 104 temples were destroyed and 110 temples shut down or repurposed in the prefecture-level city of Handan.

Around 16 May 2020 (middle of month), three folk religion temples (including the Guanye Temple) were demolished with an excavator by government officials of Xiaoxibao township, Yongnian district (Handan, Hebei). Other temple owners in the region converted the temples into public activity or fitness centres to evade demolitions. It was reported that the government of Hebei had been cracking down on folk religion temples in rural communities since April of the same year. By the end of July, 104 temples were destroyed and 110 temples shut down or repurposed in the prefecture-level city of Handan.

Around 1 March 2019 (beginning of month), a petitioner was 'taken on mandatory vacation' by stability maintenance personnel from Zhanjiang prefecture (Hubei). He tried to escape and buy a train ticket to Beijing, but he was intercepted and 'taken on vacation' again until the end of the Lianghui conventions.

Around 30 September 2019 (end of month), a petitioner from Rugao, Jiangxi was abducted by government personnel in Beijing and sent back to Rugao, Jiangxi. He was beaten up during his way back to Jiangxi.

Around 31 August 2019 (end of month), five Christian churches in Nanyang City and Zhengzhou City, both in Henan Province, were demolished or partially destroyed by the authorities as part of the CCP's campaign to combine and limit the size of the Three-Self churches and confiscate their lands.

Around 1 April 2019 (beginning of month), Mongolian herders from Tongliao city petitioned in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia over access to indigenous grazing lands and other disputes and three of them were detained by the police. They were escorted home then placed under administrative detention for eight days.

Around 31 May 2020 (end of month), a former veteran (who was also a petitioner) was taken away by a large number of officials (including the chief) from the Weibin District Public Security Bureau from Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province. He remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 31 May 2020. He had just escaped around the same time after being illegally detained by the Baoji government since November 2018. It was reported that he had been illegally detained by the local government seven times for his petitioning.

On 28 July 2020, residents were severely injured and assaulted with tear gas by forced eviction personnel and armed thugs during an unannounced demolition operation at Xitai village in Huairou district (Beijing). Around 2700 personnel were reportedly present, and the demolition was conducted over a week. It was reported that the Jiuduhe government ordered the demolition.

On 31 July 2020, several workers staged a protest at the Labour Inspection Team in Xincheng district (Hohhot, Inner Mongolia) against sudden closure of an interior design company and to demand for wage arrears.

Around 16 January 2020 (month of), an Uyghur model and ex-convict was taken away by authorities in Foshan prefecture (Guangdong) and placed under 'compulsory measures' in Kuqa county (Aksu, Xinjiang), allegedly for assaulting health workers. Authorities stated that the transferral was part of a resettlement plan to help released prisoners, however evidence also showed them suggesting 'a few days of education at his local community' (an allegedly euphemism for the political re-education camps). Between January and February, he described spending 18 days shackled and hooded with over 50 others in a jail, then at an epidemic prevention centre. He went incommunicado in Mar 2020.

On 30 August 2020, ethnic Mongolian parents gathered in protest at the Sheebert Mongolian Middle School in Shebotu town of Horqin Left Middle Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region (and five other provinces) starting with the immediate fall semester. They came to demand the release of their children, as large-scale student boycotts, strikes and demonstrations spread across the region. A Mongolian student jumped to his death after learning that the armed police had beaten his mother at the school gates.

On 1 September 2020, ethnic Mongolian taxi drivers from Xilingol League (Inner Mongolia) stood outside their taxis and sang a widely-circulated Mongolian pastoral song named 'My Mongolia - Steppe Mongolia.' They were demonstrating in support of school boycotts across the region, against a new policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region. They defied government-imposed curfews starting 31 Aug (including and not limited to Tongliao prefecture).

On 1 September 2020, ethnic Mongolian parents and students protested at No.1 Middle School in Ganqika town of Horqin Left Rear Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions).

On 31 August 2020, ethnic Mongolian parents and students demonstrated at an unspecified location in Horqin district (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions). At least 129 people in relation to the event were wanted by the police.

Around 15 February 2020 (month of), the dome and star-and-crescent symbols were removed from a Hui Muslim mosque in Zhongtou town of Jia county (Pingdingshan, Henan), then changed to a Chinese-style structure in May 2020.

Around 1 June 2020 (beginning of month), the dome of a Hui mosque in the Kuancheng district (Changchun, Jilin) was demolished by the Religious Affairs Bureau and replaced with a Chinese-style hexagonal pavilion.
Around 15 April 2020 (month of), the domes and crescent symbols of two Hui Muslim mosques in Yuzhou county (Xuchang, Henan) were demolished.

Around 1 July 2020 (beginning of month), the dome of a Hui Muslim mosque in Baicheng city (Jilin) was demolished, and its indoor Arabic-style windows were in the process of being changed to a more traditional Chinese style. The converted mosque was said to resemble more of an office building.
Around 15 June 2020 (month of), a four-faced Guanyin statue atop the Qingfeng Mountain in Ezhou prefecture (Hubei) was forcibly demolished by the Liangzihu district government.

On 2 December 2019, dozens of government personnel (from the Religious Affairs Bureau, State Land Bureau and Urban Construction Bureau) demolished a Guanyin statue outside a Buddhist temple (Sanshui Palace) in Meizhou prefecture (Guangdong) on the grounds that it was too tall and built illegally.

Around 15 April 2020 (month of), local authorities removed crosses from a Three-Self church in Zhangzhuang town of Yi'nan county (Linyi, Shandong). Crosses were removed from churches across Shandong ahead of provincial government inspections.

On 20 May 2020, more than ten local government officials, including the heads of the United Front Work Department and Religious Affairs Bureau, removed a cross from Three-Self church in Lanling county (Linyi, Shandong). The cross was removed for being 'too eye-catching.' Crosses were removed from churches across Shandong ahead of provincial government inspections.
On 19 June 2020, government authorities demolished a Three-Self Church venue that had been closed down in Songyao village of Dengfeng county (Zhengzhou, Henan).

On 8 June 2020, 100 government-sent personnel demolished the state-approved Protestant Hongqi Christian Church in Changchun prefecture (Jilin). During the demolition, dozens of congregation members gathered outside the church, holding banners protesting against the demolition and singing hymns.

Around 16 August 2019 (month of), armed police with guns and handcuffs and front loaders sent by the local government demolished the Buddhist Pujing Temple in Gaopo village of Baota district (Yan'an, Shaanxi). It was reported that many Buddhist, Daoist and folk religion temples were demolished or shutdown in Shaanxi province during the year, with at least 50 temples destroyed in Yan'an county within a one-month period.

On 29 April 2020, local authorities removed a cross from a Three-Self church from Shanghe county (Dezhou, Shandong). Crosses were removed from churches across Shandong ahead of provincial government inspections.

Around 30 April 2020 (end of month), a nine-metres-tall outdoor Buddha statue at a local flower farm in Cenxi county (Wuzhou, Guangxi) was forcibly demolished by the county's United Front Work Department, armed police officers and hired workers for being 'unapproved and illegal, too tall and too large.'

On 7 July 2020, church members were attacked and beaten by security guards in Yongfu village (Wenzhou, Zhejiang) when officials from Yongjia county (Wenzhou, Zhejiang) led a 100-personnel demolition operation (mainly private security guards) to remove crosses from two Protestant venues, including a Three-Self Church and a house church.

Around 16 October 2019 (month of), government authorities demolished an outdoor Buddha statue (Maitreya statue) at Yongfu temple in Ningyuan county (Yongzhou, Hunan). The rebuilding and fundraising of the temple was approved more than a decade ago, but the government then decided that the statue was too eye-catching.

Around 15 November 2019 (month of), an outdoor Guanyin statue in Baixiang Temple in Xingwen county (Yibin, Sichuan) was forcibly demolished by the Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau, and over 30 Bodhisattva figures in the temple were smashed the same day.

On 2 January 2020, government-hired workers destroyed 24 statues at a Taoist venue in Dayu town (Suining, Sichuan). It was reported that from Oct 2019 to May 2020, at least 160 folk religion venues were demolished or shut down in four prefectures - Suining, Mianyang, Nanchong and Meishan - of Sichuan province, of which 116 temples were in Suining alone.

Around 15 June 2019 (month of), a group of people were seen destroying and burning things at the Daoist Wuliang Temple in Taibai county (Baoji, Shaanxi). All statues and other items were smashed, and ornaments on the walls were painted over. It was reported that many Buddhist, Daoist and folk religion temples were demolished or shutdown in Shaanxi province during the year.

Around 15 April 2020 (month of), local authorities removed crosses from a Three-Self Church in Rizhao city (Shandong) and another Three-Self church on Danyang Road, Donggang district (Rizhao, Shandong). Crosses were removed from churches across Shandong ahead of provincial government inspections.

On 8 November 2019, the town mayor and CPC Secretary of Dongju village, Yangping town of Chencang district (Baoji, Shaanxi) broke into a local Buddhist temple (San'guan Hall) and removed all its religious statues overnight. The statues were found smashed and loaded on a garbage truck the next day. It was reported that many Buddhist, Daoist and folk religion temples were demolished or shutdown in Shaanxi province during the year, with at least 100 temples closed in Baoji city within a ten-month period.

Around 15 November 2019 (month of), government authorities repurposed a Catholic church in Pingding township of Yujiang district (Yingtan, Jiangxi) into an entertainment centre for mahjong and cards or dance. It was reported that officials demanded the congregation to join the CPCA prior to this, and between March and April, officials visited local believers' homes to replace religious images with those of Chairman Mao Zedong.

Around 15 April 2020 (month of), local authorities tore down religious images and symbols at a Catholic house of prayer in Changpojiao village of Jianshui county (Honghe, Yunnan), then destroyed its Hall of the Virgin Mary before repurposing the venue. A centre for weddings and funerals was built in its place two months later.

On 30 May 2020, government-hired workers smashed all statues in the folk religion Jinhai Temple in Dayu town (Suining, Sichuan) and leveled the temple to the ground the next day. It was reported that from Oct 2019 to May 2020, at least 160 folk religion venues were demolished or shut down in four prefectures - Suining, Mianyang, Nanchong and Meishan - of Sichuan province, of which 116 temples were in Suining alone.

On 28 April 2020, the United Front Work Department and workers removed the cross from the state-run Protestant Hancheng Church in Hanshan county (Ma'anshan, Anhui). It was reported that all crosses taller than government buildings had to be removed in order not to overshadow state institutions. Churches had to be 'Sinicised' and had to look like enterprises.

On 12 May 2020, in the middle of the night, government officials dispatched three cranes and hundreds of police officers to remove crosses from the state-run Protestant Lingyunshan Christian Church in Dangtu county (Ma'anshan, Anhui).

Around 26 June 2020, over 30 personnel from the Public Security Bureau and other state institutions demolished a Catholic house of prayer in Dingtou village, Xiabaishi town of Fu'an county (Ningde, Fujian) on the grounds that the venue was 'illegally constructed.' It was reportedly one of several suppressions in the Diocese of Mindong in Fujian province, because priests refused to join the CPCA.

On 30 July 2020, the local government demolished a Three-Self Church in Fengfeng Mining District (Handan, Hebei) on the grounds of being 'illegally constructed' and engineering works at a nearby river.

On 26 November 2019, about 200 police officers and officials from the Religious Affairs Bureau blocked all the roads to folk religion Jade Emperor Hall in Dongpo district (Meishan, Sichuan) and blew up [controlled explosion] the temple with all its statues inside. It was reported that from Oct 2019 to May 2020, at least 160 folk religion venues were demolished or shut down in four prefectures - Suining, Mianyang, Nanchong and Meishan - of Sichuan province.

Around 16 May 2020 (month of), a Buddhist temple in Julu county (Xingtai, Hebei) was converted into a Mao Zedong Memorial Hall under a rectification operation supervised by government-assigned personnel. Publications about Mao had to be displayed, and Buddhist statues were removed.

On 28 May 2020, government-hired workers razed the folk religion Qinglong Mountain Temple to the ground in Dayu town (Suining, Sichuan) after tearing down statues of deities since January of the same year. It was reported that from Oct 2019 to May 2020, at least 160 folk religion venues were demolished or shut down in four prefectures - Suining, Mianyang, Nanchong and Meishan - of Sichuan province, of which 116 temples were in Suining alone.

On 19 May 2020, the roof cross and a statue of the Virgin Mary were forcibly removed from a Catholic church in a village of Lanling county (Linyi, Shandong) by local officials on the grounds that the cross was taller than the village committee building. Crosses were removed from churches across Shandong ahead of provincial government inspections.
On 6 July 2020, the local government demolished a Three-Self Church in Jianzhuang township (Handan, Hebei) on the grounds of being 'illegally constructed.'

On 15 April 2020, a Three-Self church in Fuxing district (Handan, Hebei) was destroyed on the grounds of being 'an illegal building.' Officials had reportedly planned its demolition over a year ago, but the congregation attempted to postpone it.

Around 16 May 2020 (month of), two crosses were removed from a Three-Self church in Tancheng county (Linyi, Shandong) on orders of government officials in order to avoid being shut down or having all its facilities destroyed and taken away. Crosses were removed from churches across Shandong ahead of provincial government inspections.

Around 23 July 2020, as many as 100 workers staged a sit-in protest in Bazhong prefecture (Sichuan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. They continued to protest for over 10 days as of 4 August.
Around 3 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 construction workers staged a protest in Puyang county (Puyang, Henan) after their company refused to compensate for work injuries.

Around 14 July 2020 (as reported), several dozen migrant workers staged a protest at the entrance of Country Garden in Baoji prefecture (Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by the property development company.

On 20 May 2020, several migrant workers petitioned and demonstrated at the Urban Management Bureau in Puning county (Jieyang, Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction project of a water waste processing facility.
Around 16 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Jiaozhou county (Qingdao, Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.

Around 7 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Tengzhou county (Zaozhuang, Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by an interior design company. Some workers threatened to jump off a building.
Around 13 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Minhou county (Fuzhou, Fujian) to demand for social insurance owed by a food production company.
Around 3 August 2020 (as reported), 93 migrant workers staged a protest at the Labour Inspection Bureau in Lanzhou prefecture (Gansu) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project.

On 21 July 2020, as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest at the Bureau of Housing and Urban-Rural Development in Shahe City (Xingtai, Hebei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.
Around 25 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Hangzhou prefecture (Zhejiang) to demand for wage arrears owed by an educational organisation.

Around 3 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 construction workers staged a protest in Fengqing county (Lincang, Yunnan) to demand for wage arrears. At least one worker was reportedly injured by society members (triads) hired by their employer.

Around 10 August 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 taxi drivers went on strike and protested in Aluhorqin (Ar Horqin) banner (Chifeng, Inner Mongolia) against industry disputes regarding compensation and operation.
Around 25 July 2020 (as reported), at least three employees staged a protest in Harbin prefecture (Heilongjiang) to demand for wage arrears after the closure of a gym facility.
Around 28 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 employees staged a protest in Changchun prefecture (Jilin) to demand for wage arrears after the closure of a gym facility.
Around 14 July 2020 (as reported), many workers staged a protest in Changsha prefecture (Hunan) to demand for wage arrears after the closure of a medical and beauty treatment business.
On 15 July 2020, as many as 100 workers petitioned at the Bureau of Letters and Calls at Baliwan town of Hong'an county (Huanggang, Hubei) to demand for wage arrears.
Around 18 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers went on strike and protested in Putian prefecture (Fujian) to demand for wage arrears from a shoe manufacturer.

Around 29 August 2020 (as reported), many drivers staged a protest in Chengdu prefecture (Sichuan) to demand for wage arrears and other types unsettled compensation after the closure of a ridesharing company.
Around 23 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Shaxi Town (Zhongshan, Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.

Around 3 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Linxia Hui Autonomous Prefecture (Gansu) to demand for wage arrears from a state-owned railway company. They only received two rounds of wages this year.

On 13 August 2020, as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Huishui county (Qiannan Buyei and Miao Autonomous, Guizhou) to demand for wage arrears by a construction company. It was reported that they were beaten by their employer during the demonstration.

Around 4 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Nanjing prefecture (Jiangsu) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project. The workers were reportedly beaten up. Assailants not specified.

On 29 July 2020, as many as 100 migrant workers protested at a parking lot near Kaiyuan Temple in Xingtai prefecture (Hebei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project. They held up banners and blocked the parking lot entrance with vehicle(s).
Around 7 July 2020 (as reported), as many as several dozen migrant workers staged a protest in Huizhou prefecture (Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.

On 7 July 2020, a dozen migrant workers staged a protest in Huixian county (Xinxiang, Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. The workers climbed onto a construction crane and threatened to jump off.

Around 23 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Togtoh (Tuoketuo) county (Hohhot, Inner Mongolia) to demand for social insurance and wage arrears owed by a biotechnology company.
Around 5 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 farmers staged a protest in Xinfeng county (Ganzhou, Jiangxi) to demand for wage arrears from cutting crops.
Around 9 August 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 migrant workers staged a protest in Dongming county (Heze, Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned nuclear power plant facility.
Around 26 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Jimo district (Qingdao, Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction project.
Around 3 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Xi'an prefecture (Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears from a state-owned highway construction project.
Around 3 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Changchun prefecture (Jilin) to demand for wage arrears from a bathhouse.

Around 16 August 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 taxi drivers protested in Yulin prefecture (Shaanxi) against a recent industry move to introduce an app-driven bicycle rideshare scheme in the urban areas.

On 24 July 2020, as many as 100 workers staged a protest at the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development in Wuhan prefecture (Hubei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. They were reportedly beaten up by personnel hired by the employer and several self-proclaimed government workers (but this was not verified) in an attempt to stop them from filing complaints or petitions.
Around 28 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers protested in Nanjing (Jiangsu) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction project.
Around 21 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 sanitation workers staged a protest in Yuncheng City (Shanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by their company.

Around 22 July 2020 (as reported), a dozen workers staged a protest in Luonan county (Shangluo, Shaanxi) to demand for four months of wage arrears owed by a metal parts company. The county's Human Resources and Social Security Bureau responded to the protest by setting up a case to investigate the dispute.
On 27 July 2020, as many as 100 workers filed a complaint and demonstrated at the Labour Bureau in Huangmei county (Huanggang, Hubei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a furniture shopping mall.

On 27 July 2020, three workers staged a protest in Xingtai prefecture (Hebei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. Workers climbed onto a construction crane and threatened to jump off. Police arrived at the scene to evacuate personnel close to the crane. No further intervention reported
Around 26 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Beihai prefecture (Guangxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by two state-owned construction companies.

On 18 August 2020, up to 1000 taxi drivers gathered in Harbin prefecture (Heilongjiang) and attempted to drive to Beijing in protest against high operation fees demanded by their respective companies during the coronavirus, and threats to confiscate their vehicles otherwise. Taxi management companies followed closely, trying to disperse and stop them, until special police forces reportedly intercepted them at the Jilin prefecture border, and both parties entered a deadlock. The protest was ultimately called off the next day.
On 7 July 2020, as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Longchi town of Pucheng county (Weinan, Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owned by a construction company.
Around 19 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Zhengzhou prefecture (Henan) to demand for wage arrears from a state-owned railway construction company.

Around 1 September 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 drivers staged a protest in Wuyuan county (Baynnur, Inner Mongolia) against the introduction of a motorcycle ridesharing company in the 'already saturated' rideshare market in the region.

Around 14 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Pingdingshan prefecture (Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. Workers crawled atop a crane and threatened to jump off.

Around 19 August 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 taxi drivers protested in Dandong prefecture (Liaoning) against a recent industry move to invest in 5000 more bicycles in urban areas as part of an app-driven bicycles rideshare scheme.

On 20 July 2020, as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Zhoukou prefecture (Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. They succeeded in securing their wages with the help of several labour unions in Zhoukou prefecture and Chuanghui district.
Around 27 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Shangcheng county (Xinyang, Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by an environmental construction company.

Around 16 May 2019 (month of), a former female employee with the Home Affairs Bureau's Child Welfare Department was intercepted and beaten by stability maintenance officers at Xiangyang train station in Fancheng District (Xiangyang, Hubei) to prevent her from petitioning in Beijing. Prior to this, she was targeted and assaulted at least once due to disputes at her former government job, as well as forcibly admitted to a psychiatric ward.
On 14 August 2020, four urban management officers pushed and assaulted an elderly female vegetable vendor on the streets of Kaifeng prefecture (Henan) during a row about street vending activities.

On 6 November 2019, 10 government-hired workers beat up three fast food restaurant owners (the son, and his parents) from Nantong prefecture (Jiangsu) during an attempt to start construction work at their illegally demolished restaurant. They sustained injuries to their ribs and skull. It was their second government-related assault case since 2014.

On 17 August 2020, a petitioner from Caijia (Caijiagang) sub-district, Beibei district (Chongqing) was taken away by local government and police officials and held incommunicado until his release on 1 Sep. When his acquaintances inquired at the sub-district office on 26 Aug, they mentioned that he was 'in quarantine' (alluding to the coronavirus pandemic at the time). The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance ahead of an international trade conference (CIFTIS 2020) held in Beijing from 4-9 Sep.

On 10 August 2020, a construction worker was injured after law enforcement officials from the Urban Management Department of Dingyuan county (Chuzhou, Anhui) repeatedly struck the platform he was standing on, induced instability and eventual collapse. He was further assaulted by the group after falling onto the floor. Several passers-by and shopfronts were hit.

On 28 August 2020, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee was assaulted by a police officer near the CPC Committee Office of Shenxi village of Jiangyin county (Wuxi, Jiangsu) while explaining that her father needed to rest on a public bench. She was hospitalised with injuries sustained to her ribs and brain.

On 10 August 2020, a citizen was beaten up in a car by two urban management officials in Changchun prefecture (Jilin) after he remarked on the sight of the two of them overthrowing a merchant's deep-fried dough stick wok on the road. He was hospitalised and suffered from soft tissue damage and broken ribs.

On 28 August 2020, ethnic Mongolian students and parents staged protests in Hohhot prefecture (Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions).

On 31 August 2020, many ethnic Mongolian parents staged protests at three elementary schools in Ganqika town of Horqin Left Rear Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions). They came to demand the release of their children, and over 3,000 students engaged in the collective boycott. At least one parent was escorted away by the police.

Around 16 August 2020 (month of), over 660 lawyers in Hunan province had their professional licenses 'voluntarily' revoked on the grounds of 'illegally' having side jobs, signing labour contracts with non-law firms or holding overseas passports. It was alleged that the lawyers were coerced. It was reported that over 1200 lawyers in Hunan faced similar circumstances across the last four months.

On 4 August 2020, employees of private farmland management enterprise Dawu Group were assaulted by a large number of public security officers when attempting block the demolition of their office in Wuzhuang village of Xushui district (Baoding, Hebei). State-owned farm from Xushui district sent people to demolish Dawu's office, who clashed with workers who came to stop the demolition. Dawu employees were beaten by riot police who arrived on the scene to intervene, and assaulted with tear gas and chili water. Many Dawu employees were injured and hospitalised.

On 28 August 2020, ethnic Mongolian students and parents staged protests at Urad Middle Banner (Bayannur, Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions).

On 7 August 2020, thousands of people staged a demonstration at the Shaoyang City People's Government in Daxiang District (Shaoyang, Hunan) against a government campaign to ban electric vehicles, bicycles and motorcycles. The week-long dissatisfaction turned into a riot, with demonstrators blocking and damaging officials' vehicles, and assaulting traffic police officers. Many were arrested. Authorities announced a suspension of the ban immediately afterwards.

On 28 August 2020, ethnic Mongolian students and parents staged protests at Hure Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions).

On 30 August 2020, government authorities performed a regional crackdown on stores in Inner Mongolia, confiscating all literature, texts and stationary in the Mongolian language and ordering relevant books to be taken off shelves. The operation took place following the 26 Aug release of a national-level policy document, stating that Mongolian would be replaced with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions).

On 28 August 2020, ethnic Mongolian students and parents staged protests in Ordos prefecture (Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions).

Around 31 August 2020, several hundred ethnic Mongolian parents gathered at a school in Jarud Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia), and demonstrated against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region (and five other provinces) starting with the immediate fall semester. They came to demand the release of their children, as large-scale student boycotts, strikes and demonstrations spread across the region. Clashes between the parents and several hundred riot police were recorded.

Around 30 August 2020 (as reported), ethnic Mongolian students and parents protested at the Affiliated Experimental Middle School to Inner Mongolia Normal University in Saihan district (Hohhot, Inner Mongolia) and started a petition. They were protesting against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools. They were dispersed by the police.

On 17 May 2019, the chief official of an eviction operation and five of his subordinates cut the power cords to a forced evictee's house in Qujiang new district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) (coded at Xi'an City) and hit him in the face and body with twisted steel rods and picks. The evictee had to be hospitalised with concussion, soft tissue damage and broken bones. Eviction personnel on the scene claimed that perpetrators were not related to them.

On 22 May 2019, the chief official of an eviction operation and more than 20 hired private security guards cut the power cords to a forced evictee's house in Qujiang new district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) (coded at Xi'an City), and beat him with picks and wires for 30-40 minutes. The evictee was severely injured, and was transferred to three different hospitals for treatment of concussion, soft tissue damage and broken bones.

On 10 August 2020, at least 13 forced evictees petitioned and demonstrated with placards at the Chongqing Municipality Bureau of Letters and Calls in Beibei district (Chongqing) against government malpractices and repression during the handling of their demolished land.

On 9 June 2019, a forced evictee was hit unconscious after being axed in the head and neck by unknown individuals as he stepped into his own house in Qujiang new district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) (coded at Xi'an City). He had been a target of at least two violent attacks by government officials and hired personnel prior to this, and was just released from the hospital on that day.

Around 5 March 2019 (within a month from 20 February 2019), a Tibetan from Tingri County (Shigatse, Tibet) was subjected to dozens of days of interrogation, beatings and re-education during a month-long detention. He was first taken away at a police checkpoint in Lazi (Lhatse) County and transferred to the Public Security Bureau on 20 Feb. Chinese officials claimed that he had contacted foreigners and discussed about the importance of teaching Tibetan language to Tibetan chidlren.

Around 1 April 2019 (beginning of month), a Tibetan master's degree student was forcefully taken from Northwest Minzu University in Chengguan district (Lanzhou, Gansu) by the Tibet Education Bureau after he wrote an essay for his civil service entrance exam criticising the falling number of government job opportunities for Tibetans. On social media platforms such as WeChat, his essay was circulated and went viral. As of 1 May 2019, his location and condition of his arrest remain unknown.

On 24 June 2020, government authorities forcefully relocated about 60 Tibetans from 13 households from Dolying village of Payul county (Tibet) to a new settlement within Palyul county. The houses in the new settlement flew Chinese flags on their roofs and hung portraits of Communist Party leaders within the homes. Between 2018 and 2019, around 400 Tibetan families were reportedly involved in a mass forced relocation from Tibetan-majority locations to government-built settlements.

As reported around 8 March 2019, a Tibetan man was arrested and detained from Shigatse (also known as Rikaze Prefecture City, Tibet Autonomous Region) by the police on his way home from a business trip to Lhasa. He was held incommunicado since. There was no information about his charges or whereabouts by the time of report on 12 November 2019. It was reported that his arrest may be linked with his sharing of Tibetan books on WeChat, a popular Chinese social media platform.

Around 1 July 2019 (in recent days), Chinese authorities expelled 3,600 monks and nuns from the Yachen Gar Tibetan Buddhist centre in Palyul (Baiyu) county (Kardze (Ganzi) prefecture, Sichuan province). The monks and nuns were sent back to their home counties (monstly in Qinghai province) for political re-education. Since May, around 7,100 monks and nuns were forced to leave Yachen Gar, which until recent years had housed an estimated 10,000 monks, nuns, and lay practitioners devoted to scriptural study and meditation. The expulsions in May mainly involved those from Chamdo City, Tibet.

On 20 June 2019, two gathering places of a church in Haicang District (Xiamen, Fujian) were shut down by the police, citing illegal gatherings and disturbance to the public. The pastor as well as many members were taken away by police for investigation. This was part of an ongoing campaign to crack down on churches in China.

Around 16 March 2020 (month of), over 200 government-dispatched personnel demolished a local Buddhist temple in Mamiao town of Huaining county (Anqing, Anhui) as part of the national policy. To avoid public protests, the government did not inform the temple's director and villagers beforehand.

On 18 May 2020, 20 government-led personnel and police officers demolished a Buddhist temple in Shucheng county (Anhui) after declaring it a dilapidated building, and reportedly beat up two believers (including a female believer and a monk) who asked for documented approval of the demolition and tried to film the scene. Those who posted video footage of the act and submitted a petition to higher authorities were ordered to stop.

On 2 July 2020, over 100 police officers demolished a folk religion temple in one of the villages of Dangtu county (Ma'anshan, Anhui). Eight elderly believers who were protecting the temple were dragged out. A week before the demolition, over 60 villagers organized to take turns protecting the temple 24 hours a day while village officers repeatedly harassed them.

On 12 May 2020, a Three-Self church in Diaoling village (Zhoukou, Henan) was forced to demolish its cross by the government, as a pre-condition to reopening after coronavirus prevention measures were lifted. Other churches in the area were banned from reopening for reasons unrelated to hygiene or coronavirus prevention.

Around 8 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Dianjiang county (Chongqing) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. One protester was assaulted by a group of three men (their identities were not reported), and sustained injuries to his ribs and thighs.
Around 8 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Qinzhou prefecture (Guangxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.

Around 7 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 health workers staged a protest in Muchuan county (Leshan, Sichuan) to demand for wage arrears and social insurance owed by a Chinese medicine hospital.

Around 9 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Nanjing prefecture (Jiangsu) to demand for wage arrears owed by a courier company. They have been on strike since mid-Aug 2020.
Around 7 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Huangping county (Qiandongnan, Guizhou) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned highway construction project.

On 27 September 2019, a female Falun Gong member from Mengzi county (Honghe, Yunnan) was kidnapped by police officers while she was on her way back from Kunming prefecture (Yunnan) to Mengzi, after visiting a fellow Falun Gong member in the prefecture. It was reportedly part of a stability maintenance effort ahead of the military parade celebrating the 70th anniversary of the founding of China. She was later arrested by the authorities of Jianshui County on 2 November 2019, but her circumstances between 27 September and 2 November were not reported. She had been a repeated target of imprisonment, torture and re-education camps since 2001.

On 21 May 2019, a Buddhist temple in Shishou (Jingzhou City, Hubei Province) was raided by officials from the United Front Work Department, Public Security Bureau, and other government institutions. They took away all the religious texts by a prominent Buddhist monk, and ordered to have them burned. This was part of a broader effort to confiscate books by a prominent Buddhist monk, whose teachings have been banned by the CCP.

In September 2019, a Guanyin statue at a Buddhist temple in Yanshan County (Cangzhou City, Hebei Province) was demolished. Government officials were on site to supervise the demolition, and police officers threatened to arrest those who attempted to stop the demolition. This was part of a greater campaign by the CCP to remove all outdoor Buddhist statues.
As reported on 27 May 2019, as many as 100 delivery drivers went on strike and protested against an reduction in wage in Changsha City, Hunan Province.

As reported on 19 January, more than 20 migrant workers protested in Jianchang, Huludao to demand for wage arrears, amounting to more than 400,000 RMB in total, owed to them by construction company Ansteel. Protesters carried banners.

On 9 May 2019, more than 20 police demolished the office of a petitioner in Xiling District (Yichang City, Hubei City) on the ground of 'illegal structure'. The authorities arranged a TV team and a camera drone to film the demolition process.
In April 2019, more than 20 young Muslim Kazakhs in Wusu (Tarbagatay, Xinjiang) were forcibly sent to other Chinese provinces by the police. Their whereabouts have been unknown thereafter.

On 11 July 2019, more than 20 officers from the Lugang Township government in Changyuan county were dispatched to demolish the chicken farms of three chicken farming households in Qiaozhai Village, Changyuan (Xinxiang, Henan). Physical clashes broke out between the officers and the villagers who resisted the demolition. Police officers took away 7 villagers in total.

Around 25 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Zhen'an county (Shangluo, Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a secondary school construction project. Several hundred workers had not been paid since 2018.

On 13 September 2020, at least 10 residents marched in Nanshilipu community of Guancheng Hui District (Zhengzhou, Henan) against being forced by their estate management to purchase their respective car parking spots. They beat drums, and mocked the management company by holding up flags that were traditionally gifted as recognition of exemplary service. Two men suspected of being related to the company appeared mid-way to snatch the flags, but were prevented from doing so by the demonstrators.

Around 15 June 2019 (month of), three Buddhist statues -- a 9-meter-tall dripping-water Guanyin statue and a boy-girl duo symbolising good fortune -- were demolished at Puti (Bodhi) Temple in Mile county (Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous, Yunnan) on orders of the local Religious Affairs Bureau, which stated that the temple was not registered as a religious activity venue. The temple was closed down (at an unspecified date) after its director refused to convert it into an elderly activities centre.

Around 16 July 2019 (month of), a 17-meter-tall Guanyin statue on Nanzhao Customs Island in Dali (Yunnan) was demolished by the authorities for being too tall. Government authorities threatened to close the tourist attraction if the statue was not demolished. The demolition process took four months.

Around 15 November 2019 (month of), the Meishan People's Government demolished a 42-meter-tall Amitabha statue in Huazang Temple, a thousand-year-old Buddhist site in Meishan prefecture (Sichuan). More than 200 officers and officials surrounded the venue on the day, and set up checkpoints along roads leading to the site.

Around 15 February 2020 (month of), government officials demolished a 108-room nursing home in Fuzhou prefecture (Fujian) that was run by a state-approved Buddhist temple, causing most residents to leave. They also went back on their promise not to obstruct the building of a new nursing home, threatening to arrest the temple's director if he attempted to open a new centre.

On 11 April 2020, over 70 government personnel demolished a one-storey building in the courtyard of a nursing home in Gushan town (Fuzhou, Fujian) without warning. The nursing home was run by a Three-Self church, and previously approved by the local Religious Affairs Bureau.

On 2 July 2020, government personnel demolished a five-storey building in Gushan town (Fuzhou, Fujian) that operated as a nursing home, congregation venue and elderly care centre run by a Three-Self church. The nursing home was previously approved by the local Religious Affairs Bureau.

On 21 June 2020, a dozen Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau personnel and police officers raided a local house church venue in Daying county (Suining, Sichuan), confiscating 21 religious texts and removing a cross from one of the walls before shutting down the venue. They accused five members of illegal gathering, and detained the church director for a couple hours.

On 28 July 2020, more than 30 Public Security Bureau officers were dispatched to a 70-people service at a Sola Fide house church in Nanbu county (Nanchong, Sichuan), and arrested about 50 congregation members and a pastor. They confiscated all religious texts and several electronic appliances, and tore down the cross before shutting down the site. The pastor was kicked several times when he resisted his arrest and tried to reason with the police. Some were released the same day, while others were detained from 4 to 15 days.

Around 18 July 2020 (as reported), as many as eight workers staged a protest in Fuzhou prefecture (Fujian) against the closure of a web-based delivery company and to demand for three months of wage arrears.
Around 26 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Shenyang prefecture (Liaoning) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.

On 30 July 2020, at least four workers protested by driving heavy-duty vehicles to block the entrance of a construction company in Golmud county (Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous, Qinghai) to demand for wage arrears and settlement of other labour disputes. They also entered the company building. They refused to move for at least several days.

Around 31 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 taxi drivers staged a protest in Dalian prefecture (Liaoning) against the introduction of rideshare motorcycles in the region. They were seen mobilising efforts to remove the motorcycles to other areas.

Around 1 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Xilinhot county (Xilingol, Inner Mongolia) to demand for work compensation from the government. It was reported that the dispute had not been settled since three years ago.

On 2 August 2020, 3-5 workers protested by driving a loader to block the entrance of a construction company in Golmud county (Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous, Qinghai) to demand for wage arrears and settlement of other labour disputes. They also entered the company building. They refused to move for as many as 11 days, as it was reported that the demonstrators were arrested on 12 Aug. A similar demonstration was held on 30 July.

Around 2 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 30 migrant workers staged a protest in Zijin county (Heyuan, Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned wastewater infrastructure project.

Around 6 August 2020 (as reported), at least 10 workers staged a protest in Huizhou prefecture (Guangdong) against a face mask production factory for owing them wage arrears and severance pay, forcing them to take unpaid leave, and one-sidedly annulling their employment contracts. It was reported to be related to global supply chain issues faced by the mask manufacturing industry during the Covid-19 pandemic. They held up a banner.

Around 8 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 employees and parents protested in Xi'an prefecture (Shaanxi) for lesson refunds and wage arrears following the closure of an English tutorial centre.
On 9 August 2020, as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Huixian county (Xinxiang, Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. They held up a banner at the entrance.
On 10 August 2020, around 80 workers staged a protest in Nanjing prefecture (Jiangsu) to demand for wage arrears owed by a car manufacturer.

Around 12 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 employees filed a complaint and protested at the Labour Bureau in Jimo district (Qingdao, Shandong) for subsidies related to high-temperature work conditions owed by an electronics company.

On 12 August 2020, 3-5 workers staged a protest by blocking the entrance of a construction company with a loader in Golmud county (Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous, Qinghai) to demand for wage arrears and settlement of other labour disputes. They also entered the company building. The Wutumeiren police station intervened and at least five were detained or given adminstrative tickets.

Around 14 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers petitioned and demonstrated in Nantong prefecture (Jiangsu) to demand for wage arrears owed by an interior design company. It was reported that the workers never signed contracts to formalise their working relationship, allowing the company's superintendents to retain their supposed wages as personal gain.
Around 15 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged protest in Ningde prefecture (Fujian) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. They held up a banner.
Around 21 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 delivery workers stage a protest in Zhaoqing prefecture (Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a courier deliver company.

Around 21 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Zhongwei prefecture (Ningxia) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company. They had been owed wage arrears for over six years.
Around 21 August 2020 (as reported), at least 11 migrant workers stage a protest in Xi'an prefecture (Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by an ecological construction project.

Around 22 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Dali county (Weinan, Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned natural gas infrastructure project. They had not been able to collect their wages since the end of 2018.

Around 22 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 rideshare taxi drivers staged a protest in Zunyi prefecture (Guizhou) to make demands regarding government regulations, legal procedures, and services, fees and privacy concerns related to the rideshare app platform.

Around 22 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Yancheng prefecture (Jiangsu) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction project. They held up a banner.
Around 23 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 21 employees staged a protest in Jiaozuo prefecture (Henan) to demand for 10 months of wage arrears owed by a hotel.

Around 24 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Changping district (Beijing) to demand for wage arrears owed by a fitness facility. It was reported that the management threatened to beat up the workers.
Around 27 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Daye county (Huangshi, Hubei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned housing construction project.

On 27 August 2020, as many as 100 workers staged a demonstration at Houyang Electric Power Management Station in Yanghe village, Sanyang street of Ouhai district (Wenzhou, Zhejiang), blocking the entrance with a large construction vehicle to demand for wage arrears owed by the ecological park.

Around 27 August 2020 (as reported), at least six migrant workers staged a protest in Yichuan county (Shangluo, Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by the county committee's construction project. Around 50 workers had not been paid since 2018.
Around 27 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Yunfu prefecture (Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned housing construction project.

Around 16 September 2020 (as reported), between 101-1000 taxi drivers protested in Bayuquan District (Yingkou prefecture, Liaoning) against illegal rideshare vehicles that had saturated the local market.
On 17 September 2020, 101-1000 taxi drivers went on strike and gathered on the streets in Nanbu county (Nanchong, Sichuan) to protest against rideshare motorcycles in the region.
Around 14 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 44 migrant workers protested in Huangshi prefecture (Hubei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.
On 14 September 2020, six migrant workers protested in Shangluo prefecture (Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction company for two years.

Around 9 September 2020 (week of), Tibetan parents and children (students) demonstrated in Tongren (Rebgong) county (Huangnan Tibetan Autonomous, Qinghai) against being forced to send their children to government-designated boarding schools after local primary schools in several towns were closed. The police arrived to the scene and took a protester into custody. Some children fainted out of fright.

Around 15 June 2020 (month of), numerous Buddhist statues were demolished in Ezhou prefecture (Hubei) by the authorities, and some temples were repurposed into agro-tourism sites or elderly activity centers. The operation took place within a week of a meeting between the Ezhou and Huangshi prefecture governments to discuss the rectification of Buddhist and Taoist venues.

Around 15 June 2020 (month of), the government covered up a Tibetan Buddhist white stupa (a shrine housing sacred relics) on Xiaolong Mountain, Jimo district (Qingdao, Shandong), claiming that the icon distracted drivers and affected traffic along a nearby highway.

Around 15 June 2020 (month of), 97 temples (Buddhist and Daoist) were shut down or repurposed in Huangshi prefecture (Hubei) by the authorities, and their statues were removed. The operation took place after a meeting between the Ezhou and Huangshi prefecture governments to discuss the rectification of Buddhist and Taoist venues.

On 6 June 2020, government officials of Linyi county removed all crosses, other religious symbols, and benches from the Wangdangjia village church in Wangdangjia village of Linyi county (Dezhou, Shandong). Another church affiliated with the Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association (CPCA) on Cuijia Lane, Linyi County was shut down soon after. They claimed that the church gatherings were not well-attended. It was reported that even registered Catholic churches across China (those sanctioned by the government-run CPCA) were not exempt from persecutions and harassment.

On 15 May 2020, the Buddhist Taishan Temple in Shiyan prefecture (Hubei) was demolished by 200 government personnel. During the demolition, they blocked all the roads leading to the temple, and confiscated mobile phones from anyone working on the site.

Around 15 June 2019 (month of), the Younan Three-Self Church (with a congregation size of 400) in Guannan county (Lianyungang, Jiangsu) was forced to merge with a smaller church on orders of the government. The government threatened to demolish the church unless they moved out within three days. It was reported that the venue was later converted to a cultural auditorium.

Around 16 July 2020 (month of), government officials removed a cross and installed a surveillance camera at a Catholic church in Hebei province, despite the fact that the church had joined the Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association in hopes of being able to organize worship services in peace. It was reported that even registered Catholic churches across China (those sanctioned by the government-run Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association) were not exempt from persecutions and harassment.

Around 16 May 2019 (month of), government officials from Datong city rectified the Tibetan Buddhist Huiquan Temple in Xisi village (Datong, Shanxi), converting the stupa (a shrine that housed sacred relics) into a Chinese-style pavilion with gray bricks and black tiles. Traditional bronze pillars at the entrance were also demolished.

Around 16 May 2020 (middle of month), officials from the United Front Work Department, the National Security Brigade and police officers removed five crosses and an entrance signage from a state-sanctioned Catholic church in Julu county (Xingtai, Hebei). It was reported that even registered Catholic churches across China (those sanctioned by the government-run Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association) were not exempt from persecutions and harassment.

On 19 May 2020, local officials removed the cross and Virgin Mary statue from Wuqiu Village Catholic Church in Wuqiu village, Jinling town of Lanling county (Linyi, Shandong) (coded at Lanling county) on the grounds that they were positioned higher than the village committee building. It was reported that even registered Catholic churches across China (those sanctioned by the government-run Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association) were not exempt from persecutions and harassment.

Around 15 November 2019 (month of), two Guanyin statues in Xianning city (Hubei) were concealed by government officials, including a thousand-hand Guanyin statue at Guanyin Temple in Guihua town and an eight-meter-tall statue in the Guanyin Pavilion. This was part of a large-scale campaign to rectify Buddhist and Taoist venues across Hubei province.

On 2 June 2020, town officials shut down and destroyed the Roman-style pillars and removed all religious symbols (including the altar, podium, benches, images of 14 stations of the Way of the Cross) at a Western-style Catholic church in Zhangmengtun village, Dingzhou city (Baoding, Hebei). They painted over ceramic tiles with cross symbols.

On 30 September 2019, one 21.8-metre-tall, two-faced Guanyin statue at the Guiyuan Temple in Wuhan prefecture (Hubei) was covered up by the authorities. This was part of a large-scale campaign to rectify Buddhist and Taoist venues across Hubei province.

Around 16 December 2019 (month of), at least three Protestant Christian believers were assaulted by over 30 local government personnel during an operation to merge and shut down the Lu'nan Three-Self Church in Guannan county (Lianyungang, Jiangsu). They were thrown on the floor, pushed and shoved around. One elderly believer reportedly vomited and fainted, while another believer suffered a heart attack. It was reported that at least 142 Protestant churches (state-run Three-Self churches or unregistered house churches) were shut down in Lianyungang prefecture in the second half of 2019, as part of a six-month crackdown campaign in Jiangsu province.

On 9 May 2020, the Buddhist Xiabao Temple in Taizi town (Huangshi, Hubei) was destroyed by Taizi town officials and over ten urban management officers, who made a hole in the temple's back wall before demolishing the rest of the building.
Around 20 September 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 migrant workers staged a protest in Zhoukou prefecture (Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction company.

Around 20 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 rental homeowners and staff workers staged a protest in Dalian prefecture (Liaoning) to demand for wage arrears and rental deposits following the sudden closure of a property rental agency.

On 22 May 2020, a prisoner was held in solitary refinement and exposed to chlorine dioxide (highly concentrated disinfectant) at Songyuan Prison in Songyuan prefecture (Jilin) for questioning the guards after his five-minute phone call allowance with family was reduced to two. The gas left him out of breath and nearly comatose, and reportedly took him ten days to recover after the gas exposure.

On 20 August 2020, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee was punched and kicked by a dozen public security and police officers in a car that was leaving the Lijia Police Station in Lijia village (Yubei, Chongqing). She was kidnapped earlier in the day by more than a dozen people (who appeared to be colluding with the police) at Jinshansi station in Liangjiang New Area (Chongqing). She was then taken by the police to the Fengdu Public Security Bureau in Fengdu county (Chongqing), where she was tied to a tiger bench. She was reportedly detained overnight until her release the next day. She had been a target of the state in the past 20 years for her petitioning.

Around 16 May 2020 (month of), the town government took ownership of 10 clan ancestral halls (associated with China's folk religion) in Maochen town (Xiaogan, Hubei) and converted them for public use, and informed the heads of local clans that clan activities had been banned.

Around 1 September 2020 (several consecutive days after arrest), a Catholic Father from the Diocese of Mindong was tortured by police officers during interrogation at a detention house in Fu'an county (Mindong, Fujian). They tortured him by causing sleep deprivation, banging a gong next to his ear and shining a bright light into his eyes for several consecutive days.
Around 29 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Ningde prefecture (Fujian) to demand for wage arrears owed for the construction of a pig farm.
Around 29 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Kaiping county (Jiangmen, Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a property development company.

Around 21 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Yongning district (Nanning, Guangxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a web-based courier company.

Around 27 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Hefei prefecture (Anhui) to demand for wage arrears owed by an online recruitment company. They held up a banner.
