Around 26 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 employees, apartment owners and tenants staged a protest in Kunming prefecture (Yunnan) to demand for wage arrears and deposits and rents following the sudden closure of an apartment rental company.

Around 30 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers staged a protest in Yichun prefecture (Jiangxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned telecommunications company. They held up two banners at the entrance of the company.

Around 29 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 20 migrant workers staged a protest outside a construction site in Xinyi City (Xuzhou, Jiangsu) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction company since 2019.

Around 28 September 2020 (as reported), 1001-10000 taxi drivers staged a protest in Zhangzhou prefecture (Fujian) to demand for individual (instead of company) ownership of road transportation rights and operation rights.

On 25 July 2020, crosses were removed at four Three-Self Church venues in Dazhongcun town of Lanling county (Linyi, Shandong), after the town government hired workers to eliminate religious symbols and slogans from those buildings. A town official on the site stated that 'crosses must be removed from all churches because Christianity does not belong in China.' The ongoing cross removal campaign in Linyi city was launched at the beginning of 2019.

Around 16 May 2020 (month of), a folk religion temple in a village of Donggang town, Linzhou county (Anyang, Henan) was demolished by the authorities as it was located in front of the village committee office.

Around 31 May 2020 (end of month), a folk religion temple in a village in Dongyao town of Linzhou county (Anyang, Henan) was repurposed into an activity centre by local authorities, and its 23 deity statues were demolished.
On 1 June 2020, the town government sent about 30 workers to demolish statues in the Guanyin Hall (a folk religion venue) at Xianzhang village, Chadian town of Linzhou county (Anyang, Henan).

On 28 August 2020, over 100 government personnel and police officers demolished a house church venue in Xincheng town of Xiuzhou district (Jiaxing, Zhejiang), allegedly for the church's refusal to join the state-administered Three-Self Church. Prior to the event, they also installed surveillance cameras at the venue entrance.
On 13 June 2020, two folk religion temples in Rencun town of Linzhou county (Anyang, Henan) were demolished by the authorities.

Around 15 June 2020 (month of), the government-registered Buddhist temple in Shaanxi province was demolished by local authorities. The congregation was merged with another temple, despite promises to rebuild the existing temple.
Around 30 June 2020 (end of month), in the middle of the night, three folk religion temples in Longhu village of Tangyin county (Anyang, Henan) were demolished by the government.

Around 16 July 2020 (middle of month), the dome of a mosque in Kaiping district (Tangshan, Hebei) was converted into a Chinese-style pavilion by the authorities as part of the national policy to convert Islamic domes into Chinese-style structures. From Jul to Sep, at least six mosques in Tangshan were rectified. At the time of reporting on 9 Oct, 17 more mosques were planned to be rectified with a cost of at least 10,000,000 RMB.

Around 15 April 2020 (month of), local authorities demolished the state-run Three-Self Tianfeng Church in Luoyang prefecture (Henan) on the pretext of 'expanding a railway line.' Although the government initially agreed to build a new church nearby, the Religious Affairs Bureau director, urban management officers and workers again destroyed 12 pillars at the church's new ongoing construction site on 30 July 2020.

Around 16 July 2020 (month of), folk religion temples in Rencun town of Linzhou county (Anyang, Henan) were repurposed by the authorities and converted into storage facilities, natural gas management offices, fire stations, and other facilities.

On 13 September 2020, police officers broke into a house church venue in Liangshan county (Jining, Shandong) by destroying the entrance door lock, and looted its donation box and 100 chairs. Earlier in the day, they arrived at the church during a service, and declared it an illegal gathering, dispersing the congregation and confiscating four Bible copies.

On 31 July 2020, village officials demolished a Three-Self Church in Yinzhang village of Yichuan county (Luoyang, Henan) on the grounds that the church was occupying lands intended for a school. Since last year, the church had been a reported target of the government, which made repeated attempts to convert it into an activity centre for the elderly.

Around 16 August 2020 (month of), a Buddhist temple in Qipan township of Jianli county (Jingzhou, Hubei) was converted by authorities into an elderly activity center, since it did not have the registration certificate. The converted building was covered with CPC-endorsed political slogans.

On 20 August 2020, county government personnel emptied a Three-Self Church venue in Longnan county (Ganzhou, Jiangxi) and confiscated more than a dozen Bible and hymnbook copies. The congregation was not informed beforehand.

Around 15 September 2020 (month of), authorities from the Religious Affairs Bureau and United Front Work Department removed the dome of a mosque in Xiazhuang village of Kaiping district (Tangshan, Hebei) as part of the national policy to convert Islamic domes into Chinese-style structures. From Jul to Sep, at least six mosques in Tangshan were rectified. At the time of reporting on 9 Oct, 17 more mosques were planned to be rectified with a cost of at least 10,000,000 RMB.
On 5 September 2020, a Three-Self Church venue in Longnan county (Ganzhou, Jiangxi) was shut down after a police raid.

Around 16 July 2020 (month of), the dome of a mosque in Qing county (Cangzhou, Hebei) was removed by local authorities and placed in the mosque's backyard. Two days later, authorities discovered the dome through satellite imagery and immediately ordered for it to be destroyed.
Around 3 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Jinjiang county (Quanzhou, Fujian) to demand for wage arrears owed by a shoe manufacturer.

Around 5 October 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 workers protested in Pingdingshan prefecture (Henan) to demand for wage arrears and other labour compensations (incl. social insurance, medical, unemployment and living stipend) owed by a bankrupted state-owned aluminium production factory.

On 4 October 2020, several hundred property agents protested at Hangzhouwan New district of Cixi county (Ningbo, Zhejiang) to demand for wage arrears (agent fees) owed by a state-owned property developer. They threatened to jump off a building.
Around 26 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Weifang prefecture (Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a web-based delivery company.
Around 1 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Weihui county (Xinxiang, Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project.

On 1 September 2020, 1-100 migrant workers petitioned and protested in Zhangzhou prefecture (Fujian) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company, after the company's bank accounts were frozen under court orders due to other investigations.
Around 2 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Danfeng county (Shangluo, Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction project.
Around 1 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Daqing prefecture (Heilongjiang) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project.
Around 5 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers protested at Wuhan prefecture (Hubei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.

Around 5 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers protested at Xinping Yi and Dai Autonomous County (Yuxi, Yunnan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned railway construction company.

On 7 September 2020, 15 workers protested and blocked the entrance at a construction project site in Yuetang district (Xiangtan, Hunan) to demand for wage arrears from their company. Police officers arrived on the scene to mediate the dispute.

Around 3 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested at a construction site near Chengdu prefecture (Sichuan) to demand for wage arrears owed by their construction company. One protester was dragged and beaten in a room. No further details provided on the identities of the assailants.
On 10 September 2020, many construction workers protested at Shidai Tianyue in Guilin prefecture (Guangxi) to demand for wage arrears, threatening to jump off a scaffolded building.
Around 11 September 2020 (as reported), over a dozen summer student workers protested in Changsha prefecture (Hunan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a public swimming pool.

Around 14 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers protested in Yancheng prefecture (Jiangsu) to demand for RMB 3 million worth of wage arrears owed by a delivery company. They held up a banner.

Around 16 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 52 workers protested in Pingyi county (Linyi, Shandong) to demand for ten months' worth of wage arrears owed by a food processing facility. It was reported that the dispute had not been settled since two years ago.

On 17 September 2020, over a dozen delivery workers protested at the entrance of the Meituan Waimai office in Cili county (Zhangjiajie, Hunan) against a deduction in their salaries. They held up a banner.

On 17 September 2020, as many as 100 migrant workers protested in Weinan prefecture (Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a private construction company, after their project's person-in-change went incommunicado.

Around 17 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Zhuhai prefecture (Guangdong) against unpaid leave, and to demand for social insurance and wage arrears owed by a shower equipment manufacturer.

Around 18 September 2020 (as reported), 1001-10000 taxi drivers protested in Dongsheng district (Ordos, Inner Mongolia) against the introduction of rideshare motorcycles in the region after a lack of government response. They had reportedly mobilised efforts to remove existing motorcycles to other areas.
Around 23 September 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Zhouzhi county (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by Jixian Industrial Park.

Around 28 September 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 taxi drivers protested in Zhenping county (Nanyang, Henan) against the introduction of rideshare motorcycles in the region. The drivers reportedly surrounded delivery trucks carrying motorcycles with their cars.

On 8 September 2020, more than 800 taxi drivers gathered to strike and protest in Baoqing county (Shuangyashan, Heilongjiang) against rideshare motorcycles, and demanded the county government to cease introducing more rideshare motorcycles to the region. This was allegedly the largest taxi driver protest in Baoqing.

Around 29 September 2020 (as reported), three migrant workers protested in Tengzhou county (Zaozhuang, Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project, threatening to jump off a construction crane.
Around 29 September 2020 (as reported), as many as a dozen workers protested in Qingdao prefecture (Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction materials manufacturer.

Around 14 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Fengqing county (Lincang, Yunnan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a logistics company. They were able to secure partial compensation for 17 migrant workers.

Around 12 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 delivery workers protested in Changsha prefecture (Hunan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a web-based logistics company and a warehouse management company. Management and procurement issues at the logistic company's Guanshaling branch created a large backlog of tickets for the warehouse to fulfill, resulting in fines, delays and wage arrears.

Around 15 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 university students, who worked over the summer, protested in Zhengzhou prefecture (Henan) to demand for wage arrears owed by a traffic warden gig at Beilonghu. The employer-in-charge stated that compensation had been allocated to the responsible hiring intermediary.

On 31 August 2020, ethnic Mongolian parents and students protested at Mongolian No.2 Middle School in Lubei town of Jarud Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia) against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting immediately with this semester (similar changes applying to minority school curricula in five other regions).

Security measures: On 30 August 2020, government officials shut down two house church venues in Xingqi village and one venue in Xiyi village Keqiao district (Shaoxing, Zhejiang) after they repeatedly refused to join the Three-Self Church.

On 25 June 2020, the Three-Self True Jesus Church in Daqing Residential District, Hualong district (Puyang, Henan) was demolished by the authorities despite prior approval by the Religious Affairs Bureau. An excavator demolished the main entrance, then the entire building was bulldozed ten days later. In October 2019, local authorities also forced the church to take down its cross and raise the national flag.

Around 16 March 2020 (month of), a Three-Self church in Yutai county (Jining, Shandong) was demolished by the county government. They broke in during a gathering, tore up Bibles and religious images, then demolished the building with furniture and electrical appliances buried underneath.

On 30 July 2020, a Protestant church in Xuezhuang town of Xinhua district (Pingdingshan, Henan) was converted into a school for massage therapists. It had been closed down by the district management committee since September 2018.
Security measures: Around 16 July 2020 (month of), the police raided and shut down a Sola Fide meeting venue in Wucheng district (Jinhua, Zhejiang).

Around 20 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Qingdao prefecture (Shandong) to demand for wage arrears from an electronics manufacturer. They were reportedly beaten by people from their company.
Around 21 October 2020 (as reported), many teachers protested in Fuzhou prefecture (Fujian) to demand for wage arrears from an education institute.
On 19 October 2020, many delivery workers protested in Fuzhou prefecture (Fujian) to demand for wage arrears owed by a courier company.

Around 20 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers protested in Xi'an prefecture (Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears from a construction site after seeking labour arbitration on 29 Sep.

Around 19 October 2020 (as reported), dozens of teachers protested at a mining vocational training school on Wanjin Road, Shishan town of Nanhai district (Foshan, Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears following a business merger at the school. They wore t-shirts with slogans on them.

Around 22 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Dalian prefecture (Liaoning) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction company. Protesters were beaten by the project manager and his crew.

On 31 August 2020, government authorities imposed a curfew in Lubei town of Jarud Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia) in response to days of demonstrations against a new policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region. Cars were not allowed to leave or enter the city.

On 23 August 2020, 12 police officers and government officials raided a Great Praise Church venue in Gushi county (Xinyang, Henan), and emptied the venue. Another venue was raided the same day, with officials taking away the donation box, electrical appliances, furniture and religious texts.
On 29 July 2020, a folk religion temple in Kaifeng prefecture (Henan) was demolished by about 200 Public Security Bureau and Urban Management Bureau officials and police officers.

On 24 June 2020, about 300 government-dispatched workers demolished a folk religion temple in Fuzhou prefecture (Fujian). Two believers were pressed and pushed to the ground for asking to see a demolition order and to relocate statues of deities from the temple.
Around 16 July 2020 (month of), a folk religion temple in Shiguan village (now known as Wu village), Nanle county (Puyang, Henan) was demolished by the authorities.
On 10 April 2020, a folk religion temple in Zhengzhou prefecture (Henan) was leveled to the ground by the authorities at night and without warning.
Around 15 June 2020 (month of), a folk religion temple in Fuzhou prefecture (Fujian) was demolished by over 100 personnel sent by the authorities.
Around 16 May 2020 (month of), a folk religion temple was destroyed by authorities in Dengfeng county (Zhengzhou, Henan) on the pretext of widening a road.

Around 16 May 2020 (month of), three folk religion temples in Gongyi county (Zhengzhou, Henan) were demolished by the authorities. Another folk religion temple was converted into a Chinese Civil War memorial hall.
On 14 April 2020, a folk religion temple in Dengfeng county (Zhengzhou, Henan) was demolished by the authorities.

Around 16 May 2020 (month of), many folk religion temples were repurposed by authorities to be used as storehouses and other use in Ci county (Handan, Hebei). One temple was converted into an activity centre.

On 2 August 2020, local authorities burned books from the Buddhist Ciyun Temple in Lingyuan county (Chaoyang, Liaoning). Seven pickup trucks worth of books authored by Master Chin Kung and the Dalai Lama were carried outside the temple and burnt overnight.
On 3 September 2020, a folk religion temple was demolished by authorities in Dengfeng county (Zhengzhou, Henan).

On 7 July 2020, a folk religion temple in Guangzong county (Xingtai, Hebei) was demolished by authorities along with the religious statues left inside. People later built a small temple on the original foundation, but the government soon destroyed it as well.
Around 26 October 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 delivery workers protested and went on strike in Jinan prefecture (Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a delivery company.

Around 29 October 2020 (as reported), dozens of workers protested in Changchun prefecture (Jilin) to demand for wage arrears following the regional closure of a private education company. This company's closure and wages owned sparked a major demonstration in Beijing in the previous week.
Around 26 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Changsha prefecture (Hunan) to demand for two months of wage arrears owed by a cleaning company.
Around 28 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Zhuanghe county (Dalian, Liaoning) to demand for wage arrears from a hotel.

Around 26 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Dasi town (Xiqing, Tianjin) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project. They were also collectively beaten, but the assailants were not reported. At least one worker suffered facial injuries.

Around 29 October 2020 (as reported), 1001-10000 taxi drivers staged a protest in Kaifeng prefecture (Henan) to boycott against a prefecture-wide government mandate to replace all of their vehicles with electric cars, and to switch to a single specific car model.

On 26 October 2020, 1001-10000 taxi drivers petitioned and protested at the Transportation Bureau in Zhongyuan district (Zhengzhou, Henan) against decreasing wages due to increased competition from the proliferation of web-based rideshare car drivers. The unrest was also prompted by the death of a taxi driver, who died in car accident on 30 Jun from overworking.

Around 29 October 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 taxi drivers staged a protest in Lushan county (Pingdingshan, Henan) against the addition of several thousands of web-based rideshare motorcycles in the county.

On 9 September 2020, petitioners from Chengdu protested at a Sichuan Province High People's Court in Chengdu prefecture (Sichuan) to demand that the Chief Judge rectified wrongful convictions and miscarriages of justice, and punished those who were responsible.

On 27 October 2020, petitioners from Chengdu and its surrounding counties collectively protested at Sichuan Higher People's Court in Chengdu prefecture (Sichuan) to demand for a meeting with the Chief Judge, in relation to the fifth plenary session of the 19th Central Committee of the CPC that commenced in Beijing. It was reported that petitioners had coordinated at least two weekly gatherings and nightly demonstrations with banners in front of the High Court for more than a month leading up to the plenary session.

On 28 October 2020, a female petitioner was harassed and assaulted by an unidentified person in Fengwu village, Quan'an town of Shizhong district (Neijiang, Sichuan), before disappearing and going incommunicado until she was hospitalised for emergency response on 31 Oct. Prior to this, she was intercepted in Chengdu prefecture and escorted back to her home in Neijiang on 26 Oct, then forbidden by district and town officers from releasing news about the interception (and alleged assault). It was reported that she did not obey the orders and published a post that got some attention on Weixin.

On 20 October 2020, a petitioner from Chongqing was intercepted by local government officials from a train carriage in Zhengzhou prefecture (Henan), his situation remained unknown at the time of reporting on 29 Oct 2020. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance in relation to the fifth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee set to commence in Beijing.

On 18 October 2019, a Christian church in Funan County (Fuyang City, Anhui Province) was demolished by the local authorities, as part of a nationwide effort to 'sinicize' religion in China. All property was destroyed. Some Christians who knelt before the police were sent to the hospital after fainting. The persons in charge of the church were also arrested on the next day.

On 17 June 2019, several buddhist temples in the scenic area of Cangu in Yi County (Hebei Province) were demolished by more than 100 government officials, on the grounds that they were 'illegal constructions'.

Around 1 September 2019 (beginning of month), the meeting venue of a house church in Dongping County (Tai'an City, Shandong Province) was forced to shut down by government officials. This is part of the government's effort to crackdown on religious groups, which it considers to be 'criminal'.

On 13 October 2019, a house church in Jinan City, Shandong Province was shut down by the Ethnic and Religious Affirs Bureau, with its crosses and other religious symbols in the venue destroyed by the authorities. The host was forced to sign an statement to 'stop gatherings involuntarily', with the congregation receiving threats not to gather in the future.

On 15 October 2019, a Sola Fide house church in Jinan City was raided by officials from the Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau. The host was forced to sign a statement to 'stop gatherings involuntarily'.

On 29 October 2019, a Three-Self Church in Wuning County (Jiujiang City, Jiangxi Province) was raided by personnel from the Religious Affairs Bureau. They removed the words 'Christian Church' from the wall, and took away all religious symbols. They also destroyed the cross on the roof and replaced it with the Chinese national flag. It was claimed that these measures were taken because 'Christians were involved in the anti-extradition bill protests in Hong Kong'.

On 1 December 2019, a house church in Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province was raided by the police, claiming that it was 'holding illegal meetings and disturbing public order'. The police damaged the church's blackboard, seized Bibles and hymnbooks, and took away more than 800RMB of donation money.

On 10 January 2019, a Bible study group was studying the Bible in a church in Chengdu City, Sichuan Province, when the local police and Department of Civil Affairs raided the church, announced that the gathering was illegal, and that the church would be shut down. They warned the congregation that 'religious activities cannot be organised illegally'. Some books were taken away from the church.

On 29 October 2019, five police officers stormed into a house church meeting venue in Lushan County (Pingdingshan City, Henan Province) and told the congregation that 'Jesus is a God of Western countries' and to 'believe in the God of China'. They confiscated Bibles, dismantled the cross, and also took photos of all nearly 70 believers. This was part of a broader campaign to pressure house churches to join the state-run churches.

Around 31 October 2019 (end of month), a house church venue in Weidong District (Pingdingshan City, Henan Province) was raided by officials who smashed down its door. They confiscated religious books and other items, and shut down the venue. The person in charge was told that these gatherings are 'illegal' as they were not approved by the government. This was part of a broader campaign to pressure house churches to join the state-run churches.

On 1 December 2019, the meeting venue of a church in Nubu Residential District, Lanxi City (Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province) was forcibly shut down by the government, on the grounds that it was not registered. The government personnel confiscated tables, chairs, pianos and tableware. When the congregation members tried to block the personnel from removing the items in the venue, they were beaten. It was reported that many people were bleeding and some sustained fractures. 5 male believers were later detained in a detention centre on 3 January 2002, on charges that they were 'disrupting public order'.

As reported on 8 March 2020, the cross from a church in Huaishang District (Bengbu City, Anhui Province) was dismantled by the local authorities. This was part of a broader campaign initiated by the Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau of Anhui Province for public security units to continue cracking down on 'illegal evangelism'.

On 13 March 2020, the cross from a church in Woyang County (Bozhou City, Anhui Province) was dismantled by the local authorities. This was part of a broader campaign initiated by the Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau of Anhui Province for public security units to continue cracking down on 'illegal evangelism'.

On 30 March 2020, a university student in Shandong was reportedly held incommunicado, after publishing a video on his Twitter calling for Xi Jinping to step down. It was been reported by RFA that he had been taken for questioning by the local police, on suspicion of 'picking quarrels and stirring up trouble'. In the video, he criticised the Communist Party of China for its land reform, Cultural Revolution, persecution of Falun Gong believers, Tibetans, Hong Kong and Xinjiang among other issues. He had previously been administratively detained for five days for speaking out against the government. At the time of reporting on 1 April 2020, he had remained uncontactable.

On 8 October 2019, a Tibetan man was taken by the police from his residence in Geso Tsalhi village, Nagqu Town (Nagqu, Tibet) on unknown charges. He had since been held incommunicado. He was taken into custody after being told by the police not to leave the area. Some sources stated that he was likely to be arrested for 'leaking state secrets'. There had been no news about his whereabouts and the reason for his arrest by the time of reporting on 15 November 2019. The man had been outspoken on issues concerning the reunion of Tibetan people inside Tibet and in exile, and expressed hope for Dalai Lama's return to Tibet.

On 12 April 2020, a Three-Self church located on Shengli Road, Chengxi District (Xining City, Qinghai Province) was demolished by around 10 officials from the municipal government, on the grounds that it was an 'illegal building' with 'building safety hazards'. It was reported that the majority of believers in the church was female.

On 30 May 2020, a poet was taken to an unknown location after 40 police officers captured him from his home in Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Prefecture (Yunnan). Several of the poet's relatives were interrogated and others were placed under forced house arrest. He was charged with 'inciting subversion of state power' this time after being targeted repeatedly for the online political commentaries he uploaded between 2003 to 2014. While the police informed his family that he is under criminal detention, the police were unable to state where he was held, and his whereabouts remained unknown at the time of reporting on 14 September 2020.

Around 16 September 2020 (as reported), female Utsul students held a sit-in outside Tianya Utsul Primary School in Tianya district (Sanya, Hainan) as part of protests against a neighbourhood-specific ban of traditional Islamic dress in schools and government offices. The ban was temporarily lifted on 22 Sep after hundreds of pupils at three schools refused to obey and boycotted classes, which Han students also reportedly joined to show solidarity for their 'ethnic minority comrades.' The exact prompt of the ban was not known, but it was verified that a CPC working document from 2019 detailed 'sinicisation' measures aiming at the only two Hui- and Utsul-dominant neighbourhoods in the district and Sanya in general.

On 11 April 2019, the Gazhuang Mosque in Zheqiaozhen Town, Linxia City (Linxia Hui Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu) was demolished without warning by dozens of government personnel just a month after it was built, on the basis that it was 'too Arabic'. Muslims at the scene who recorded the incident were arrested.

On 3 February 2020, the cross of a Three-Self church in Hexi Village, Lanling County (Linyi City, Shandong Province) was removed by workers hired by a representative of the Zhuangwu town government, on the grounds that the representative 'could be dismissed from office' if his superiors saw the cross. This was part of a broader campaign launched by the central government to remove crosses from churches across China.

In October 2019, all Arabic words were removed from a signboard of a Hui-run restaurant in Chaoyang City, Liaoning Province, after the owner was ordered to do so by over ten officers from the United Front Work Department and the Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau following a raid. This was part of the CCP's policy to 'sinicize' Hui Muslims across China, where Arabic script and Islamic symbols were ordered to be removed from shops and restaurants.

Around 15 October 2019 (month of), all Bibles, hymnbooks, evangelism handbooks, and other religious books were confiscated from a Three-Self church in Hukou County (Jiujiang City, Jiangxi Province) by four officials from the Culture Broadcasting Bureau, on the grounds that 'they were not produced by approved publishers'. This was part of a broader campaign to crack down on faith-related materials not approved by the state, in order to advance the CCP's 'sinicization' policy.

Around 15 June 2020 (month of), the town government rectified ten clan ancestral halls (associated with China's folk religion) in Maochen town (Xiaogan, Hubei), one of which was converted into a cultural activity centre for the elderly. Slogans promoting 'destroying the Four Olds' (a popular motto during the Cultural Revolution) were displayed in some of the halls.

Around 16 July 2020 (month of), a Three-Self church in Lusigang township, Yugan county (Shangrao, Jiangxi) was demolished by the township government on the pretext of 'building a high-speed highway.' While the church was demolished, the public restroom next to it was not.

Around 15 April 2020 (month of), five mosques in Minquan County (Shangqiu City, Henan Province) were forcibly rectified on orders from the central government to 'sinicize' over 1,000 mosques across the province. Domes with star-and-crescent symbols were removed from the mosques to make them look 'more Chinese'.

In July 2019, a True Jesus Church (Protestant) venue in Jianyang City (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province) was shut down by government officials, on the grounds that it was 'illegal'. The government officials also arranged for workers to saw off the cross and block the door of the venue.

On 11 March 2020, a mosque in Yinchuan City, Ningxia Region was 'sinicized' by the government. During the rectification process, local Muslims were prohibited from interfering, or sharing information or discussing the rectification.

Around 15 September 2019 (month of), a couple who had been petitioning for 18 years was beaten up by the authorities while they were submitting their petition at the letters and calls bureau in Qionglai City (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province). They were then detained at a local police station for 7 days for 'disrupting work unit order'.

On 27 May 2019, an activist in Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province was 'taken on mandatory vacation' by the police to Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture (Hunan). It was reported that the act might be part of a national campaign by the authorities to silence dissent and religious individuals before the 30th anniversary of Tiananmen Square protests.

Around 3 August 2019 (between 19 July - 19 August), 19 drivers petitioned at the Sanmenxia People's Government in Sanmenxia prefecture (Henan) about a labour dispute. It was suspected that their repeated visits and threats to take their unresolved disputes to Beijing angered local government officials, who later claimed that the drivers were members of an 'evil criminal organisation' and arrested them all later in the day.

On 11 May 2020, a female petitioner was forced to sit on a 'tiger bench' for more than 20 hours while being detained at a police station in Quan'an Town (Neijiang City, Sichuan Province). She had been forcibly taken away by the deputy secretary of Quan'an Town while she was submitting a petition at the Sichuan Provincial Letters and Calls Bureau the day before. She was released in the morning of 12 May 2020.

On 20 October 2020, a petitioner from Jiangsu was beaten by many unidentified men on Changhan Lu (north of Jingliang Lu) in Changyang town (Fangshan, Beijing) and kidnapped onto a car with a Jiangsu provincial car plate. He was then held at a 'black jail' in Rugao county (Nantong, Jiangsu) from 21 Oct until 24 Oct 2020. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance in relation to the fifth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee set to commence in Beijing.

On 25 December 2019, the self-built house of a petitioner in Cangshan District (Fuzhou City, Fujian Province) was forcibly demolished by the local authorities, while the petitioner was still being detained in a detention centre for being charged with 'provoking trouble' in September 2018.

On 1 September 2019, a street vendor was beaten and choked to death by 7 to 8 urban management/'chengguan' officers in Liudongzhen, Yunyang, in Hebei province for not letting the chengguan officials take things from him. One of the vendor's relative tried to stop the officials from beating him but was unsuccessful.

On 15 May 2020, a petitioner from Fujian was taken away by private security personnel hired by Jin'an district government outside the Letters and Visits Bureau of People's Government of Fujian Province in Gulou District (Fuzhou City, Fujian Province). He was then detained in a 'black jail' in Jin'an district. It was reported that he was forcibly taken away to prevent him from petitioning during the annual parliamentary sessions due to start on 21 May 2020.

On 19 May 2020, a female petitioner was intercepted by personnel from Neijiang city government, the police station, and village staff members while she was waiting for the train to Beijing at Chengdu North Railway Station at Xindu District (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province). She was taken away to a police station in Quan'an Town (Neijiang, Sichuan), where she was forced to sit on a 'tiger bench'. She was released the next day.

Around 16 January 2019 (month of), nine Kazakh women from Ghulja (Yining) county (Ili Kazak Autonomous, Xinjiang) were sent back to an 'internment' camp by the authorities after they refused to sign a labor contract with a monthly salary of 600 yuan, which was around 40 percent of a typical wage for a manual worker. Originally, they had been sent to work in the Jiafang Garments Industrial Park (in Yidong Industrial District) after being released from an internment camp, where they would work 12-hour shifts sewing gloves and undergo an hour's 'political education' every day for the money.

On 25 May 2020, a house church in Jiaotan Town (Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province) was raided and ordered to be shut down by the police and officials from the county's Religious Affairs Bureau, on the grounds that the place was not registered with the government and is therefore 'illegal'. The police and government personnel removed a religious sign, and other banners and slogans in the church. All the chairs and properties in the church were also removed.

On 16 February 2020, a villager from Huizhai Village of Hualong District (Puyang City, Henan Province) was reportedly tied to a pole by epidemic prevention personnel for failing to wear a mask while going out. The incident prompted strong reactions from internet users, leading to the set up of a working group by local authorities to investigate the incident. It was later reported that the villager failed to wear a mask everyday or obey the personnel's advice, prompting 'more extreme measures' to be taken against them.

On 30 April 2020, the mother of a human rights activist and several other people demonstrated in Sichuan Province, calling on the authorities to release the human rights activist so that the mother and son could meet 'one last time' due to the mother's deteriorating health. The activist was sentenced to 12 years in prison in July 2019, on the grounds of 'leaking state secrets to foreigners'. At least 6 people held placards.

On 5 March 2020, during a visit by CCP officials, residents of a housing compound in Qingshan District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province) demonstrated from within their apartments, repeatedly shouting 'fake' during the official's visit. It was reported that residents were told by the local residential committee to stay in their homes during their visit, with 'volunteers' staging delivery of meat and vegetables to residents. The demonstration by the residents were in response to the delivery of 'fake goods'.

Around 9 May 2019 (from the start of Ramadan on 5 May to 13 May 2019), during the month of Ramadan, more than 500 Kazakh female factory workers, aged between 16 and 25, in Ili Kazak Autonomous were forcibly sent on a train to an unknown place by the police and have been missing since. At the same time, more than 300 men were transferred from re-education camps to reconstructed factories to carry out foced labour and attend 'political education' classes.

On 23 February 2020, the dome and other parts of a mosque in Lushan County (Pingdingshan City, Henan Province) were demolished by the local government. It was reported that the demolition took place while Hui villagers were away from the village for 22 consecutive days, providing free lunch for frontline medical and sanitation workers, and urban management personnel who were fighting against the coronavirus outbreak. It was part of a broader five-year plan to 'sinicize' Islam in China.

In August 2019, Arabic characters were removed from the signboards of at least 250 Muslim shops in Xinxiang City, Henan Province, on the grounds of 'unifying Chinese characters'. Shops were also required to remove the halal signs from food packaging. It was part of a broader five-year plan to 'sinicize' Islam in China.
On 3 December 2019, a church in Xining, Qinghai Province was forced to shut down on the grounds that it 'did not meet the fire safety measures'.

On 19 May 2020, a female petitioner was transferred from the Public Security Bureau of Yunyang County (Chongqing Municipality) by government officials to a hotel at the edge of Yunyang county for 'compulsory quarantine' for 14 days, possibly as a pretext to prevent her from travelling to Beijing during the annual parliamentary sessions to petition. She had been forcibly taken away from a hotel in Zhuozhou City (Baoding City, Hebei Province) by government officials from Yunyang County on 17 May 2020, before she was repatriated to Yunyang and subsequently detained in the basement of the Public Security Bureau of Yunyang County on 18 May 2020.

On 28 June 2020, a female petitioner with high paraplegia was forcibly repatriated by the village secretary and three 'assistants' from the Dazhong subdistrict office in Dazhong Subdistrict, Dafeng District (Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province), after requesting the office to pay the agreed medical expenses as soon as possible. After the petitioner refused to get into the car, her clothes and pants were reportedly removed by the 'assistants', although the details for removing her clothes were not mentioned in the report.

On 12 June 2020, more than 20 petitioners petitioned and demonstrated at the Sichuan Province Public Security Department in Qingyang District (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province), stating that they had been illegally 'stabilised' by the local police in their respective petitioning activities and demanded that the Public Security Department take legal disciplinary action against the local stability maintenance personnel. They also reported that the local police arbitrarily intercepted, beat up and detained petitioners during the annual parliamentary sessions.

On 29 June 2020, a forced evictee was beaten up by seven to eight eviction operation personnel at his home in Qujiang district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) (coded at Xi'an City) then held at a 'black jail' for a day. When he returned, they had demolished his house, looted four vehicles worth of belongings, a mortgage agreement and proof of his hospital stays and medical diagnosis.

On 21 January 2020, 15 petitioners went to the Pingxiang Anyuan People's Court in Anyuan District (Pingxiang, Jiangxi Province) to file a lawsuit against the Pingxiang City Letters and Calls Bureau, and the city's local newspaper including its president and responsible editors for publishing fake news. It was reported that the judge at the court refused to accept the lawsuit, on the grounds that the petitioners 'did not provide the addresses of the president and editors'.

On 7 August 2019, a female petitioner was transferred from the police station in Qingxi town of Shaoshan (Xiangtan, Hunan) to the psychiatric ward of Xiangtan No.5 Hospital, where she witnessed medicine 'arbitrarily administered' and inserted into her meals. She was taken away by the officials onto a taxi on 6 Aug, when town government officials promised to resolve the issues she was petitioning about and deceived her into meeting. They sent her to the Qingxi town police station the day after, and confiscated her luggage and identity documents. She was detained at the psychiatric ward until 26 October 2019, and claimed that she was forcibly administered ecstasy tablets during this period.

On 7 April 2020, a pro-democracy dissident was transferred from a prison in Qingjiang Town (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province) to a hotel in an undisclosed location, after serving his 10-year jail term. It was reported that while the authorities had used the pretext of 'quarantine' for coronavirus, the dissident remained uncontactable and had yet been released at the time of reporting.

On 19 June 2019, a democracy-cum-labour activist became incommunicado after the police took him away from his toy factory workplace in Heyuan prefecture (Guangdong). He was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location for four months. He was later charged with 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' (any in-between release was not reported), and officially arrested on 22 Nov for spreading democracy and freedom online. On 4 Aug 2020, his family learnt that he was imprisoned after a secret trial. It was revealed on 27 Oct 2020 that he received an 18-month prison sentence for crimes still unknown (location coded at Yuancheng, municipal seat of Heyuan).

It was reported as one of the government's efforts to conceal or destroy outdoor icons and statues at Buddhist temples across the province.

Property destruction: On 22 November 2019, over 50 government-dispatched personnel shut down a Buddhist temple in Miyi county (Panzhihua, Sichuan), and destroyed statues and an incense burner. It was reported as one of the government's efforts to conceal or destroy outdoor icons and statues at Buddhist temples across the province.

Security measures: Around 15 June 2020 (month of), the United Front Work Department merged and shut down all venues subordinate to the Three-Self churches in Jinan prefecture (Shandong) (location coded at Lixia, seat of Jinan), ahead of each inspection visit by high-level CPC officials. Six out of 30 subordinate sites of a church remained open, with the rest shut down after having their activity certificates revoked. Three out of 36 licensed Three-Self venues in Tianqiao district were allowed to remain open.

Security measures: Around 15 September 2020 (month of), all unlicensed Protestant Three-Self Church venues in Zhaozhaizi town of Gaotang county (Liaocheng, Shandong) were shut down by officials. Liaocheng prefecture's CPC committee dispatched 12 teams to 36 towns and townships to inspect grassroots CPC organisations. It was reported that religious issues play a central part in these inspections, which were planned for Sep through mid-Dec 2020.

Property destruction: Around 15 June 2020 (month of), officials destroyed all statues at two Buddhist temples in Renhe district (Panzhihua, Sichuan). It was reported as one of the government's efforts to conceal or destroy outdoor icons and statues at Buddhist temples across the province.

Property destruction: Around 30 November 2019 (end of month), the township government shut down and destroyed statues at a Buddhist temple in Geliping township of Xi district (Panzhihua, Sichuan). It was reported as one of the government's efforts to conceal or destroy outdoor icons and statues at Buddhist temples across the province.

Around 4 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Dongguan prefecture (Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears from a construction company. The police stood by on the scene but did not intervene (location coded as Nancheng, municipal seat of Dongguan).

On 20 October 2020, villagers bearing long knives, wooden batons and stones assaulted public security officers and criminal investigation bureau officers who conducted unannounced forced eviction and demolition operations in Hantang village, Futang township of Lianshan County (Qingyuan, Guangdong). Thirteen suspects were arrested by the time of reporting on 1 Nov 2020.
Property destruction: Around 15 April 2020 (month of), authorities demolished some buildings at a Taoist Temple in Liaoyang county (Liaoyang, Liaoning). It was shut down last year.

Property destruction: On 13 August 2020, about 300 county officials and police officers demolished a Buddhist temple in Susong county (Anqing, Anhui). The temple director was kept at home under police control until the demolition was completed.

Security measures: Around 30 September 2020 (end of month), the local government shut down a church venue in Yushan county (Shangrao, Jiangxi) after the congregation was asked but refused to join the state-run Three-Self Church, raise the national flag, and hang propaganda slogans.
Land seizure: Around 16 July 2020 (month of), authorities converted a Taoist Temple in Donggang county (Dandong, Liaoning) into a nursing home. It had been sealed off since Sep 2018.
Property destruction: On 28 June 2019, the Buddhist Bailong Temple in Jiujiang prefecture (Jiangxi) [coded to Xunyang district] was demolished by the local government.

Property destruction: Around 15 June 2020 (month of), the Lingxi town government sent about 100 workers to demolish two buildings in a Taoist Temple in Lingxi town of Cangnan county (Wenzhou, Zhejiang). The demolition of the accommodation facilities made it impossible to host pilgrims and worshippers visiting the temple.

Property destruction: On 6 September 2020, the government of Xiaokou town in Taihe county (Fuyang, Anhui) destroyed four folk religion temples on the pretext of preventing river erosion. Over 30 government personnel were sent to disperse the residents opposing the demolition, prohibiting them from photographing the scene.
Property destruction: On 27 September 2020, in the middle of the night, the town government demolished a newly-built Taoist Temple in Fan town of Ruichang county (Jiujiang, Jiangxi).

On 27 August 2020, near dawn, about 400 police officers and local officials came to a Buddhist temple Taihu county (Anqing, Anhui) to implement a demolition order, and chased away six believers guarding the temple by shocking them with electric batons. One elderly man died on the spot from a cardiac arrest induced by the shocks.

On 15 September 2020, local residents were beaten during a demolition operation led by the county government, who dispatched over 100 police officers and workers to demolish a folk religion temple in Xiushui county (Jiujiang, Jiangxi). The residents were beaten and one person suffered a concussion. While local authorities declared that their plans to demolish the temple were suspended, government-hired workers later demolished the temple in the early morning of 17 Sep.

On 17 October 2020, Buddhist believers were stopped and beaten during an operation by ten law enforcement officers and over ten unidentified men to demolish the newly-built walls of the once-demolished the Buddhist Bailong Temple in Jiujiang prefecture (Jiangxi) [coded to Xunyang district].
Security measures: On 23 July 2020, authorities shut down a house church venue in Nanzhao county (Nanyang, Henan).
Security measures: Around 16 October 2020 (month of), nine old local Churches in Yushan county (Shangrao, Jiangxi) were shut down by government authorities.

Property destruction: Around 15 June 2020 (month of), local officials destroyed a Buddhist temple in Danyang town of Bowang district (Ma'anshan prefecture, Anhui) under the orders of the prefecture government.

Property destruction: Around 16 August 2019 (month of), the government demolished a two-story building used for accommodating visiting worshippers at a Taoist temple in Ji'an county (Tonghua, Jilin). It had suffered harassment from local officials since 2018 - namely those from the United Front Work Department and Religious Affairs Bureau. It had been forced to turn over donation money, with its religious statues taken away in Sep 2018, and incense burner and signboard removed in Nov 2018.
Security measures: On 9 August 2020, authorities shut down a Sola Fide house church venue in Neixiang county (Nanyang, Henan).
Around 13 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers held a sit-in protest in Chishui county (Zunyi, Guizhou) to demand for wage arrears owed by a property developer.

Around 12 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Wuhan prefecture (Hubei) [coded to Jiang'an district] to demand for wage arrears owed by an telecommunications firm. They held up a banner.

On 22 June 2020, a woman was cuffed and beaten by the police of Sanmiaoqian Township Police Station while visiting farmlands confiscated by the village government in Wan'an village, Sanmiaoqian township of Poyang county (Shangrao, Jiangxi). She sustained bruises and fractures to her skull and ribs.

On 17 November 2020, over 100 residents demonstrated in a residential complex of Xiaotangshan town in Changping district (Beijing) against the town government-backed, black-clad personnel (wearing uniforms typical of riot police) who arrived the night before to enforce a forced eviction operation. They called for their evictors and law enforcement to abide by legal procedures. They chanted slogans, and set up metal barricades to block the entrance of the complex. Clashes were reported between the residents and over 100 armed riot police and security guards present.

Property destruction: Around 16 October 2019 (month of), a 14-meter-tall white Guanyin statue outside a Buddhist temple in Xiangshan town in Daying county (Suining, Sichuan), was demolished by about 20 local officials and police officers. Another Guanyin statue at a separate temple in the same county was destroyed by authorities in the same month.

Property destruction: Around 15 April 2020 (month of), authorities destroyed a Bodhisattva statue outside a Buddhist temple in Dongshagou village, Wujinshan town of Yuci district (Jinzhong, Shanxi) on orders to destroy all statues taller than ten metres.
Property destruction: Around 16 January 2020 (month of), a Guanyin statue outside a Buddhist temple in Linhai county (Taizhou, Zhejiang) was demolished by authorities.

Property destruction: Around 15 February 2020 (month of), the Tengzhou city government demolished a three-faced Guanyin statue in the Longshan Scenic Area in Tengzhou county (Zaozhuang, Shandong) over 20 days.

Property destruction: Around 15 April 2020 (month of), some halls of a Buddhist temple on the Guangfu Mountain in Cangshan district (Fuzhou, Fujian) were demolished by the local government due to plans to build a new road.
Property destruction: Around 16 August 2019 (month of), the Zhazuo town government cut a three-faced Guanyin statue into pieces in Zhazuo town (Guiyang, Guizhou) for being too tall.
Property destruction: Around 15 September 2019 (month of), a Guanyin statue in Duqiao town of Linhai county (Taizhou, Zhejiang) was removed by authorities claiming that it had distracted drivers.
Property destruction: On 30 June 2020, a Taoist temple in Gushan town of Jin'an district (Fuzhou, Fujian) was demolished as local authorities requisitioned the land on which it stood.

Property destruction: Around 3 October 2020 (beginning of month), a Buddhist temple and its residential house were demolished by the Religious Affairs Bureau in Zhengzhou prefecture (Henan) (coded to Zhongyuan) on the grounds of river and flood management. This happened three months after Religious Affairs Bureau officials ordered all Buddhist residents to move out on 3 July.

Land seizure: Around 15 November 2019 (month of), the local government took over and converted a Taoist temple in Qicun town of Shizhong district (Zaozhuang, Shandong) and converted it into a tourist centre. The temple's signboard and statues were destroyed.

Property destruction: Around 16 August 2020 (month of), the signboard and three Buddhist statues at its entrance of a Buddhist temple in Jinzhong prefecture (Shanxi) (coded to Yuci) were removed on orders of the Jinzhong Religious Affairs Bureau. On 10 September 2020, the prefecture government in the northern province of Shanxi shut down the temple, claiming that it lacked proper building certificates, and occupied arable land.

Security measures: Around 16 July 2020 (month of), the prefecture government shut down a Buddhist hall within an urban residence in Shuozhou prefecture (Shanxi) (coded to Shuocheng) because it didn't have a religious activity venue registration certificate.

Property destruction: Around 1 July 2020 (beginning of month), the district government demolished a three-faced Guanyin statue outside a Buddhist temple on Zhongnan Mountain, Chang'an district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) with claims that its construction was not approved. Over 300 public security and special police officers guarded the site and blocked all roads leading to the temple. One demolition worker was detained for posting photos of the demolition.

Property destruction: On 8 July 2020, over 30 town government officials and urban management personnel removed all religious statues, and destroyed a Buddhist temple in Da'a town of Xinfeng county (Ganzhou, Jiangxi).
Property destruction: On 6 January 2019, a 30-meter-tall Guanyin statue in Zhujia Villa of Zaozhuang prefecture (Shandong) (location coded as Xuecheng) was demolished by authorities.
Property destruction: On 10 October 2020, the town government demolished a Taoist temple in Shanggan town of Minhou county (Fuzhou, Fujian) on the grounds of road construction.

Property destruction: On 20 October 2020, the county government demolished a Taoist temple in Shangli county (Pingxiang, Jiangxi), on the pretext of having to widening a road and rejuvenating the environment. It was reported, however, that the temple was not close to any roads foreseen to be widened or spaces allocated for urban greening.

Property destruction: On 27 June 2020, authorities demolished a Buddhist temple to the ground in Cangshan district (Fuzhou, Fujian) on the pretext of building an expressway. Another Buddhist temple on Longyan Mountain was also destroyed in the same month.
Around 16 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Xiajin county (Dezhou, Shandong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction company.

Around 15 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Shaoyang prefecture (Hunan) (coded to Daxiang) to demand for wage arrears owed by an interior decoration company. They held up banners.

Around 17 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Guigang prefecture (Guangxi) (coded to Gangbei) to demand for wage arrears owed by a car factory. They held up a banner.

Security measures: On 20 June 2019, government-backed people used container homes to create roadblocks at the North, West and East Gates of Liulin village in Jinshui district (Zhengzhou, Henan) as part of a months-long operation to cut off economic support and force villagers to evict. Over twenty hired individuals stayed behind to guard the roadblocks. The hired-individuals later also set up checkpoints to intercept villagers and vehicles, welded shut the gates, and used containers to enhance the roadblocks. The roadblocks remained in place at least until 26 August.

On 10 July 2019, a resident was assaulted by the village committee head and a villager in Liulin village, Jinshui district (Zhengzhou, Henan). This was part of a months-long operation to cut off economic support and force villagers to evict, during which several hundred government-hired villagers gathered to block roads within and at the South Gate of the village. The government-hired individuals had set up checkpoints to intercept villagers and vehicles. There had reportedly been other assault cases between 4 and 15 July.

Property destruction: On 10 February 2020, the town government demolished a 200-square-metre Protestant house church in Tushan town of Pizhou county (Xuzhou, Jiangsu). The government also trucked away church belongings worth about 25,000 RMB two days before the demolition.

Property destruction: Around 15 April 2019 (month of), the local government closed a Three-Self Church in Shuyang county (Suqian, Jiangsu) and tore down the two top floors it occupied, on the grounds that the building was higher than the county committee office.
Property destruction: Around 16 August 2019 (month of), four Three-Self churches (including one located in Zhangjiaxu town) were demolished in Siyang county (Suqian, Jiangsu).

Property destruction: Around 16 December 2019 (month of), a Protestant house church was leveled by the Yuhang district government (Hangzhou, Jiangsu) on the pretext that it was an illegal religious venue built without proper approval. The church was demolished previously to allegedly build a railway, and now to allegedly erect a new building.

Looting: On 20 September 2020, the police and Religious Affairs Bureau officials raided a house church in Qinzhou prefecture (Guangxi) (coded to Qinbei) during a gathering with over 50 believers. The police confiscated all Bible copies, religious books, benches, a piano, and several electrical appliances.

Around 25 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 sanitation workers protested in Wuhan prefecture (Hubei) (coded to Jiang'an) to demand for 19 years of cleaning fees owed by a serviced apartments management company.
Around 24 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Gaoyao district (Zhaoqing, Guangdong) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction site. They held up placards.

Around 24 November 2020 (as reported), over 100 workers protested in Jining prefecture (Shandong) (coded to Rencheng) to demand for wage arrears owed by a squatter area reconstruction project in Balimiao village.

Around 23 November 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 drivers went on strike and protested with their cars at the Transportation Bureau in Qingdao prefecture (Shandong) (coded to Shinan) against illegally operated taxis.

Around 24 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers held a sit-in protest in Jinzhou District (Dalian, Liaoning) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction project. They held up banners to express their demands.
On 24 November 2020, hundreds of drivers went on strike and protested with their cars at the Transportation Bureau in Huashan District (Ma'anshan, Anhui) against illegally operated taxis.

Around 23 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested at Taicun town of Xunyi county (Xianyang, Shaanxi) to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned Chinese medicine factory construction project.

Around 27 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Handan prefecture (Hebei) (coded to Congtai) to demand for wage arrears owed by a construction site. They held up banners to express their demands.

Around 7 July 2018 (as reported), a renowned Hunanese media commentator was being held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) by Chenzhou city (Hunan) police in an undisclosed location. Chen disappeared and lost contact several days after his 25 June 2018 reporting on the professional negligence and malfeasance of the Shaoyang Commission for Discipline Inspection Secretary. His wife and two brothers were also arrested.

Around 15 February 2018 (month of), a top Uyghur soccer player who played professionally for Jiangsu Suning F.C. was captured by the police while visiting Dorbiljin Market in Emin (Dorbiljin) county of the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture. He had been reportedly detained at a re-education camp for visiting foreign countries after returning to China after training and competitions overseas.

On 10 July 2018, as many as 200 Buddhist novices (under the age of 16) were evicted from Sershul monastery in Sershul county of Garze Tibetan Autonomous Region to be enrolled into a secular school run by the Chinese government. If they resisted, the monastery faced closure and punishment. The Sershul monastery is both a prominent Gelugpa centre and the only Buddhist monastic university in the Kham region.

On 9 January 2018, several thousand residents continued to demonstrate and marched on the streets of Fusong county (Baishan, Jilin) to protest against the unannounced relocation of Fusong No.1 Secondary School. Almost all shops and businesses went on strike. Police forces attempted to disperse the crowds, and arrested at least two protesters. The government responded to the first day with a withdrawal of relocation plans, but protesters were still concerned that the original teaching staff and administration would be reassigned to the new school.

On 19 December 2018, law enforcement officers forcibly evicted a convent in Qiqihar City (Heilongjiang). The convent had one hour to move their belongings after officers showed up with an eviction notice.

On 16 December 2018, several Early Rain Covenant church members and a former teacher at the Sichuan Jiaotong University were arrested in Chengdu (Sichuan) and detained incommunicado by police for 32 hours for participating in an outdoor Sunday worship. Adherents were forced to sign statements saying they won't participate in church activities in order to be released. 3 adherents who refused were tortured and severely beaten up by police.

Around 19 December 2018 (as reported), since the mass arrest of Early Rain Covenant church in Chengdu (Sichuan) members on 9 December 2018, 6 church members have been disappeared, 18 elders are in detention, about 100 members have been monitored and followed, and 50 theology students have been sent back to their hometowns and interrogated.

On 16 December 2018, about 30 people from the local Religious Affairs Department and Gulou Police Station charged into a church in Lu'an City (Anhui) and took away electronic devices and furniture by force.

On 16 December 2018, the Taiyuan Cornerstone Church was banned by the Xiaodian District Bureau of Ethnic and Religious Affairs (Taiyuan, Shanxi) on the basis that it was carrying out religious activities without official approval.

On 24 December 2018, Christmas Eve, more than 10 police officers raided a gospel church affiliated to the Early Rain Covenant Church in Chengdu City (Sichuan), taking away all the book, bibles, and computers. Police also changed the locks to the building to prevent members from having a Christmas gathering.

On 24 December 2018, Christmas Eve, the Early Rain Covenant Church in Qingyang District (Chengdu, Sichuan) was taken over by government authorities and turned into a Community Office where all community employees will be stationed. This is part of an ongoing crackdown by the authorities on the Early Rain Covenant Church.

On 5 October 2018, about 300 people, including veterans, from Qingdao, Shandong, and several other provinces gathered at the Pingdu People's Hall Square in Pingdu City (Qingdao, Shandong) in opposition to the beating up of veterans by authorities early this month. Protesters carried banners, chanted slogans, cordoned off an area, and were supplied with wooden sticks, sledgehammers, fire extinguishers, and putty powder.

On 10 July 2018, 7 families were beaten up by groups sent by the government and property developers during an unannounced forced eviction and property seizure in Xixiao village of Haicheng district, Beihai, Guangxi. The Beihai Government's statement on Weibo reported that two villagers threw stones at law enforcement officers and injured many of them, and that a gun was found in one of the villagers' homes. The government claimed that the properties seized were unauthorized building works. Exact injuries and number of victims unknown.

On 11 July 2018, residents were beaten up by groups sent by the government and property developers during an unannounced forced eviction and property seizure operation in Xixiao village of Haicheng district, Beihai, Guangxi. The Beihai Government's statement on Weibo reported that five villagers attacked law enforcers with knives and metal batons, resulting in 9 injuries, 5 of which were on the law enforcers' side. The government justified that the properties seized were unauthorized building works. More than 30 households were demolished, and 8 residents were hospitalized for injuries including concussions and bone fractures.

On 15 July 2018, a few hundred teachers protested to demand for wage arrears in front of the Wuwei Supervisory Commission in Wuwei county of Wuhu, Anhui. By law, teaching wages must not fall below the wage standard for public servants, which contrasted with the reality of growing wage disparities between the two labour groups.

On 17 July 2018, around 1000-1500 teachers protested to demand for wage arrears at the Municipal People's Government Plaza in Huaibei, Anhui. By law, teaching wages must not fall below the wage standard for public servants, which contrasted with the reality of growing wage disparities between the two labour groups. Police forces were present but with no violent interferences. On the next day, the Anhui's People Government responded to the protest with a welfare and workers protection plan.

On 12 March 2018, 100 to 200 villagers at Yintacun (Fugu, Yulin, Shaanxi) gathered to stop the government from building a road on their land. They had been protesting at the land site for about 2 weeks until 29 March 2018 when police started arresting a dozen of villagers.

On 2 April 2018, between hundreds to thousands retired community teachers gathered at the Heilongjiang provincial education bureau in Nangang District (Harbin, Heilongjiang) to protest against unpaid pension and social insurance. They continued protesting at the government offices until at least 10 April 2018. It was reported that 5 elected representatives of the teachers were taken by the authority on 9 April 2018.

On 2 April 2018, up to 500 workers with pneumoconiosis gathered at the Disease Control Centre in Youxian (Zhuzhou, Hunan) to protest against the authorities delaying the issuance of medical examination files. They had gathered everyday outside of the Centre's office starting from 26 March. Authorities began arresting demonstrators on 2 April 2020. At the time of reporting on 4 April 2018, at least 4 workers who organised the protest had since been detained.

On 1 August 2018, a few thousand residents, protesting against an aluminium oxide development project plan, marched to the Chaoyang People's Government in Shuangta district (Chaoyang, Liaoning). When two protesters were arrested, the protest spread to the Public Security Bureau adjacent to the Government. In the midst of the protest, the city government announced their decision to scrap the project. RFA reported a few thousand people participated, while CRLW put the figure at over 10,000.

On 3 August 2018, as many as 100 migrant workers protested at the Hunchun People's Government in Hunchun city, Jilin to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned coal mining company (Baoshan Meikuang).

On 4 October 2018, 38 petitioners-cum-veterans from Pindu (Qingdao, Shandong) were assaulted by the chief police officer and his team in Dongying prefecture (Shandong) while on their way to petition in Beijing. At least three of them sustained injuries to their leg, shoulder and head respectively. Seventeen veterans were taken away on the day, and one was taken away on 8 Oct. Two months later, it was made known that four of them were detained at a gardening farm in Pingdu, and others were separately detained at Xiguan Primary School and Olympic Sports Centre. Details about their situation unknown.

Around 5 April 2018 (week of), a Tibetan woman was taken away by plain clothes officers from the Domestic Security Bureau while she was passing through Darlag County (Golog, Qinghai) and disappeared thereafter. She was en route to Lhasa from her home in Bola Village, Xiahe, Gansu for a pilgrimage. Her friends and family who were on pilgrimage with her were warned against telling others about her detention. The reason of her arrest was reportedly due to her visits to another Tibetan monk who were detained for protesting activities.

Around 9 August 2018 (as reported), government authorities have demolished seven out of eight mosques in Lianmuqin town, Shanshan county of Xinjiang Uighur Autonomous Region. The remaining mosque is under tight population control and surveillance by law enforcement authorities, creating discomfort for worshippers and deterring them from visiting.

On 1 February 2018, around 100 people gathered outside the Standing Committee of Shaanxi Provincial People's Congress in Xi'an, Shaanxi to demand a refund from a real estate development company in which they had invested.

On 28 January 2018, a Tibetan political activist went missing in Lhasa, Tibet and was believed to be in police custody, likely in connection to a protest the man conducted in front of the Potala Palace in Lhasa calling for the return of the Dalai Lama to Tibet. He had since been held incommunicado until it was reported on 18 April 2019 that he was sentenced to eighteen years in prison, likely around September or October 2018, according to his nephew who resides in India, for releasing a video on social media calling for world peace. His partner was also given a two-year prison sentence for filming the video. He was last traced to a prison in his hometown Sog county (Nagchu prefecture) as of 7 Feb. Both of them were allegedly sentenced without a court trial, and their location remained unknown as of 18 April 2019.

On 12 August 2018, a few hundred villagers protested within and around the village of Yakou in Nanlang, Zhongshan while police forces stood by. Since 23 July, they had been demanding compensation after learning that village officials had secretly sold vast areas of farmlands to the government in 2013. With a population size of 3000, Yankou village is one of the last places in China to follow and implement the renmingongshe people's commune system - which stated that the communes owned management and control rights over rural resources, including land.

On 23 August 2018, parents petitioned at the Hunan Provincial Education Department (Furong district of Changsha) until government officials from their respective villages arrived on scene to convince them to put an end to their protest. They were protesting after losing a lawsuit against the government. Their children suffered during a pneumonia outbreak in August 2017, which reportedly got out of hand due to a government-led information campaign since August 2016 to keep development of the outbreak under secrecy.

On 27 August 2018, several hundred Christians gathered and defended a Three-Self Church in Xingyang county of Zhengzhou prefecture, Henan from an excavator and some black-clad men who attempted to take its cross down. The petitioner had sought to petition for her rights after her former employee demanded money for a road accident involving the petitioner and another driver. She remained detained illegally at the hotel at the time of reporting on 25 February 2018.

On 5 June 2018, the government authorities demolished a Roman Catholic Way of the Cross at the Our Lady of Mount Carmel pilgrimage site in Tianjiajing Village (Anyang City, Henan Province). Officials removed images of Jesus at the site.
