Around 1 January 2018 (beginning of month), a female petitioner from Heze, Shandong was suspected of pharmacological torture during her sentence at Jinan Female Prison (Jinan, Shandong) when the prison informed her family around 17 Jan that she would be transferred for hospital treatment due to the deterioration of her health. It was reported that she developed respiratory and cardiovascular diseases after serving her sentence in prison, but her illness became more severe since her daughter last visited around 17 December 2017.

On 12 June 2018, a retired, disabled soldier was beaten up by 4 police officers at his house in Jiqing Township (Deyang City, Sichuan Province) for planning to attend a court hearing of another retired soldier in Ya'an City. After he was cuffed at his hands and feet, and sent to the Jiqing Township Police Station, police officers beat him again. His whole body was hurt, his face was sprayed with pepper water, and he was sent to the hospital after that. News of the assault spread in the veteran community, and sparked a subsequent protest at the station.

On 13 June 2018, around 402 retired soldiers from different cities and counties gathered at the Jiqing Township Police Station in Jiqingzhen Township (Deyang City, Sichuan Province) demanding justice for the retired disabled soldier who was beaten by the police on 12 June 2018. The township mayor arrived at the scene at night and apologized for the event.
On 14 June 2018, food delivery motorcyclists protested against mobile apps Meituan and Ele.me in Zhejiang Province, opposing drastically cut pay due to increased competition among delivery platforms.
On 14 June 2018, food delivery motorcyclists protested against mobile apps Meituan and Ele.me in Shandong Province, opposing drastically cut pay due to increased competition among delivery platforms.
On 14 June 2018, food delivery motorcyclists protested against mobile apps Meituan and Ele.me in Shaanxi Province, opposing drastically cut pay due to increased competition among delivery platforms.

On 15 June 2018, a female petitioner died after stability maintenance personnel captured her in Wuyi Road Residential District of Qiaodong District (Xingtai City, Hebei Province) to prevent her from staging a planned petition in Beijing. After being intercepted, she demanded to take a breath because she felt chest discomfort. However, the stability maintenance personnel forcibly pushed her onto a car. It was reported that she had a heart attack and lost her consciousness, but the stability maintenance personnel did not perform CPR on her.

On 16 June 2018, around 300 teachers held a sit-in protest at the Susong County Government in Susong County (Anqing City, Anhui Province) to demand wage arrears and one-time bonus to them. Many stability maintenance personnel were at the scene and blocked the entrance of the government building.

On 2 January 2018, more than 500 public primary and secondary school teachers protested on the main streets of Huize County (Qujing, Yunnan), and outside the county government gate for teachers to receive salary pay and increase equal to other civil servants. Multiple demonstrations took place simulteaneously all across Qujing, including a march in Shizong county that was attended by more than 300 teachers, and involved special police and public security forces in attempts to suppress the march.

On 8 January 2018, several thousands of residents marched on the streets of Fusong town (Baishan, Jilin) to protest against the unannounced relocation of Fusong No.1 Secondary School to a developing subdistrict.

On 20 June 2018, between a few hundred and thousand community, substitute and kindergarten teachers from Yulin, Yan'an, Shangluo held a sit-in protest at the Shaanxi Education Department in Yanta District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province) to demand urban pension scheme, career support, retirement compensation and social insurance. Demonstrators carried banners and shouted slogans. Some police pushed and shoved demonstrators and seized their banners. Many teachers were also intercepted by district stability maintenance personnel at the scene and the surrounding area.

On 2 April 2018, hundreds of police and government employed personnel beat up villagers at Shuitian Village (Yanjin county, Zhaotong, Yunan) with electric batons to forcibly take over their farmland to build a road. It was suspected that some of the people wearing police uniforms were local triad members employed by the government. Several villagers were injured, including children. Ten villagers were also arrested by police.

On 11 June 2018, more than 20 workers blocked the entrance of a construction site in Sanmenxia City, Henan Province. The workers hung a banner and 2 life-sized dummies in the scene. The police arrived, removed the dummies, and took away the workers who had created the dummies.

On 17 April 2018, the local government tore down a church connected to the residence of an underground Catholic priest in Hutuo Village (Zhengzhou, Henan) in Catholic Diocese of Luoyang, forcibly evicted the priest, and destroyed the tombstone of the late bishop for the second time. It was a part of a governmental campaign to crack down on underground religious institutions in Henan Province.

On 7 November 2019, four Tibetan monks from the Dza Wonpo Ganden Shedrub Monastery staged a protest in front of the local government building of Dza Wonpo Village, Shiqu County (Garze Tibetan Autonomous Region, Sichuan Province). They called for freedom, human rights, protection of locals' rights, and an end to political campaigns, after local Tibetans were forced to resettle and put up pictures of President Xi by Chinese officials. All four were arrested. One more monk was later taken away by the police on the same day in relation to this protest, while other monk was arrested on 18 November for posting online in support of those arrested.

On 1 April 2018, the local authorities confiscated the properties which belonged to two churches where two underground Catholic priests served in the Catholic Diocese of Luoyang (Henan), forcibly evicted two priests, and forbade them to hold religious gatherings in churches. It was a part of a governmental campaign to crack down on underground religious institutions in Henan Province.

On 17 April 2018, the local authorities confiscated religious objects during a raid on Gaoqiangyintang Catholic Church in Hua County (Anyang, Henan) in Catholic Diocese of Anyang. They also forcibly evicted the staffs, and forbade the renovation of the built houses of the church. It was a part of a governmental campaign to crack down the underground religious institutions in Henan Province.

Around 17 April 2018 (as reported), the local authorities tore down Catholic churches in the Catholic Diocese of Puyang in Puyang City (Henan). It was a part of a governmental campaign to crack down the underground religious institutions in Henan Province.

On 5 June 2018, people hired by the local government demolished 14 Stations of the Cross along the paths of Shengmu Mountain, a Catholic Christian holy mountain in the Catholic Diocese of Anyang, in Yuankang Town (Anyang, Henan) with excavators and pickup trucks. One month ago, the government personnel from the Henan Provincial Government tried to convince the Bishop of the Anyang Diocese to take down the Stations of the Cross.

On 17 July 2018, around 70 people sent by the local government demolished Liangwang Catholic Church in Jinan Catholic Diocese in Liangwang Village (Jinan, Shandong) (event coded at Jinan City) for the reason that the church was within the area for the new real estate development planned by the local government. Three female followers of the church were on duty that day and forcibly taken out from the church by the people who demolished the church, and had their phones were confiscated. All properties of the church were buried under the ruin. Earlier in the year, the Shilihe Catholic Church in the same diocese was also demolished by the local authority.

On 23 July 2018, followers of the Liangwang Catholic Church staged a protest at the demolished church in Liangwang Village (Jinan, Shandong) (event coded at Jinan City) and prayed over the forcible demolition of the church and unfulfilled compensations promised by the local government for the lost church properties and a temporary gathering venue for the church followers. The church was demolished on 17 July 2018 and was the second church to be demolished in Jinan Catholic Diocese in 2018.

On 13 August 2018, more than 170 people sent by the government demolished Qianwang Catholic Church in Jinan Catholic Diocese in Qianwang Village (Jinan, Shandong), destroyed the religious statues inside, and the donation box was missing afterwards. The church was demolished for the reason that it was within the area for the new real estate development plan of the government, and this is the third demolished church in the Jinan Catholic Diocese in 2018. It was reported that the Catholic Diocese had contacted relevant government departments on the demolition and selection of site for the resettlement of the church, but the resettlement plan had yet come to fruition after four years.

On 2 January 2018, more than 200 villagers of Yuanluo village, Xi'an petitioned at the Shaanxi Provincial People's Government in Xincheng district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) and submitted a petition letter with 930 signatures asking for resettlement and compensation after a government-led land reformation project.

On 10 January 2018, a small group of residents continued to demonstrate on the streets of Fusong county (Baishan, Jilin) to protest against the unannounced relocation of Fusong No.1 Secondary School, and stepped up their demands to ask for their relocated county government to be moved back to Fusong. This was after the government already announced the withdrawal of relocation plans, and decision to retain all administrative and teaching staff. Police forces attempted to disperse the crowds, resulting in a confrontation between the two sides. A number of residents were hospitalised.

Around 6 January 2018 (between 3-10 January), a Uyghur female student disappeared after returning to Yili (Ili, Xinjiang) in the midst of studying abroad for her master's degree. On 11 Oct 2016, she had been forcibly admitted to the psychiatric ward of Houfengyan General Hospital in Beibei District before being transferred to Hechuan District. She was forced to take pills and receive daily injections that she reacted to badly.

On 11 January 2018, about ten petitioners gathered in front of the International Convention Center in Hanyang, Wuhan, to express their grievances toward People's Representatives of Hubei. Then the polices were sent to beat and detain five petitioners.

Around 15 April 2018 (month of), a petitioner who was placed under house arrest was beaten up by triad group and drug users hired by the local stability maintenance personnel at his house in Wanzhou District of Chongqing. He was left injured with ruptured eardrums, brain concussion, cervical spine damages and soft tissue damages.

On 18 June 2018, evicted villagers chanted slogans and carried banners in Tao Yu Lu of Zhushan District (Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province) to protest low compensation for the eviction. They also claimed the expropriations that were carried out without proper justification. Protesters had been demonstrating from 15 June.

On 23 August 2018, around 100 private security forces hired by the government attacked residents in Xiayang village, Chengmen town (Cangshan, Fuzhou, Fujian) during an unannounced forced demolition. Elderly and women were among those resisting the demolition, many villagers were injured, including two women who bled and became unconscious.

On 25 October 2018, a farmer from Wuzhou, Jiangxi disappeared after being released from the Ganjiang Prison in Xinjian District (Nanchang, Jiangxi) and his family suspects that he has been put into black jail by the Le'an county government in Anle County. The farmer was sentenced to jail due to his petition over the local government levying his land and was going to be released on 25 October 2018, but the family didn't see him when they went to pick him up, and the jail administration said that the Le'an county law enforcement has took him out of jail 3 days ago.

On 5 September 2018, between dozens to hundreds of police and government employees raided Qiupo Church at Dongwangji Town, Tanghe county (Nanyang, Henan) as part of a fresh campaign to remove crosses from churches. This was one of a few churches targeted by authorities on this day, where authorities were reported to have forcibly removed the cross, cleared out the church, and set fire to bibles and the cross. It was also reported that believers who tried to stop the damage were either arrested or dragged away.

On 4 February 2018, two female residents in Niezhuang in Cigouxiang (Xuchang, Henan) was injured by the forced eviction personnel when the residents try to prevent them from entering their home. The forced eviction was led by the officials from the local County Government and around 30 unidentified people.

Around 26 February 2018, a dissident from Rongchang District, Chongqing was taken away by the police from Rongchang District (Chongqing), and detained in a psychiatric hospital until his release on 15 April 2018. He had previously been summoned to the police station on 26 February 2018 and warned not to breach the firewall on the internet and criticise the government. This was the sixth time he had been taken away to a psychiatric hospital.

On 17 July 2018, around 500 former military officers turned volunteers from Chongqing gathered in front of the Chongqing Civil Affairs Bureau in Yubei district to demand for better social welfare and housing arrangement for veterans. This was as part of a nationwide support of the recent oppression of veteran rights protests.

On 17 October 2018, around 40 Pneumoconiosis patients who used to be miners in a Yiyang county mining company held a demonstration in Yiyang county (Luoyang, Henan) to raise the awareness of Pneumoconiosis as an occupational disease and to encourage the government to take responsibility for the matter.

On 8 May 2018, two people in Wuhan (Hubei) reportedly became unreachable because their friend, a well-known political dissident in China, was about to be tried on the 11 May 2018 in Wuhan. There was no further report about their whereabouts at the time of reporting on 10 May 2018. It was reported that the authorities had illegally controlled a number of people concerned with the case, to prevent them from going to the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court to attend the court case.

On 21 February 2018, a human rights activist was taken away by the police from Xiangtang Village in Pukou District (Nanjing, Jiangsu) and taken to the Zhujiang police station. The human rights activist was visiting a Nanjing dissident living in Xiangtang Village, who had been placed under house arrest for more than a year by the National Security Bureau. While at the police station, the activist was physically and verbally abused. He was later released after being detained for about 24 hours.

On 10 September 2018, about 2000 veterans petitioned for their legal rights at the Department of Civil Affairs of Sichuan Province located in Jinjiang District (Chengdu, Sichuan). During the petition, multiple police forces showed up and clashed with the veterans, both sides pushed and fought the other, and some of the veterans were wounded. Later on the same day, the veterans went on petitioning in front of the Provincial Government of Sichuan province, the police were again at the site and clashed with the veterans with fights and pushes, wounding some of the veterans. The police also used tear gas during the clash.

Around 27 January 2018 (between 23-31 January), a man was administered psychotropic drugs at the Liaocheng No.4 People's Hospital in Dongchangfu district (Liaocheng, Shandong). He had been forcibly admitted and held incommunicado from 23 to 31 Jan by the CPC Secretary and Chief of Yangdian village, Dutang town of Dingtao county. It was reported that he appealed on behalf of his father three times that year, resulting in three forced psychiatric ward admissions.

On 4 December 2018, dozens of rights defenders staged a protest by singing the Chinese national anthem across the street from the Wuhan Government in Jiang'an district (Wuhan, Hubei) over their campaign on the Chinese Constitution Day being intervened by the police.

On 5 September 2018, thousands of demonstrators clashed with hundreds of police at Guanshan boulevard (Hongshan, Wuhan) during a demonstration against the construction of a substation near their community.

On 26 December 2018, a previous petitioner was taken from a hotel near Guanyinsi police station in Huangcun town (Daxing, Beijing) by the police to the Majialou detention centre. When he was having a rest in the hotel after arranging the cremation of his deceased son and dealing with related issues, police officers searched his room and took him to the detention centre for unclear reasons since he had not petitioned in the past two years.

On 28 November 2018, the previously imprisoned university professor and New Democracy Party of China founder was summoned by the Hanzhongmen police station in Gulou district (Nanjing) and held incommunicado. It is suspected that he was detained because he shared his political opinions through Wechat.

On 17 April 2018, a dissident from Rongchang District, Chongqing was taken away by the police from Rongchang District (Chongqing), and detained in a psychiatric hospital for the seventh time. He had yet been released at the time of reporting on 21 May 2018. He had been detained multiple times by the police since 2008 for his commentaries on the internet, which were critical of the Communist Party of China.

On 19 February 2018, three people, one of whom was released from a detention centre on the same day and the other two are her parents, were taken away by police in Pingnan (Ningde, Fujian). Their whereabouts were unknown. This happened on the same day the daughter was released after being held detained for 10 days for disrupting order and refusing to sign a land acquisition paper.

On 17 September 2018, a petitioner was forcibly abducted by local police and authorities when she was about to get on a train at the railway station in Wuxi, Jiangsu. Her whereabouts remained unknown as of 18 September 2018.

On 7 June 2018, a female petitioner, who was placed under house arrest, was attacked by 3 security personnel appointed by the government in the Huang Ni Tou village in the Guangyi Residential District of the Chong'an District, Liangxi District (Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province) when she demanded to leave her house. She was seriously injured as a result of the attack.

Around 5 March 2018 (between 2-9 March), a man was administered psychotropic drugs at the Heze No.3 People's Hospital in Mudan district (Heze, Shandong). He had been forcibly admitted and held incommunicado from 2 to 9 Mar by the CPC Secretary and Chief of Yangdian village, Dutang town of Dingtao county. It was reported that he appealed on behalf of his father three times that year, resulting in three coerced psychiatric ward admissions.

On 25 March 2018, the daughter of a female petitioner, together with a group of petitioners, protested in front of the Jianxin Police Department in Cangshan District (Fuzhou, Fujian) over the physical abuse towards the petitioner from a group of unidentified men when she was detained in the Jianxin Police department and Detention Centre. The protesters held placards and called the police from the Fuzhou Police Department to complain that the male personnel was allowed to enter the female detention room and physically abuse the detainee in the Jianxin Police Department.

On 10 August 2018, several hundred veterans gathered outside the Hunan Provincial Committee in Furong district (Changsha) to demand for the guaranteed protection of veteran rights, and for aided reintegration into the workforce as outlined by army retirement policies. The Provincial Committee Office was heavily guarded by police and minor verbal altercation broke out between the two parties. After police drove them onto the pavements outside, the veterans decided to advocate to pedestrians instead.

On 18 July 2018, as many as 100 teachers protested to demand for wage arrears at the Huaibei City Hall Plaza in the third district of Huaibei, Anhui. By law, teaching wages must not fall below the wage standard for public servants, which contrasted with the reality of growing wage disparities between the two labour groups. Police forces were present but with no violent interferences. On the same day, the Anhui's People Government responded to the protest with a welfare and workers protection plan.

On 17 June 2018, evicted villagers chanted slogans and carried banners in Tao Yu Lu of Zhushan District (Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province) to protest low compensation for the eviction. They also claimed the expropriations that were carried out without proper justification. Protesters demonstrated until 18 June.

On 20 August 2018, at night, several thousand veterans and citizens gathered in Meilu sub-district of Wuchuan city (Zhenjiang, Guangzhou), at the location where a veteran and his wife had been beaten up by personnel from the Urban Administrative and Law Enforcement Bureau (UALEB) earlier that day, to express their solidarity for the couple. The demonstrators surrounded police and UALEB officers and violent clashes ensued, and injured people were reported to have been taken away on stretchers. Authorites sent armoured vehicles to disperse the crowd, while the Vice Mayor of Wuchuan and the Secretary of the UALEB arrived on scene to pacify the situation.
On 31 August 2018, several hundred veterans protested on the streets of Xi'an, Shaanxi to defend their rights.

On 25 August 2018, citizens clashed with the police in Dabuba Village in Yazhou district (Sanya, Hainan), when police came by to investigate why the former had vandalized display boards at a questionnaire activity organized by an agriculture cultivation governing body earlier that day (this was because of a land dispute). Several citizens and policemen on each side were injured, and police cars were damaged to varying degrees.

On 20 August 2018, Urban Administrative and Law Enforcement Bureau (UALEB) personnel tried to confiscate the goods of and shut down a store operated by a veteran and his wife in Meilu sub-district of Wuchuan city (Zhenjiang, Guangzhou) on the basis that the goods were blocking the streets. The officials beat up the owners when the latter resisted, and the wife was beaten unconscious. The violent act led to a massive civil commotion later that same night. This incident is linked to tensions between veterans and authorities that intensified in June 2018.

On 18 October 2018, a group of Tibetan nomads staged a sit-in protest in front of the local government offices in Nyinpa (Niba) Township in Chone county (Gannan, Gansu) and demaned the unpaid compensation owed to them by the local government.

Around 4 February 2018 (between 1 - 8 February), the local Religious Affairs Bureau forcibly closed down more than 14 house churches in Huiji District (Zhengzhou, Henan). It was reported that two other house churches with more than 500 believers in another district of the same city were shut down during the same period. This was part of a campaign to suppress religious activities in Henan.

Around 15 February 2018 (month of), an Uyghur student was taken to a re-education camp in Xinjiang and interrogated under abusive conditions for multiple days with hands and feet tied to a chair for up to nine hours daily. He was studying international relations at Kazakhstan when the police from Turpan called him threatening trouble to his family if he didn't return immediately.

On 9 September 2018, a group of workers and students protested at Shaoshan city (Xiangtan, Hunan) in support of the workers' movement in Shenzhen, and were arrested by local police during their protest.

On 4 October 2018, more than 1000 veterans demonstrated in Pingdu city (Qingdao, Shandong), stating that they had not been adequately compensated for their services. Demonstrators reportedly attacked the police with fire extinguishers and rods. Across five days from 30 September to 4 October, a total of 34 people were reportedly injured. Online reports anticipated that 3000 veterans from outside of Shandong would come to Pingdu to show their support. The city government responded that many veterans faked their injuries.

On 10 January 2019, 5 workers climbed on the top of a building with banners in Jinan, Shandong and demanded for wages owed to them by a construction company.

On 15 January 2018, about 100 victims of capital fraud protested at the Xi'an Public Security Bureau in Lianhu District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to demand for justice following an investment fraud that occurred more than two years ago.

On 8 January 2018, more than 1000 labourers and low-insurance staff hired by the residential districts (subdistricts) gathered at the Changsha City People's Government in Yuelu District (Changsha, Hunan) to protest about labour issues, relating to their status, income, workload and benefits. The government employed police forces to suppress the protest scene.

On 5 January 2018, more than 150 tenants protested in East Yulanding, Miqin Road in Baoqiao district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) against two years of unstable, temporary electricity, water and heating supply amidst a winter season with heavy snow. After their property developer stated that utilities would not be available before 8 Feb, the tenants took to the streets and stood at the roundabout at Shijia Street of Dong'erwan. They held banners, and asked to be heard by the government.

On 1 May 2018, nearly 100 crane operators gathered with a large banner in Anhui Province to protest against low salaries and they threatened to not return to work until employers agreed to increase payment. This is a part of a nation-wide strike among crane operators from several provinces to demand for better payment.

On 19 May 2018, a man was reportedly assaulted by the police after being taken away to the Jimazhuang Police Station in Xihu District (Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province). It was reported that he was dragged into the police car by three plainclothes officers, while he was visiting a prostitute. He was pronounced dead after being detained for one hour at the police station, leading his family members and netizens to believe that he had been abused during his short detention at the station. The police did not deny the death of the man, but did not provide reasons to the cause of the man's death.

On 11 April 2018, it was reported that former students from 14 villages in Chengduo County (also known as Chindu County) in Yushu (Qinghai Province) who have become monks and nuns, were forced to receive military training. Compulsorily recruited local students were warned from refusing participation and threaten that their family members will not be allowed to dig cordyceps and will be subject to economic punishment.

On 31 January 2018, more than 100 people hired by a demolition company forcibly demolished villagers homes in Miaohu Village, Hancheng, Shaanxi in the early hours of the morning. These homes had been marked for demolition by the local government for a development project.

On 28 March 2018, several dozen people were injured during a clash with Liuzhou authorities during the forced eviction in Caiyuantun in Liunan (Liuzhou, Guangxi). Around 60 villagers used wooden boxes and cupboards to set up two road blocks, threw bricks at law enforcement officials, and attacked with wooden sticks, metal shovels and sledgehammers. The police used truncheons and shields to attack the rioters resisting the eviction, and four people were also detained. Among those injured, 17 of them were law enforcement officials, 4 of which were hospitalised; there were at least 4 rioters who sustained scratches, and 1 had reportedly been hospitalised for a broken leg. Online rumours said that one person died, but this has yet to be verified.

On 10 January 2018, about ten petitioners gathered in front of the International Convention Center in Hanyang, Wuhan, to express their grievances toward People's Representatives of Hubei. No violent actions were reported during the protest.

On 24 May 2018, nearly 20 representatives of herdsmen across Inner Mongolia petitioned at the Letters and Calls Bureau in Xincheng District (Hohhot City, Inner Mongolia), to appeal against the corruption of local officials, and to demand for the crop and pasture subsidies owed to them after the pastures owned by them were destroyed for various construction projects by the government.

Around 5 December 2018 (as reported), a private Arabic language school in Kongtong district (Pingliang, Gansu) was shut down by local authorities after the Gansu government ordered to shut down local private schools with a religious undertone.

Around 15 April 2018 (month of), an ethnic Kazakh artist from Ili Prefecture, Xinjiang was sent to a 'political study concentration camp' without any reason provided. It was reported that she is being held in Hoboksar County (Tacheng, Xinjiang), but her exact location is unknown and her family has not been able to visit her since. On 4 January 2019, it was reported that she was sentenced to three years' imprisonment in a secret trial.

On 6 January 2018, about 1000 workers gathered in front of the People's Government of Changsha City located in Yuelu District (Changsha, Hunan) to protest low compensation of basic life allowance. Protesters then were dispersed by the police.

Around 8 January 2018 (as reported), about 300 Christians of a Catholic church in Xi'an gathered in front of the government of Huyi District (Xi'an. Shaanxi) to demonstrate against the illegal demolition of their church by the authorities about 10 days ago.

On 27 February 2018, a female petitioner was intercepted and beaten by the Lanmu village party secretary and his associate at Nanchang, Jiangxi Province. She was preparing to take the train the next day with three other female petitioners from Nanchang to travel to Beijing to petition. The petitioner suffered severe injuries after being hit with a wine bottle in the head.

On 11 November 2018, Tibetan residents in Se Tsang township in Chone county (Gansu) staged a protest over the government's plan to divert fresh drinking water from a local source to a neighboring area. The police was present and threatened to arrest the protesters.

On 28 May 2018, some retired soldiers surrounded the Zhuzhou People's Government in Tianyuan District (Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province), opposing to the attack and humiliation against 2 veteran fellows that happened a few days ago. They chanted slogans loudly and held a banner that read 'Restore dignity to veterans, Impose heavy penalty for the attacker'.

On 4 June 2018, around 200 people joined an annual candlelight vigil organised by the Macau Union for Democratic Development in Senado Square in Macao, marking the 29th anniversary of the Tiananmen demonstrations on 4 June 1989.

On 6 August 2018, three hundred to four hundred veterans were arrested by police forces while protesting in front of the Jinan People's Government in Jinan, Shandong to demand for better welfare previously promised. They were led onto the buses and detained at local schools and sports stadiums, before some were released gradually within the same day.

On 24 August 2018, more than 20 Guangdong police forces arrested at least eight editors and staff of Red Reference and Epoch Pioneer at their offices in Suzhuang, Fangshan district of Beijing, after both Maoist website organisations were involved in the Jiashi workers unionization labour movement. Their whereabouts are unknown. During the search, the police confiscated books, computers and broke furniture, and sealed off the premise.

On 4 May 2018, around 20 Mongolian herdsmen from Urad Middle Banner went to the Urad Middle Banner People's Government in Hailiutu Town (Urad Middle Banner, Bayannur, Inner Mongolia) to petition and demand superior government's intervention because local authorities had seized their pasture and leased it to foreign mining companies, causing environmental damages to the land.

Arrests: Around 15 November 2018 (month of), large numbers of police officials broke into the homes of villagers of Sanhongqicun in Shunde, Foshan late in the night to arrest them. This was in retaliation to the villagers' large-scale protest against the unauthorised selling of land by village officials.

On 26 March 2018, up to 500 miners who have Pneumoconiosis staged a sit-in protest outside the Youxian Disease Prevention and Control Centre (Zhuzhou, Hunan) over the delayed release of their health check documents which were important for them to apply for compensation. It was reported that they had gathered everyday outside of the Centre's office starting from 26 March. Authorities began arresting demonstrators on 2 April 2020.

On 9 August 2018, Xingtan government authorities forcibly confiscated and demolished land belonging to fishers and villagers in Gaozhan village, Xingtan town of Shunde district (Foshan city), Guangdong taking out all the fish being cultivated and bulldozing into the ponds.

Around 4 August 2018 (week of), several dozens of investors and ex-employees of financial services conglomerate HNA protested at its Hainan headquarters (Longhua district, Haikou) after financing fraud, and demanded for a return of their initial principal investment.

On 23 May 2018, hundreds of villagers gathered at Mapeng Village (Yulin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region) to protest against the plan of rare earth mining activities near their water source. Police oppressed the protest by beating the protesters and arrested 16 people. A few people had to be sent to a hospital.

On 11 November 2018, staff from Religious Affairs Bureau and policemen broke into the gathering of a family church in Huozhou (Linfen, Shanxi), and shut it down for exceeding the legally permitted size of gatherings.

On 1 May 2018, nearly 80 crane operators in Yongzhou city (Hunan) went on strike and held a large banner in public to protest against low salaries of crane operators as a profession. They threatened to not return to work until their salaries were increased. It was reported that more people would join the strike.

On 18 January 2018, a group of police officers rushed into a Christian church in Zhengzhou, Henan. They accused the church of not having legal documents. Polices dispersed church members and closed down the church venue. Police also smashed up tables, speakers, and religious items in the church.

On 15 April 2018, a petitioner was forcibly taken to detention by police while at the Beijing International Film Festival in Huairou District, Beijing. On 6 May 2018, a Han Chinese person drove into Tibetan farmers after a string of quarrels and fights in Deqing village of Duilongdeqing district of Lhasa, resulting in several collisions and at least 3 hospitalised with severe injuries. The farmers also reported ethnic discrimination in the handling of this case, where village authorities did not hold the driver accountable for his attacks.

On 22 April 2018, more than a dozen petitioners were met by local officials and security guards at the Cangshan International Convention and Exhibition Center (Cangshan District, Fuzhou). Several other petitioners at the scene were also reported to have been arrested and threatened by local officials and security guards.

On 30 April 2018, more than 1,000 residents from Gaoling Town (Susong, Anqing, Anhui) blocked roads at the town government building to protest against the government's plan to build a local waste incineration plant that was too near the residential area and could also possibly affect a local river. They blocked roads for 3 days.

On 3 April 2018, dozens of villagers gathered outside the town government in Beijiao Town (Shunde, Foshan, Guangdong) demanding the dismissal of village officials due to lack of trust related to private sales of land and other corruption. Authorities sent police to disperse the villagers. 6-7 people were arrested and some were sent to administrative detention for five days. Among the arrested, a 70-year-old woman who was handcuffed to her legs later died of excessive fright at her home. It was suspected by her family that the woman was tortured during detention but this was not confirmed.

On 1 December 2018, more than 10,000 residents from Teng'ao town, Haicheng city, Liaoning Province and neighbouring townships took to the streets to protest against the construction of a large waste incineration plant close to their homes. Almost 3,000 police were deployed to suppress the protest. They were armed with shields and batons and beat up protestors indiscriminately.

On 9 November 2018, around 1000 unemployed workers of Bo'en Guangxue factory and their families staged a protest in front of the factory in Huiyang district (Huizhou, Guangdong) over the layoff by the factory caused by the reduction of orders from Apple. During the four-day protest, the armed police was allegedly mobilised at least once to disperse them. They continued protesting until 12 November 2018.

On 10 October 2019, more than 200 students at the Tsuen Wan Public Ho Chuen Yiu Memorial College (New Territories, Hong Kong) came to school wearing black clothes to protest against the police's abuse of force in the recent crackdowns of the pro-democracy demonstrations. The event was also meant in particular to support a boy from the college that was shot by the police during a demonstration earlier this month.

On 14 October 2019, nearly 200 students at the Hon Wah College, Eastern District (Hong Kong) formed a human chain outside of the school in the morning to protest against the mask ban. A student from the college was rebuked earlier on the 9 October because he wore a face mask to school.

On 20 August 2019, about 50 anti-ELAB masked protesters in full gear participated in a silent protest at Tuen Mun MTR station in Tuen Mun against deteriorating safety conditions in Hong Kong caused by police's excessive use of force against protesters.

On 20 November 2019, nearly 100 people gathered at Taikoo Garden in Eastern District, Hong Kong to join a 'lunch with you' rally protesting for the Five Demands. They also marched around the park shortly before leaving. During the protest, there was a person who shouted 'fake democracy' and 'Hong Kong is part of the Greater Bay Area'. He was accompanied to leave by the security guards. There was police car standing by. No further violence or police engagement was reported on this occasion.

On 21 June 2019, more than 1000 people joined a memorial ceremony of an anti-ELAB protester who committed suicide by jumping off a building last week in Admiralty (Central and Western district, Hong Kong). Before the ceremony, volunteers read the final wish of the protester, which included getting rid of the name 'rioter', release the arrestees and Chief Executive to step down.

On 25 September 2019, almost 100 students and people joined a protest at the Chinese University of Hong Kong in Sha Tin, Hong Kong in support of two Uyghur scholars who were to be sentenced to death soon.

On 12 September 2019, students from many schools in Tuen Mun formed a 3.5-km long human chain along Tuen Mun River to pressure the government to respond to people's five political demands. They shouted slogans.

On 26 September 2019, more than 200 students from 8 secondary schools joined a rally at the Oxford Road Playground in Kowloon City to ask for the realisation for the Five Demands. They displayed banners and sang protest songs.

On 12 September 2019, a few hundred students and alumni from at least nine schools formed a human chain in the Eastern district of Hong Kong stretching from Fortress Hill to Causeway Way to call for the realisation of the five demands. They sang songs and shouted slogans.

On 16 December 2019, dozens of protesters gathered around IFC Mall in Central and Western District (Hong Kong) to call for the fulfilment of the five demands. They chanted slogans and wrote Christmas cards to those arrested during the anti-ELAB movement.

On 9 June 2020, about 50 demonstrators held a 'Lunch with You' rally at Taikoo Shing in Eastern District (Hong Kong). They sang the anti-ELAB protest anthem 'Glory to Hong Kong' and chanted slogans calling 'Hongkongers, build our nation'. This was one of the 'Lunch with You' rally held on the same day in 7 districts across Hong Kong, in commemoration of the first anniversary of the first major anti-ELAB rally held on 9 June 2019, where 1.03 million people reportedly participated in the march.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 11 October 2019, nearly 200 residents at the Greenwood Terrace Car Park, Eastern District (Hong Kong) gathered at the estate management to demand limited police access into the housing complex after police had raided the complex and arrested people earlier during the day. On 22 September 2019, more than 100 anti-ELAB demonstrators gathered at a shopping mall in Nam Cheong near Sham Shui Po to attempt to disturb operation of pro-government shops and businesses. Inside the shopping mall in Nam Cheong, protesters sat in and sang protest songs and shouted slogans. On 2 October 2019, more than 100 students at the Ying Wa College (Sham Shui Po) gathered at the sports ground to sing 'Glory to Hong Kong'. This is part of a strike by several hundred students from several colleges in Hong Kong to support the anti-ELAB demonstrations that took place a day ago.

On 28 December 2020, five members of The Alliance (including a former legislator) marched to and petitioned at the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Western district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western) for the release of a citizen journalist, a human rights lawyer, and 12 fugitives arrested in mainland China while attempting to flee for Taiwan (all facing charges related to their involvement in the anti-ELAB movement).

On 18 February 2018, ahead of the announcement of the Hong Kong Budget 2018/19, around 20 members of the Democratic Party Hong Kong marched to the government headquarters in Admiralty (Central and Western district, Hong Kong) to call on the government to make good use of the financial reserve, and redistribute the huge surplus to the people of Hong Kong. On the same day, members of the DAB also protested at the government headquarters to demand the government to increase the medical subsidy for the seniors and to implement a series of measures to improve people's livelihood

On 15 March 2018, around 30 taxis staged a protest outside the Central Government Complex in Central District (Hong Kong) over the operation of uber and other car-sharing services which caused damage to taxi drivers' income. the taxis drivers held protest signs, as well as covered their taxi with protest signs and tied black ribbons to the tail of their taxis, circled with slow speed outside the Government Complex, and handed petition letter to the representatives from the Transport and Housing Bureau.

On 23 May 2020, 6 unidentified persons assaulted 3 people (2 men and 1 woman) at a 'Lennon Wall' at the North District Town Hall in North District (Hong Kong). It was reported that the group of 3 people confronted the other group of 6 as they were putting up posters on the Lennon Wall. Both groups got into an altercation due to political differences, with some pushing and shoving, before the group of 6 people attacked the other group with umbrellas and bicycles. They escaped after the assault. The group of 3 sustained injuries in their shoulders and arms.

On 27 September 2019, more than 300 students from at least 10 schools attended a sit-in gathering at Festival Walk in Kowloon Tong near Kowloon City, Hong Kong to support the Five Demands Movement and call on students to participate in the class boycott on 30 September. They sang protest songs and chanted slogans such as 'Five Demands, not one less'.

On 27 December 2018, a member of the Tseung Kwan O faction of the Sun Yee On Triad was ambushed and attacked by three masked attackers carrying knives. The victim suffered injuries to his hands, feet and abdomen. The attackers were believed to have set fire to their car after escaping and driving away for about ten minutes. 1 man was subsequently arrested in relation to the incident. The attack was reported to be part of an intra-triad turf war between two factions of the Sun Yee On Triad.

On 14 September 2018, nearly 100 supporters of the police gathered outside the High Court of Hong Kong located in Central and Western District to express their support for a prosecuted police officer and the police force, as well as protesting against the guilty sentence of the police. They shouted slogans during the demonstration.

On 7 June 2020, more than 10 members of the League of Social Democrats and several foreigners demonstrated outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Central and Western District (Hong Kong), to protest against police brutality and racial discrimination in the United States, following the death of George Floyd. They held placards, kneeled on one knee in solidarity with the events in the United States. The group also criticised police brutality in Hong Kong.

On 1 June 2020, more than 70 people held a 'Lunch with You' rally at Landmark in Central and Western District (Hong Kong), to demonstrate against the national security law which had been approved by the Chinese central government last week. They sang 'Glory to Hong Kong' and chanted slogans calling for the five demands, as well as for Hong Kong independence. Some people waved the old British colonial flag.

On 13 May 2019, 950 people carrying their pets participated in the second march this month organised by an animal protection group, Love Animals, No Animal Abuse, in the Central and Western District of Hong Kong. Protesters held banners and shouted slogansto protest against culling to control stray animals. The march responded to the 3-month public consultation on Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Ordinance launched by the government.

On 31 March 2019, nearly 100 residents held a rally initiated by the Democratic Party in Sun Tin Wai Estate, Sha Tin District (Hong Kong), to protest against the increase in rent proposed by Foshan Sunlink Group Company Limited, which owned the shopping mall in the estate. They claimed small business holders had been pushed out of the shopping mall under the new management, and the proposed increase in rent would only forced the only supermarket in the estate to shut.

On 1 October 2018, around 30 people from Student Independence Union and Hong Kong National Front gathered outside Southorn Playground (Hong Kong) and held demonstration to advocate the independence of Hong Kong.

On 25 June 2019, six members from the Labour Party Hong Kong (including a district councillor) protested at the Adventist Hospital in Tsuen Wan (Hong Kong) to demand an official apology from the hospital regarding the case where the hospital reported the whereabouts of an injured protester to the police. On 22 February 2019, representatives from the City University of Hong Kong Staff Association and the HKCTU demonstrated in front of the 'democracy wall' at City University of Hong Kong in Kowloon City District (Hong Kong). On 24 June 2018, almost 100 people and the Yuen Long district councillor participated in a rally organised by a LJL lawmaker in Yuen Long District of Hong Kong to oppose plans for a HK$1.7 billion footbridge in the area. Protesters chanted slogans during the rally.

On 24 June 2019, at least three pro-government groups, and the Hong Kong Civil Servants General Union, Government Employees Association, Chinese Academy of Governance Hong Kong Alumni Association gathered at the Police Headquarters in Wan Chai (Hong Kong) to show support for the Hong Kong police force by sending refreshments for them as gifts. Some groups shouted slogans and sent thank-you letters to the police.

On 20 September 2019, more than 100 students from at least nine secondary schools in Tsuen Wan formed a human chain in Tsuen Wan in support of the Five Demands Movement. They shouted slogans such as 'liberate Hong Kong, revolutions of our time' and 'five demands, not one less' and sang songs.

On 27 January 2020, members of LSD, HKCTU and Hong Kong Labour Party, as well as several Legco members of pro-democracy parties demonstrated with banners at the Government House located in Central, Hong Kong to demand for the closure of all checkpoints between Hong Kong and Mainland China to stop Mainland tourists from coming in and spreading the novel coronavirus pandemic.

On 11 January 2019, members of DAB and NTAS petitioned at the Government Headquarters in Central, Hong Kong to speak against the HKSAR government's decision of forcibly binding the pension reform plan with the budget plan and pass it without consulting the public.
On 3 June 2018, car owners of Hing Tung Estate launched a protest at their residential area located in Eastern, Hong Kong to oppose the property management's decision of raising parking fee.

On 20 July 2019, some citizens marched to the New City Plaza mall in Sha Tin, Hong Kong to protest the mall's management for calling police forces into the mall to arrest protesters during the 14 July demonstration in the mall.

On 13 November 2019, some senior citizens protested at British Consulate General and U.S. Consulate General in Central, Hong Kong to protest Hong Kong police's excessive use of force during the anti-ELAB movement.

On 5 June 2020, between dozens and about 50 people held a 'Lunch with You' rally at IFC mall in Central and Western District (Hong Kong). They chanted slogans, held banners with slogans for 'Hong Kong Independence' and 'Liberate Hong Kong, revolution of our times', and also sang the anti-ELAB protest anthem 'Glory to Hong Kong'. It was reported that the police were on alert outside the mall but did not intervene.

On 24 March 2019, police deputies stormed into a Protestant church in Haidian District (Beijing), banned it, and shut it down because it was a 'privately-established meeting venue'. All church goers who were attending a gathering there were taken away by police for investigation. Church belongings were confiscated. This happened a day after Beijing Municipal Government announced the decision to shut down house churches in Beijing, which is part of an ongoing campaign to crack down on house churches in China.

On 30 April 2018, around 30 people from Justice and Peace Commission of the Hong Kong Catholic Diocese, Christians For Hong Kong Society, Hong Kong Christian Fellowship of Social Concern, and Hong Kong Christian Institute staged a protest outside the Hong Kong Liaison Office in Central and Western District (Hong Kong) over the government of Mainland China suppressing religious freedom and cracking down religious institutions. Protesters held banners and a wooden cross circling around the Liaison Office. Earlier, a joint statement condemning the religious freedom suppression from the Mainland China government was drafted which was intended to send to various foreign embassies in Hong Kong, foreign media outlets, and international human rights organizations.

Arrests: On 21 April 2019, around 60 petitioners from Shanghai who were on their way to petition in Beijing were besieged by police at Beijing South Railway Station in Fengtai district (Beijing), most of which were arrested. This took place before the Belt and Road Forum which was due to commence in Beijing on 25 April 2019.

On 9 September 2018, the Bureau of Civil Affairs of Beijing Chaoyang District closed down Zion Church in Chaoyang District (Beijing), and released official announcement to outlaw the house church, and 20 to 30 vehicles including fire engines and ambulances were deployed. Evicted church followers were transferred to a hotel. The priest of the church was taken into custody by the personnel from several governmental departments, and four followers of the church were taken into the bus used to carry the evicted followers.

Around 28 December 2018 (as reported), up to 100 construction workers staged a protest at the China Railway Museum in Chaoyang District (Beijing) over wage arrears owed by the museum. The protesters held placards during the protest.

On 23 March 2019, almost 300 food delivery drivers went on strike and staged a sit-in protest in Haidian District (Beijing Municipality) in opposition to a reduction in the number of orders they were receiving.
As reported on 10 October 2019, nearly 100 workers at a Sino-Japanese factory in Beijing (Chaoyang District) gathered at the factory's location to demand for compensations as the factory was closed.
As reported on 27 May 2019, as many as 100 employees protested in Haidian District of Beijing City to demand for wage arrears owed to them by an educational company.

Around 30 April 2018 (as reported), at least 3 employees of a technology company protested in Haidian District, Beijing, demanding an owed three-months wage arrear and unpaid social insurance. It was reported that employees got beaten by people from the company.
On 9 October 2019, 100 to 200 employees of the Hanergy corporation gathered at the headquarters in Chaoyang district (Beijing) to protest against unpaid wages.

Around 21 May 2018 (as reported), up to 100 employees held a sit-in protest in the central business district in Chaoyang District (Beijing), against wage arrears owed to them by an engineering company.
Around 16 August 2018 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Chaoyang, Beijing to demand for wage arrears owed by a real estate developer (Sihai Fangdican) since 2016.

As reported on 23 December 2019, as many as 100 workers protested in Chaoyang District, Beijing to demand more than 10 million RMB worth of wage arrears owed to more than 300 of them by a construction project.
On 2 July 2018, between 1-100 workers protested over wage arrears owed by a private interior decoration company on Fulite Commercial Street in Xicheng district, Beijing municipality.
Around 28 November 2019 (as reported), at least 3 workers gathered in front of a restaurant in Haidian District (Beijing) to demand wage arrears owed by the restaurant.
On 2 February 2018, fewer than 100 workers protested in Qinghe, Haidian (Beijing) in response to unpaid wages.
Around 13 February 2018 (as reported), less than 100 workers protested in Chaoyang District (Beijing) against unpaid wages owed by a food services company.
On 21 December 2020, more than 10 workers protested at the Beijing Books Building in Xicheng district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing-Xicheng) to demand for wage arrears.

On 5 December 2018, up to 100 workers of Chuizi Technology company staged a protest in front of the company's headquarters in Chaoyang district (Beijing) over wage arrears owed by the company. The protesters held banners.

As reported on 15 July 2019, as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Dongcheng district, Beijing to demand for unpaid compensation and salary owed to them by a battery company. Workers blocked the entrance of the factory, roads and bridges.

As reported on 4 November 2019, nearly 30 employees from an agriculture company gathered at the company headquarters in Chaoyang District (Beijing) to demand wage arrears owed by the company. They held two large banners outside of the office building.

Around 2 May 2018 (as reported), at least 30 employees and commercial agents of a technology company held large banners in front of the company offices in Haidian District, Beijing, demanding wage arrears and unpaid social insurance owed by the company.
As reported on 11 July 2019, as many as 100 workers staged a sit-in protest in Fengtai, Beijing to demand for wage arrears owed to them by CCCC Tunnel Engineering Co.,Ltd
As reported on 25 July 2019, as many as 100 workers staged a protest in Dongcheng, Beijing against wage arrears owned to 75 workers by a jewelry shop.

As reported on 8 May 2019, as many as 100 retrenched employees of a US-based software company protested against the compensation plan in front of their office building in Haidian district of Beijing City. It was reported that around 900 employees were laid off because of the organization being reorganized.

On 25 October 2019, 30-50 workers that suffer from pneumoconiosis disease from Ziyang county in Shaanxi Province went to petition in Haidian District (Beijing) to demand for a solution for their cases and protest against officials' crackdown on their previous petitions.

On 15 May 2020, at least 8 members of the HKFTU petitioned at the government headquarters in Central and Western District (Hong Kong), urging the government to close the loopholes in the Employment Support Scheme (ESS). They called on the government to consider the unique nature of each industry, to accept other forms other than Mandatory Provident Fund records, such tax bills or employment contracts for the application of financial support, to strengthen the coverage under the ESS of employees aged 65 and above.

On 12 May 2020, two women's rights groups petitioned at the Equal Opportunities Commission in Southern District (Hong Kong), to express their dissatisfaction and condemn the recent broadcast of a TV programme, where two female police officers were subjected to sexual harassment and mocked with obscene language. They called on the Commission to follow up on the incident.

On 2 May 2019, DAB lawmakers, district councillors and residents from Kwun Tong District protested at the government headquarters in the Central and Western District of Hong Kong. They called the government to investigate the construction flaws of the East Kowloon Cultural Centre and hold the accountability of the construction firm, Leighton.

On 8 March 2018, a female petitioner was arrested by two policemen from Fuyou street near the Zhongnanhai in Xicheng District (Beijing) when she was about to mail petition documents. She was then detained in the Beijing Jiujingzhuang Jieji Service Centre (a black jail) in Fengtai District (Beijing). No further report on this event.

On 7 July 2019, more than 100 petitioners gathered at the Supreme People's Court in Dongcheng, Beijing to sue the National Public Complaints and Proposals Adminstration for corruption and frauds. They could not submit the statement in the end.

On 5 March 2018, a petitioner from Kangle Town, Chongqing was taken away by unidentified persons from Yindi Home Land in Fengtai District (Beijing) and sent to a black jail in Beijing Gaojiachang room 46-3.

On 26 April 2019, 3 female petitioners from Caidian District of Wuhan City were kidnapped by government officers of the Wuhan City People's Government Beijing Office outside the Ministry of Agriculture in Chaoyang District of Beijing after they submitted petitions. They were sent back to Wuhan by cars and held incommunicado. It was part of a campaign by the local police to silence dissent before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation which held in Beijing on April 25-27.

On 1 March 2018, two petitioners, who were also brothers, were taken away by private security forces hired by a government official from Jiujingzhuang in Fengtai District (Beijing). On 1 March 2018, two female petitoners were taken from the KFC Youanmen Branch in Fengtai District (Beijing) by the chief police officer of the Henan Xuchang Xiangcheng County Cigouxiang Police Department when they were on their way to petition over forced eviction to the delegates of the National People's Congress, and they were kept in the Beijing-based Office of the Henan Government for several days.

On 12 September 2019, a female petitioner was taken to a police office in Xicheng District (Beijing) by the police after she delivered her petition to the central government. Then, she was sent to be detained in Majialou 'black jail' in Beijing for an unreported amount of time before being transferred back to Shanghai, where she was subsequently detained for 15 days in prison.

On 6 March 2019, officers claiming to work for the State Bureau for Letters and Calls intercepted and kidnapped two female petitioners from Chengjiang subdistrict of Jiangyin, Jiangsu while they were lining up at the State Bureau in Chaoyang district (Beijing). They took their identity cards and cell devices. On 7 Mar, liaison public security officers took them back the Jiangyin, where one of them fled upon arrival at Changzhou North train station. The other was forced onto the next train, and was later seen taken away by a dozen special police from the petitioning bureau. She continued to be incommunicado as of 11 Mar.

On 26 August 2019, a petitioner from Wuxue, Hubei was taken away by local security officers outside the National Letters and Calls Bureau in Xicheng, Beijing. He was not able to be contacted thereafter and is suspected to have been kidnapped.

On 22 August 2019, 11 protesters protested at the Ministry of Water Resources National Environmental Protection Bureau in Xicheng, Beijing to demand for social security compensation owed to them by the Tuokou hydroelectric station in Huaihua, Hunan. Personnel from the Bureau denied any responsibility in this matter.

On 29 November 2018, a petitioner was arrested and taken to the Tiananmen police station after he was stopped for a security check while passing by Tiananmen in Dongcheng district (Beijing). His wife suspected that he was held in Majialou Detention Centre.

On 22 May 2019, a female petitioner from Rudong, Jiangsu was abducted by police from a hotel in Xicheng (Beijing) and put into a black jail in Majialou, Fengtai, Beijing. She was sent back to Rudong, Jiangsu the next day.

On 19 March 2018, a couple from Shanghai Zhabei District, who were petitioning about force eviction at Public Complaints and Proposals Reception of the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau in Dongcheng District (Beijing), went incommunicado after they were intercepted and taken by a group of unidentified people. When they were standing in line at the reception and waiting to petition, the interceptors were trying to take the husband and failed, but a group of unidentified people intercepted them in a Hutong around the reception when the couple went to buy lunch.
On 14 March 2019, a female petitioner was stopped at Lixue Hutong in Xicheng District, Beijing by the police and taken away. Her whereabouts were unknown.
On 15 March 2019, a Shanghaiese petitioner went incommunicado after petitioning at the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development in Haidian district (Beijing).

On 14 March 2019, a woman from Yangpu District, Shanghai was forcibly abducted by police officers (including plainclothes officers) on orders of the Yangpu District Letters and Calls Bureau when she was submitting a complaint at the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development in Haidian District, Beijing. It was reported that six police officers and plainclothes police beat her up, slapped her and sat on her. She was later sent back on the train to Shanghai. Details of her injuries were not confirmed.

On 1 March 2018, three female petitioners from Wuhan Jianrong Village went incommunicado after they were taken by the police officers when they passed by Tiananmen Square in Dongcheng District (Beijing) on their way to petition at the National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration.

On 8 March 2019, two people from Shuangliu district, Chengdu were delivering mail at Lixue Hutong in Xicheng district (Beijing) when they were stopped by the local police and taken to Fuyou Street police station. Three hours later, several unidentified men drove away one of the detainees by car, and the situation of the other detainee remained unknown.

On 5 March 2018, a female petitioner was taken away from the B Exit of Caofang Underground Station in Chaoyang District (Beijing) and sent to a black jail in Beijing Gaojiachang room 46-3 by officers from Chongqing Yubei District Police Department and the local Stability Maintenance Bureau.

On 28 October 2020, a female petitioner from Shanghai was intercepted in Dongjiaominxiang Police Station in Dongcheng District (Beijing) by police officers and escorted back to Shanghai by train on the same day. She was expected to arrive at Hongqiao Station before midnight, but remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 2 Nov 2020 (location coded as Beijing-Dongcheng).

They forcibly repatriated him to Heilongjiang province by car, and illegally restrained him to a room in a public bathhouse for 15 days on the grounds of 'coronavirus quarantine.' After 15 days on 11 June, a police officer instead informed the victim that he would be detained for 'a case he filed for in Beijing.' He was still detained at the time of reporting on 29 Oct 2020.

On 24 May 2020, two female petitioners from Wuxi, Jiangsu were forcibly taken away from Tiananmen Square in Dongcheng District (Beijing) by Beijing police. They were taken to the police station, before being transferred to a hotel and detained by officials from the Beijing Liaison Office of Jiangsu Province.

On 22 May 2020, a woman from Chongqing was forcibly taken away from a police station at Tiananmen Square in Dongcheng District (Beijing), by a person claiming to be from the Beijing Liaison Office of Chongqing Provincial Government (although the person did not produce documents to prove this). She was subsequently taken to Gaojiachang 'black jail'. After being tested negative for COVID-19, she was repatriated to her hometown in Liangping District, Chongqing.

On 20 December 2019, a petitioner from Rugao, Jiangxi was taken away by police forces in Tiananmen (Dongcheng, Beijing) after he had submitted litigation documents to the central government. He was sent back to Rugao and then locked up in a hotel room.

On 18 December 2019, two activists from Chongqing City were taken away to a police station from Dongcheng District, Beijing and detained for no reason. After being detained for nearly 8 hours, both of them were taken to a 'black jail' by 7-8 people from the local public security bureau and were detained there until the next day.

On 8 April 2018, a man was tortured by being forced to squat outside for an entire night when the temperature was 3 degree Celcius by police in Shijingshan District, Beijing after being taken to Beijing Public Security Bureau Shijingshan Branch by Police and national security personnel. The reason for being taken by the police is related to the man's wife, who was participating in a march organized by missing human rights lawyer Wang Quanzhang's wife. Police had asked the man to bring his wife home and retaliated when he refused to cooperate.

On 4 December 2018, two petitioners, who attended the study group organized by petitioners on rule of law on the Chinese Constitution Day, in Taoranting Park in Xicheng district (Beijing) were taken away by the police to Majialou Detention Centre, which is a black jail for petitioners. They were later released by the Majialou Detention Centre together with other petitioners, and they also saw three buses filled up with petitioners while they arrived at Majialou Detention Centre.

On 26 May 2019, a family of 4 people gathered near Tiananmen Square in Dongcheng (Beijing) to air their grievances after their home had been forcibly demolished. They were taken away by police and held incommunicado since then.

Around 19 November 2018 (as reported), around six petitioners staged a protest in front of Guoxin Hotel in Xicheng district (Beijing) and demanded for the release of a female petitioner, as well as the secretary and governor of Henan province to step down. They held placards during the protest.

Around 16 May 2020 (month of), a female petitioner from Chengdu was intercepted in Xicheng district (Beijing) by officials from her hometown, ahead of the Lianghui annual parliamentary session, then transferred to a temporary extralegal detention center in Fangshan district. It was reported that she was then repatriated to Chengdu, where she was held under soft detention until the annual parliamentary session concluded.

On 23 December 2019, 24 migrant workers from Heilongjiang Province went to the State Bureau for Letters and Calls, Central Discipline Inspection Commission, and other departments in Beijing to petition for wage arrears owed to them for a construction project.

On 21 February 2019, a petitioner from Wuhan City was intercepted and abducted into a black car by a government official from Wuhan City at the Xidan Post Office in Xicheng District (Beijing). His whereabouts since being taken away were unknown.

On 2 September 2019, a large group of police took away petitioners from around China who had queued up outside the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng, Beijing to petition. They petitioners were taken away in four full coaches and detained at the Majialou 'black jail' in Fengtai, Beijing until early the following day. Some of them were sent to other places after being released from Majialou. This was part of the crackdown on petitioners before the 70th anniversary of the establishment of the PRC in October.

On 1 March 2019, a man who regularly participated in activism activities prepared to be forcibly admitted to a mental institution after a one-day notice from the Fengtai district (Beijing) security forces. The incident is allegedly in relation to the apporaching annual Lianghui conventions.

On 29 June 2018, former employees of China Construction Bank were surrounded by policemen while protesting in Xicheng District of Beijing. The protesters demanded pensions and medical benefits from the bank but did not dare to hold up banners. No clashes or injuries were reported.

On 8 February 2019, at least 8 Beijing-based homeless petitioners held a demonstration in front of the Beijing 12345 sign in Beijing South Railway Station (Fengtai District, Beijing). They held a banner which referenced the experience of another petitioner, who reported that he was tortured with a 'dog leash' over the Lunar New Year 2018 during his detention.

On 19 August 2020, public security officials from Beijing West Train Station assaulted a female petitioner from Chongqing during a soft detention at Huaxiang Hospital in Fengtai district (Beijing). Earlier that day, officers from the Chongqing Liaison Office, Longxi Sub-district Office and Xinpaifang Police Station boarded her train while it stopped at Shijiazhuang train station, and intercepted her trip to Beijing. She was escorted back to Chongqing the next day, 'restrained' at an unreported location then transferred to home surveillance.

On 8 May 2020, a female petitioner was taken away by four local 'interceptors' while she was working at the World Flower Garden in Fengtai District (Beijing). She was forcibly repatriated to Liaoning, where she was detained in a hotel for 14 days, on the grounds of being quarantined as part of the prevention measures during the COVID-19 pandemic. During this time, clashes broke out between the group and another group (14 people in total, according to the police report) over political differences. At least 7 people were injured, with 5 sent to the hospital for treatment. 15 people were arrested. This was one of two scuffles that took place at a 'Lennon Wall' in Hong Kong this week.

On 18 January 2020, about 50 members of a group named 'Hong Kong Peace Forces' went to the Mong Kok Police Station, protesting against universities for cultivating 'thugs'. The representative emphasized that universities should not be turned into 'political places'. They also shouted slogans in support of the Hong Kong Police, and called for an end to the violence first initiated by the extradition bill.

On 2 January 2020, more than 100 protesters gathered in and around Statue Square in Central (Central and Western district, Hong Kong) to join a 'lunch with you' rally to support the call for the five demands. They held signs and shouted slogans, marching towards the HSBC headquarters in Central.

On 25 May 2018, at least 8 representatives from the KMB Employees Union, Citybus Limited Employees Union and New World First Bus Company Staff Union (including members of the Labour Party) petitioned at the bus stop of Cross Harbour Tunnel in Hung Hom, Kowloon City District (Hong Kong), in response to the failure of the Transport Department to satisfactorily address their earlier appeals. They criticised the Transport Department for maintaining 14 hours as the maximum working hours, and its failure to establish the renumeration guidelines.

On 4 November 2019, nearly 200 students at Po Leung Kuk Tang Yuk Tien College in Tuen Mun District (New Territories, Hong Kong) gathered at the college gate to support one schoolmate who was a volunteer paramedic and got burned by tear gas during the demonstration on 2 November. They also condemned the police's abuse of force and urged the college to respond with more support for the students.

On 9 September 2018, several hundred foreign laborers marched to Government Headquarters located at Central, Hong Kong to petition for a rise in minimum wages and compensations, a guarantee of weekend break time, and acceptable accomodations.

On 11 January 2020, about 30 people gathered in Times Square, Causeway Bay (Wan Chai District, Hong Kong), periodically chanting slogans and singing the anthem of the 2019 Anti-Extradition Bill Protest. This was part of a wider Hong Kong-wide campaign to rebuild the Lennon Wall in 18 districts.

On 8 May 2019, members of LSD - including former LegCo member Leung Kwok-Hung - protested outside the High Court in the Central and Western District of Hong Kong during a judicial review hearing regarding the amended the rules of procedure in 2017 which reduced the quorum at Legco's committee level from 35 lawmakers to 20. The protesters, including the judicial review applicant, protested against the amendment and argued that the change violated article 75 of the Basic Law.

On 28 November 2019, nearly 50 students gathered at the Hong Kong Design Institute in Tseung Kwan O, Sai Kung District (New Territories, Hong Kong) to protest against the shut down of the campus. Some of them also urged the university to disclose video footage regarding the drowning death of a female student of the school, who was allegedly involved in the anti-government demonstrations. The students left after around half an hour.

On 21 February 2020, members of the Legislative Council and an alliance representing education centres went to the government headquarters (Central and Western District, Hong Kong) to petition for the government to include tuition and education centres in the government's support package of HK$30 billion for the coronavirus outbreak. They also called for the government to provide rent allowances.

On 9 December 2019, some demonstrators attempted to block MTR doors from closing at Tai Wai MTR station near Sha Tin (Hong Kong). Some other people condemned the demonstrators for their disruption to traffic. The demonstration was to mark the six-month anniversary of anti-ELAB unrest with a citywide strike. At least 5 people from 'protect MTR squad' were patrolling on the platforms and taking pictures of the demonstrators.
