notes: On 24 September 2018, the Hong Kong Government officially banned the pro-independence Hong Kong National Party (HKNP) on the basis that it posed a threat to national security and public order. The ban is the first of its kind in Hong Kong. On 26 Feb 2019, the Hong Kong Government announced that the party's appeal had been rejected, that the ban was final, and that the central government had expressed its support for the ban and requested that the Chief Executive send them a report on the matter.
On 19 September 2018, construction workers gathered in front of a hotel in Beijing to protest for their owed wages.
On 18 September 2018, workers protested in front of a decoration company located in Tianjin to demand for owed wages.
On 9 September 2018, fewer than 100 workers blocked the gate of a construction company in Shanghai to demand for owed wages during the construction of a subway line in Shenyang.

On 3 September 2018, community police officers kept a female petitioner in the village secretary's office in Shenxi village, Lingang sub-district of Jiangyin county, Wuxi, Jiangsu after she was kidnapped for petitioning in Beijing then sent back to her hometown. A officer confiscated her bag and forced her to give up on her petition. She refused and was subsequently placed under house arrest.
Around 1 September 2018 (as reported), as many as 100 student workers protested in Chongqing to demand for wage arrears owed by an after school child care service provider (Chongqing Xilantu).

Other: Around 1 September 2018 (as reported), Chinese authorities had issued orders that small religious gatherings of less than three participants could also be subjected to persecution and were to be reported by locals. This new order would impact house churches in particular. The location coded as Beijing.
On 29 August 2018, at least three workers protested at a construction site in Chongqing to demand for wage arrears owed by a property development project (Hengda Shijicheng).

Around 27 August 2018 (as reported), 14 environmental activists, ocean enthusiasts, islanders and fishers union representatives protested on a beach in Hong Kong against land reclamation proposals amidst the 2018 Land Supply Public Consultation meetings. They worried about air and water pollution, ecological destruction and the impact on small-scale fishers, urging the government to designate marine protected zones to facilitate the sustainable planning of marine resources.

On 27 August 2018, a female vaccine scandal victim was kidnapped in Beijing by law enforcement officials and incommunicado once again. She was in town to arrange a press release on 23-24 Aug with other parents affected by the vaccine scandal, some of whom experienced being detained, intimidated or sent back home by law enforcement.

On 21 August 2018, several dozen migrant workers protested in Beijing to demand for wage arrears owed by an interior decoration company (Beijing Jinyuan Jianzhuzhuangshi). The company hired people to disperse the workers with force.
Around 18 August 2018 (as reported), several workers stood in the middle of a road in Tianjin and protested to demand for wage arrears owed by a private construction project.

On 17 August 2018, a female vaccine scandal victim was kidnapped and carried out of her rented apartment in Beijing by four law enforcement personnel from her home province, Ningxia Autonomous Region. She disappeared incommunicado for seven days, before succeeding in returning to her apartment in Beijing. She realized that all her belongings were taken and the room was empty.

Around 8 August 2018 (as reported), as many as 100 workers organized a sit-in in Beijing to protest to demand for wage arrears owed by a private road construction project. On the same day, as many as 100 workers protested in Beijing to demand for wage arrears owed by a delivery company.

On 6 August 2018, a group of people who had fallen victim to P2P investment fraud gathered at Yuetan Park in Xicheng District (Beijing) but were immediately taken away by police officers on public buses. More than 120 buses were lined up along the roads near the China Banking Regulatory Commission, where a mass protest against the government's failure to prevent P2P fraud was supposed to take place. Hundreds of policemen were dispatched in Beijing to escort petitioners away from the area. They checked pedestrians' IDs to identify petitioners and hotels around the area were instructed to turn away petitioners. It was reported that police planned to take these people to black jails. Others en route to Beijing for the protest from Heilongjiang and Shanghai were also intercepted and intimidated by local police forces at train stations, highways, and private residences. An estimate of over 8,000 people had been expected to participate in the protest in Beijing.

On 1 August 2018, more than 20 residents of Kwai Tsing district, led by district councilor Ivan Wong Yun-Tat, protested in Hong Kong prior to a public consultation meeting hosted by the Electoral Affairs Commission. The meeting was held to address the EAC's tentative redistricting plan for the 2019 Hong Kong District Council Elections. Protesters believed that the redistricting was politically motivated, and that reverting to the original arrangement would better address the needs of the community.
Around 1 August 2018 (as reported), between 100 to 1000 drivers protested and went on strike in Chongqing demanding pay increase and higher bonuses from taxi service provider Didi Chuxing.

On 31 July 2018, over 100 residents took to the roads in Jing'an district of Shanghai to protest against the building of a refuse interchange station. A dozen policemen arrived on the scene to disperse the protest and arrested several protesters.
On 30 July 2018, local authorities raided a house church in Shapingba District, Chongqing and took away books, properties, and donations boxes. Some believers were also taken away by the officials.
On 27 July 2018, a Shanghaiese veteran was taken away by the police from Xujiaohui station in Xuhui district (Shanghai). He was detained incommunicado for over 24 hours as of the reporting.

On 27 July 2018, a Shanghaiese veteran was taken away by the police from Tilanqiao station in Hongkou district (Shanghai). He resisted and was beaten up by the police as a result, and was detained incommunicado for over 24 hours as of the reporting.

Around 24 July 2018 (as reported), around 1500 mall shop owners protested at the petitioning bureau in Chongqing (Chongqing Mass Visit Reception Centre) against accrued financial losses due to the failed planning of a shopping mall construction project, resulting in reduced property area and traffic flow to their businesses.
Around 22 July 2018 (as reported), about 6 workers protested in Beijing to demand for wage arrears owed by a private elderly housekeeping agency (Qicai Leju).

On 20 July 2018, Christian Social Concern Fellowship, Neo Democrats, People Power, and more than 60 civil society groups held a press conference in Hong Kong for their joint statement to protest against the police ban on the operation of Hong Kong National Party, and two Council Front Legislative Council lawmakers were also present in the conference. The representatives of the groups held placard in the confrerence and claimed that the decision from the government violated Freedom of Association.

On 18 July 2018, a petitioner and his mother were beaten up by 6-7 triad members hired by Yueyang Liaison Office in Beijing and Xiangyin county government in a hotel in Beijing. They were forcibly taken back to Xiangyin and kept in an apartment, where they were guarded by 4-5 people.
On 17 July 2018, as many as 100 sales workers held a demonstration to demand for wage arrears owed by a private cosmetics company (Watsons and Univinson) in Chongqing city.
On 16 July 2018, at least 20 workers organized an occupy sit-in at a private online education company in Yuzhong district, Chongqing to demand for wage arrears owed to them.
On 16 July 2018, as many as 100 construction workers protested to demand for wage arrears in Beijing.
On 15 July 2018, as many as 100 children's indoor playground staff protested to demand for wage arrears at Joy City shopping mall in Nankai, Tianjin.
On 14 July 2018, as many as 100 workers protested in Tianjin Municipality against wage arrears owed by a private shopping mall (Nankai Dayuecheng).
On 6 July 2018, between 1-100 workers protested over wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction company in Shanghai municipality. Unknown exact location within Shanghai municipality.
On 4 July 2018, between 1-100 workers protested wage arrears owed by a private housekeeping agency (Sanding Housekeeping) in Tianjin municipality. Unknown exact location within Tianjin municipality.

Around 1 July 2018 (beginning of month), a businessman from Changyi, Shandong went missing after travelling to Beijing to submit a petition about the Changyi police's reluctance to open a case on the fraud committed by his business partner. It is not the first time authorities had intervene, monitored or a forcibly removed him from protest activities, and as of 22 July 2018, this time, he had gone incommunicado for weeks.
Around 28 June 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers staged a sit-in protest in Beijing to demand wage arrears owed to them by a construction company. Police arrived to disperse the protesters.
Around 28 June 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers went on strike and protested in Chongqing City to demand wage arrears and material payments owed to them by a construction company.

On 27 June 2018, a Shanghaiese woman was beaten up by a local policemen at the entrance of the Shanghai Municipal Public Security Bureau in Xuhui district after shouting her grievances of their delay and refusal to process her legalised hukou assignment transfer since 2009. She was taken into custody for eight hours, and sustained injuries to her head, chest and broke two ribs.
Around 23 June 2018 (week of), up to 100 employees protested in Shanghai to demand wage arrears owed to them by a chain restaurant. The employees had lost contact with their employer.
Around 23 June 2018 (week of), up to 100 employees held a sit-in protest in Chongqing City to demand wage arrears owed to them by an internet company.
Around 22 June 2018 (week of), up to 100 workers held banners and held a sit-in protest in Beijing to demand wage arrears owed to them by a geotechnical engineering company.

On 15 June 2018, in the early hours of the morning, an officer of the Zhangjiakou City Wuyi Road Subdistrict, along with dozens of police officers, besieged a hotel in Beijing where 21 petitioners from Zhangjiakou City were spending the night before petitioning. The police dragged the villagers onto a truck to prevent them from petitioning, and a female petitioner died during the process. The direct cause of death was unknown.
Around 15 June 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers protested in Beijing City to demand wage arrears and supplier payments owed to them by an interior design company.
On 12 June 2018, around 10000 enterprise employees protested at the Letters and Calls Bureau in Huangpu District of Shanghai City, demanding the same pension payment as civil servants.
Around 6 June 2018 (as reported), up to 100 employees protested in Chongqing Municipality to demand wage arrears owed to them by an electronic production company.

On 30 May 2018, more than 100 petitioners holding placards demonstrated peacefully in the Shanghai People's Park in Huangpu District of Shanghai City, calling for the rule of law and social justice. More than 100 Special Police were present and arrested some petitioners. Stability maintenance officers from a few Residential District Offices also took away some protesters who lived in their administrative areas.

On 28 May 2018, more than 1000 protesters staged a petition outside the Chongqing Bureau for Letters and Calls in Yuzhong District, Chongqing City. Some businessmen who suffered a loss due to the breach of contracts chanted slogans and asked for the rule of law, human rights and resolution of historical issues. Police arrived to disperse the crowd and arrested 7 to 8 people.

On 28 May 2018, a female activist from Wuxi, Jiangsu was inspected by police when she was visiting a friend in Beijing and was forcibly detained in the Beijing Jiujingzhuang Jieji Service Centre (a black jail) in Fengtai, Beijing. She disappeared after being taken away from the Service Centre by people from the Beijing-based Wuxi Government Office. It is suspected that she has been sent back to Wuxi but her whereabouts were unknown.

On 27 May 2018, around 300 migrant worker labour groups, as well as pro-democracy political group Socialist Action, marched in Hong Kong to protest against the New People's Party Legislative Council (LegCo) member Eunice Yung Hoi-Yan, for her discrimination and defamation of ethnic minorities and asylum seekers during her LegCo election campaign.
Around 26 May 2018 (as reported), up to 100 employees demonstrated in Shanghai against wage arrears owed to them by an electrical appliance company. They held banners during the demonstration.

Around 24 May 2018 (as reported), the KMB Employees Union held a press conference in Hong Kong, calling on union members to participate in the demonstration to be launched on the next day. They also urged the KMB to increase the salaries of all employees by 12 per cent, and set the minimum monthly salary of a bus captain at no less than HKD 23,000. At least 6 people held placards, while at least another 3 were involved in delivering the press conference.

Around 23 May 2018 (as reported), up to 100 employees demonstrated in Tianjin against wage arrears owed to them by a second-hand car dealer which had ceased operations. They held banners during the demonstration.

Around 23 May 2018 (as reported), up to 100 migrant workers demonstrated in Chongqing, demanding for wage arrears owed to them by a construction company. It was reported that they had been owed their wages since July 2017.

On 23 May 2018, a disabled female petitioner from Jiangsu Yancheng City was intercepted by government personnel in Beijing and detained in a hotel in Dahongmen Residential District. It was reported that she and her husband consistently submitted petitions in Beijing regarding the resettlement of their house.

Around 21 May 2018 (as reported), at least 9 employees demonstrated in Beijing, against wage arrears owed to them by a decoration company after the company had ceased operations. They held banners during the demonstration.
Around 20 May 2018 (as reported), up to 100 employees, proprietors and suppliers demonstrated in Shanghai, against wage arrears and money owed to them by a mud commune decoration company.

On 18 May 2018, a human rights lawyer residing in Shanghai was reportedly missing after issuing an appeal at 5am to netizens to change their profile picture on WeChat into the portrait of another human rights lawyer to express solidarity with the lawyer who had been illegally detained. The lawyer remained uncontactable at 11pm on the same day.

Around 16 May 2018 (as reported), more than 100 deliverymen of the group buying website Meituan.com demonstrated in Chongqing City against the order management system which does not allow deliverymen to accept orders voluntarily. They also protested against the continued reduction in commission rate.

On 14 May 2018, up to 100 employees of a bicycle sharing company demonstrated in Jing'an District (Shanghai) against the company's layoffs. They held banners during the demonstration, and demanded that the company pay its social insurance contributions.
Around 11 May 2018 (as reported), a group of workers staged a protest in Chongqing City to opposed pay cuts and demand for wage arrears owed to them by a construction company.

Around 7 May 2018 (as reported), at least a dozen customers and employees of an interior decoration company in Jiangbei District (Chongqing) protested at the company's site to demand compensations and wage arrears after the company suddenly shut down and its owner ran away.
Around 7 May 2018 (as reported), a group of workers staged a protest in Shanghai to demand for wage arrears owed to them by a decoration company. Protesters carried a banner.

Around 3 May 2018 (as reported), a Baoji petitioner and activist was found out missing in Beijing. In the past, the activist had been persecuted by the government and was nearly killed by stability maintenance forces. Prior to his disappearance, he and fellow villagers were violently intercepted by local security at the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng, Beijing on 28 April 2018 when petitioning to express their dissatisfaction regarding local authorities' violent treatment of petitioners.

On 1 May 2018, three staff members of the Neighbourhood and Worker's Service Centre held a sit-in in Hong Kong after the May Day rally, protesting their sudden dismissal. A day before the sit-in, the three attended a meeting where Leung Yiu-chung, politician, Legislative Council member and Neighbourhood and Worker's Service Centre member, told them their salaries would not be paid anymore starting 31 May, but that they are not being fired. The three pointed at Leung Yiu-chung's plans to allocate resource for elections as the reason for the dismissal, but Leung denied the allegations.

On 27 April 2018, crane operators protested in Chongqing for a collective wage increase and better working conditions. It was reported that police arrested 11 operators. This protest was part of a larger nation-wide crane operators strike movement that took place in at least 18 provinces.
Around 26 April 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers of a technology company hung a large banner on the street to protest against wage arrears owed by the company in Tianjin.
Around 25 April 2018 (as reported), workers protested layoffs and wage arrears owed by a share bike company in Shanghai.
On 21 April 2018, up to 100 workers of a construction company held a sit-in protest to demand for wage arrears at the company's bureau in Beijing.
On 20 April 2018, up to 100 workers of an express delivery company held a collective protest to demand compensation for wage arrears at the company's headquarters in Shanghai.
Around 18 April 2018 (as reported), at least 15-20 workers of an educational centre held banners in Beijing to demand wage arrears owed by the company.

On 18 April 2018, at least dozens of petitioners gathered at People's Park in Huangpu District (Shanghai) which is next to the Shanghai city petition offices to participate a collective petition event. People used placards and banners. The event finished around noon. Some of the petitioners were taken to be questioned by police after the event but released on the same day.
Around 3 April 2018 (as reported), at least 3 up to 100 delivery workers blocked company entrance protesting against wage arrears in Beijing. They also put a large banner outside of the buildings.

On 1 April 2018, a female petitioner was taken by government stability maintenance personnel in Chongqing because she was planning to go to petition in Beijing. She managed to call others before being taken, then she became missing until the time of reporting on 2 April 2018.
Around 31 March 2018, up to 100 workers staged a protest in Shanghai over wage arrears owed by Baidu Food Delivery Company.

On 30 March 2018, about 100 street cleaners put on a four-day protest outside the Changning District's Greening and City Appearance Administration in Shanghai, protesting the reduction of pay rate by several street cleaning companies. It was reported that the protest lasted for four days and appeared to be resolved by 2 April 2018.

On 27 March 2018, hundreds of sanitation workers from Changning District (Shanghai) gathered at the District Government offices to protest against a wage decrease and demanding their fundamental labour rights. The protest started on 26 March 2018 at the District Government offices where protesters were beaten and detained by police. Starting from 27 March 2018, police were observing the protest but did not intervene. There was no response from the government. The protest lasted until at least 31 March 2018.

On 26 March 2018, a group of sanitation workers from Changning District held a protest and strike in Changning District, Shanghai, opposing a wage decrease and demanding their fundamental labour rights. Protesters were beaten and detained by police. The strike was triggered by a message issued by the Shanghai Gaojie Environmental Sanitation Service regarding workers' allowance cancelled for morning and evening shifts, and a general wage cut.
Around 22 March 2018, up to 100 workers staged a protest in Chongqing over unpaid social security and wage arrears owed by the Shiji Hualian Supermarket.
Around 16 March 2018, up to 100 workers staged a protest in Chongqing over wage arrears owed by the Zhonggguo Jiafang Bedding Store.

On 15 March 2018, liaison officers kidnapped and assaulted a female petitioner from Yangjian town, Wuxi while she was in Beijing mailing reporting materials to high-level government officials. Her clothes were torn and damaged amidst physical altercations. They drove her back to the police station in Yangjian, and when they arrived, the police refused to file her assault case and pretended not to hear or acknowledge her.
Around 14 March 2018, up to 100 interior decoration workers staged a sit-in protest in Beijing over wage arrears owed by the Fudi Fenghuang Hotel.

Around 14 March 2018, up to 100 construction workers staged a protest in Chongqing over wage arrears owed by the Zhonghang Zhongyangcheng construction project. After being merged by Hengda Corporation, Zhonghang Company refused to pay the construction workers.

On 13 March 2018, a female rights defender was sent back to Shanghai from Beijing, kept in Room 912 in Shanghai Chongming District Changxin Island Hotel, and the room was guarded, as well as her phone and public transport card were confiscated by six men and two women. The petitioner went on a hunger strike when she was kept in the hotel, and she was later sent to Shanghai Yangpu District Jungong Road No. 2180 Gongqing Forest Holiday Resort where she started a hunger strike again. She was released on 27 March 2018.

On 12 March 2018, a petitioner who petitioned against foced eviction and the under-valuation of her property was taken into a van by a group of unidentified kidnappers who broke into her temporary residence in Beijing (Beijing) and detained at the Beijing Reception Management and Service Center in Fengtai district Youwai Dongzhuang 90.
Around 12 March 2018, up to 100 workers staged a protest in Beijing over wage arrears owed by the Sanding Housework Agency.
Around 11 March 2018, up to 100 student workers staged a protest in Chongqing over wage arrears owed by the Wanhao Hotel. The student workers held banners during the protest.

On 11 March 2018, a female petitioner from Wujing town of Minhang district, Shanghai went incommunicado after she was taken back to Shanghai from Beijing, and was taken in for investigation at the police station. The police denied detaining her, and said village authorities took her away, although they also denied the same. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation in which the rights defenders and petitioners were their targets.

On 10 March 2018, a female petitioner was intercepted by a stability maintenance personnel of the Chongqing Liangjiang New Area Administration Committee and 6-7 unidentified people at a residential area in Beijing and detained at a black prison named Yuquanying Gaojiachang (Fengtai District, Beijing). The detention is related to the woman's repeated attempts to petition for monetary compensation for medical expenses on injuries caused to her while being violently abducted and beaten by unidentified people in Chongqing in 2017. Upon negotiation, she went back to Chongqing with the stability maintenance personnel on 11 March 2018 and checked into a hospital.

Around 6 March 2018 (as reported), a petitioner from Wuhan City was taken in Beijing by unidentified people when he was petitioning in Beijing. He remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 6 March 2018.

On 3 March 2018, three petitioners from Wuxi, Jiangsu was taken in Beijing by the Beijing police and sent to Beijing Jiujingzhuang Jieji Service Centre (black jail) after being interrogated by the Beijing police.

On 2 March 2018, several unidentified people, who claimed to be police but refused to show their documents, broke into a house in Beijing and beat the occupants before taking them away to the police station. Two of the occupants had just been released from prison, while another two were victims of forced demolition in Changzhou (Jiangsu). During the incident one of the victims attempted to take pictures, but then had their phone taken from them.

On 2 March 2018, a female petitioner from Chongqing Jiangbei District Nanqiaosi Village was taken to a police station by the police when she was at a bus station in Beijing on her way to petition at the National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration, and later the personnel from the Office of the Chongqing Government to Beijing sent her back to Chongqing, and the Chongqing police kept her in Zhulin Hotel. After she refused to stay in the hotel, the police officers attacked her, injured her eye, caused multiple bruises over her body and bleeding on her palms.

On 2 March 2018, a female petitioner from Jiang'an District, Wuhan was taken away from Beijing by the Beijing Police and sent back to Wuhan City, Hubei by the Wuhan stability maintenance agents while she was petitioning in Beijing during the Lianghui Conventions. She remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 6 March 2018.

On 28 February 2018, a petitioner from Shanghai was beaten into unconsciousness in a car by five unidentified people on the way to a hotel after they took away his cane, cover his head with a black hood, and forced him into a car. He was subsequently detained for 22 days before they threw him by the side of a road. He believes his kidnappers were from the government.

Around 25 February 2018 (as reported), at least 7 human rights activists from the Cao Shunli Human Rights Group protested in Shanghai for the 8th time to demand the government lift the ban on political parties and remove restrictions on freedom of speech and the media. Protesters held a banner.

On 24 February 2018, a woman farmer from Dashuijing Village, Chongqing was abducted by police and Chongqing South Railway Station administration in Chongqing South Railway Station, Yuzhong District when trying to visit Beijing. The next day, police illegally abducted her to a small island in Changshou Lake, Chongqing, where she was restricted.
Around 13 February 2018 (as reported), less than 100 workers protested in Shanghai against unpaid wages owed by a construction company.

Around 13 February 2018 (as reported), a group of workers protested in Chongqing against unpaid wages owed by a construction company. The workers were beaten by unidentified people connected to the company. No fatalities were reported.
Around 8 February 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers gathered in Shapingba District (Chongqing) to protest against unpaid wages. Protesters held banners.
Around 8 February 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers gathered in Shanghai (Shanghai) to protest against unpaid wages.

Around 28 January 2018 (as reported), the husband of an environmental activist involved in a dispute with the local government in Funing County, Jiangsu over the illegal occupation of farmers' land has been missing for almost a month. He was last seen in Beijing and is suspected to have been abducted, but it is unclear as to whom he was abducted by.
Around 26 January 2018 (as reported), between 1 to 100 workers staged a protest to demand for wage arrears owed by a hotel in Beijing.
Around 26 January 2018 (as reported), between 1 to 100 workers staged a protest to demand for wage arrears owed by an interior decoration company in Tianjin.

On 20 January 2018, a Swedish scholar and bookseller was arrested by authorities while on a train to Beijing. He has been incommunicado for at least 2 weeks since. The book merchant had been arrested in 2015 and kept under surveillance in Beijing for more than 2 years in connection with the Causeway bookstore incident in Hong Kong.

Around 16 January 2018 (as reported), a banker went incommunicado in Hong Kong after his father, General and Former Vice Chairman of the Central Military Commission, was summoned for case review. The disappearance was suspected to be related to a change of power within the Communist Party and an anti-corruption campaign led by President Xi.
Around 16 January 2018 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest to demand for wage arrears owed by technology company in Chongqing municipality.
On 12 January 2018, at least 4 civil rights lawyers protested outside of a prison, after officers rejected their request to meet with an activist detained in Tianjin.
On 9 January 2018, dozens of pro-democracy protesters in Hong Kong gathered outside of the court to protest against the prosecution of nine pro-democracy leaders by the government.

On 9 January 2018, a Hong Kong pro-democracy activist and legislative by-election hopeful, who is also one of the Umbrella Movement leaders facing trial, was attacked by two unknown men in Hong Kong. According to Hong Kong police, the attack was politically motivated, since the activist received a threatening letter in the same day.

Around 8 January 2018 (between 7 - 8 January), around 9 members of an elderly and disability care home facilities concern group, which included LegCo and LP members and physiotherapists from Physio Action, organised an outdoor press conference in Hong Kong to raise awareness and propose solutions to the cramped living conditions at these facilities and accessibility issues. They created a physical setup modelled after a typical care facility, in order to allow passerbys to experience the lack of space in private-owned and -operated elderly & disabled care facilities.
Around 7 January 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers protested to demand for wage arrears owed by a restaurant in Beijing.

On 6 January 2018, a large group of elderly retirees protested in Shanghai to demand for a raise in retirement funds equal to those for civil servants amidst rising cost of living in the city. They shouted slogans.
Around 5 January 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers held a sit-in protest against wage arrears owed by construction company in Beijing.

On 1 August 2019, three Tibetan Bon monks were taken into custody in Ngawa county (also Ngaba, Aba) (Ngawa Tibetan and Qiang Autonomous, Sichuan). While two of them were released a few days after, one of the monks remained detained and held incommunicado. It was reported on 2 Dec 2020 that his now-shut down social media account and website about Tibet had drawn the attention of police for several years. The National Security Bureau officially notified his family on 23 Mar 2020 about the charges brought against him - inciting separatism. Local police verbally informed his family on 26 Mar 2021 that the victim had been held at a prison in Chengdu prefecture for four and a half years, and would be accepting visitors now.

On 26 October 2020, a Tibetan monk from the Kirti monastery in Ngawa Tibetan and Qiang Autonomous prefecture - and Buddhist scholar and educator, vocal on democratic rights and advocacy for academic freedom in monastic education settings, was held in incommunicado detention in Chengdu prefecture (Sichuan) (coded to Wuhou). His whereabouts and reason for arrest were still unknown at the time of reporting on 9 April 2021. It was reported that security personnel from Tibet crossed provincial borders to make the arrest.

On 16 April 2021, many citizens and pro-democracy public figures - lawyers and former legislators (representing CP, Hong Kong Labour Party) - gathered in solidarity at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts in Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Sham Shui Po) to show support for nine pro-democracy veterans and protest organisers on trial for illegal assembly on two unauthorised protests in Aug 2019. Some held up the hand gesture in support of the five demands, as well symbolic objects such as yellow umbrellas and copies of the Apple Daily newspaper. They chanted slogans, and held up placards and smartphones as the defendants left the court. There were also several opposition demonstrators (including Politihk Social Strategic), who came with banners and popped champagne bottles when prison sentences were announced. Police intervened during a row between protesters on both sides, arresting a pro-democracy protester for refusing to put his mask back on, and spitting on the police.

On 23 March 2021, a Tibetan writer and former political prisoner was arrested by the police in Seda county (Ganzi, Sichuan) for unknown reasons. His whereabouts were still unknown at the time of reporting on 15 April 2021.

On 22 March 2021, a Tibetan political activist was taken away by the police in Ganzi prefecture (Sichuan) (coded to Kangding City) for unknown reasons. His whereabouts were still unknown at the time of reporting on 15 April 2021.

actor1: Police Forces of China (2012-) People's Armed Police
notes: On 5 March 2021, several Tibetans, who had posted on social media expressing concern about the police torture and death of a young Buddhist monk, were taken away by the Snow Wolf Commandos (a unit of the paramilitary People's Armed Police) in Wonpo township of Ganzi prefecture (Sichuan) (coded to Kangding City). Around 19 September 2021 (as reported), delivery workers protested in Nantong city, Jiangsu (coded to Chongchuan) to demand wage arrears owed by a courier.
Around 25 October 2021 (as reported), over 100 delivery workers of the China Post protested and went on strike in Huai'an city (Huaian, Jiangsu) to demand wage arrears.
Around 26 October 2021, workers protested in Dalian city, Liaoning (coded to Xigang) to demand wage arrears owed by a real estate developer (Evergrande Group).
Around 25 October 2021 (as reported), construction workers protested in Dalian city, Liaoning (coded to Xigang) to demand wage arrears.
Around 23 September 2021 (as reported), 37 workers protested in Jiangshan Town (Ningbo, Zhejiang) to demand wage arrears owed by a furniture factory.
Around 18 October 2021 (as reported), over 100 delivery workers of Yunda Express protested and went on strike in Nanjing city, Jiangsu (coded to Xuanwu) to demand wage arrears owed by the courier.
Around 17 October 2021 (as reported), delivery workers of STO Express went on strike and protested in Nanjing city, Jiangsu (coded to Xuanwu) to demand wage arrears owed by the courier.
Around 4 October 2021 (as reported), delivery workers of Yunda Express protested and went on strike in Nanjing city, Jiangsu (coded to Xuanwu) to demand wage arrears owed by the courier.
Around 24 October 2021 (as reported), delivery workers of ZTO Express protested and went on strike in Nanchang city (Nanchang, Jiangxi) to demand wage arrears owed by the courier.
Around 17 October 2021 (as reported), workers protested in Ruichang city (Jiangxi, Jiujiang) to demand wage arrears owed by a construction company.
Around 8 October 2021 (as reported), staff of an esports company protested in Shangrao city, Jiangxi (coded to Xinzhou) to demand wage arrears.
Around 27 November 2021 (as reported), over 100 delivery workers of Yunda Express protested and went on strike in Changchun city, Jilin (coded to Chaoyang) to demand wage arrears.
Around 21 October 2021 (as reported), bus drivers also protested and went on strike in Chaoyang district (Changchun, Jilin), demanding wage arrears.
Around 21 October 2021 (as reported), construction workers (migrant workers) were hit by project management during a protest in Chaoyang district (Changchun, Jilin) where they demanded wage arrears.
Around 17 October 2021 (as reported), delivery workers of YTO Express went on strike and protested in Changchun city, Jilin (coded to Chaoyang) to demand wage arrears owed by the courier.

Around 15 October 2021 (as reported), a few hundred self-employed taxi drivers went on strike and demonstrated with their vehicles in Weixin county (Zhaotong, Yunnan) to protest the new policy of requiring them to operate under a taxi firm.
Around 12 October 2021 (as reported), construction workers protested in Zhoushan city, Zhejiang (coded to Dinghai) to demand wage arrears owed by the Evergrande Group.
Around 14 October 2021 (as reported), 9 workers protested in Huangyuan county (Xining, Qinghai) to demand wage arrears owed by a construction company.
On 20 October 2021, workers protested in Xian city, Shaanxi (coded to Baqiao) to demand wage arrears owed by a gym.
Around 12 October 2021 (as reported), over 100 teachers protested in Xian city, Shaanxi (coded to Baqiao) to demand wage arrears owed by an educational and training center.
On 29 November 2021, over 100 taxi drivers gathered at Shaanxi Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xincheng district (Xian, Shaanxi), calling for fuel subsidy.
Around 16 October 2021 (as reported), employees protested in Zichang city (Yanan, Shaanxi) to demand wage arrears owed by a restaurant.
Around 17 October 2021 (as reported), delivery workers of YTO Express went on strike and protested in Anqiu city (Weifang, Shandong) to demand wage arrears owed by the courier.
Around 2 December 2021 (as reported), delivery workers of Yunda Express protested and went on strike in Liaocheng city, Shandong (coded to Dongchangfu) to demand wage arrears.
Around 26 October 2021, workers protested in Habahe county (Altay, Xinjiang) to demand wage arrears owed by construction projects.
Around 12 October 2021 (as reported), workers protested in Kunming city, Yunnan (coded to Chenggong) to demand wage arrears owed by a residential property managers company.
Around 27 October 2021, over 10 workers protested in Jinghong City (Xishuangbanna, Yunnan) to demand wage arrears owed by a construction company.
On 12 October 2021, employees protested in Chengdu city, Sichuan (coded to Wuhou) to demand wage arrears owed by a property developer.
Around 21 October 2021 (as reported), employees protested in Hangzhou city, Zhejiang (coded to Jianggan), to demand wage arrears owed by a now-shuttered piano school.

On 21 November 2021, a female petitioner was intercepted by Zhangjiabao Sub-district Office officers at Xi'an Railway Station in Xincheng district (Xian, Shaanxi) as she was traveling to Beijing to submit a petition. A few 'thugs' snatched away her personal belongings and pushed her to the ground, causing her to fall unconscious. She later woke up inside a car in Yandong Unit but was forbidden to seek help from police and medics until she was dumped out of the vehicle on Wenjing road after midnight.

On 24 November 2021, four petitioner-cum-forced-evictees were intercepted and beat up by Suzhou Gusu Public Complaints and Proposals Administration officers and police upon arriving at Nanjing railway station in Xuanwu district (Nanjing, Jiangsu) when they were on their way to submit petition documents to Nanjing High People's Court. An old petitioner was therefore suffered from tension headache and coma and needed to admit to a hospital. The three others were repatriated to Suzhou city, where an injured female petitioner was detained immediately at a police station in Gusu district.

On 30 November 2021, at least 4 members of DAB protested at the Government House in Central District (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western), urging the government to provide a physical QR code to the elderly who cannot use the LeaveHomeSafe app to record their locations visited. The protest came after the authorities enforced the mandatory use of the app for entry into government buildings and public locations starting from 1 November 2021. However, many older adults did not have smartphones or did not know how to use the app even when they had smartphones.

On 26 November 2021, representatives of Concerning Grassroot Housing Rights Alliance demonstrated and held a press conference in Hong Kong to protest the perceived insufficient amount and long-waiting time of government-built transitional housing allocated to low-income people. They held placards to express their demands.

On 1 December 2021, members of Federation of Public Housing Estates demonstrated and held a press conference in Hong Kong, calling the government to introduce new anti-property speculation measures over subsidized housing. They suggested extending the restriction on resale at the original price and separating the subsidized housing market from the private one. They held placards to express their demands.

On 2 December 2021, a pro-establishment civil group, 'Justice Power,' rallied at the Police Headquarters in Wan Chai district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Wan Chai) to protest a Legislative Council election survey done by the Hong Kong Public Opinion Research Institute, which suggested that around half of the interviewees are inclined to vote in next month's 'patriots only' legislative election. They accused the institute of conspiring with foreign forces and demanded a police investigation into the institute.

On 1 December 2021, a legislation election candidate and his supporters protested at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western), urging the government to introduce market competition in the new railway project and reform the MTR management.

On 1 June 2020, more than 400 Mongolian herders were marching from Bayan-Uul Sum (or district) to Lindong Town (Chifeng City, Inner Mongolia), to protest against land grabbing by the CCP carried out under the pretext of 'ecology'. The banner government had notified herders that a national nature conservancy would be established on their grazing land in February 2020. Demonstrators were stopped en route to Lindong Town, with many pepper sprayed and beaten before being detained by local police and SWAT teams. Nearly 200 people were arrested. Two of the activists who supported the demonstration were sentenced to eight months and four months in jail on 5 June 2020. It was reported that hundreds of herders still managed to reach the banner government to protest on 1 June, and continued to protest the next day.

On 2 September 2020, over 300 ethnic Mongolian employees of Inner Mongolia Radio Station and Inner Mongolia TV Station gathered in Inner Mongolia amidst student strikes and boycotts to sign a joint statement, rejecting the new policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction for three subjects in elementary and middle schools for minority groups across the autonomous region starting with the immediate fall semester. The group signed a document that they are prepared to resign en masse, if any of their ten colleagues loses their job for refusing orders to send their children back to school.

Other: Around 20 August 2020, South Mongolian Human Rights Information Centre leaked information about an official document detailing a new language policy from the central government that had been kept secret. The new policy required all elementary and middle schools across Inner Mongolia to replace Mongolian language with Chinese language as the language of instruction starting from 1 Sep 2020, as ordered by the central government. The leaked document detailing the plan had since prompted protests across Inner Mongolia. The location coded as Beijing.

Around 8 November 2021 (as reported), a female activist from Shangqiu city, Henan (coded to Suiyang), went missing. Her appearance came after her online activism, urging for the immediate release of jailed citizen journalist Zhang Zhan, who was close to death during an intermittent hunger strike to protest her imprisonment for reporting news from Wuhan in the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic. It was suspected that she was taken away by the police.

On 30 October 2021, a female activist was taken away by local government officers in Beijing municipality and became incommunicado, as reported on 8 November 2021. Her disappearance came after her online activism urging for the immediate release of jailed citizen journalist Zhang Zhan, who was close to death during an intermittent hunger strike to protest her imprisonment for reporting news from Wuhan in the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic.

On 18 October 2021, a woman was placed under residential surveillance in a designated location by police in Pinghai township (Putian, Fujian) on suspicion of supplying food for her ex-husband - a now-deceased murder suspect. Her arrest came after her ex-husband killed himself in a cave as authorities closed in to arrest him for allegedly murdering two people and injuring three others in a land dispute on 10 October 2021. The suicide of the murder suspect drew national attention and elicited an outpouring of sympathy for the accused.

On 19 September 2021, a female independent journalist and an activist were taken away by police at a residence in Haizhu district, Guangzhou, ahead of the journalist's planned departure to study in the UK via Hong Kong. The pair was placed under residential surveillance in a designated location for 'incitement to subvert state power', mainly due to the regular gatherings of friends at the activist's home. On 5 November 2021, their family members received an arrest notice, stating that they had been officially arrested on 27 October 2021 and detained at Guangzhou No. 1 Detention Centre.

On 23 June 2021, the wife of a rights defender was captured from her residence in Caoyuancun village, Xi county (Xinyang, Henan) for the second time in a week by two police officers from Huaihe Police Station and detained in a local hotel for unreported reason. During her absence from home, stability maintenance officials destroyed security cameras in her house.

On 21 June 2021, the wife of a rights defender was captured from her residence in Caoyuancun village, Xi county (Xinyang, Henan) by two police officers from Huaihe Police Station and some community secretaries from Caoyuancun for unreported reason. She was detained in a hotel for a day before being allowed to return to her place of residence under surveillance on the following day.

On 2 April 2021, a female activist disappeared after completing mandatory coronavirus quarantine in Shenzhen city (Guangdong), and remained incommunicado at the time of reporting on 10 May 2021. Intending to visit her mother, she had told friends that she wouldn't stay in mainland China for long due to safety concerns, and planned to return during late April or May. They suspected that she was secretly detained for participating in the local pro-democracy movement since immigrating to Hong Kong.

On 2 April 2021, a Tibetan female activist and former political prisoner was taken away by the police in Ganzi prefecture (Sichuan) (coded to Kangding City) for unknown reasons. Her whereabouts were still unknown at the time of reporting on 15 April 2021.

On 6 March 2021, a female rights defender was sexually harassed by drunk officials at the Taohua Police Station in Changshou district (Chongqing), and bruised her back and arms while resisting. The incident was reported as one of multiple stability maintenance efforts carried out against petitioners nationwide during the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 4 April 2020, a villager from Dingliu Village was taken away by the police in Gaoqu Township, Sanyuan County (Xianyang City, Shaanxi Province) (coded at Sanyuan County), for attempting to reason with a construction company that their construction project had affected the discharge of sewage from the village. The construction company later called the police and the villager was taken away for interrogation on the grounds of attempting to 'block construction'. After a few hours later at the police station, the villager was sent to the intensive care unit of a hospital because he was comatose from severe trauma. While the police alleged that the villager inflicted the injuries upon himself, his two daughters claimed they heard sounds of someone getting beaten from across the police station, and strongly believed that he was attacked by the police during his detention. The daughters were also pinned to the ground by police officers at the police station, and one of them sustained injuries to her hand, face and waist.

On 20 December 2019, the mother of a man who was prosecuted for 'illegal' possession of state secrets' was intercepted and beaten by four unidentified persons in front of her house in Chongqing Province. One of the men claimed to act on behalf of the Chinese government, though this has not been confirmed. The incident happened one day after she granted permission to travel to Beijing to testify at her son's trial.

On 12 October 2019, a female candidate who was running for District Council was attacked at her booth in the City Garden constituency of North Point, Eastern District (Hong Kong), by a middle-aged man. The man tore up her election leaflet in front of her, and punched her in the head twice. She was then taken to Ruttonjee Hospital after feeling dizzy and nauseous.

On 8 October 2019, a female candidate who was running for District Council in the Yuet Wah constituency in Kwun Tong District (New Territories, Hong Kong) was attacked in the back of her head with an unknown object while she was waiting to cross the road. She did not suffer major injuries from this attack. She had been harassed via text message and on Facebook by unknown people aiming to deter her from campaigning.

Around 30 September 2019 (between 16 September and 17 October 2019), a female human rights defender in Nanchong City (Sichuan Province) was detained by police and beaten while in custody due to her Twitter post supporting the anti-ELAB demonstrations in Hong Kong.

On 5 July 2019, a female human rights activist from Jiaozuo, Henan was forcibly abducted in Muxidi, Xicheng District (Beijing) by more than 10 unidentified people dressed in black. According to CRLW, she was later confirmed to be detained by the Jiaozuo local government for crime of picking quarrels and provoking troubles on 7 July 2019.

On 6 May 2019, the 86-year-old mother of a dissident, who had been under house arrest for 5 months, was attacked by a National Security Force officer in Wuhou (Chengdu City, Sichuan Province) on their way home from a local hospital. The mother was repeatedly pushed and had her thumb sprained by the officer when they were quarrelling.

As reported on 26 March 2019, a woman petitioner from Yaohai district, Hefei, who was being held in administrative detention in Hefei city (Anhui), was transferred to a hotel and held there for 7 more days before being allowed to go home. Her niece was also detained at the hotel for seven days. The incident was allegedly related to the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 20 March 2019, a female human rights defender was arrested from her home in Shanghai by the police together with her husband. While her husband was released on probation in April, she had been held incommunicado for more than 6 months until the authority announced that she was charged with 'subversion of state power' in October 2019.
On 19 March 2019, a farmer-turned-human rights defender from Shanghai was secretly taken away by Shanghai police from her home. It is not known why she was taken away.

On 12 March 2019, a human rights defender from Shanghai was picked up from her home and detained at a 'black jail' in Suzhou City (Jiangsu) by police officers from Shanghai's Jing'an District Public Security Bureau.

On 11 March 2019, the mother of a prominent human rights defender was roughly dragged about by a group of people keeping watch on her home as she was on her way out of her home in Wenjiang District (Chengdu, Sichuan). She was planning to visit her son in Mianyang city the next day but might not be able to make the journey after the incident.
On 11 March 2019, a female activist from Wuxi, Jiangsu was abducted in Xicheng, Beijing by nine suspected stability maintenance officials from Wuxi and was since then held incommunicado.
On 8 March 2019, a human rights defender from Shenyang was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' from the Shenyang City government from her home in Beijing and sent to Shenyang.
On 8 March 2019, a human rights defender from Heilongjiang was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' from the Heilongjiang government near her home in Beijing.
On 8 March 2019, a human rights defender from Liaoning was kidnapped by personnel from the Liaoning Court while she was in Fengtai (Beijing).

On 5 March 2019, a human rights defender who had just been released from prison after serving a 4-year sentence was kidnapped by more than 10 men beside the bus stop at Jiangshan Road and Sanquan Road in Huiji district (Zhengzhou, Henan). It was reported that authorities arrived in 3 to 4 private cars and pushed her inside.

On 5 March 2019, a human rights defender from Pudong New Area, Shanghai was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' backed by the Shanhai government while she was in Beijing Municipality. She was sent back to Shanghai and detained at a 'black jail' in Hengsha Island.
On 1 March 2019, the superintendent of Huaihe subdistrict police station locked up the wife of a human rights defender at Jinxiu Hotel in the farmers market in Xi county (Xinyang, Henan).
On 1 March 2019, a human rights defender in Qiaokou District (Wuhan, Hubei) was incommunicado after leaving her home and is suspected to have been kidnapped.

On 26 February 2019, the mother of a Sichuanese human rights defender was dragged and beaten by a group of stability maintenance agents in her residential district in Sichuan province. They were stalking her after she visited various government authorities with another human rights defender, and followed her home after attacking her. They attempted to enter her house and she resisted. However, a couple days later, it was said that stability maintenance agents had moved in to conduct residential surveillance on the eve of the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 23 February 2019, a human rights defender was kidnapped by government personnel and thugs from the Tianning District government while she was petitioning in Beijing Municipality. She was severely beaten up before being transferred to a 'black jail' in Tianning, where she was forbidden from eating or sleeping until she was released 21 days later.

On 14 February 2019, police stormed into the home of the mother of an activist in Chengdu (Sichuan) and took away her three friends and her lawyer with force, hours after she had a meeting with ambassadors from five foreign embassies in Chengdu. She could not be contacted and was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) since.

On 7 December 2018, the mother of a rights defender and her female companion were taken away by police officers and national stability maintenance officers in the Beijing West Railway Station in Fengtai district (Beijing). The two women were not able to be contacted thereafter and are suspected to have been held at the Sichuan government in Beijing. They were followed in Beijing while visiting to attend a civil pretrial conference of the rights defender. The mother was pushed and fell on the floor before they were taken away.

Around 1 December 2018 (beginning of month), the elderly mother of a prominent human rights defender and founder of 64 Tianwang, a website documenting human rights abuses in China, was taken away by personnel from the Sichuan government while she was at Beijing West Railway Station in Fengtai District (Beijing) and has been incommunicado for over a month since. She has been actively advocating for her son's release since his arrest 2 years ago.

On 12 November 2018, two daughters of a deceased workers' rights activist were forced into a police car by Shenyang government representatives in Beijing (Beijing) while on their way from Qianmen Dazhong Hostel in Xicheng district to China Mobile's Beijing office. They were taken to Liujiaoyao Liyuan Hotel, where the representative office of Shenyang government in Bejing was located. Their phones were confiscated when they tried to call the police.

On 18 September 2018, the mother of a petitioner cum victim of a defective rabies vaccine was suspected to have been kidnapped in Yangpu, about two weeks after her daughter's disappearance. She was being followed and surveiled around the clock before her disappearance. As of 19 February 2019, she has been disappeared for 154 days.

On 9 August 2018, a petitioner was detained in a 'black jail' at Shanghai Pattaya Holiday Inn in Yangpu district (Yangpu, Shanghai) for appealing against the forced demolition of her house. During this period, she was violently beaten twice by a security guard, which caused deafness in her left ear. Her elder sister was also beaten.

Around 15 May 2018 (month of), a Kazakh journalist was arrested in Kuytun (Ili, Xinjiang) and detained incommunicado, reportedly in a re-education camp. It was reported that her sister and brother were also detained. She was later sentenced to 19 years at Kunes prison and is likely undertaking forced labour. The reasons for her detention and subsequent sentence are unknown.

On 13 May 2018, two female members of the LGBT community were beaten by 7 to 8 security guards at the 798 Art Zone in Chaoyang District (Beijing), while they were out distributing rainbow badges and flyers to raise awareness about the upcoming International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia on 17 May 2018. The assault happened after a security guard refused to put on the rainbow badge, and got into an altercation with the female LGBT members. One of them were reportedly pushed to the ground during the assault.

On 6 May 2018, a Uyghur woman from Moyu municipality (Hotan, Xinjiang) was detained and sent to either Qaraqash County No. 2 or No. 4 re-education camp. Her current status is unknown and no official reason has been given for her arrest, but the reasons stated on her record discovered in a leaked government file were: being a person who served a prison sentence and later labeled as a danger to public safety due to her role in the 2008 riots in Hotan, being a member of a pan-Islamist fundamentalist organisation, and having relatives who were detained before the 'strike hard' campaign.
On 28 April 2018, the sister of a Uyghur political refugee living in Sweden was sent to re-education centre in Urumuqi, Xinjiang.

Around 16 March 2018 (month of), security guards hired by local authorities used electric batons on a farmer's wife and her sister in Lingchuan Town (Putian, Fujian) and the women were knocked unconscious. The farmer had died in custody a few days ago and the women had gone to the police station and town secretary to bring the farmer's body back for a memorial service.

On 11 March 2018, during the Lianghui conventions, a petitioner's daughter living in Weicheng District (Xianyang, Shaanxi) was sent to take on mandatory vacation by the officials from the Weicheng Sub-district Office. The petitioner had petitioned over the years because his son was attacked by a colleague when he was working for the Thermal Power Company the Third Bureau, but the company refused to compensate, and the perpetrator was not charged.

Around 5 March 2018, the daughter of a rights defender was taken away from Xinyang, Henan and detained in a hotel (a black jail) in Xi County in Xinyang by more than ten police officers from the Xiazhuang Town and the Xiaohuidian Town police stations led by Xi County Police Chief Officer, when she intended to go to Xinyang.

Around 1 March 2018 (beginning of month), a female Uyghur insurance company worker and part-time Mandarin tutor residing in Yining City (Ili Kazakh Autonomous, Xinjiang) was detained in a 'transformation-through-education' facility. Although authorities provided no explicit reasons, the victim had made money transfers to Australia in 2013 to help pay for the house of her parents, who were accused for being 'fleeing terrorists.' Some photos of her wearing headscarves were accused of 'promoting extremism.' She suffered from liver damage in the facility but did not receive 'adequate medical treatment', and was released in Dec 2018. She was arrested again on 9 April 2019 and held in a pre-trial detention center. Her trial was reportedly held in June 2019, and she was finally sentenced for 'funding terrorism' in January 2020. She was released again on 4 September 2020 and admitted to hospital without a reason. After a stay of 'months' she was returned to the detention center.

On 28 February 2018, a petitioner and human rights defender, who had suffered problems with forced demolition and land seizures, went missing in Beijing after having travelled to the city to seek medical advice. Upon arriving in Beijing, she was met by a police officer from her home town, Kunshan (Suzhou, Jiangsu), who asked her to return to Kunshan. She refused to return, and left a note saying if they disappeared then it was because they had been kidnapped by the government. She remained uncontactable as of 1 March 2018.

Around 10 February 2018, a human rights activist was forcibly disappeared from her home in Gaoyou (Yangzhou, Jiangsu). It was reported that she had been tracked and monitored by personnel sent by the police since she applied to listen in the hearing of a lawyer on 31 January 2018 and was not able to be contacted from 10 Feb onwards. On 22 Feb, her son received a call from Gaoyou Police Station confirming that his mother had been detained at the police station.

On 7 October 2020, many education interest groups (current and former LegCo members with DP and LSD, district councillors, teachers, students) held a press conference at the Legislative Council in Central district (Hong Kong) to express their dissatisfaction with the Education Bureau, regarding its decision to deregister a primary school teacher for purportedly promoting a pro-independence stance in his/her teaching materials last year. They called it an act of 'white terror,' signed a joint statement, and held up placards in solidarity.

On 24 April 2019, 200 to 1,000 supporters gathered for a candlelight event outside Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre in Sham Shui Po District (Hong Kong) to show solidarity with the eight of the 'Occupy Central Nine' who were sentenced earlier in the day. Present were four of the convicted - two former student leaders, a Democratic Party member and a Baptist pastor - Joseph Zen of the Catholic Church in Hong Kong, and many pro-democracy political figures and LegCo members, including Claudia Mo, League of Social Democrats Leung Kwok-hung and Labour Party Lee Cheuk-yan. The protesters wore yellow t-shirts with the phrase 'I was not incited,' a reference to the 'incitement to incite' public nuisance charges brought against the sentenced activists.

Around 7 December 2021 (as reported), construction workers went on strike and demonstrated in Guangzhou city (Guangzhou, Guangdong) to demand wage arrears owed by a residential property management company.

On 25 November 2021, a female petitioner and her fellow villager were taken away by police when they passed by the France Embassy in Chaoyang district, Beijing (coded as Beijing - Chaoyang) without a known reason. They were tortured, humiliated, and had their pants forcibly taken off for searching on a car journey before being repatriated to Fuzhou. The next day, the petitioner was detained at a Jin'an government-run 'black jail' in Fuzhou and had remained incommunicado at the time of reporting on 10 December 2021.

Around 24 June 2021 (between 13 June - 4 July), a female petitioner was locked up and tortured at a 'black jail' in the mountain area in Jin'an district (Fuzhou, Fujian). She was abducted on 13 June 2021 for an unknown reason and was dumped in the mountain on 4 July 2021.

On 17 May 2021, two petitioners, who were a married couple, were intercepted by Loufeng Residential District police officers and government officials at Suzhou Railway Station in Gusu district (Suzhou, Jiangsu) while they were about to travel to Beijing to submit a petition. The interceptors pressed on their bodies and stripped their pants, resulting in one of them suffering from fractured bones.

On 10 December 2021, a pro-establishment civil group, Johnny Patriotic 101, protested at the ICAC Headquarters in North Point, Eastern district (Hong Kong)(coded as Hong Kong - Eastern). They opposed a Legislative Council election poll done by the Hong Kong Public Opinion Research Institute that indicated the public's desire to vote in the 'patriots only' election. The group accused the institute of influencing election turnout.

On 4 December 2021, members of Platform of Concerning Subdivided Flats in Hong Kong and subdivided flats tenants rallied outside Sham Shui Po station in Sham Shui Po district, Hong Kong (coded as Hong Kong - Sham Shui Po). They called on the government to plug up four loopholes of the new rent-control law that will come into effect in a month, including fixing the initial rental rate, regulating old contracts, and stronger rental regulations.

On 7 December 2021, members of League of Social Democrats rallied outside the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to protest the setting up of special Hong Kong-mainland border voting stations. They also urged people to 'vote according to their conscience.'

On 9 December 2021, members of a pro-Beijing citizen group, 'Apple Daily Fake News Monitoring Group,' gathered outside the Wanchai Law Courts Building in Wanchai district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Wan Chai) during a court session. They carried signs to protest Apple Daily founder Jimmy Lai, one of the three pro-democracy figures who had been convicted of charges linked to the banned Tiananmen Massacre vigil in 2020.

On 10 December 2021, HKFTU representatives carrying a banner protested outside the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They called on the government to issue consumption vouchers, introduce measures to solve the housing shortage, and resume cross-border travel between the mainland and Hong Kong.

On 10 December 2021, people protested at the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau at Chater Garden in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against the virtual Summit for Democracy held in Washington, accusing the U.S. of intervening Hong Kong affairs. They also condemned 'fugitive' ex-lawmaker Nathan Law, who would speak at the Summit.

On 27 July 2019, 26 Falun Gong petitioners were arrested by the police at a residential house in Zhuyang Residential District, Dazhu County (Dazhou, Sichuan), while studying Falun Gong. Six people of the group were charged with involving cult and detained at custody facilities.

On 9 December 2021, Defend Hong Kong Campaign representatives protested at the Police Headquarters in Wanchai district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Wan Chai) against self-exiled ex-lawmaker Nathan Law for his speech at the virtual Summit for Democracy held by Washington, accusing him of slandering the Central and Hong Kong governments. They called for an investigation on him for encouraging people to cast blank votes in the next legislative election.

On 9 December 2021, people staged a protest and submitted petitions at Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau at Chater Garden in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against the virtual Summit for Democracy held in Washington, calling it a tool for anti-China forces in the West to meddle in domestic affairs in China. They condemned self-exiled ex-lawmaker Nathan Law, who would speak at the Summit, for betraying the country and Hong Kong.

On 12 July 2021, local township government officers and police officers kidnapped a businessman-cum-petitioner living at Shuanggou township (Xiangyang, Hubei) and detained him at a psychiatric hospital in Huangji township. The businessman petitioned about the loss of ownership of his factory. He was transferred to Xiangfan Anding Hospital on 31 August 2021, to Shuanggou Township An Yi Tai Hospital on 14 October 2021, and remained detained as reported on 24 December 2021.

On 19 December 2021, 3 to 4 members of the League of Social Democrats protested outside the Raimondi College polling station in Mid-Levels Central district, Hong Kong (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western), where Chief Executive cast her vote in the 'patriots only' Legislative Council election. They criticized the electoral revamp and urged people to 'vote according to their conscience.'
Around 13 December 2021 (as reported), lorry drivers protested in Ganquan county (Yanan, Shaanxi) to demand wage arrears owed by a logistics company.
Around 19 December 2021 (as reported), workers protested in Nanjing city, Jiangsu (coded to Xuanwu) to demand wage arrears owed by a now-closed construction company.
