On 30 September 2020, a petitioner from Heping district, Shenyang was kidnapped and assaulted by several hired men near the Dadushe Police Station in Dadushe village of Majuqiao town (Tongzhou, Beijing). He was taken into a car with a Liaoning provincial police car plate, and beaten until became unconscious. The victim was admitted to a hospital at Suizhong county (Huludao, Liaoning) but became unconscious again, during which he was transferred by car to the Xingshun police station in Tiexi district of Shenyang prefecture. The victim was detained despite multiple severe internal organ injuries and fractures, and transferred between four police stations in Shenyang without official documentation until release on 6 November 2020.

Around 1 October 2019 (week of), a citizen from Wuyi county (Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province) was abducted from Beijing (no specific location in Beijing reported) because of his petition activities. He was taken by some 'gangsters' hired by the county government of Wuyi and kept in police detention there for at least a week.

Around 14 November 2020 (between 12 November - 16 November), two men from Nianyutao, Jiangqiao sub-district of Gaoxin district of Runzhou district (Zhenjiang, Jiangsu) were beaten by hired personnel at the headquarters of a government-led forced demolition operation in an attempt to coerce them into signing an agreement to the operation. Following their kidnapping on 12 November, they were repeatedly beaten and transferred to various places. One of the men was hospitalised for bone fracture.

On 5 June 2018, a police officer from Zibo City, Shandong was attacked by six assailants outside the Shandong Provincial Public Security Bureau in Shinan District (Qingdao City, Shandong Province). It was reported that the assailants were 'thugs' hired by the director of the Zhoucun District's Public Security Bureau, and the police officer sustained 17 scars on his body. The police officer had attempted to report the director on corruption, bribery and embezzlement of funds. This was the fifth time the police officer had been attacked for the same reason.

On 2 April 2021, a police officer-cum-CPC member under the Huang county (Anyang, Henan) Public Security Bureau tailed by three different cars (identified as 'dark evil forces') while driving in Zhengzhou prefecture (Henan) (coded to Zhongyuan), leading to his car being hit several times. It was purported that the aggressors intended to create a car accident to mask the murdering of the police officer. The officer had been subjected to smearing, isolation, attacks and retaliations since reporting corruption of state leadership to the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection in 2016.

On 2 August 2019, around noon, village officials leading dozens of black-clad men with shields restricted a villager's mobility at his house in Da Tong village of Yancun township in Fangshan District, Beijing, as a practice of forced evictions. In the evening, the black-clad men forced their way into the villager's home, confiscated his properties, and beat him, causing him to be seriously injured and needed to be admitted to a hospital.

On 2 June 2021, a petitioner from Chongqing was beaten by local 'black forces' while visiting Beijing municipality to reflect his demands. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

Around 16 May 2018 (month of), a petitioner from Hubei Qianjiang was kidnapped by some unidentified people hired by the government in You'anmen Residential District in Beijing - Fengtai. It was not clear the reason for the abduction.

On 12 May 2018, a petitioner from Wuhan was intercepted by government officials from Wuhan City while submitting an appeal in Beijing. He was then taken away and repatriated to Wuhan by private security personnel employed by the local government officials. While he was detained at a police station in Changfeng Residential District, Wuhan, a dozen unidentified persons arrived at the police station to transfer the petitioner to a 'black jail.' When the petitioner resisted, the unidentified persons stabbed his left wrist with a knife. Due to his injury, he was instead sent to the hospital where they found two ruptured tendons.

Around 10 March 2019 (between 5 - 15 March), during the annual Lianghui conventions, a female petitioner and her mother living in Changning district (Shanghai) were invaded at their residence by district government-hired 'thugs', and injured. Leading up to the incident, she had been in discussion with the Huayang Rd Sub-district's Head of Petitions, who wanted to convince her to cancel her planned visit to the People's Supreme Court in Beijing. At the time of the attack, she already agreed - in good faith - to cancel her visit to the People's Supreme Court in Beijing, where she had planned to report unlawful procedures and forgery of documents by local officials during a house expropriation case in 2016.

On 6 March 2021, a petitioner from Wanshougonggong village of Dongxihu district (Wuhan, Hubei) and her husband were intercepted on her train ride to Beijing and forced by a group of people (identity unreported) to get off at Shijiazhuang Train Station in Qiaoxi district (Shijiazhuang, Hebei), where they were forcibly returned to a 'black jail' arrangement at Xinhua Hospital in Wuhan. Earlier during the train ride, eight men in casual wear had approached the petitioner and her husband to persuade them out of visiting Beijing during the Lianghui conventions, and men hired by the CPC Secretary of Cihui Subdistrict called from Xinhua Hospital to inquire about their location. Leading up the incident, the petitioner had been receiving treatment at Xinhua for high blood pressure and cerebral hemorrhage since 5 Jan 2021, during which government-hired men appeared and started guarding her ward around the clock, restricting her personal freedom. The petitioner was still held at the hospital as of 15 Mar 2021.

On 24 November 2018, a land rights defender was beaten up by a dozen 'thugs' hired by the local eviction department authorities in Jiangyin county (Wuxi, Jiangsu) after more than 20 of them kidnapped him near Yangjian Town Langxia vegetable market in Xishan district (Wuxi). They forced him to sign an eviction agreement, and when he was released later that night, he had to be treated in Jiangying People's Hospital for brain concussion.

On 12 September 2019, a female petitioner and her son were assaulted by two government officials and six 'thugs' at the Xiangyang Letters And Calls Bureau in Xiangcheng District (Xiangyang City, Hubei Province). It was reported that the female petitioner tried reporting the case to the police, but did not receive any assistance, on the grounds that assault happened due to her petitioning activities.

On 28 March 2018, around 5 unknown individuals (likely to be hired by government officials) beat up a couple near a restaurant in Xiangcheng District (Suzhou, Jiangsu) who were petitioners since 2010 because of their demolished house. Two men pulled the woman's hair and beat her. Her husband was also beaten by other 3-4 men wearing face masks. Their friends called the police, but there was no further update from the police. The couple had been harassed by government employed personnel in the past.

On 3 June 2020, at least three petitioners were taken away from Beibei District (Chongqing) by 20-30 unidentified persons hired by the Chongqing stability maintenance office. While they were being dragged into the car, the group of unidentified persons assaulted several petitioners. The petitioners were subsequently taken to Daxigou police station in Chongqing.

On 12 September 2019, a female activist from Wuhan was beaten up and kidnapped in Donghu, Hongshan, Wuhan in Hubei province by a group of three 'thugs' related to local stability maintenance force, who warned her a day before at her doorstep not to petition until the end of October. They promised her to give her 20,000 RMB if she did not go petitioning, but she rejected. She was locked up in Guandong police station and was allowed to go home on 15 September. She went to the hospital for a check-up.

On 9 March 2021, the son of a petitioner from Wanshougonggong village of Dongxihu district was held in a 'black jail' at Room 904, Black 5 of Kangju II in Cihui subdistrict of Dongxihu district (Wuhan, Hubei) by hired men ('evil forces') working for the CPC Secretary of Cihui Subdistrict of Dongxihu district. Both of his parents had been forcibly held at Xinhua Hospital since 6 Mar to prevent them from petitioning in Beijing during the Lianghui conventions. The son was still detained at the time of reporting on 16 Mar 2021.

On 16 December 2019, the mother of an activist was attacked in her home in Guangshan, Henan, by people hired by the local government. They attacked her with knives, and she sustained injuries in her tendons in both her arms.

On 28 February 2019, six men hired by the Huanggang Subdistrict Office and the Comprehensive Management Commission broke in and beat up a petitioner at his house in Huanggang Subdistrict, Liangxi district (Wuxi, Jiangsu) . Police officers who arrived on scene after an emergency call left after seeing stability maintenance officers in the apartment.

On 2 April 2018, a military veteran was assaulted in Lingyan Mountain in Wuzhong District (Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province) by six to seven local 'ruffians' who were reportedly hired by government officials. The assailants hit the top of his head with a tree branch, and kicked him in the waist. A passer-by attempted to file a police report but was told by the police that the assailants were sent by the local government for 'stability maintenance.' One of his ribs was fractured. It was reported that the military veteran had been placed under surveillance at his own residence by 'thugs' hired by government officials to stop him from petitioning after he was sentenced to six months in prison in 2001.

On 11 February 2022, representatives of the Democratic Party carrying placards staged a demonstration and held a press conference in Hong Kong. They criticized the government for lacking strategies to cope with the coronavirus pandemic and allocate human resources. They urged the government to prioritize high-need Delta variant cases, distribute 15,000 HKD in cash to all citizens, and provide 20,000 HKD to each building to subsidize cleaning expenses during the anti-epidemic period.

On 10 February 2022, members of Kwai Chung Subdivided Flat Residents Alliance demonstrated and held a press conference in Hong Kong. They protested the perceived long-waiting time of public housing allocated to low-income people in Kwai Chung, resulting in extra stress and financial pressure on people. They held placards to express their demands.

On 11 February 2022, DAB lawmakers demonstrated and held a press conference at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They urged the government to seek aid from the Chinese central government amid the coronavirus surge.

Around 16 March 2020 (month of), a detained political dissident (the webmaster of Esuweiji -- a group of doxxing websites focused on President Xi and his relatives) was attacked in police detention in Maoming city, Guangdong (coded to Maonan). According to his lawyer, the victim had stripped, suspended from the ceiling, and his genitals burned with a lighter.

On 12 May 2021, in the evening, the residents of Baoli Xiangxue Community in Shimahe sub-district of Jiangbei district (Chongqing) retaliated after 600 men in black - at least one admitted to being hired by the Yubei district government - occupied the community during the day, and assaulted children and elderly residents indiscriminately. Both sides engaged in a massive fight until the men retreated during the early morning on 13 May. Riot police who stood by outside the community since day time also left. The residents destroyed rooms housing the community office preparatory team and the police, and captured a few of their attackers. Since 2014, the residents of the Baoli Xiangxue Community and the Shimahe sub-district government were in disagreement about the construction of a community office.

Around 15 April 2019 (month of), a woman was violently treated by demolition officials during the forced demolition (government operation) of a garage in Mingjing village of Panyu district (Guangdong, Guangzhou).

Around 15 October 2019 (month of), a detained political dissident (the webmaster of Esuweiji -- a group of doxxing websites focused on President Xi and his relatives) was tortured and resulted in injury to his right hand in police detention in Maoming city, Guangdong (coded to Maonan).

On 18 April 2018, a man was beaten up in Wenfeng District (Anyang, Henan) while defending his home from being demolished by more than 300 people, including law enforcement and police personnel, people from security companies, and 'gangsters.' The man had first climbed onto the roof of his house and was hit with a water gun before being beaten up by the gangsters. He was then detained by police for 10 days.

On 10 February 2022, investors protested outside the headquarters of Cedar Holdings in Huangpu district (Guangzhou, Guangdong) to demand the company repays investors in its wealth management products.

On 12 May 2021, during the day, 600 men in black forcibly broke through the Fifth Door of Baoli Xiangxue Community in Shimahe sub-district of Jiangbei district (Chongqing), and assaulted residents indiscriminately. Caught off-guard, most of the victims were the elderly and children as young and middle-aged adults were at work. Some were dragged into vehicles and taken away. Riot police equipped with storm water cannons lined up outside the community prior to the mass attack, and at least one of the men in black was reported to have been hired as a part-timer by the Yubei district government. Since 2014, the residents of the Baoli Xiangxue Community and the Shimahe sub-district government were in disagreement about the construction of a community office.

On 15 October 2018, a homeowner was beaten up by 20 to 30 members of a demolition team (hired by the government) when he tried to stop them from demolishing his house in Hangji Town (Yangzhou, Jiangsu). Later in the day, in retaliation, the homeowner would drive his car into the demolition team members, causing 3 deaths and 7 injuries.

On 19 April 2018, some ruffians employed by a real estate company assaulted farm villagers in Lanshuicun (Qingcheng District, Qingyuan, Guangdong) while the villagers tried to stop them taking their land. A peasant woman holding a two-years old child was knocked to the ground and lost consciousness. Police were called but refused to take any action. The company had reportedly been working with local government to illegally seizing land from over 600 households in Lanshuicun since 2002. Villager tried to petition to superior governments but faced all sorts of oppression from the local government.

On 28 April 2018, a man was seized, attacked and tortured by a dozen hired 'gangsters' in Rudong (Jiangsu). The man and his wife were driving back from a social gathering and were hit by a surveillance van. The man continued driving despite the accident but was intercepted by another vehicle and attacked by more than a dozen 'gangsters.' The couple's phones were robbed, the man was beaten with an electroshock weapon, and his mouth was restrained with a cloth gag. The man was then dragged into the gangsters' vehicle and taken to an unknown house while continuing to suffer beatings and electric shocks. At the house, his clothes were torn and he was splashed with cold water while forced to lie down on the floor, and his body was stepped on. The gangster said they were sent because of the house demolition and threatened that if he did not sign his consent for compensation agreement for demolition, he would be killed. The man was punched, kicked and slapped until signing a compensation agreement.

On 13 March 2019, a human rights defender from Shanghai was forced to board a train back to Shanghai by police officers after petitioning at the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng (Beijing). She was suspected to have been kidnapped for at least 2 days after arriving in Shanghai Municipality.

On 9 February 2022, a petitioner was pushed and beaten up by a bureau director at the offices of Pizhou Letters And Calls Bureau in Pizhou (Xuzhou, Jiangsu) as he was requesting to close his petition case. He was later arrested by the police and detained for half an hour. The petitioner was a repeated target of arrest, forced disappearance, and prosecution for 18 years due to his petition.

On 9 March 2018, a female petitioner, when on her way back from Beijing where she petitioned for her husband about the Huangpu District Construct and Management Committee, as well as the sub-district office, violating laws and persecuting him, was 'secretly kidnapped' by Shanghai liaison officers and hired 'thugs', then sent on a train and taken to a 'black jail' in Shanghai Qingpu District Qingcheng area.

On 29 May 2018, a disabled petitioner was held incommunicado and under 24 hours of surveillance by 'thugs' hired by the police in a hotel in Beijing. It was part of a national campaign by the authorities to suppress dissidents ahead of the 30th anniversary of Tiananmen Square protests.

On 29 October 2018, 10 petitioners and other 3 people staying in the same hotel were abducted in two hotels around Beijing Yongdingmen Coach Station and Beijing South Railway Station in Beijing - Dongcheng by 14 unidentified 'thugs' who claim to work in Beijing security force. 14 'thugs' broke into their rooms and foced them into a van, and 13 people were beaten and got their phones, ID, and money confiscated by 14 thugs before they were thrown out in the area next to Xingyu bus station.

On 30 August 2021, around four petitioners from Wuhan and Hubei, were kidnapped by government-hired 'thugs' onto two black cars in front of Jianguomen Police Station in Dongcheng district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Dongcheng) after they reported the presence of Wuhan 'black jails' to the Beijing police. They have been held incommunicado since then. Their friend said that they were likely to be sent back to their hometown for illegal detention.

Around 2 December 2020 (as reported), four villagers were pressed on the ground and beaten by village government-hired thugs during a forced eviction operation in Beiguan village of Yingshan sub-district, Guangshui county (Suizhou, Hubei).

On 2 August 2018, a legal rights activist was beaten in the face, chest and abdomen by a police officer and four young 'thugs' at Zhoujiaqiao police station in Changning district, Shanghai before being sent to the 'black jail' at Huangshadao Recreational Fishing Centre for 20 days. They refused to give him access to medical treatment, basic necessities, and placed him under 24-hour surveillance.

On 15 September 2021, on the International Day of Democracy, a man was tracked down to an internet bar by two black-clad men in Yuanjiagang community district of Yuzhong district (Yuzhong, Chongqing). The black-clad men slapped him, beat him up, and kicked him in order to stop him from attending a memorial event at Monument to the people's Liberation in the city center. It was suspected that four members of local government and police officials were behind the attack.

On 21 June 2018, more than 10 unidentified people hired by the local government kidnapped a woman and her son from their house in Yangjiabang of Xishan District (Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province). The woman and son were detained in a 'black jail' under the surveillance by 4 civilians hired by the government. 2 houses owned by the family were demolished immediately by the authorities after they were kidnapped.

Around 30 October 2019 (from 29 - 31 October), a woman was abducted by a group of 'thugs' at the Shenyang North Station in Shenhe District (Shenyang, Liaoning) and threatened and beaten while being detained in the station's lactation room for three days. On 29 October, she was stopped by a group of unknown people while she was about to take the train at the station and was trapped after her wheelchair, luggage and other belongings were all taken away. She had been a target of government's retaliatory measures for filming an anti-government documentary. The incident came amid the upcoming national CCP meeting. She reported to the police but they refused to register the case.

On 29 May 2018, a business woman was attacked by urban management officers and unidentified individuals in Gangzha District (Nantong City, Jiangsu Province), following a dispute between them over the location of a billboard. The urban management officers ordered 7 to 8 'gangsters' to drag the woman on the ground and pulled her on a stone. The officers confiscated her billboard.

On 2 November 2018, Xi'an Gaoxing district ubran management committee deployed thousands of policemen and 'thugs' to demolish the buildings in Xi'an Yuhuazhai village in Yanta district (Xi'an, Shanxi) in the name of forced eviction. During the process, the police and 'thugs' attacked many villagers who came to stop them and also some by-standers.

On 6 February 2022, a few DAB lawmakers protested outside the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They urged the government to extend financial support to more industries in the new round of the Anti-epidemic Fund for the coronavirus pandemic and seek help from the central government for implementing mass testing.

On 6 February 2022, representatives of the Society for Community Organization and low-income citizens demonstrated and held a press conference in Hong Kong. They criticized the government for not doing enough to tackle poverty and urged authorities to offer more subsidies to support those losing their jobs amid the coronavirus pandemic. They carried placards to express their demands.

On 7 February 2022, East Kowloon District Residents' Committee and a lawmaker protested outside the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They carried signs and a banner to express their demands on the 2022-2023 Budget, including re-distributing 10,000 HKD of electronic consumer vouchers to eligible citizens and relaunching an unemployment support scheme.
Around 14 December 2021 (as reported), over 100 taxi drivers went on strike and gathered in Kaiyuan city (Tieling, Liaoning) to protest the presence of unlicensed taxis in the city.

On 25 October 2019, a detained Christian petitioner was transferred from the Zhenjiang city detention facility in Runzhou district (Jingkou, Zhenjiang, Jiangsu) and placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location near Beishan Reservoir in Jurong city, at the People's Armed Forces Department in Dantu District, and at the Weida Driving School in Jungkou district, during which they beat him up. He was then held there for four months without hot water for showering and he would often catch a cold because he had always been very ill. On 27 February 2020, he was transferred back to the Zhenjiang city detention facility.

On 21 June 2018, around 1000 retired Chinese soldiers gathered at the government offices in Runzhou District (Zhenjiang, Jiangsu) to demand answers over the alleged beating of a fellow veteran by government-hired thugs. The demonstrators used bricks and rods to hurt 65 officers and staff in three days. Some spouses of the soldiers were also beaten up by the police.

On 13 October 2021, officials raided a church school in Zhenjiang city, Jiangsu (coded to Runzhou), and arrested over 10 children, three teachers, and three parents to the police station. The children were released shortly afterward, but the parents and teachers remained uncontactable.
Around 26 November 2021 (as reported), delivery workers of Yunda Express protested and went on strike in Zhenjiang city, Jiangsu (coded to Runzhou) to demand wage arrears owed by the company.

Around 22 May 2018 (as reported), up to 100 migrant workers demonstrated in Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, against wage arrears owed to them by a construction company. It was reported that the workers were assaulted during the demonstration by other people working for the company. 5 migrant workers were hospitalised as a result of the assault.
Around 18 April 2018 (as reported), at least a dozen workers of a real estate construction company held a banner at the company site in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu and protested against wage arrears.
Around 9 August 2021 (as reported), workers protested in Zhenjiang city (Jiangsu) (coded to Runzhou) to demand wage arrears owed by a construction company.

Around 5 April 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers protested against wage arrears owed by a construction company in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu. The company owed wages to migrant workers who came from Shanghai and had ran out of all money. They had been in Zhenjiang for nearly a month as a result of owed wages.

Around 9 April 2018 (as reported), at least 5 up to 100 workers gathered and hung up a large banner outside of a hotel in Zhenjiang (Jiangsu) to protest against eight months' worth of wage arrears and pension owed by the hotel.

On 23 June 2018, around 1000 retired Chinese soldiers gathered at the government offices in Runzhou District (Zhenjiang, Jiangsu) to demand answers over the alleged beating of a fellow veteran by government-hired thugs. The demonstrators used bricks and rods to hurt 65 officers and staff in three days.

On 22 June 2018, around 1000 retired Chinese soldiers gathered at the government offices in Runzhou District (Zhenjiang, Jiangsu) to demand answers over the alleged beating of a fellow veteran by government-hired thugs. The demonstrators used bricks and rods to hurt 65 officers and staff in three days.

On 19 June 2018, retired veterans gathered at the Zhenjiang City Hall in Runzhou district to make three economic demands and fight for fair treatment. Unidentified personnel responded with attacks, beatings and tried to suppress the demonstration. No report of hospitalised victims.

On 22 June 2018, retired veterans continued to sit-in at the front of the Zhenjiang City Hall by setting up outdoor camps. Government authorities prevented local residents from delivering water and food supplies, and mobile reception at the demonstration location was blocked to prevent further communication. During the late night, at least 10,000 dispatched policemen carried out a violent dispersion and clearance of the site. Asleep veteran protestors were attacked and arrested, and many had gone missing since then. Unconfirmed online sources reported 3 deaths, 15 severe injuries, over 500 total injuries and many missing.

On 21 June 2018, retired veterans continued to sit-in at the front of the Zhenjiang City Hall by setting up outdoor camps. Government authorities prevented local residents from delivering water and food supplies, and mobile reception at the demonstration location was blocked to prevent further communication. Retired veterans from at least 11 provinces arrived to support the Zhenjiang demonstration, but were stopped by authorities at highway checkpoints.

On 20 June 2018, retired veterans continued to sit-in at the front of the Zhenjiang City Hall by setting up outdoor camps. Government authorities prevented local residents from delivering water and food supplies, and mobile reception at the demonstration location was blocked to prevent further communication. Retired veterans from at least 11 provinces arrived to support the Zhenjiang demonstration, but were stopped by authorities at highway checkpoints.

In May 2019, a 20 meters tall Buddhist Goddess Guanyin statue in Dahebei Ecological Garden Cemetery in Tieling county (Tieling City, Liaoning Province) was altered by the local authorities to save it from being demolished according to the CCP's policy to prohibit the spread of 'feudal and superstitious' activities and reduce outdoor religious objects. The statue's head was re-decorated in the shape of a lotus flower and the renovation took around three months. In the same county, another over-10-meter-tall statue of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in the Junlongquan Cemetery was also covered twice to prevent it from being demolished due to the same campaign.

In March 2019, 14 meeting venues established by a Three-Self church in Xiongguantun Township, Tieling county (Tieling City, Liaoning Province) were shut down by the authorities. The government proclaimed that it had to be done to 'prevent external infiltration' and because 'too many meeting venues cause trouble for management'.

On 19 October 2018, a house church in Yaopu Town, Tieling City (Liaoning) was shut down by local government officials after it refused to join the state-sanctioned Protestant Three-Self Church. This closure follows a meeting of neighbourhood committee employees convened by the United Front Work Department to launch a crackdown on religious home gatherings.

On 18 August 2021, a woman from Gaokeng town (Pingxiang city, Jiangxi Province) was abducted by local government officers at her home after submitting petitions at the Public Complaints and Proposals Administration. She was then held at the psychiatry department at Pingkuang General Hospital in Anyuan district, Jiangxi province, for so-called 'compulsory mental health treatment.' She was denied visits by her friends, forced to take many psychiatric drugs, and subjected to violence when she refused to obey. She was released on 25 August 2021.

On 9 January 2020, a woman petitioner (also a member of Holy Love Fellowship) was taken away by 'interceptors' at Beijing South Railway Station in Beijing - Fengtai and had since disappeared. She was on her way to attend a court hearing of another petitioner's lawsuit. It was also reported that she had been intercepted several times for her petition in Beijing and was previously placed under house arrest.

Around 16 January 2019 (month of), police officers tortured a Kazakh Muslim woman and her 7-year-old daughter during detention in the basement of a police station in Xinjiang province (coded to Shuimogou), with electric shock, impaling nails into their hands, tying them by their hair, and putting needles under their nails. They were detained after the woman's husband in Kazakhstan complained to rights organisations about her condition (after she had been sent to a re-education camp for 15 months after returning to China in 2017, with her passport withheld.)

On 15 October 2018, officers from Hushan Village Police Department together with a group of unidentified people broke into the house of a female petitioner, her sister and her mother in Hushan village of Guangshan county (Xingyang, Henan). They used cooking knives and sticks to attack three women and sprayed a drug potion on them, took them away, and confiscated some of their properties.

On 6 March 2019, a female petitioner from Liangxi district, Wuxi was carried away from her rental accommodation in Beijing, and thrown into a car by four 'thugs' hired by liaison officers. They stomped on her and took her phone away. She was not allowed to seek medical help.

On 22 May 2021, police and officials intercepted a couple from Fan village in Beijing municipality during their long-lasting petition journey in the capital. Police transferred and detained the couple in hostels and sightseeing areas in Fan village of Hein county, Shanxi, where the female petitioner was hit and injured by the police. As reported on 21 August 2021, the couple had been detained for almost 90 days.

On 21 October 2021, a female forced eviction petitioner was beaten up by local government personnel from Xinjiekou Residential District at Xuanwu district (Nanjing, Jiangsu), causing her to suffer from neck injuries and fractured coccyx and breastbone. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance before the sixth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee in Beijing.

Around 17 March 2018 (between 9 March - 25 March), a female petitioner was covered with a duvet, pushed around, physically abused by a group of men in the Jianxin Police Department in Cangshan District (Fuzhou, Fujian), and later she was abused by these men again in the Fuzhou Detention Center No.406 detention room. The female petitioner was taken to the Jianxin Police Department by a group of plain-clothes police officers on 9 March 2018 because she previously petitioned over the forced eviction.

On 24 September 2021, a female petitioner from Wuhan, Hubei, was intercepted by Wuhan stability maintenance officers and Beijing private security in Beijing. On the next day, she was escorted back to Wuhan and forcibly admitted to the psychiatric ward of Wuhan Hanyang Hospital. On 2 October 2021, the police arrested 10 of her supporters, attempting to rescue her from the hospital.

On 4 August 2020, a female petitioner (and employee of farmland management enterprise) was assaulted at the Public Security Bureau in Xushui district (Baoding, Hebei). She was kicked, tripped, slapped, and her clothes were torn. She was one of 39 people arrested that day after submitting a petition to the the Public Security Bureau.

On 3 September 2018, a female petitioner was severely beaten up by 5 to 6 people hired by stability maintenance forces of Suzhou in Suzhou (Jiangsu) (coded to Gusu) while she was on her way to petition in Beijing. She was severely injured and sent to a hospital.

On 8 November 2021, a female petitioner was taken away by 5-6 unknown people in her neighbourhood in Jiangyan district (Taizhou, Jiangsu) ahead of a court hearing that she sued against the Hai'an environmental department. The petitioner, her husband, and two older adults of her family had become incommunicado as reported on 9 November 2021, resulting in the court hearing being cancelled.

On 2 November 2018, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Liangxi district (Wuxi, Jiangsu) was taken away by around 8 'gangsters' led by Yangming Residential District officers. She was guarded in Room 101 of 61 Jinguiyuan residential estates for 9 days, during which she called the police many times but had no active response from the police. She had been subjected to detention and interception since 2011 due to her petitioning.

On 8 March 2018, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Liangxi district (Wuxi, Jiangsu) was taken away by around 8 'gangsters' led by Yangming Residential District officers. She was guarded and under close surveillance in Room 101 of 61 Jinguiyuan residential estates for 13 days. She had been subjected to detention and interception since 2011 due to her petitioning.

On 8 August 2020, a female petitioner from Chongqing was sent to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' in Fengtai district after being taken away by the police at Beijing Railway Station in Beijing - Dongcheng. The incident was reported to be part of a series of interception and detentions to prevent politically-motivated travels to Beijing during the Beidaihe convention in Qinhuangdao prefecture (Hebei).

On 19 March 2019, a female teacher from Haimen, Jiangsu was intercepted and beaten by many unidentified 'thugs' while she was boarding a bus at Taoranqiao North Bus Station in Beijing - Xicheng. She was carrying documents on behalf of the Ministry of Education and All-China Federation of Trade Unions, and on her way to submit her appeal to the National Letters and Calls Bureau. While they were driving her to the police station in Yuelai town (Jiangsu), she was coerced into urinating in front of all the men. She was interrogated for more than two hours by more than 10 people (including the chief of the police station and the secretary of the local government). At Taoranqiao North Bus Station, a fellow petitioner tried calling the police, but was also beaten up by five to six unidentified persons. The female teacher reportedly sustained bruises to her arms and right calf.

On 15 May 2018, a woman was beaten by police at a police station in Baqiao town, Dadukou district (Chongqing) for questioning related to her partner, who was held in custody for his activism related to an environmental group, Green Leaf Action. She was slapped by the police several times during the 20 hours of interrogation when she was repeatedly asked by police to produce a written summons.

On 24 February 2021, a woman was beaten up by several black-clad men in the stairwell of the administrative hall in Zhongya Building on Renhe St. in Yuzhong district (coded to Chongqing-Yuzhong) after being denied entry to Chongqing No.5 Intermediate People's Court during security inspections. When they reported the incident to the police, they explained that the matter was out of their hands as they were not as powerful as the courts.

On 8 March 2021, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Xiaoshan district (Hangzhou, Zhejiang) was intercepted by officers in a queue outside the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Xicheng) and kidnapped onto a car where the officers broke her fingers. After being escorted back to her hometown, she was hospitalized until 11 March 2021 and placed under eight days of administrative detention.

On 12 September 2018, a female petitioner was kidnapped by the officials from the Jiangsu representative office in Beijing and three 'gangsters' at Yongdingmen West No. 20 bus station in Beijing - Dongcheng while she was in the process of petitioning at the State Bureau for Letters and Calls. Leaving all her belongings behind, she was illegally detained at Room 102 of Jinghua Hotel in Fengtai district (Bejing). She was subsequently repatriated to Jiangyi City, Jiangsu where she was placed under house arrest.

On 27 February 2018, a female petitioner was beaten to unconsciousness by Nanmu Village Secretary in a restaurant in Yuanzhou (Yichun City, Jiangxi) while the village secretary and two other colleagues of demanded her stop further petitioning. She had just been taken back to Yichun by the same people from Nanchang on 26 February 2018 on her way to Beijing. After the assault, she was sent to the hospital by local police.

On 16 October 2021, a disabled female petitioner from Changchun, Jilin, went missing and became incommunicado at Changchun Railway Station in Kuancheng district (Changchun, Jilin) at the night she was planning to travel to Beijing to petition at the Central Military Commission. Earlier the night, she was called by the police several times to instruct her not to go petitioning.

On 26 October 2020, a female petitioner from Hongkou, Shanghai was captured by an unreported group of people near the Great Hall of the People in Beijing - Xicheng. She was escorted back to Shanghai, but her circumstances had remained unknown at the time of reporting on 29 Oct 2020. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance in relation to the fifth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee that had commenced in Beijing.

On 31 May 2021, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Xiaoshan district (Hangzhou, Zhejiang) was held captive and attacked by government officers at a service station in Yixing city, Jiangsu, leaving her being severely injured and sent to Shaw Hospital for surgery. Government officers first intercepted her in Fengtai district, Beijing, on 29 May 2021 and escorted her back to her hometown. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 19 March 2018, during the Lianghui conventions, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Qiaokou DIstrict (Wuhan, Hubei) was sent to a 'black jail' in Wuhan City (Hubei), and the 'black jail' was guarded by 7-8 people hired by the Secretary of the Qiaokou District Liujiao Stree Sub-district. They confiscated her ID and was not given food for at least five days. It was reported that as a result of the lack of food, her vision became blurry and she started feeling the effects of high blood pressure and heart disease, and her head and eyes also hurt, but she had no medication.

On 4 March 2021, a female petitioner was beaten up by 'evil forces' hired by the Hanzheng Residential District Government of Qiaokou District (Wuhan, Hubei) while detained at Wucheng Zhuanshi Hotel 'black jail' (in the mentioned Residential District). She became unconscious and was left unattended without basic sustenance for two days. She was released on 17 Mar 2021.

On 24 April 2018, a petitioner from Wanshougonggong village of Dongxihu district - now living in Qiaokou district (Wuhan, Hubei) - was sent to a 'black jail' by hired men ('evil forces') working for the CPC Secretary of Cihui Subdistrict of Dongxihu district. During her detention, the men forced her into signing an eviction agreement on behalf of her family. She was held at a 'black jail' for 112 days.
On 14 March 2019, a female petitioner was intercepted by local authorities in Beijing and put in a 'black jail' in Shenxi Village in Jiangyin, Jiangsu.

On 15 February 2022, nine labor unions in the catering sector protested separately and submitted petitions outside the Government Headquarters in Admiralty, Hong Kong - Central and Western. They urged the government to extend financial support to the catering sector in the Anti-epidemic Fund to relieve the workers' financial burdens during the coronavirus pandemic. Protesting groups included The Federation of Hong Kong Food & Beverage Industries Trade Unions (affiliated with HKFLU), 'Federation of Chinese and Western Catering,' Association of Hong Kong Employees in Wine, Spirit and Food Shops and Super-Mar (affiliated with HKFLU), and The Roast and Dried Meat and Catering Professionals Association (affiliated with HKFLU).

On 13 February 2022, the Society for Community Organization representatives demonstrated and held a press conference in Hong Kong, demanding 'timely anti-epidemic allowance' and 'short-term unemployment and underemployment assistance' in the 2022/23 Hong Kong Budget in light of the difficult time with the more severe 5th wave of the coronavirus pandemic. They carried placards and a banner to urge the government to distribute a million HKD to the poor.

Around 15 January 2022 (month of), many nomadic Tibetans were arrested in Likhog town near Luhuo (also known as Drago) county (Ganzi, Sichuan) and sent to labor camps, including a camp in Thangnagma, after being found with deemed politically inappropriate content in their mobile phones. Security measures had been strengthened throughout Tibet ahead of the Beijing Winter Olympics.

Around 16 February 2022 (as reported), protesters carrying placards held a demonstration in Yueyang city, Hunan (coded to Yueyanglou). They demanded the government's investigation into the case of the mother of eight children, who was found chained in a freezing outbuilding in Feng county, Xuzhou. The case sparked a wave of public outrage over rampant human trafficking on the internet.

On 7 March 2018, a female petitioner was detained a 'black jail' in a four-storey building located in a valley of the 3303 military industrial district in Jiangxia district (Wuhan, Hubei), and disciplined after all her clothes were taken off. Her supervisors were allegedly government-hired farmers who spoke with a Honghu district accent, claiming to be sent by the 'Legal Education Base of the Six Central-Southern Provinces.' She was intercepted in Beijing and escorted back to her hometown under the orders of the Wuchan Petitioning Bureau. She was repeatedly tortured until her release on 17 Oct 2018.

On 23 May 2018, a female petitioner was tied to a bed and assaulted while detained at a 'black jail' in a four-storey building located in a valley of the 3303 military industrial district in Jiangxia district (Wuhan, Hubei). Her supervisors were allegedly government-hired farmers who spoke with a Honghu district accent, claiming to be sent by the 'Legal Education Base of the Six Central-Southern Provinces.' They pressed against her and scrubbed her face with a plastic slipper until she bled. She was repeatedly tortured while abducted between 7 Mar and 17 Oct 2018.

On 10 September 2018, a female petitioner was subjected to suffocation while detained at a 'black jail' in a four-storey building located in a valley of the 3303 military industrial district in Jiangxia district (Wuhan, Hubei). Her supervisors were government-hired farmers who spoke with a Honghu district accent, claiming to be sent by the 'Legal Education Base of the Six Central-Southern Provinces.' They burnt fuel outside while using an exhaust fan to direct fumes into her compartment, sealing off all doors and windows with blankets. She was repeatedly tortured while abducted between 7 Mar and 17 Oct 2018.

On 13 March 2018, a petitioner who had been detained in a black jail in Fengtai District, Beijing (coded to Beijing - Fengtai) the previous day was transferred to a black jail in Shanghai by a staff of the Shanghai Pudong District Kangqiao Town government and some 'gangsters.' Her food was poisoned during her detention there until 27 March 2018.

On 28 February 2019, a petitioner from Beihe Village, Gansu Province and her 10-year-old daughter were taken from their home in Bejing to the Huangcun Police Station in Daxing District (Beijing) by police officers and government personnel. They were incommunicado thereafter and are suspected to have been kidnapped.

Around 14 October 2020 (between 14 - 15 October), a female petitioner from Xinglong sub-district was beaten and tortured by government-hired 'thugs' while illegally detained at 188 Xinglong Dajie, Jianye district (Nanjing, Jiangsu). She sustained injuries to her right leg while restricted to a room adjacent to the Xinlong Sub-District Office. On 14 Oct, authorities had intercepted her in Beijing for petitioning and released her home, but she was forced to visit to a coronavirus testing centre the next day. She was then isolated despite negative results, and remained detained at the time of reporting on 19 Oct 2020.

On 4 March 2018, a female petitioner was beaten by 4 'thugs' employed by the local government at her home in Luyang District (Hefei, Anhui) for the reason of 'stability maintenance.' She was severely injured with 2-6 fractured ribs and subarachnoid haemorrhage, but was only hospitalised on 11 March because the government employed people kept bringing her back from hospital. People from the local government offices denied connection with the gangsters. She reported to the police but the police refused to intervene.

On 20 September 2021, three petitioners from Qianjiang city, Hubei, including two women, were kidnapped by about 100 people, including a CCP officer of their village, onto a car outside the Heyi Police station in Fengtai District, Beijing (coded as Beijing - Fengtai), after they had attempted to escape from petition interceptors throughout the day. They were beaten up on the car journey before being dumped at Dongtan village, Qianjiang.

Around 31 October 2019 (end of month), a female petitioner from Fujian Province was beaten by government employees and government employed 'thugs' in Beijing when she was on a trip in Beijing with her father. She was then taken back to Pingnan (Fuzhou, Fujian). There was no further report on this event.

On 28 October 2018, a woman petitioner was abducted and detained by a policeman from Pudong police department Hangtou office and 2 'gangsters' at Hangtou police office in Pudong district (Shanghai) (coded to Pudong New Area) while China International Import Expo was held in Shanghai.

On 24 September 2021, a female teacher from Zhangjia Yanxia village, Shandong, went missing and became incommunicado after sending the last message on the phone. She had been subjected to detention and interception since October 2018 due to her petitioning.

Around 28 August 2021 (week of), a single mother was beaten up in Nanle (Puyang, Henan) by 4-5 men ordered by the office director at the offices of the National Health Commission, as she tried to petition regarding the death of her 12-year-old daughter after having a coronavirus vaccine.

On 14 February 2022, a disabled petitioner-cum-forced evictee was intercepted by unidentified people at a crossroad in the Ninghua Residential District of Taijiang district (Fuzhou, Fujian). Despite a police presence, he was taken away and then held at no.147, a premise opposite to Huanxi Police Station. The incident was likely a case of stability maintenance ahead of the upcoming Lianghui conventions 'Two Sessions' to be held in Beijing.

Around 16 March 2018 (month of), a female petitioner was beaten by government employed 'ruffians' while she was detained in a hotel room in Fuping county (Weinan, Shaanxi). The petitioner were taken on 28 February 2018 when she and her husband were called to the town government office to discuss their case. 4-5 government employed ruffians kidnapped them to a hotel, and shortly after that they took her to another hotel in Fuping county and detained her there until 31 March 2018 when she was sent back home. It was reported that the female petitioner was beaten several times, and once she fainted after one of the ruffians pushed her to the floor and stepped on her head. It was also reported that, during her detention, she had a blood sample taken and felt numbness in her hands after eating some meals brought by the guards.

On 18 September 2019, more than 10 people who self-claimed to be police broke into the home of a female CCP distinguished party member in Xihongmenzhen, Daxing, Beijing and took her away in a police car. She was incommunicado since then. Her phone was confisticated.

On 27 July 2019, a female petitioner was abducted and beaten up by 'thugs' hired by village leaders in Xinxin village, Qianjiang. She was then transferred to Yonglin village, where she was subjected to violence, forced prolonged positioning, and 24 hours surveillance intending to force her to sign a house demolition agreement. She was detained for 101 days and finally set free on 5 November 2019.

On 5 March 2019, a petitioner from Chenzhuang Village, Hewu Town, Henan and her daughter were kidnapped by officials from the Hewu Township Government while they were in Songzhuangzhen Town in Tongzhou District (Beijing). They were brought to the Hewu Town Police Station and were incommunicado thereafter.

On 10 September 2020, citizens (including district councillors, People Power and LSD representatives) gathered at the Lai Chi Kok detention centre in Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) to protest in solidarity with the arrested Vice-Chairman of People Power. They shouted slogans and held up placards.

On 11 February 2022, two women who attempted to report a case at a police office in Sunlou township, Feng county (Xuzhou, Jiangsu), were detained for some days, during which one of them was attacked by police officers. The victim was beaten, forcibly suffocated with a laptop bag, and interrogated for long hours until the police released both of them on 16 February 2022. They initially traveled to a hospital in Feng county trying to visit a human trafficking victim, who went viral online after being filmed chained in a freezing outbuilding in Feng county. This incident caused public outrage calling for investigation. However, they were blocked from entering the site and had their mobile briefly confiscated.

On 14 February 2022, over 100-200 students, including around 30 black-clad students' union (SU) members, held a 'parting ceremony' and rallied at the City University of Hong Kong in Hong Kong - Kowloon City on the last day of the SU's eviction notice. They protested against the university for taking back the SU's premises and demanded freedom of thought and academic autonomy at the university. Many students staged a walk, chanted slogans, and painted phrases, including '[we will] not yield a single step' and 'resist till the end' at the entrance of a store the SU operated.

On 24 February 2022, 16-20 residents walked out of their rooms at the Penny's Bay quarantine center in Hong Kong - Islands to protest the isolation camp's chaotic arrangements and the delay of their scheduled release. After a 4-hour protest, they were allowed to leave after medical staff verified that they were all qualified to be released.

On 21 February 2022, over 100 drivers from ride-hailing platform T3 went on strike and demonstrated at a depot in Huqiu district (Suzhou, Jiangsu) to demand car rent reduction. The protest came as the ride-hailing platform refused to reduce car rent or end contracts with the drivers whose incomes were significantly impacted by the coronavirus pandemic.
Around 21 February 2022 (as reported), over 100 taxi drivers protested in Tianjin City (Tianjin) to demand fuel subsidies for the industry.

On 19 February 2022, a petitioner, who was admitted to a hospital, was abducted by the deputy director of Qingdao Public Security Bureau Shibei Branch and his people from the hospital in Cangzhou city, Hebei (coded to Yunhe). He was transferred to a hotel on 77 Heilongjiang S Rd, Shibei District, Qingdao, and was deprived of food for over 50 hours. Prior to the abduction, he had just been released from arbitrary two-year detention in Qingdao as he insisted on submitting a petition.

actor1: Police Forces of China (2012-) People's Armed Police
notes: Around 20 November 2021 (week of), two Tibetan men were arrested by the armed police force in Litang county (Ganzi, Sichuan) and transferred to the Shangri-La Public Security Bureau. They became uncontactable for three months as of the time of reporting on 22 February 2022.

On 18 February 2022, a dissident was kidnapped by a few unidentified men in Dalingxin village in Xixiangtang District (Nanning, Guangxi) and became incommunicado. It was suspected that his forced disappearance was due to his activism calling for an investigation into the case of a human trafficking incident where a woman was filmed chained in a freezing outbuilding in Feng county, Xuzhou. This incident has gone viral online after her video was released and caused public outrage calling for investigation.

On 2 March 2018, a man was taken from his barber shop in Ranyizhen (Ya'an, Sichuan) by four local CCP leaders, government employees and more than 10 'thugs.' The man was beaten in a car with his head covered and was taken to a flat owned by the village committee to be detained until 2 April 2018 when he was repatriated to his shop by some thugs. During his detention, the sister and niece of the man went to CCP leaders to ask for his whereabouts and got beaten by some thugs as well. Similar abduction happened to the man in 2017 and lasted for 47 days. Reason for the abduction was to prevent him from petitioning in Beijing.

Around 15 April 2018 (month of), an Uyghur man from Anju (Mayaqdong) village in Moyu (Karakax) county (Hotan, Xinjiang) was sent to a camp by the authorities. As of 2017-2018, he was listed as belonging to the WASFRY group, or 'endangering (state) security released persons,' after being released from his first detention.

On 30 December 2020, patriotic citizen group 'Johnny Patriotic 101' staged a sit-in and protested overnight at the Court of Final Appeal in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western) ahead of the trial of media mogul Jimmy Lai, calling for the decision regarding his bail release to be redacted. They held up a banner and chanted slogans.

On 24 December 2020, a small number of citizens held a candlelight vigil gathering outside the Shatin Town Hall in Shatin district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Sha Tin) to 'commemorate the death of Hong Kong,' particularly the families of activists and protesters who were detained or extradited to mainland China. They sang the anti-ELAB anthem and other Christmas carols. Similar gatherings in at least three other districts were seemingly cancelled due to forewarned police presence. Two young men were arrested around the Town Hall for possession of slingshots and BB guns (participation in gathering was not reported).

On 10 December 2020, at least 10 female petitioners from Shanghai held up placards outside Beijing South Railway Station in Fengtai District (Beijing) (coded as Beijing-Fengtai) to protest against the Shanghai government's violation of their right to petition, subjecting them to persecution, torture, abductions and abuse for years. It was reported that two of them were later detained at Youwaidongzhuang 90 Relief Centre 'black jail' on the same day.

On 9 December 2020, citizens protested at the Facebook office headquarters in Quarry Bay, Eastern district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Eastern) after the social media platform shut down a self-claimed patriotic 'SaveHK' Facebook group without notice or explanation.

On 7 December 2020, supporters gathered and held up the hand gestures for the five demands outside the Eastern Magistrates' Courts in Eastern district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Eastern) as a sign of protest in support of 10 accused suspects, who were tried for 'conspiracy to harm police officers illegally and maliciously' during the anti-ELAB demonstrations. They also shouted slogans.

On 2 December 2020, hundreds of people gathered at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts in Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Sham Shui Po) to show solidarity with three pro-democracy activists-cum-former Demosisto members. They protested against the length of prison sentences handed down to them. They shouted slogans and raised the hand gesture for five demands. Around 100 police officers attempted to disperse the crowds but did not otherwise intervene. Another small group of pro-Beijing protesters held banners and signs urging for a heavy sentence for the 'serious offenders who harmed Hong Kong.'

On 30 November 2020, citizens gathered at Prince Edward MTR station in Yau Tsim Mong district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Yau Tsim Mong) to commemorate the 15th month anniversary of the '8.31 Prince Edward MTR Incident' (part of the anti-ELAB demonstrations), where they believed demonstrators had died as a result of the police's use of force. They placed flowers outside the station as a sign of protest, and shouted slogans like 'Hong Kong, add oil!' and raised awareness about alleged police brutality during several anti-ELAB demonstration events.

On 29 November 2020, several citizens hiked to Amah Rock, Shatin district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Sha Tin) to protest in solidarity on the 100th day of detention of the 12 fugitives, arrested in mainland China while fleeing for Taiwan (all facing charges related to their involvement in the anti-ELAB movement). They lit up an electronic signboard that said 'SAVE 12' as a sign of protest.

On 21 November 2020, four labour sector concern group members protested outside a polling centre at the Home Affairs Department Mei Foo Community Hall, Lai Chi Kok, Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Sham Shui Po) against the Labour Department for qualifying pro-democracy candidates, who had allegedly 'breached' the national security law, for the Labour Advisory Board's election of employee representatives. They held up pickets and a banner.

On 19 November 2020, citizens gathered at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts in Cheung Sha Wan, Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Sham Shui Po) to show solidarity with three former and current pro-democracy legislators on trial for throwing foul-smelling objects during a Legislative Council meeting. They held up placards that called the accusations an act of 'political oppression.'

On 12 November 2020, citizens demonstrated on a footbridge near the Cross Harbour Tunnel, opposite Polytechnic University in Hung Hom, Kowloon City district (Hong Kong) [coded as Hong Kong-Kowloon City] on the one-year anniversary of the siege of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University during the anti-ELAB demonstrations last year. They used locks to spell out the slogans 'Liberate Hong Kong' and 'SAVE 12' (the latter referring to 12 anti-ELAB fugitives intercepted in mainland waters while fleeing for Taiwan). More anti-ELAB phrases were written on the locks themselves.

actor1: Government of China (2017-) Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
notes: Non-violent activity: On 12 November 2020, 15 pro-democracy legislators (from DP, CP) announced their resignations, as an act of protest against the Hong Kong government's decision the day before to disqualify four other pro-democracy legislators. On 11 November 2020, around 10 people held a silent sit-in protest outside the Shatin Town Hall, Shatin district (Hong Kong) [coded as Hong Kong-Sha Tin] on the one-year anniversary of the siege of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University during the anti-ELAB demonstrations last year. They held up lit-up smartphones, a yellow umbrella and the hand gestures for the five demands. While around 10 police officers arrived to check the press passes of reporters, a man shouted slogans to 'disband the police.'

On 10 November 2020, a large group of media industry workers and journalists, RTHK Programme Staff Union, Hong Kong Journalists Association, pro-democracy activists and many political groups (former legislators and current district councillors, DP, LSD, ADPL) gathered at the Fanling Magistrates' Courts in Fanling, North district (Hong Kong) [coded as Hong Kong-North] to show in solidarity with an RTHK producer arrested for her documentary on the '7.21 incident,' a mob attack targeting anti-ELAB demonstrators on 21 July 2019. They shouted slogans and held up banners that called for the truth behind the incident. They also held up placards that said 'stand up for journalists' and 'journalism is not a crime.'

On 8 November 2020, student group St Politicism organised a street counter in Causeway Bay, Wanchai district (Hong Kong) [coded as Hong Kong-Wan Chai] to commemorate the one-year death anniversary of a student protester, who fell to his death during an anti-ELAB demonstration last year. They held up placards with his name, and the slogans 'just want to be happy' and 'justice is yet to be served.'

On 5 November 2020, at least four people from two pro-establishment citizen groups ('Love HK Alliance' and 'Monitoring DQ Councilors Alliance') protested at the Legislative Council, Central district (Hong Kong) to urge the LegCo chair to prevent filibustering by pro-democracy legislators from obstructing the passing and voting of bills in the Legislative Council. They held up banners, placards and the SAR flag (location coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western).

On 2 November 2020, a pro-establishment citizen group ('Tong Sum Wu Gong') rallied outside the Department of Justice on Queensway, Central district (Hong Kong) for the Department to appeal a district court decision to acquit seven anti-ELAB demonstrators of rioting during a demonstration on 31 Aug in the previous year. They held up banners, placards and caricatures (location coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western).

notes: Arrests: Around 1 November 2020 (between 31 Oct and 2 Nov), the police arrested eight pro-democracy politicians, including four DP lawmakers, two members of the Labour Party, and former legislators from the LJL and PP in Hong Kong, over scuffles with security guards. Around 28 October 2020 (between 23 October and 3 November), the mother of an underaged rape victim was subjected to torture while she was administratively detained at the Public Security Bureau of Yunyang county (Chongqing). She was transferred to the Bureau from Beijing by public security officers and officials from the petitioning offices of Yunyang county, Panlong town and her residential district on 23 October 2020, and detained until 3 November 2020. On 24 October 2020, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Qiaokou district, Wuhan was intercepted in Beijing Municipality by police officers from Qiaokou's Changfengjie Police Station and escorted back to Wuhan by car, where she was 'illegally detained' at a 'black jail' by police officers until 4 Nov. On 9 October 2020, a petitioner from Wuxi, Jiangxi was strangled and beaten by a public security officer and interceptors while being chased from outside the National Bureau of Letters and Calls in Xicheng District (Beijing) (coded as Beijing-Xicheng), where he was filing a petition against his local government after escaping from house arrest. He was taken to Jinghua Hotel, then escorted back to Wuxi by hired workers. He was charged for 'provoking troubles,' and resumed being under house arrest.

Property destruction: On 7 September 2020, authorities demolished a Three-Self church in Dingyuan county (Chuzhou, Anhui) for having 'illegal gatherings.'

On 21 August 2020, at least three citizens protested outside of the West Kowloon Magistrate' Courts in Cheung Sha Wan, Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) during the criminal intimidation trial of Apple Daily founder and media mogul Jimmy Lai, and accused him of colluding with the US government and 'selling out Hong Kong.'

Property destruction: Around 16 August 2020 (month of), officials removed a small cross and a signboard 'Salvation Church' from a state-run Protestant church in Ganzhou prefecture (Jiangxi) (coded to Zhanggong) for being too eye-catching.

Around 15 August 2020 (month of), the priest of Yongshan Miaozu (Miao ethnic group) Church and his parents were taken away by the police in Zhaotong prefecture (Yunnan) and held in secret detention. The exact reason for the disappearance was not known, although the priest's last post on social media on 29 Jul expressed a request to authorities to leave his family alone should he be 'arbitrarily sentenced.' Around 14 August 2020 (month of), a female Tibetan herder-cum-detainee was hospitalized in Biru (Driru) county (Nagqu, Tibet) amidst her detention, 'badly bruised' and unable to speak. She was first taken into custody in June along with her cousin, both for sending religious books to India and having a history of promoting Tibetan culture, language and identity. She died two days after her hospitalization on 16 August 2020.

Land seizure: On 7 August 2020, the county government merged a state-run Three-Self church in Linquan county (Fuyang, Anhui) with another church venue for 'disobeying the government,' 'being too close to a school,' and 'because the building was dilapidated.' They seized the building and took away donation money amounting to 420,000 RMB and all belongings.

Property destruction: On 2 August 2020, police officers and government officials raided a house church in Luyi county (Zhoukou, Henan), confiscating eight Bibles and destroying 60 wooden benches on the pretext that house churches 'were illegal' as they go against the Communist Party.

On 17 July 2020, at least 4 members of the group 'Tuen Mun Concern Group' demonstrated at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) against the Hong Kong Autonomy Act signed by the US President, and against US intervention with China and Hong Kong's internal affairs.

Property destruction: Around 16 July 2020 (month of), the United Front Work Department locked up a state-run Catholic church in Hedong district (Linyi, Shandong) after removing its cross and signage that said 'Catholic Church' and 'Creator of All Things' at its entrance.

Property destruction: Around 16 July 2020 (month of), the county government demolished a Three-Self church in Yutai county (Jining, Shandong) after claims that the church was too close to the village committee building and that 'believing in Jesus meant going against the Communist Party.'
