On 6 June 2018, a group of people from 'New Millenarian' demonstrated outside the Legislative Council in Central, Hong Kong, demanding LegCo members to respect public opinion and pass the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link (Co-location) Ordinance.

On 5 June 2018, a female former employee of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China was taken by the police in Beijing to Jiujingzhuang Petition Service Centre, then handed over to officers from the Hunan Liaison Office, and detained at a black jail in Beijing. It was reported that she had been protesting against the 'fraudulent' employee buyout package offered by the bank since 2004.

On 4 June 2018, an underground Protestant church, the Early Rain Covenant Church, in Qingyang District (Chengdu, Sichuan) was stormed by hundreds of police from Chengdu's Caoshijie police station and officials from the religious affairs bureau, before a planned evening service to commemorate the Tiananmen Square anniversary. When a preacher tried to stop the police, the police got hold of him, pinched his neck and body, pushed him against a glass, slapped him around the head and attacked his cheek and forehead. A few church members were also beaten by the police. A total of 17 church members, including 4 preachers, were arrested on the ground of 'illegal assembly' and released on the next day.

On 4 June 2018, more than 100 people in total gathered in different parts of Tsim Sha Tsui (Yau Tsim Mong District, Hong Kong) to commemorate the 29th anniversary of the Tiananmen demonstrations on 4 June 1989. Between 10 and 100 people, including local citizens and foreigners, gathered at the Square of the Freedom Fighter for an English memorial event organised by an activist. Dozens of police were present at the scene but were not reported to have intervened. Meanwhile, more than 10 pro-Hong Kong independence protesters held a flag that read 'Hong Kong independence' in the Star Ferry Pier.

On 3 June 2018, an activist from Suining county was 'taken on mandatory vacation' by Suining county law enforcement and government officials - the police, the Party Secretary of the Political and Legal Commission and guobao state security officers - from his residence in Zhongxinxiaoqu of Changsha prefecture (Hunan) due to the stability maintenance before the 29th anniversary of the Tiananmen demonstrations on 4 June 1989. He was taken to Shaoshan City, Zhangshu Village of Xiangyin County, Changle Village of Miluo City and Changsha City before returning to Suining County on 8 June 2018. His phone was confiscated during the journey.

On 3 June 2018, more than 10 artists took part in a bike ride from Lok Fu to the CCCD Artspace 'Green Wave Art' in Yau Ma Tei (Yau Tsim Mong, Hong Kong) to commemorate the 29th anniversary of the Tiananmen demonstrations on 4 June 1989. Bikes carried banners that read 'never forget 4 June 'and 'Democracy, freedom, civil rights'.

Around 3 June 2018 (between 31 May - 6 June), three dissidents and one female dissident-cum-journalist were 'taken on mandatory vacation' by the police in Beijing due to the stability maintenance before the 29th anniversary of the Tiananmen demonstrations on 4 June 1989. One was taken to Huangshan City in Anhui and then placed under house arrest back in Beijing on 5 June. Another was taken to Harbin City in Heilongjiang and then transferred to Jilin Province. Another was taken to Guizhou Province, and last reported in Changsha, Hunan Province. It was reported that the extension of their 'vacation' after 4 June might be due to the stability maintenance during the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit in Qingdao between 9 and 10 June.

On 2 June 2018, local law enforcement officers arrested over 40 Buddhist worshippers in Panlong district of Kunming, Yunnan after they were tipped about 'an illegal gathering' - reading scripture in a tent on a mountain. A vehicle full of scripture and other household items was seized, and a detainee was injured when they were brought in for interrogations. At an unspecified date after their release, urban management personnel returned to the mountain and demolished two dwellings.

Around 1 June 2018 (beginning of month), over 30 personnel from the local National Security Division, Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau, and other government institutions raided the 'Home of Christ' fellowship at Shantou University in Jinping District (Shantou City, Guangdong Province). They confiscated over 5,000 books, including 200 Bibles, amounting to over RMB 100,000. The 'Home of Christ' attempted to negotiate with the authorities to reclaim the books, but the officials stated that the publications were 'illegal' and they would be burnt if the fellowship insisted on claiming them back.

Around 1 June 2018 (beginning of month), police raided the home of a dissident who had been preparing to commemorate the 29th anniversary of the June 4th massacre. The dissident was then forcibly admitted to a mental hospital in Rongchang District (Chongqing) by 'stability maintenance agents' from the local government and held there for 3 months.

Around 1 June 2018 (beginning of month), a female petitioner from Hunan Linxiang were intercepted by the police while petitioning in Beijing and were sent to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail'. She was detained in Jiujingzhuang and the Linxiang government office in Beijing for a few days before sending back to Linxiang.

Around 29 May 2018 (as reported), 2 retired soldiers were beaten by a traffic police when they drove through a security checkpoint in Zhuzhou City of Hunan Province. The police also insulted them with 'humiliating language.'

On 28 May 2018, the Xiacheng District Government sold a 1500-square-meters land owned by the Catholic Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception in Xiacheng District (Hangzhou City, Zhejiang City) and the police forcibly sealed off the land in the early morning on the day before. Some church members hung a banner that read 'no occupying religious property' outside the church.

On 27 May 2018, more than 40 Special Police, along with officials from the local Religious Affairs Department and officials from the Residential District Office, closed a protestant church in Lanzhou City, Gansu Province on the ground of 'setting up religious venues and organising religious activities without permission'. The police arrested 7 church leaders and released them on the same day. The police also carried away the church offering box, the lectern and other items. It was reported that a total of 5 significant churches in Lanzhou City were closed by the authorities since February, affecting around 700 church members.

On 27 May 2018, more than 100 people of domestic workers groups, including the Asian Migrants Coordinating Body and International Migrants Alliance, marched from Central to the headquarters of the New People's Party in the Wanchai District of Hong Kong. They called for lawmaker Eunice Yung to apologise over remarks which deemed offensive and insensitive to domestic workers. Protesters dressed up in red, held placards and chanted slogans. Yung collected their petition letter and said 'sorry' to the group representatives.

On 27 May 2018, between 610 and 1100 people, including members of DP and CP and students, participated in an annual march organised by The Alliance commemorating the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests in Hong Kong. The protesters marched from Wan Chai to the Beijing's Liaison Office in Sai Ying Pun, Central and Western District (Hong Kong), holding banners that read 'Mourn 4 June, Resist Authoritarianism'. They chanted slogans, calling for the accountability for the massacre and the ending of one-party dictatorship in China. They also demanded the release of human rights defenders in China, including Liu Xia, who was the widow of late Chinese Nobel Peace Prize-winning political dissident Liu Xiaobo.

Around 24 May 2018 (as reported), a number of civil society organisations (including current and former legislative councillors) held a press conference in Hong Kong, urging the government to adopt the '8+8 scheme' and increase the size of newly-built elderly homes and facilities for persons with disabilities to 16 square metres. At least 10 people held placards.

On 24 May 2018, a petitioner and her husband from Tongde Village were intercepted in the suburbs of Beijing, and taken away by an interceptor from Yancheng City and local government officials from Tongde Village and Datong Town. They were subsequently detained in a 'black jail' in Fengtai District. The petitioner had been petitioning for her rights for nearly six years, after she was left paralysed following an attack by triad members.
Around 20 May 2018 (week of), authorities demolished a Three-Self Church in Zhentian village in Xinyu City, Jiangxi Province, citing the '3 Renovations 1 Demolition' movement as justification.

On 20 May 2018, up to 100 teachers demonstrated outside the Xi'an People's Government office in Weiyang District (Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province), holding banners and calling for 'same salary and benefits for same job'. They demanded for the performance pay that were owed to them.

On 20 May 2018, a group of activists from The Alliance demonstrated at Clear Water Bay Country Park in Sai Kung (Hong Kong), in commemoration of the victims of the 1989 Tiananmen massacre, and called for the release of those who had been jailed for their rights advocacy in China. They flew two kites, with the words 'resist authoritarianism and commemorate June 4' and 'end one-party dictatorship', during the demonstration. The Alliance had been holding these kite-flying demonstrations at the same site since 1993.

Around 19 May 2018 (as reported), a number of civil society organisations petitioned in Hong Kong, outside the venue where the Community Care Fund was holding a public consultation, calling for the reinstatement of the 'N-nothing' scheme. The chairperson of Community Care Fund was present to personally receive all the petition letters.

Arrests: Around 18 May 2018 (between 11 - 25 May 2018), the Shanxi Provincial Public Security Department launched an operation to 'combat religions' in Shanxi. By employing tactics for eliminating gang crime to crackdown on religious groups, they arrested at least 1500 people within the first two weeks. It was reported that authorities had discussed tactics to target members of Islamic and Christian movements such as the Shouters, The Church of Almighty God, and Falun Gong during a meeting related to the operation.

Around 18 May 2018 (as reported), up to 100 workers demonstrated in Gaoling (Baoding City, Hebei Province) against wage arrears owed to them by the coal-to-gas project. During the demonstration, the workers held protest banners and wore T-shirts painted with Chinese characters demanding for their 'hard-earned money'.

On 17 May 2018, the taxi branch of the Motor Transport Workers General Union and CTOD Association Company Limited demonstrated at the taxi waiting area of Lok Ma Chau Spur Line Control Point in North District (Hong Kong), criticising the outsourcing management company for the poor management of the queueing system at the waiting area. They urged the Transport Department to supervise the management company for dereliction of duty. It was in response to a recent incident where some taxi drivers were told by several men to move to the back of the line in the waiting area because they were not 'members'.

Around 16 May 2018 (month of), a Christian couple were arrested at their house in Xinjiang by two community workers and two policemen and sent to a 'transformation through education' camps. The husband was released by August, but his wife was not and continued to be held at an unspecified camp.

Around 16 May 2018 (month of), a Uyghur business founder of a language and vocational school and a financial services company in Korla county (Bayingolin Mongol Autonomous, Xinjiang) was detained and sent to an 'internment camp' in Hejing county. It was reported that although the language school only used state-approved teaching materials, it offered classes in Turkish in 2014-2015 due to growing interest among Uyghurs to visit Turkey, which was among the blacklisted countries for travel by Uyghurs.

Around 16 May 2018 (month of), a Uyghur farmer from Bulaq village of Putao (Uzumchilik) town of Gaochang district (Turpan, Xinjiang) was sent to 'political vocational training centre' for making a pilgrimage to Mecca in the past, which was seen as a violation of Articles 123 and 124 of the Penal Code. He was released in early 2019 with compromised health, and placed under house arrest. At least nine of her family members experienced being sent to camps or restricted from leaving their villages.

On 16 May 2018, at a hearing for the '709 crackdown' at the Beijing Lawyers Association Chaoyang Lawyer Service Center in Chaoyang District (Beijing), a photographer from the Hong Kong-based Now TV was violently pushed to the ground by three plainclothes police officers, and handcuffed by two uniformed officers. It was reported that he was beaten by 'between five to six' police officers until he was bleeding. A human rights lawyer (the defendant) was also beaten by the police when he attempted to stop the assault of the journalist. Both of them were then forcibly dragged into a van. The lawyer was detained for 5-6 hours, while the journalist was released four hours later, reportedly after the State Council's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office had 'mediated' at the request of the Hong Kong government.

On 14 May 2018, more than 400 social workers from 101 social welfare organisations demonstrated outside the Legislative Council in Central and Western District (Hong Kong), urging the government to introduce comprehensive reforms for the existing social welfare system. Demonstrators chanted slogans calling for a rejection of 'minor changes', and that they wanted to be a 'real social worker'. The demonstration took place while the Welfare Committee of the Legislative Council held a public hearing.

Around 13 May 2018 (week of), authorities brought down and targeted one Three-Self Church in Zhongyuan village in Xinyu City, Jiangxi Province, citing the '3 Renovations 1 Demolition' movement as justification.

On 13 May 2018, the local government seized a Three-Self Church in Nanhua community of Minquan District (Shangqiu City, Henan Province). The local government posted a sign on the roof of the church that read 'Nanhua Community Party Service Center' and replaced the cross with a party emblem. The church became an office of the Chuwa Village Committee.

On 13 May 2018, a Kazakh man (a Kazakhstani green card holder) from Habahe County (Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang) was taken away by the authorities and sent to a re-education camp, reportedly for 'disloyalty to China'. He was still recovering from his surgical treatment for oral cancer at a hospital at the time when he was taken away. He was formally released in December 2018 and had since returned to Kazakhstan.

On 13 May 2018, the Community Care and Nursing Home Workers General Union demonstrated at the headquarters of the Hong Kong Lutheran Social Service in Ho Man Tin, Kowloon City District (Hong Kong), criticising the organisation for exploiting its employees. They alleged that the organisation hired 'support service staff' at lower wages, which covered the same job responsibilities as the higher-paid caregivers. The union estimated the organisation had exploited more than HKD700,000 off of its workers, and claimed that this was in violation of the law. The Hong Kong Lutheran Social Service had since refuted the claims.

On 12 May 2018, at least 200 parents gathered at the original location of Juyuan Middle School in Dujiangyan city (Chengdu, Sichuan) to commemorate their children who died during the 2008 Sichuan earthquake after the poorly constructed school buildings collapsed. They also called for the government to investigate the reason causing the collapse. During the event, a reporter from Hong Kong i-Cable Television was beaten by two unknown individuals. Later on the same day, the two assailants were taken by the Dujiangyan government to publicly apologise to the reporter, and they both denied any connection with the government. On the same day, the government in Sichuan also organised a commemorative event and officially named 12 May the day of 'being grateful', which provoked further dissatisfaction among the families of the earthquake victims.

On 12 May 2018, a large number up to 10,000 people voluntarily went to a commemoration site at the centre of Beichuan county (Mianyang, Sichuan) to offer flowers to the victims of the 2008 Sichuan earthquake which affected Beichuan county the worst. People also called for the government to investigate the reason of the earthquake causing such serious damage pointing at the broader issue of construction quality of houses. It was reported that plain-clothes police were sent to monitor the scene. On the same day, the government in Sichuan also organised a commemorative event and officially named 12 May the day of 'being grateful', which provoked further dissatisfaction among the families of the earthquake victims.

On 12 May 2018, around 30 activists, organised by the animal rights group Dolphin Family, protested outside Ocean Park in Southern District (Hong Kong) as part of the sixth annual Empty The Tanks Worldwide initiative to raise awareness on the problems with cetacean captivity. They chanted slogans such as 'dolphins belong to the ocean, not a park' and 'release the dolphins'. A small scuffle broke out when many security guards tried to take away banners from the protesters. Several plainclothes and a uniformed police officer were also at the scene.

On 11 May 2018, a pastor and a preacher of the Early Rain Covenant protestant church were taken away by police in Chengdu, Sichuan for 'suspected provocations', after posting online that he is planning to host a special prayer meeting in commemoration of the victims of Sichuan earthquake on the 10th anniversary of the earthquake.

On 11 May 2018, the local government tore down the cross from the Gospel Church in Beishankou town (Zhengzhou City, Henan Province), on the grounds that 'Chinese churches cannot be like foreign churches, therefore, cannot use the cross as a symbol'. The words 'Gospel Church' on the plaque were also removed. This was part of a broader campaign to remove crosses on churches across China.

On 11 May 2018, dozens of house owners in Xi'an City (Shaanxi) went to petition at the provincial government offices in Xincheng District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) and ask the government to intervene in getting the estate developing company that built their houses to issue them house ownership certificates which were promised to be issued in 2010. It was reported that this matter affected 314 households in total in a community called 'Ningmeng Gongshe'. Protesters put out a large banner in front of the government building.

On 11 May 2018, about 20 people from several groups including the League of Social Democrats and the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China held a march from Western Police Station in Western District to the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in Hong Kong, in a display of solidarity with mainland dissident Qin Yongmin, as his trial began today. Protesters held banners and chanted slogans, criticizing the CCP for delaying the trial of Qin Yongmin since 2015 and demanded to abolish the 'inciting subversion of state power' crime.

On 10 May 2018, a Muslim local living in Shawan county, Xinjiang (Tarbagatay prefecture) was sent to a 'transformation through education' camp after officers showed up at his house, and lured him to the police station under false pretexts. His family had been denied visitation rights since his arrest.

On 9 May 2018, more than 1,000 previously laid-off preschool and substitute teachers held a protest at Shaanxi Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xincheng District, Xi'an, Shaanxi, asking the government to solve the retirement insurance problem and demanding social insurance and pension payment. Protesters held banners and Chinese flags, shouted slogans, and sang songs. After not receiving satisfying answers, they moved to sit-in in front of the Shaanxi Provincial Government Offices which is located in the same block. Police formed a 'human wall' trying to stop protesters and take away their banners. 3 teachers were taken away from the scene by police.

On 8 May 2018, at least 10 members of CP, CF and Neo Democrats protested using placards outside the Legislative Council in Central District to demand the council to open an investigation regarding the constitutionality of allowing government administrative staff to participate in legislative meetings and potentially 'spy' on Legislative Councillors. The event was triggered by an earlier incident in which a LegCo member tried to snatch the phone of a female security bureau executive officer suspected of security breach.

On 8 May 2018, 33 representatives of nearly 460,000 farmers in Shanghai whose lands had been confiscated by the government demonstrated at the Shanghai Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security in Pudong New Area (Shanghai). They demanded to be included in the 'city dwellers' social security system, instead of the 'rural dwellers' scheme. The Bureau Chief refused to meet the group, and the protesters left. They decided to gather again on 12 June 2018 for another collective petition.

On 7 May 2018, more than 500 laid-off teachers held a protest and petitioned at the Liaoning Province Department of Education in Huanggu District, Shenyang. Protesting teachers demanded medical insurance and pension payment and protected their collective rights. Protesters shouted slogans and sang songs. After the protest, many police officers were sent to intercept protesters at the train station. It was also reported that many of the participants had to arrive at the protest by carpooling because they were 'blacklisted' after petitioning more than once.

On 7 May 2018, representatives of around 60 households in Xi'an City (Shaanxi) demonstrated at the Xi'an City petition offices in Beilin District (Xi'an, Shaanxi) and asked the government to intervene in getting the estate developing company that built their houses to deliver the apartments which were promised to be built no later than 2008 and pay them compensations. The issue was reportedly affecting more than 200 households in the same community named 'Yangguang Chengshi', but more than 150 of them had asked the company to refund their houses.

Around 7 May 2018 (as reported), 8 Shanghai rights defenders protested on the street in Shanghai against the Shanghai Government and the Legal Affairs Office of the State Council, after filing an application for administrative reconsideration to the Legal Affairs Office of the State Council along with 57 other people in August 2017, and not receiving any decision back from the Office. Protesters held a banner with the words 'Where is China's rule of law?'.

On 6 May 2018, village authorities shut down and demolished a state-sanctioned Three-Self Church in Zaomushan village, Fengyi county of Xinyu with less than a day's notice. Almost a hundred church members were affected. The alleged reason for the act was that the church was an 'eyesore' located near the tomb of Xi Zaochi, a historical figure of whom President Xi Jinping is a 55th generation descendant.

On 6 May 2018, dozens of people, including members of the Democratic Party and university students, protested at the Police Headquarters in Wan Chai, Hong Kong, to demonstrate their dissatisfaction with the government's monitoring of parliament members, following the arrest of parliament member and Democratic Party member Hui Chi-fung for snatched the mobile phone of a government official who was 'observing' parliament members. Protesters were holding signs.

On 4 May 2018, more than 100 Guozhai village residents held a sit-in at the gate of the Demolition Office in Guozhai Village, Cangshan District (Fuzhou, Fujian) protesting against illegal land acquisition and demolition. Protesters wore shirts with their message. Dozens of 'black security guards' and police cars were at the event, and the guards forcibly threw away rice porridge and other food that was sent to the protesters, who were mostly elderly people.

On 4 May 2018, a Kazakh businesswoman from Wusu city was placed in a tiger chair during an interrogation in Gongliu county (Ili, Xinjiang) after the police called her to the station regarding changes in household registration. She often traveled between Kazakhstan and China, and had been interrogated and encountered troubles with customs since November 2017. After her interrogation, she learnt of being on a list to be sent to an 'internment camp', and sought asylum in Kazakhstan.

On 4 May 2018, at least 3 Demosisto members demonstrated at a school in Tai Kok Tsui, Yau Tsim Mong District (Hong Kong) where the Education Secretary was visiting on the same day. They stated that the Education Bureau should not allow the rewriting of Hong Kong's liberal studies curriculum and textbooks after the Education Bureau's Textbook Review Group criticized specific phrases in the books regarding Hong Kong's political status as being 'problematic'. Protesters held signs and called the government not to let politics come before education.

On 3 May 2018, more than 60 people led by the Hong Kong Island Federation and the Southern District Community Association protested at the Legislative Council in Central District (Hong Kong) against an earlier incident in which a Democratic Party Legislative Councillor snatched the mobile phone of a female government official suspected of 'observing' Legislative Council members. They urged the legislator to resign and demanded the Council and the police to open an investigation. On the same day, 40 members of the Federation of Hong Kong Kowloon New Territories Hawkers Association and Po Kin Hai Liu Association protested at the LegCo against the same incident and they demanded the LegCo to start the impeachment procedure against the legislator.

On 2 May 2018, up to 200 customers, suppliers and employees of a company called 'No 1 Home Renovation' gathered outside of the company's building in Wuhan (Hubei) while the company suddenly became bankrupt and the owner could not be found. People put out large banners outside of the building. Police were on alert at the scene, but no intervention was reported.

On 2 May 2018, nearly 100 house owners from a community named 'Feicui Mingzhu' demonstrated at the Beilin District Government Offices (Xi'an, Shaanxi) and asked the government to intervene in getting the estate developing company that built their houses to issue them house ownership certificates as promised in the contracts. The company also raised prices for the unpaid instalments. Protesters required the government to order the company to issue ownership certificates and charge the originally agreed price.

On 30 April 2018, more than 40 members of several groups including DP, Neo Democrats (including Legislative Councillors) collectively complained and protested at the Office of the Ombudsman in Central District (Hong Kong) about government misconduct. Protesters held signs and argued that the government had exceeded its authority by sending administrative staff to the Legislative Council to monitor the whereabouts of its members. The event was triggered by an earlier incident in which a Democratic Party Legislative Councillor snatched the mobile phone of a government official suspected of 'observing' Legislative Council members.

Around 29 April 2018 (from 28 to 30 April), local police interrogated two villagers for three days and nights without sleep in Wanzhai Village (Sanming, Fujian). The villagers had been arrested on 28 April for 'directing other villagers to destroy a mining company' and 'disturbing social order' and detained for a total of 32 days.

On 29 April 2018, nearly 30 people from six different groups including Labour Party, the LSD, the Concerning Grassroots' Housing Rights Alliance and the LJL protested at the Fanling Golf Club in Hong Kong North, urging the government to seize the land of the golf course and use it for residential purposes, affordable housing, and elderly retirement homes once the golf course lease terminates. Protesters held banners and signs and claimed that the land is being 'occupied' by the rich.

On 25 April 2018, nearly 10 Mongolian herdsmen went to the municipality government offices of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region in Xincheng District (Hohhot, Inner Mongolia) to petition and protest against the oppression and threats they suffered from local 'stability maintenance' authorities. They all had different issues with local governments, ranging from seized pasture, damage of the ecological environment, and corruption of government personnel.

On 22 April 2018, a dozen citizens led by animal protection organisations such as 'Paws Hero' and '99 Bus' protested outside of the Government Headquarters at Admiralty in Central District (Hong Kong) to urge the government to pass more comprehensive animal protection law.

On 21 April 2018, more than ten members of social groups including the League of Social Democrats, and Legislative Council members protested outside a hotel where a conference on promoting Basic Law Article 23 was held in Tsim Sha Tsui Hong kong. Police dispatched a large number of police officers to prevent the protesters from harassing former chairman of the Hong Kong Basic Law Committee, Qiao Xiaoyang, who attended the conference and had to enter the hotel under police protection due to the protesters. Protesters held signs and shouted slogans such as 'End the one-party dictatorship in China', 'Release all political prisoners' and 'Oppose the Basic Law Article 23 legislation'.

On 20 April 2018, at least 6 family members and lawyers of two arrested individuals in the '4 June Liqueur' case gathered in front of the Intermediate Court in Chengdu, Sichuan to protest against their prolonged detention which was nearly two years. They held a large banner at the court's gate that read 'no trial or judgement in 2 years, we want our families back'. They also delivered a letter to the residing judge of the case signed by the wives of the two arrested.

On 20 April 2018, at least 8 members of an organisation called Protect Harbourfront Community gathered at the Hong Kong Heritage Discovery Centre in Tsim Sha Tsui (Yau Tsim Mong District, Hong Kong) while the Lands Department was having a meeting there. They protested against the government for shutting down the General Post Office Headquarters in Central District, and advocated for preserving its historical and architectural value by converting it into a public space. They petitioned, held a large banner and shouted 'returning the harbour to the people'.

On 19 April 2018, the church of Hutuo Village in Gongyi City (Zhengzhou, Henan) was demolished by the authority as a part of a coordinated action against 'underground' Catholic churches conducted across Henan province in April 2018.

On 19 April 2018, a dozen people led by the DAB and two of its legislative councillors gathered at the Justice Place in Central Hong Kong to demand the Department of Justice to prosecute and charge the law professor that had recently spoke about the 'independence' of Hong Kong at a conference in Taiwan.

On 17 April 2018, it was reported that Public Security officers, village and county governments, raided a Catholic church in Xin Village (Linzhou, Anyang, Henan) and took away the church's sacred object as a part of a coordinated action against 'underground' Catholic churches conducted across Henan province in April 2018. It was also reported that many Christian house churches in a village in Linzhou City were raided by village officials on the same day, where the officials forcibly removed religious couplets, and took away portraits of Jesus and religious calendars. This was part of a broader campaign launched by the town government to disrupt Christian religious activities.

On 17 April 2018, the government confiscated the finances of the Church of Beixishang Village (Jiaozuo, Henan) and ordered the church to demolish its cross. This event was reported as a part of a coordinated action against 'underground' Catholic churches conducted across Henan province in April 2018.

On 16 April 2018, a Christian church in Yucheng County (Shangqiu City, Henan Province) was demolished by the township government, on the grounds that they were 'building a cultural square'. This was part of a broader campaign to crack down on places of worship across China.

Around 15 April 2018 (month of), more than 40 Muslim men from the same vilage in Wusu (Tarbagatay, Xinjiang) were taken by authorities to a 'transformation through education' camp after being tricked by authorities to visit the local commune for 'study classes.'

Around 15 April 2018 (month of), government personnel demolished the upper dome, minaret, crescent moon, and a large plaque of Wujiawan Grand Mosque in Baofeng town (Shizuishan, Ningxia), on the grounds that the mosque was not reconstructed according to the state-prescribed official rules. They then replaced these symbols with the national flag. This was carried out under the new Regulation on Religious Affairs to 'Sinicize' religious venues in the region.

Around 15 April 2018 (month of), the local government removed the cross from the Shanchuan Church in Beishankou town (Zhengzhou City, Henan Province) and printed the name of the church in red. The slogan 'National law trumps religious law' was written on the exterior wall. This was part of a broader campaign to remove crosses on churches across China.

Around 15 April 2018 (month of), more than 30 young Kazakhs was taken by the local authority in Bo'erbosong Village (Ili, Xinjiang) and sent to 'political education camp' according to the relatives of the Kazakhs. They had yet been released at the time of reporting on September 2018. It is a part of a governmental campaign to suppress the Kazakh ethnic minorities in Xinjiang.

On 15 April 2018, dozens of retired workers gathered at a field in the centre of Shaoyang City (Human) to protest against unequal pension treatment between the people who retired from private sectors and the people who retired from public sectors. They sang 'revolutionary songs' and talked to the passers-by about the unfairness of the pension system. Police used tear gas or pepper spray to disperse people as more and more people started gathering. A few people were injured.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 15 April 2018, nearly 10 members of the LSD were surrounded by 30-50 police near the Conrad Hotel in Admiralty (Central District, Hong Kong) when they were on the way to the hotel to protest against further legislation based on the Hong Kong Basic Law Article 23 at a national security conference. Protesters held signs and shouted slogans opposing further legislation such as 'People come before the county'.

Around 15 April 2018 (as reported), a female petitioner was taken by police in Beijing and sent to the 'Gaojiachang black jail' in Fengtai District (Beijing). Upon arrival at the black jail, she was searched by some government stability maintenance people and hired triad members. They also slapped her and beat her with electric baton. She received multiple injuries.

Around 12 April 2018 (as reported), motorists in Changde City (Hunan province) parked up with lights flashing, emitting long honking sounds on their horns, in a protest against the shut down of a radio program by the State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television because its content was 'inappropriate'. It was reported that similar events took place in other locations within Hunan province as well.

On 12 April 2018, authorities turned up at a government-controlled Three-Self Denglongba Church in Lushui, Yunnan and demolished it after a three-day notice from the Bureau of Religious Affairs cancelling its certification. Under the 'Lushui City Religious Activities Sites Consolidation Program,' the church was told to merge its congregation with another church in the city - Christian Two Meetings' Center Church. Three-Self churches are typically approved by the government and this one cost nearly 500,000 RMB member fees to build.

On 12 April 2018, more than 60 clients of the Agricultural Bank of China gathered outside the gate of the Agricultural Bank of China branch in Chenggaozi Town, Xiangfang District, Harbin, in opposition to the bank's failure to deliver a 'high-interest guarantee' these clients purchased five years ago. Demonstrators clashed with the police, and three people were charged with 'attacking the police' and detained for seven days.

Around 12 April 2018 (as reported), rows of cars with headlights and hazard lights flashing were seen stationary in the middle of a highway in Jiangsu province, while people stood holding a banner in the middle of the road supporting a recently shut down radio program by the State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television because its content was 'inappropriate'.

On 12 April 2018, five Christians representing more than 20 Christian groups protested at the Chief Executive's Office in Admiralty, Central and Western District (Hong Kong), condemning the Hong Kong Government and Beijing for combatting Dai Yaoting for his 'Hong Kong independence' speech.

On 11 April 2018, a Muslim man living in Shawan county, Xinjiang (Tarbagatay prefecture) was sent to a 'transformation through education' camp after police called him to the police station. He suspects that he was caught because his phone had been monitored, and not long ago, a message he sent expressing 'his faith in God' alerted the police. Two days ago, the police also sent his brother to the same camp.

On 11 April 2018, around 140 people gathered with their cars at Minghu Square in Xishi District (Yingkou city, Liaoning) to protest against the State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television in Beijing shutting down a radio program because its content was 'inappropriate'. The radio program was very popular among drivers.

On 11 April 2018, 5 people visited the graveyard of a deceased Hunan human rights activist in Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province and held a large banner that read 'China might be the biggest winner if democracy and freedom were to be realised'. They were separately summoned and detained by police after the gathering.

On 11 April 2018, two women were beaten up by dozens of people including security police and street and community personnel in Shijingshan District (Beijing) when they tried to visit the wife of a '709' lawyer (the lawyer had been missing for around 1,000 days). The group of government personnel had been gathering at the residence of the human rights lawyer to prevent anyone from entering or exiting the house. They kicked the victims and attacked them with a chair. The two victims were sent to hospital later. Some journalist on the scene was also dragged out of a car and beaten by the police.

On 11 April 2018, a rights defender in Sichuan was taken by security police to be detained in a hotel room after leaving her relative's wedding because of the annual meetings of 'lianghui'. She was released on 20 April 2018 after 'lianghui' was over. The defender was verbally abused and humiliated during detainment. Also, she was taken to a psychiatric hospital in Nanchong (Sichuan) on 15 April 2018, and had to resist very hard to avoid being injected. After being released, she continued being monitored by security police.

On 10 April 2018, nearly 100 people gathered outside State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television in Xicheng District (Beijing) to protest against the government shutting down a radio program because its content was 'inappropriate'. They drove their cars to gather together at night and stayed until early morning on the 11 April 2018.

On 10 April 2018, around 10 family members of the four Hong Kong fishers who were involved in a drug related case and 'unreasonably prosecuted' in the Philippines went to the Consulate General of the Philippines at Admiralty in Central District (Hong Kong) to deliver a petition letter to the visiting President of the Philippines. A member of the Legislative Council accompanied the group. They demanded the Philippine authority to award justice to the four fishers.

On 10 April 2018, a woman that was participating in the march to search for the last missing '709 lawyer' was taken by police from Tianjin and sent to Xushui District (Baoding, Hebei) for a 'mandatory vacation'. Her husband was taken on the same day by police and sent to the same place to be restricted together with her. They were not told how long they would be restricted at the 'vacation place'.

On 9 April 2018, a Muslim man living in Shawan county, Xinjiang (Tarbagatay prefecture) was sent to a 'transformation through education' camp after officers showed up at his house, and lured him to the police station under false pretexts. His brother was also sent to the same camp by the police two days later.

On 9 April 2018, nearly 20 people marched from the University of Hong Kong MTR station to the law faculty on campus (Western District, Hong Kong) to protest against the professor that had recently spoke about the 'independence' of Hong Kong at a conference in Taiwan. They also delivered a petition letter to the university that asked to remove this professor from this teaching position.

On 8 April 2018, nearly 100 people gathered in Chencun Town (Foshan, Guangdong) to protest against government forcibly taking over their lands. They held a large banner that read 'town government robbed us our lands'. Police took away the banner and people dispersed.

On 7 April 2018, about 30 protesters demonstrated outside the Hong Kong government headquarters, asking the SAR Government and the University of Hong Kong to deal with Dai Yaoting's remarks and his teaching position, and called to resolutely condemn and punish him for his 'Hong Kong independence' remarks. About 30 demonstrators held banners with the words 'Remove the tumor as soon as possible', and shouting 'Dai Yaoting is a national scum.'

On 6 April 2018, thousands of villagers from two villages in Changqi Town (Wuchuan, Zhanjiang, Guangdong) fought in two groups with each other while performing a traditional 'march with God' new year ceremony. They fought during the day with iron sticks and at night by shooting fireworks as weapons. The authority sent hundreds of police to stop the situation. 4 villagers were injured.

Property destruction: On 6 April 2018, police forces of China demolished a petitioner's house in Cigou Village, Xuchang City, Henan Province. In the past, the petitioner had been both under administrative arrests and criminal arrests. She had been accused of 'damage the government's image' and was suspected of 'provoking trouble' by posting her whereabouts on the internet.

On 5 April 2018, dozens of people from the Alliance, the Tiananmen Mothers and Democratic Party in Hong Kong gathered at the Clock Tower in Tsim Sha Tsui (Yau Tsim Mong District, Kowloon City, Hong Kong) to commemorate the victims of the Tiananmen Massacre and other rights defenders that had died in China. They wore T-shirts printed with slogans 'anti-authoritarianism, mourn June 4th'.

On 4 April 2018, an 82-year-old man was taken by 4 police officers from his home to the nearby police office in Tiedong District (Siping, Jilin) because he was planning to go to Beijing for petition. He was forced to sit on a 'tiger bench' during interrogation and was kept in the police office for 8 hours and were not given food or water. The police let him go home at around midnight.

On 4 April 2018, at least 5 people related with the '709' lawyers started a 1000-kilometre march from Chaoyang District, Beijing to the Tianjin No.2 Intermediate Court which allegedly had approved the detention of the last missing lawyer that was arrested in July 2015 to protest his 1,000 days disappearance. Participants of the march included 3 wives of the '709' lawyers and other friends.

On 3 April 2018, at least 7-8 members of a pro-government organisation 'Justice Complaints' gathered at the University of Hong Kong in Central and Western District (Hong Kong) with a large banner to protest against a professor from the law faculty that had recently spoke about the 'independence' of Hong Kong in public. They urged the university to stop employing the law professor. The chairman of the DHKC was reported to be leading the group.

On 3 April 2018, at least 30 people from an organisation called 'new era' marched from Admiralty Centre Shopping Arcade to the Legislative Council Complex in Central Hong Kong to protest against the Legislative Council members that were against the controversial plan to allow mainland police to operate in a section of a train station in Hong Kong that lies at the boarder with the mainland. They held banners and placards.

On 2 April 2018, nearly 10 members from a patriotic organisation gathered at the University of Hong Kong in Central and Western District (Hong Kong) with placards that read 'Dai Yaoting/Benny Tai Yiu-ting' to protest against the professor who had recently spoke about the 'independence' of Hong Kong in public. They urged the university to stop employing the law professor. Someone from the university accepted their petition letter.

On 2 April 2018, two women were shot by unknown individuals using an air gun in Iao Hon Market Garden in Macao in the morning, when they were singing China's communist revolution themed 'red songs' in the park together with a group of mostly middle-aged and elderly women. It was also reported that another similar incident took place at the same spot about 10 days ago leaving one person injured. No deaths reported.

On 1 April 2018, a Uyghur Muslim man in hiding was shot dead on a culvert in Liangfanchang at Huocheng county of Ili prefecture, after a 70,000-persons police manhunt following his escape from internment at a 'transformation through education' camp. He had made multiple attempts to resist arrest since May 2017, when he was first arrested for 'participating in unlawful religious activities.'

Around 31 March 2018 (end of month), an old imam and his son living in Ulan-Usu town of Shawan county (Tarbagatay prefecture, Xinjiang) were sent to a 'transformation through education' camp after police officers charged into their home, and lured them to the police station under false pretexts. The imam became progressively sick due to unhygienic and filthy living conditions; he was sent to the hospital for treatment, then brought back to the camp after recovery.

On 31 March 2018, an Uyghur woman from Urumqi, Xinjiang was called by the local neighbourhood administration and then taken to a local police station for interrogation. She was fixed to the tiger chair during the interrogation about her marriage to a Pakistani and her bank transfers to Pakistan. She was then taken to a re-education camp where she was detained for around 2 months until her release on 2 June 2018. Before she left China, she was reportedly forced to pay a RMB 18,000 fine for her third child being born 'outside the plan', and was forced to undergo sterilization on 22 October 2018 in order to be given permission to leave the country. Her family left for Pakistan in January 2019 and later went to the US in April 2019 to apply for asylum.

On 31 March 2018, 50 residents from the Tsz Wan Shan Market Residents Concern Group, Tsz Wan Shan Construction Force, and Supervision of Public Market Development Alliance gathered outside the closed Haoyun Wet Market in Wong Tai Sin District (Kowloon City, Hong Kong) to protest the outsourcing of the first floor to 'Jianhua Group'. During the protest, criticism was pointed to the district councillors for allowing the situation. The Chief Secretary of the LSD was reported to participate the event.

On 31 March 2018, many residents in a community concern group protested at 'Ho Wan Market' in Tsz Wan Shan Shopping Centre, Wong Tai Sin district, Hong Kong against rising rents and overcrowding after new management reduced the food market to a single floor.

On 30 March 2018, a female petitioner, together with other petitioners, was taken by the police at the entrance of Xihongmen Underground Station in Daxing District (Beijing), after inspecting her ID and found out that she was a monitored subject, and sent her to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail'. She was later picked up by the personnel from the Beijing Office of the Shanghai Government and sent back to Shanghai on 31 March 2018.

Around 30 March 2018, a retired judge from Xinjiang was transferred by the police from the Detention Centre of Tumxuk (Xinjiang) to the Centre of Legal Education and placed under 'Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location' after the court revoked the charge. The retired judge was arrested because he assisted the defence of the rights of employees in the Third Agricultural Division Farm.

On 29 March 2018, the underground Archbishop of Roman Catholic Diocese of Funing, possibly together with the Diocesan Secretary, were 'forcibly traveled' from Ningde (Fujian) to Xiamen and were only allowed to return on 31 March 2018. It was also reported that the Archbishop and his secretary were summoned by the State Administration for Religious Affairs on 26 March 2018 and detained for around 24 hours.

On 27 March 2018, a Tibetan monk of Labrang monastery in Gansu's Sangchu (in Chinese, Xiahe) county, disappeared after receiving a call from the Chinese state security officers. He was released on 5 April 2018 'without explanation' after being detained 'in secret' by the police for questioning. There were no signs that he had suffered any torture or been beaten. It was also reported that he had been previously held for questioning for a few days around 10 March 2018, the anniversary of a failed 1959 national uprising against Chinese rule in Tibet.

On 27 March 2018, eight Mongolian petitioners from Bayan Nur City Urad Middle Banner and Dengkou County were taken by the police around Zhongnanhai in Xicheng District (Beijing) and sent to Majialou 'black jail' when they were on their way to submit petition documents to National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration. They were later taken back by the Bayan Nur City police and detained.

On 26 March 2018, a petitioner was captured by 'unemployed triad members' right after she was released from police custody. Police officers had barged into her home in Beijing on 14 March 2018 and transported her to a detention center in Wuhan City (where she was originally from), where she was illegally detained for 10 days. The triad members detained her for 3 months before transferring her to a 'citizens' learning centre black jail' in Dongxihu District, Wuhan on 1 July. On 2 August 2018, she was transferred to a police station before being released.

On 25 March 2018, a petitioner, together with another petitioner from Nantong, was taken from their rental house in Yancun Town Dadong Village (Fangshan, Beijing) by more than ten police and sent to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail', together with around eight other petitioners in the police car. He was later picked up by four people from the Beijing-based Office of the Dandong Government, send to Dandong Qidao Police Station and a small hotel in Jinshan Town, and kept in the hotel, but when he was released and went back to Beijing, he was detained again in the Beijing Railway Station police station, sent by the personnel from the Beijing-Based Office of the Dandong Government to Longhugong Hotel where their Office is, and kept there for three hours before his release.

On 25 March 2018, up to 700 protesters, including Canadian and American students in Hong Kong, participated in 'March For Our Lives' demonstration and marched from Central Pier No.10 to Hong Kong City Hall in Central District (Hong Kong) to show solidarity with the gun violence protests in the US. The protesters wore blue t-shirts and held protest signs.

On 22 March 2018, a house church established by Koreans in Chuxiong City (Chuxiong Yi Autonomous, Yunnan) was shut down by the police and government officials, on the grounds that 'the church was not registered, and the meeting place is illegal'. On the day of the raid, more than 100 police officers were mobilised, and the pastor, elder, and seven deacons of the church were arrested.

Around 19 March 2018 (between 14 - 24 March), a dissident from Nanjing was physically abused and injured by the officers in the bathroom of the Nanjing Detention Centre in Pukou District (Nanjing, Jiangsu) after he repeatedly chanted 'overthrow Soviet Mao Communist Party'. The dissident was was taken to the detention centre on 14 March because he posted anti-CCP and mocking-constitution-amendment posts online during the Lianghui Conventions. He was originally supposed to be detained for 14 days, but was released early and sent to the hospital after being beaten up because the police were afraid he would die in custody.

Around 16 March 2018 (month of), local police forcibly took away three Muslim brothers from Huocheng County (Ili Kazak Autonomous, Xinjiang) and put them into a 'transformation through education' camp, for using a file-sharing mobile app.

Around 16 March 2018 (month of), 30 Tibetans in Xiaqu Town (Nagqu, Tibet) were arrested and beaten by the authorities for opposing a mining project in their region and for suspicion of 'leaking information' about the local opposition shortly after it was reported by media outside Tibet in early March 2018. The village leader was arrested by authority in February 2018 and his whereabouts remained unknown. Authorities had increased control over Xiaqu Town, blocking locals' communication channels such as WeChat and internet and telephone signal.

Around 16 March 2018 (month of), a Kazakh policeman and Kazakhstan green card holder living in Oyman Bulaq village, Qaragash township of Ghulja (Yining) county (Ili, Xinjiang) was detained and sent to an 'internment camp' for 18 months before being sentenced in Oct 2019 to 10 years of prison (in Wusu Prison) and forced labour, and five years of deprivation of political rights. He was arrested for inciting ethnic hatred via posting on Weibo. Official accounts said he was sentenced on 11 Apr 2018 without ever having been in a political re-education centre.

On 16 March 2018, two wives of the lawyers in the '709 Crackdown' and more than 10 of their supporters went to petition and submit a complaint letter at the Complaints and Proposals Bureau of the Supreme People's Court in Chaoyang District (Beijing), but they were stopped by the security guards at the security check and were not able to submit the letter in the end.

On 15 March 2018, a female petitioner from Shanghai was taken away in Gaoqiao Town (Pudong, Shanghai) by four to five people from the Public Complaints and Proposals Administration. She was detained overnight at Gaoqiao Police Station before being held at Chongming Island (a 'black jail') until 20 March 2018. She was then transferred to a hotel opposite Gaoqiao Police Station where her husband, son, and daughter were also detained. The petitioner and her daughter were released on 23 March 2018. On 21 March 2018, the local government also demolished her residence.

On 13 March 2018, a petitioner was sent back to Shanghai from Beijing by a government interceptor and handed over to 4 unknown individuals at an underground parking lot in Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station (Minhang District, Shanghai). The 4 unknown individuals took him to a 'black jail', presumably in Shanghai, where he was beaten upon arrival and detained for 12 days. He was dropped on a road in Pudong New Area (Shanghai) on 24 March 2018.

On 12 March 2018, several petitioners from Wuhan were taken in Beijing to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' by the police officers patrolling in streets in Beijing when they went to petition at the National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration and the hotels where the representatives of the National People's Congress were staying.

On 11 March 2018, police raided a Christian house church in Urumqi, Xinjiang and sealed it off. The police confiscated over 100 books from the church and detained several leaders of the church. One of them was made to sit on the torture device known as the 'tiger bench' during the interrogation.

Around 11 March 2018 (from 3 - 20 March), during the Lianghui conventions, a female petitioner was detained by the Beijing police when she was receiving medical treatment in Beijing and, after sending back to Shanghai, was kept in a 'black jail' for ten days by the Minhang District Wujing Town Government. The petitioner has petitioned over property infringement by the Wujing Town Government and was previously kept in 'black jails'.

On 9 March 2018, a female petitioner from Shanghai was taken away by the police and detained in a hotel in Beijing. On the next day, she was transferred to Shanghai, interrogated in the police office and detained in a 'black jail' again for 10 days. It was part of a campaign by the local police to silence dissent during the annual meetings of Two Sessions.

On 8 March 2018, a woman petitioner was arrested by police in Beijing and detained in the Beijing Jiujingzhuang Jieji Service Centre 'black prison'. Later the same day, she was taken back to a prison in her hometown in Zhangjiagang (Suzhou, Jiangsu). The petitioner is a victim of the illegal demolition of their home, for which she did not receive compensation, and travelled to Beijing to petition for her rights. During her detention in Beijing, the petitioner suffered injuries to her arms and body after being violently dragged out of the Jiujingzhuang black prison by several unidentified people.

On 7 March 2018, a Uyghur woman from Yingxiehai'er Village, Karakax County (Hotan Prefecture, Xinjiang) was sent to a re-education camp by the authorities. Additional government records also showed that she had started a 3-month 'housekeeping training' course in December 2018 at the same facility. The likely reason for her detention was having more children than allowed in the family planning policy.

On 6 March 2018, 3 family members of an activist being held in a black prison near to Lutun Town (Yingkou, Liaoning) went to visit the activist, but while at the detention site, they got into an argument with the 'stability maintenance special task forces' guarding their family members and one of them was violently knocked to the floor by the guards.

On 5 March 2018, 7 people protested near to Changyang Town in Fangshan District (Beijing) against recurring 'old problems' such as illegal and violent land acquisition, judicial injustices as seen in the case of Nie Shubin and problems with equality in the education system. Protesters raised banners. The protest occurred while the 'two sessions' were being held.

On 5 March 2018, during the Lianghui conventions, a female petitioner was taken by unidentified people to Fuyou Street Police Station in Xicheng District (Beijing) when she was going to send a petition letter at Lixue Hutong in Xicheng District (Beijing), and she was sent to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail'. She was sent back to Shenyang the same night, then 'taken on mandatory holiday' by stability maintenance personnel across various locations in Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning from 6-13 March. She escaped on 14 Mar from the Dandong Fenghuang City Dongtang Town Wanze Hot Spring Holiday Hotel.

On 5 March 2018, a Shanghainese human rights defender was sent back to Shanghai by police while he was taking the subway in Beijing. He was then detained at a private security firm for a day before being sent to a 'black jail' in Jiangxi province where he was detained until the First Session of the 13th National People's Congress closed on 20 March 2018.

On 4 March 2018, a petitioner was taken from Haining (Jiaxing, Zhejiang) by police from Shanghai and sent back to Shanghai to be detained in a 'black jail' in Qingpu District until 21 March 2018. The reason of the detention is to prevent him from petitioning during the 'two sessions' of the National People's Congress and the Chinese Political Consultative Conference (NPC & CPPCC).

On 4 March 2018, during the national 'two sessions', a pro-democracy activist was 'taken on mandatory vacation' in Qiandao Lake, together with his wife, by national security agents after being released from the Fourth Prison of Zhejiang Province in Yuhang District in Hangzhou (Zhejiang). During this period, he was placed under surveillance by the national security agents who stayed in the hotel room next to his. The activist was released after serving his sentence of seven years in prison for 'inciting subversion of state power' on 10 February 2012.

On 3 March 2018, when the Lianghui conventions started, a female petitioner in Suzhou (Jiangsu) was kept by stability maintenance personnel in Suzhou Dingtai Garden, a 'black jail' and suffered from headache, as well as fainting, caused by no food offered by the personnel. She was kept in 'black jail' during the Lianghui conventions because she petitioned against forced eviction previously.

On 2 March 2018, a Three-Self Church in Chengguan town, Yichuan county of Luoyang city, Henan was sealed off by workers from the local district government and soon closed down. The workers claimed that 'central authorities were coming in for an inspection' even though the church had proper documentation in order.

On 2 March 2018, a female petitioner who had been detained for the past 3 days was taken away by the Chief of the Yellow Crane Tower Police Station of Wuchang District (Wuhan, Hubei), and had been missing at least until the time of report on 12 April 2018. No further news about her whereabouts. It was suspected that she was taken to be detained in a 'black jail' in Wuhan city. Her disappearance was part of the authorities' crackdown on petitioners around the 'lianghui' period.

On 2 March 2018, a petitioner was disappeared and detained in a 'black jail' after lodging a police report in Beijing. He had been missing at least until the date of report on 12 April 2018. No further news on this person. His disappearance was part of the authorities' crackdown on petitioners around the 'lianghui' period.

On 2 March 2018, a human rights activist was taken away by the police in Beijing to 'take a mandatory vacation' while the 'two sessions' were being held in the city. It was reported that he was taken to Zhongshan until 22 March 2018 when the 'two sessions' ended.

On 1 March 2018, two petitioners, who were husband and wife, were taken away by the secretary of the Anqing City Bridge Subdistrict Office and the police from their apartment in Xiaobailou Village in Daxing District of Beijing. They were sent back to their hometown, Anqing City, and was subsequently detained in 'black jail' separately. During the detention, subdistrict office personnel repeatedly threatened the wife to sign a resettlement agreement and refused her seeing a doctor. The husband was detained until 12 April. The wife was detained in an abandoned hostel until 3 May.

Around 1 March 2018 (beginning of month), a female petitioner from Wuxi Beitang District was intercepted by inspectors while traveling on a bus in Beijing on her way to petition at the Supreme People's Court, and sent to an inspection centre. Later, she was sent to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' by the Tongzhou District Police. On the next day, she was sent back to Wuxi and placed under residential surveillance.

On 1 March 2018, a 'black security guard' snatched a female petitioner's phone while she was walking about in Beijing. She was then sent back to her hometown, Wuhan City, and was subsequently detained in a 'black jail' and had not been released by the date of report on 12 April 2018. Her disappearance is part of the authorities' crackdown on petitioners around the 'lianghui' period.

On 28 February 2018, a local Muslim and his son were taken away from Huocheng County (Ili Kazak Autonomous, Xinjiang) by local authorities and detained in a 'transformation through education camp' for applying for passports.

Around 28 February 2018 (end of month), a Kazakh woman (originally from Emin County, now a Kazakhstan citizen) was taken away by the authorities in Emin County (Tacheng, Xinjiang) and sent to a re-education camp. She had recently returned to China on 14 December 2017 to undergo a household de-registration process in order to give up her Chinese citizenship, which had been reported as a likely reason for her detention. During her detention, she was forced to learn 'red songs' and the Chinese language. She was later released at the end of November 2018, and returned to Kazakhstan sometime after.

On 27 February 2018, shortly before the 'Lianghui' period, police illegally detained a retired professor of Shandong University and held him incommunicado for 40 days in Yanzi Mountain Villa in Lixia District, Jinan, Shandong. He was detained as authorities feared he would carry out activities commemorating the Tiananmen massacre during this period. He was released on 7 April and went back to his home in Shandong University, Jinan City (Shandong), where he continued to be monitored.

On 26 February 2018, the local government tore down two bell towers and statues, as well as the cross on the top of a Catholic church in Yining City (Ili, Xinjiang), and the religious symbols on the outer wall of the church were also painted over for the reason that the church was not in conformance of 'sinicization'.

On 25 February 2018, before the Lianghui Conventions, eight petitioners were taken away by ten police officers from a rental house in Dadong Village (Fangshan, Beijing) and sent to Jingjiuzhuang 'black jail' in Beijing. This was part of a broad campaign to prevent petitioners from travelling to Beijing to petition during the Lianghui Conventions.

On 25 February 2018, between 100 and more than 200 people from 16 trade unions and organisations, including the Hong Kong Confederation of Trade Unions (HKCTU) and the Living Wage Alliance, and a district councillor from ADPL, protested in Wan chai District (Hong Kong) as part of the '225 Outsourcing 225 Reform Outsourcing Parade' which demands equal pay for equal work for outsourced workers, criticised the government for encouraging the exploitation of outsourced workers and called for the government to reform the outsourcing system to improve the treatment of workers. The parade left Southorn Stadium in Wan Chai and marched to the government headquarters in Central and Western District. After the march, members from the Living Wage Alliance handed a petition to a representative of the Labour and Welfare Bureau. Protesters held banners.

On 25 February 2018, a human rights activist from Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province was sent from Beijing to Kunshan City by government personnel who had beaten her up the day before. She was detained under surveillance in a temporary residence in Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province before being taken away on 26 February 2019 by unidentified persons, who then detained her in a 'black jail' at an unreported location for one month. She was released on the evening of 24 March 2019.

On 24 February 2018, a human rights activist from Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province was taken away and beaten in Beijing by personnel from the Kunshan Municipal Government, on the eve of the 'lianghui'. Her two mobile phones and identity card were also forcibly taken away. She was later sent to a temporary residence in Kunshan City on 25 February 2018, where she was detained under surveillance.

On 23 February 2018, a female petitioner was beaten at home in Wu'an town (Nanzhang, Xiangyang, Hubei) by a local community officer and a dozen 'unemployed people' hired by the government. She was then taken to the community office, a hotel and eventually a 'black jail' at the intersection of Xinji (Nanzhang county), Leihe and Liuhou townships (Yicheng county). She was detained until the morning of 28 March 2018 when three people dropped her at a place more than 20 km away from her home. The petitioner was suspected to have been given illegal drugs and reported that she had been suffering weakness and motoric problems since being taken to detention.

On 23 February 2018, tens of thousands of petitioners gathered outside the National Bureau of Letters and Calls in Xicheng District (Beijing), waiting in line at the office to submit a petition for their individual reasons in response to a call for solidarity. During this period, an unreported number of people in the crowd started chanting 'we want human rights, we want fairness, we want rule of law, we want justice', before other petitioners joined in the chorus of chants. It was reported that earlier on 22 January 2018, petitioners had designated 23 February 2018 as the monthly 'National Day of Solidarity for Petitioners'.

On 21 February 2018, 6 people (who had reportedly petitioned before) were abducted by triad members in Taoranting Park in Xicheng District (Beijing - Xicheng) and forcibly repatriated to Fuzhou. It was reported that the group had already been intercepted by police officers earlier in the afternoon while visiting Tiananmen Square and taken away to the Tiananmen Public Security Branch. The officials had attempted to transfer the group to a 'black jail', but they were released as the 'black jail' was closed during Chinese New Year. After making their way back to Taoranting Park, they were taken away by triad members and repatriated to Fuzhou (Fujian). 1 man in group was beaten during the journey, leaving his face bloodied.

On 19 February 2018, a 24 years old Kazakh man from Koktagai Village, Aqdala Township (Ili Kazakh Autonomous, Xinjiang) was taken by the police and sent to a 'political education camp'. He had returned to Xinjiang from Kazakhstan in January 2018 to sell his residence, but had his passport confiscated by the local police. It was claimed that his sister was also sent to a 'political education camp' after she returned to China, though reports from Xinjiang Victims Database suggest that she was put to a 'special camp' for two months, likely between June and August, to attend classes daily and was allowed to return home each evening.

Around 15 February 2018 (month of), men from 17 households in a village in Xinjiang were arrested by authorities and sent to 'transformation through education' camps for unspecified sentences and release dates. At least one of these men practised Islamic worship.

Around 14 February 2018 (month of), a family of ten members were forcibly taken away from Huocheng County (Ili Kazak Autonomous, Xinjiang) while they were reading the Quran at home. They were detained in a 'transformation through education camp' for having a 'gang gathering'. They remained detained in the education camp at the time of reporting on 3 October 2018.

Around 14 February 2018 (month of), a Uyghur woman residing in Urumqi, Xinijang was taken away by the authorities and detained in an 'internment camp' somewhere around Dawan neighbourhood in Urumqi. She was reportedly released on 1 May 2019, but was not allowed to contact her children who are residing in the US. The reasons for her detention were unclear.

Around 14 February 2018 (month of), a Kazakhstan citizen originally from Tacheng county (Tacheng, Xinjiang) in China was first intercepted by authorities while travelling to Beijing for business, before being forced to fly to Tacheng, where he was held at a detention centre for four days and sent to several 'internment camps'. The official reason for his detention was for failing to 'de-register' from his Chinese citizenship as a dual citizenship holder, although the victim stated this was completed back in 2002. In mid-April 2018, officials admitted to having no grounds for holding him, before he and two other Kazakhstan citizens were released and allowed to return home.

On 26 January 2018, during the 'two sessions' of Jiangsu Province, a female petitioner was taken by 7 to 8 people from the Kunshan City Urban Management Committee including the Secretary of Chaoyang District from the train station in Kunshan county-level city (Suzhou, Jiangsu) and first detained at Hongfeng sub-district office and then at Baigao Hotel for 65 days in Kunshan until 30 March 2018 when the national 'two sessions' ended. The petitioner has been petitioning for many years on house demolitions and contracting of bus routes. In the past, she was also repeatedly illegally detained by the government in the name of maintaining stability.

On 12 April 2021, in the early hours, four masked men trespassed on a printing plant in Tsuen Wan district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Tsuen Wan) belonging to Epoch Times, a newspaper and media company affiliated with Falun Gong, a spiritual and religious movement banned in mainland China. They smashed printing equipment and several computer screens with their sledgehammers, and scattered concrete powder and rubble into the core mechanical components. They threatened the staff members on duty, and looted several central processing units (CPUs).

On 15 February 2020, unidentified persons threw petrol bomb at a general outpatient clinic in Tai Po (Tai Po District, Hong Kong), leaving its gate blackened by the fire. The general outpatient clinic had recently been listed as one of the 18 designated clinics for the treatment of coronavirus. No arrests reported. This was one of numerous cases of these designated clinics being targeted using petrol bombs, since the government announced the list of 18 designated clinics.

Around 30 September 2019 (end of month), a labour unionist running in the upcoming district council elections was assaulted by at least three men in Sai Kung district (Hong Kong). The assailants smashed his hands with metal rods. Vigilante violence had been reportedly increasing on both sides of the ideological divide in Hong Kong after a few months of demonstrations, and victims often include rally organisers, opposition lawmakers, student leaders and people standing for upcoming polls.

On 14 February 2020, unidentified persons threw petrol bombs at a community health centre in Kwai Chung (Kwai Tsing District, Hong Kong), which caught fire on the rolling shutters at the main entrance. It was reported that the government had listed the hospital as a designated clinic for coronavirus treatment, which had caused dissatisfaction for their failure to consult the public. It was the second incident of petrol bombs hurled at the same hospital in a week.

On 1 March 2020, unidentified black-clad persons hurled petrol bombs at a general outpatient clinic in Kowloon Bay, Kwun Tong District (Hong Kong). The clinic was one of the 18 designated clinics for treating suspected coronavirus patients. No arrest reported. This was one of many incidents of designated clinics or quarantine centres across Hong Kong targeted using petrol bombs since the government announced its plan for the coronavirus outbreak.

On 19 November 2019, 4 unknown individuals wearing black clothes set fire around 3am to a print factory at Mong Kok, Yau Tsim Mong District (Kowloon City, Hong Kong) which printed for the anti-CCP newspaper, The Epoch Times.

On 4 February 2019, the home of a petitioner in Chengyang, Qingdao, including its windows and gates, was locked up from the outside with metal chains by members of anti-petitioning groups. Members of the vigilante group stood guard outside the family's home for at least eight days, preventing entry or exit.

On 22 July 2019, anti-ELAB demonstrators and students vandalised LegCo member and lawyer Junius Ho Kwan-yiu's branch office at Tsuen Fung Centre, Tsuen Wan district (Hong Kong) after a white-clad mob attacked demonstrators and rail passengers at the Yuen Long MTR station the night before (known later as the '7.21 incident.') They smashed windows and wrecked property. The act took place after the pro-Beijing lawmaker was filmed - in a video widely shared on social media - shaking hands with men in white outfits on the night of the incident.

On 4 July 2019, about 100 people surrounded a district councillor from the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong and her assistant in Tin Shui Wai, Yuen Long, in opposition to her collecting public opinion on the 'violent storming of the Legislature'. Mistaken as a volunteer of the pro-Beijing party, one citizen was mildly hurt by the crowd.

On 10 November 2018, a group of unidentified people cut off power from, smashed CCTVs, threw things, and poured human excrement into the residence of a petitioner who was foced evicted in Fengtai district (Beijing).

On 4 October 2019, more than 10 people in black clothes wearing face masks attacked a train that just arrived at the Fanling Station in North District (Hong Kong) at around 11pm and were bound for Guangzhou city. They vandalised the train's windows with hammers and sticks. This event was reported to take place after the government announced the anti-mask emergency law earlier on the same day.

On 5 March 2020, more than 101 tenants protested at a clothing wholesale market in Liwan District (Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province), asking for a waiver for the rent for the months of February and March. This was due to the coronavirus outbreak, which had impacted their income. The demonstrators marched in the venue, holding placards.

On 20 March 2020, more than 100 merchants from a clothing wholesale market held a protest march in Shahe, Tianhe District (Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province), calling for a waiver of rental fee. The demonstration was held in response to the rent reduction policy, which the merchants claimed they were unable to benefit from, due to the subletting contracts at the wholesale market. A large number of police officers were at the scene, and raised a warning flag at one point, but did not intervene.

On 19 January 2019, a China-born Australian author who has been critical of the Chinese government was seized from Guangzhou Airport in Baiyun District (Guangzhou, Guangdong) and taken to Beijing by state security police to be interrogated with his wife. His wife was released after the interrogation, but the author was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) in Beijing. His RSDL term was due to expire on 19 July, but on 17 July, he was formally arrested on charges of endangering national security and transferred to a detention centre in Beijing.

On 13 September 2021, a few hundred private security guards employed by the government beat up a man during an eviction raid in Chongchuan district (Nantong, Jiangsu). The man suffered from ribs fractured. The local government demolished a farm without any notice or following any legal procedure.

The interception was part of the campaign to suppress dissentients before the 20th National Congress of the CCP in Beijing scheduled to started on 16 October 2022.

The attempts were part of the local officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the 20th National Congress of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 16 October 2022.
