It was further stated that this was conducted as a first warning, and a real bomb targeting the customs will be planned if the demands for border closure and medical staff strike were not met.

On 29 October 2019, a petitioner was intercepted by a dozen government employees at Beijing West Station (Fengtai District, Beijing) and detained in a hotel on the Gulou West Street (Beijing - Fengtai). By the time of report, 1 November 2019, he was still detained. The detentions were part of local officials' campaign to stifle dissent during the Fourth Plenum of the Nineteenth Party Congress, scheduled to commence on 28 October and conclude four days later.

On 31 March 2020, around 300 to 500 business owneres held a banner and chanted slogans at a wholesale market in Hanchuan City (Xiaogan City, Hubei Province), demanding for a reduction in rent. The demonstration began with five business owners, who then called on a large number of business owners and their own family members to hold banners and shout slogans in front of the wholesale market during the demonstration, leading to around 300 to 500 business owners joining. The police issued a statement on 6 April 2020 that the demonstration was an 'illegal gathering', and 3 of the 5 business owners have been placed under administrative detention. This was one of two demonstrations reported on the same day in China, led by business owners demanding a reduction in rent due to the negative impact on their businesses during the coronavirus outbreak.

As reported on 24 August 2019, as many as 100 workers protested in Zhongshan, Guangdong to demand for wage arrears owed to them by a construction project. The company agreed to pay the workers in 10 days.

On 5 June 2021, a female petitioner detained at Chengxi Police Station of the Fengdu County Public Security Bureau was transferred to a 'black jail' set up by the Xinjian Village Committee of Sanhe Subdistrict. Triad members guarded the facility. Before being detained, she had been beaten unconscious by unknown persons. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 10 November 2018, a petitioner was struck on the head by a triad member during his visit to the Wuyi County Petitioning Bureau (Jinhua, Zhejiang). The Bureau Chief threatened to prosecute the petitioner and warned him against taking his grievances to higher-ups in Beijing.

On 22 June 2021, three women were detained, under the watch of over 20 triad members, at a 'black jail' facility set up by the Xinjian Village Committee of Sanhe subdistrict, Fengdu district (Chongqing). The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 4 July 2021, over 10 triad members allegedly sent by the village leaders raided a civilian's house and attacked a petitioner in Xiajing village (Fuzhou, Fujian). Triad members threatened to take his life if he insisted on filing complaints about construction plans undertaken by the village mayor and secretary. He left his teeth and ribs broken, however, the police refused to step into the case.

On 23 June 2021, a petitioner from Wuxi, Jiangsu, who sought protection from police after submitting a petition, was taken away by personnel from the Beijing office of the Jiangsu Provincial Government in front of the National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration in Xicheng district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Xicheng). He was taken in a car to Jinghua Hotel in Xicheng district (Beijing) where he was placed under triad members' watch. During the 10-hour detention, he was knocked to the ground and lost consciousness and was suffering from food deprivation. He was transferred to Shuofang Police Station (Wuxi) on 24 June before being released on 25 June.

On 4 July 2021, a man from Xiyuan village, Fujian, was beaten up by government-backed triad members in a guesthouse in Emei village (Fuzhou, Fujian) as retaliation after he sought help from a policeman walking outside. An hour later, the policeman returned and set him free at Xindian Police station. Triad members first intercepted him at Beijing West station, Beijing, on 28 June 2021 and detained him at the house, where he was monitored, threatened, tortured, and attacked.

On 19 February 2022, at around 2 am, four Triad members ordered by the Wufeng Subdistrict government wearing anti-chemical clothes raided the room of a detained female petitioner and beat her up in Room 8605 in Super 8 hotel in Gulou district (Fuzhou, Fujian). They took away the female petitioner's identity card, mobile phone, and other personal belongings, and stayed behind to guard her room. The petitioner was intercepted by Fuzhou Government officers in Beijing on 17 February and was detained at the hotel for COVID-19 quarantine.

On 26 February 2022, three men raided the room of a detained female petitioner and suffocated her in Room 8605 in Super 8 hotel in Gulou district (Fuzhou, Fujian). The petitioner was intercepted by Fuzhou Government officers in Beijing on 17 February midnight and was detained at the hotel for COVID-19 quarantine. On 5 March 2022, she was transferred by quarantine workers to the hands of Triad members and held in another confined hostel room until being released at 10 pm on 14 March 2022.

On 5 April 2022, a petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Qianjiang, Hubei, was abducted by members of unknown triad groups outside a subway station in Beijing - Fengtai. He was sent to Yuanlin Police station in Qianjiang, Hubei and detained at a hospital for 15 days. On 21 April 2022, he was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) in an unknown location. On 1 June, he was officially charged with 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' and detained in custody.

On 5 April 2022, a female petitioner was abducted by a group of government-hired Triad members outside a subway exit in Nanyuan Residential District in Beijing - Fengtai after holding a sole demonstration at Beijing South Station. She was sent back to her hometown in Wuhan, Hubei, and became incommunicado. On 18 June 2022, it was reported that she was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL).

On 20 May 2022, two Xiaohongmen police station officers and a Hongsi Village manager leading almost 70 people (including 50-60 urban management officers and some triad members) kidnapped two married petitioners near the Supreme People's Court Shensu Li'an Hall in Beijing - Chaoyang. The petitioners were beaten up before dragging onto a vehicle and repatriating back to their hometown in Hubei in Shiyan city. Upon arriving Shiyan, they were held at multiple locations, including a canteen near a mental hospital.

On 28 September 2022, a local triad member sent by a party official beat up a 77-year-old female petitioner with a bamboo broom, causing her right eye to bulge and bleed, in Changle district (Fuzhou, Fujian). She had to be taken to a hospital afterwards and it is unclear whether she could recover from the injuries. She had been a long-time petitioner against the party official. A day ago, she was en route to Beijing to file a complaint against the party official for colluding with triad members and appropriating public resources, before she was intercepted by the police and taken back to Fuzhou.

On 17 October 2022, triad members hired by the Shiyan government's Beijing office detained the daughter of a Shiyan-based petitioner in a hostel, after taking her away in Beijing - Fengtai. The daughter was 'traveling', presumably going to submit petitions, in Beijing, and had had difficulties finding work and education because of her mother's petitions.

On 21 March 2023, 14 representatives of the Alliance of Four, including four lawmakers, held banners and placards, and handed a petition letter to a government official, outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the government considers the railway company's profits before approving the rate of fare hikes that it proposes.

On 20 March 2023, around 20 members of the Asian Migrants' Coordinating Body held placards and banners outside a government building in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They were dissatisfied that the government is considering changing the law to restrict their ability to change their employers, which they said constitutes discrimination and an infringement of their labor rights.

Around 12 March 2023 (week of), stability maintenance officials sent by the local government beat up a petitioner twice in multiple hostels in Minhang district (Minhang, Shanghai), where they detained him and his partner from 4 March 2023 to 14 March 2023. The officers had picked him and his partner up from a police station in the city. The couples were there because the petitioner had called the police after people hired by the local government tried to intercept him when he was getting on a car to travel to Ningbo. The detentions were part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 4 March 2023.

On 20 March 2023, police beat up a Tibetan woman, causing injuries to her right arm, in a police station in Chengguan district (Lhasa, Tibet). They had detained her there for protesting for the release of her brother, who had been put on life sentence on loan fraud charges in 2008 after the government accused him of being a secessionist for supporting anti-government protests and having political connections with the exiled Tibetan community.

On 4 June 2020, a Tibetan writer became incommunicado after police took him away from his home in Ngawa County (Aba, Sichuan). It was known in December 2022 that he had been sentenced to four years in prison on charges of 'inciting splittist acts and spreading rumours in WeChat groups'. In May 2020, he wrote an essay advocating for Tibetans' right to learn the Tibetan language, as schools in the area he lived in only taught Mandarin.

On 23 January 2020, a petitioner and her sister from Fuzhou, Fujian were intercepted by 'rogue gangsters' hired by the government at the Fuzhou Railway Station in Jin'an (Fujian). Her sister had her mobile phone taken by the triad members and left on one of the roads in Xindian Town, Jin'an District. The sister later received a call from a staff member of a mental hospital that the petitioner had been brought to and detained in a mental hospital.

On 30 April 2019, two petitioners were transferred by a triad leader, employed by the government, from a black jail in Chongming Island, Shanghai to an unknown place. It was part of a campaign by the CCP to silence dissent before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation which held in Beijing on April 25-27.

On 7 July 2019, a female petitioner was beaten up and taken away by members of unknown triad groups in Qianjiang, Hubei. She was illegally detained in a house in Yuanlin Village, where she was forced to kneel down for two hours, three times a day. Throughout her detention, she was repeatedly threatened and assaulted by the triad members, who forced her to sign an agreement to have her home demolished by the government. She was also forced to turn in her identity documents and receive 5000 RMB and a letter of guaranty. On 5 November 2019, she was released after she had signed the agreement.

On 27 September 2019, four triad members employed by a communal office beat two petitioners at Hushan village in Yiwu City (Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province) because of their previous petitions against the Yiwu City government. The two petitioners were sent to the hospital later. They reported the incident to the police but the police refused to register the case without giving any reason.

On 1 June 2019, two petitioners from Xinjiang were abducted in Beijing by triad members hired by stability maintenance officials of Yingshan, Sichuan. They were naked while being taken away and sent back to Yingshan, Sichuan and were then detained in an iron cage there.

Around 20 October 2019 (between 13 - 28 Oct), a petitioner was abducted by police from Zhushan County and some gangsters at Wuhan City Train Station (Hubei Province) and sent to the nursing home in Majiadu Town (Zhushan County, Shiyan City, Hubei Province) at night. During his 15-day detention, petitioner was beaten several times by the director of the nursing home together with the leader of a local triad and others on orders of the town government. The petition went on hunger strike during his detention in protest. After his family shared the pictures online which showed that the police had followed him on the train before he was abducted, he was treated medically and released on 28 October 2019.

On 20 May 2020, two mother-and-son petitioners were taken away after seeking help at the Dongcheng district police station (Beijing - Dongcheng) and transferred to Jiujingzhuang Relief Center 'black jail'. On the same night, they were escorted by 20-30 officers and around 10 hired triad members to Yongdingmen Hotel (the Changzhou Liaison Office in Beijing), then on 21 May to Jiutouniao Hotel, and on 22 May to Gaoqing gas station in Zibo, Shandong. On 22 May, they returned to Changzhou and were locked in Zhengzhang Hotel 'black jail' until the mother was forcibly admitted to a local psychiatric ward on 3 June, and her son remained until his release on 22 July. From 20 May to 22 July, they were reportedly beaten and robbed by officers, triad members, government officials, and put in abusive situations harmful to their health and personal hygiene.

On 10 September 2018, mayor of the Yujing Town of Qianshan City (Anqing, Anhui), along with a well-known member of a local triad group, beat up villagers of Huangling Village who spoke and petitioned against the election fraud and the disqualification of two Villager's Committee candidates in the upcoming election.

On 26 September 2020, a female petitioner was kicked and beaten up by stability maintenance officers and 6-7 triad members at her home in Pingzhou village of Heyao township, Xiangdong district (Pingxiang, Jiangxi). They had been guarding her house since intercepting her the day before at the Pingxiang Bureau of Letters and Calls, where she petitioned for compensation of housing damages due to a government mining operation.

On 21 February 2021, a labour rights activist working for a state-owned railway construction company in Nangang district, Harbin was kidnapped by triad members at the Chaoyang Train Station in Chaoyang district (Beijing) (coded to Beijing - Chaoyang). The incident was reported on 24 Feb 2021 as one of many stability maintenance efforts ahead of the annual Lianghui meetings.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 21 September 2019, more than 200 demonstrators organised a sit-in at YOHO Mall in Yuen Long district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Yuen Long) against the police inaction during the attack at Yuen Long MTR station on 21 July 2019. They sang the song 'Glory to Hong Kong' and chanted Five Demands slogans. They threw two Molotov cocktails on the road, with one hitting a police car. Some 50 demonstrators set up barricades, obstructing traffic. Around 100 riot police came. Riot police fired at least three tear gas during clearance operation. Many residents were dissatisfied with police action and scolded them. A passer-by was hospitalised after a group of demonstrators targeted him with pepper spray and glass bottles, and claimed that he was previously seen removing messages from a Lennon Wall. A woman was also reportedly sexually harassed by a man, who then fainted. At least four people were taken away by police.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 7 July 2019, 56,000-230,000 people participated in a march to the West Kowloon High-Speed Rail Station in Yau Tsim Mong district (Hong Kong) (coded to Hong Kong - Yau Tsim Mong), which was initiated by online dissenters to spread awareness of the anti-ELAB movement to mainland tourists, and to urge the government to fulfill their 'five demands'. Many people refused to leave after reaching the destination at around 4pm. Some of them got into confrontations with police from across road barriers and directed lasers at them. At night, after the march, a few hundred demonstrators gathered at the tourist area of Canton Road. As they attempted to proceed to the Tsim Sha Tsui Ferry Pier, police formed a chain to block them. Clashes broke out, resulting in injuries and several arrests. At 10 p.m., the demonstrators proceeded to Mong Kok. Police began efforts to disperse them around 11 p.m. and further clashes, injuries, and arrests ensued. A female passerby was rounded up by at least three demonstrators, choked, bruised and sexually assaulted. She was targeted for taking photos of the demonstration and mistaken to be an undercover officer. The 'clearance operation' ended around 2 a.m. the following day.

On 29 March 2023, around 40 residents of a village held placards and banners outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western to protest against the government's rehousing policy, as it planned to demolish their village for redevelopment.

On 26 March 2023, around 100 teachers chanted slogans and held banners and placards outside the school in which they worked in Leping city (Jingdezhen, Jiangxi). They demanded equal work, equal pay and demanded to be paid according to their performance.

On 31 March 2023, many transgender persons held placards outside the Immigration Department in Hong Kong - Wan Chai to demand that the department allows them to change the gender on their identification cards without reassignment surgery, which the Court of Final Appeal had ruled in favor of in February.

Around 6 June 2021 (between 4 June - 8 June), four out of at least seven rights defending citizens from Chongqing had become incommunicado after conveying forced demolition issues in Beijing municipality, and 'being retaliated against by their local government.' The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

Around 6 June 2021 (as reported), a rights defender was tortured while serving his sentence at No.3 Detention Centre in Zhengzhou prefecture (Henan) (coded to Zhongyuan). It was reportedly an act of retaliation by the detention officers, after his family members filed a complaint against how late a gift of theirs was delivered to the rights defender.

On 3 June 2021, local authorities captured and detained a rights defender at a hotel 'black jail' in Panjin prefecture (Liaoning) (coded to Xinglongtai). The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 29 May 2021, a rights defender from Wushun, Liaoning was kidnapped onto a car with no license plate near the Xingcheng Meilianmei Supermarket in Yancun town of Fangshan district (Beijing), and transported to a soft detention arrangement at Xinfu No.3 Hospital in Fushun prefecture (Liaoning). Many 'black security guards' stood by in the corridor.

On 17 May 2021, five of the 10 pro-democracy politicians and activists - lawyers, former legislators and district councillors, and members of the CHRF, DP, LSD and The Alliance - shouted slogans before their trial at the District Court in Wan Chai district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Wan Chai). The popular democracy slogans they shouted were 'Fight for Freedom,' 'there are no thugs, only tyranny,' 'peaceful demonstrations are innocent, political persecution is shameful, and all political prisoners should be released,' and 'Five Demands not One Less.' A group of LSD representatives and a district councillor also showed up while holding up a banner in solidarity with political prisoners.

On 12 May 2021, parents gathered at Dujiangyan Juyuan Middle School in Dujiangyan district (Chengdu, Sichuan) for the thirteenth year, and commemorated student victims of the Sichuan Wenchuan Earthquake. Police officers tried to cordon off the road, but ultimately allowed the gathering to carry on. The parents lit firecrackers, burnt offerings and left flowers. They used the event to advance their rights-defending efforts, seeking justice for those who died due to 'tofu-dregs schoolhouses' - a term referring to the controversial subpar school structures revealed to be poorly built after collapse during the earthquake.

On 11 May 2021, a detained rights defender was beaten up at the Tiaodenghe Police Station in Chenghua district (Chengdu, Sichuan) after being rounded up at a demonstration at the local secondary school, where he was caught photographing the scene. He was also slapped in the police car on their way to the station.

On 30 April 2021, a rights defender from Yubei district, Chongqing was released from Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' in Fengtai district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Fengtai), then intercepted at the 485 Rd Bus Stop nearby by five to six liaison officials and police officers from Longxing Police Station (of Chongqing). He was incommunicado for at least 24 hours. On 3 May, the victim communicated that he was on his way home, riding a coach bus with the escort of Longxing workers (assumed to be representing the police or local government).

On 27 April 2021, The Alliance, CHRF and labour unions organised a joint street counter on the footbridge outside the Immigration Tower in Wanchai district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Wan Chai) to oppose the Immigration Ordinance amendments ahead of its second LegCo reading. They held up a placard to express their concerns.

On 22 April 2021, multiple organisations - the Alliance, CHRF, HKCTU and other industry groups representing 'white collar workers,' tourism and insurance industries - held a joint press conference and demonstrated in Hong Kong to urge the government to promise that the 2020 Immigration (Amendment) Ordinance would not pose threats to Hong Kongers' freedom of leaving borders. The Ordinance would undergo a second reading at the Legislative Council the following week. They held up placards to express their demands.

On 21 April 2021, a lawyer was beaten up by some unidentified men while taking a stroll with his wife in a residential area near Donglinjicang, 302 Guangshanyi Lu, Tianhe district of Guangzhou city (Guangdong). The hospital diagnosed him with multiple bodily and facial injuries, bruises and fractures. National security officers were suspected to be involved in the incident by way of threatening him and his family to move out of Guangdong province, and back to his home province of Hunan. The lawyer had been a target of the state since 2018 for rights defending efforts, and representing tuberculosis patients in the suing of the Taojiang county government (in Hunan) for professional malpractice.

On 15 April 2021, a rights activist was kicked and choked at the Qiema Subdistrict Office in Beibei district (Chongqing) by the Vice Chief of the district's Sub-Bureau Security Bureau, then detained at the Qiema Police Station for nine hours. At the time, he had just been intercepted in Beijing with six other petitioners, and escorted back to Chongqing.

Around 4 April 2021, a renowned rights activist from Jilin was sent to Jilin Guowen Hospital in Gongzhuling district (Siping, Jilin) with a brain hemorrhage while serving his 13-year jail term at Gongzhuling Prison. Upon hospitalisation, he was emaciated and unable to breath on his own. Surgeons removed 'a large piece of bone' from his artery that was blocking blood supply to his brain. He died on 9 April after having two operations and becoming comatose. It was reported that the victim was held in solitary confinement in a two-metre-square cell, and was subjected to prolong torture by authorities in order to get him to confess to charged offences. He was jailed after lodging an official complaint for embezzlement against several local officers but lost, and allegedly, for his public support for the pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong.

On 25 March 2021, at night time, a rights activist residing in Pidu district (Chengdu, Sichuan) with his mother was kidnapped by a group of unidentified individuals (assumed to be linked to the government). Political dissidents acquainted with the victim alleged that the act was a form of retaliation by the Chengdu police against him for openly commemorating lives of students lost during the 5.12 earthquake.

On 20 March 2021, rights defenders held up placards in Wuxi Prefecture (Jiangxi) (coded to Binhu) to protest against the Secretary of the Wuxi Municipal Party Committee for keeping the Jiangsu Provincial Political and Legal Team Education and Rectification Steering Group hidden.

On 4 March 2021, a rights defender placed under house arrest in Sanfangqixiang subdistrict of Gulou district (Fuzhou, Fujian) was beaten by local authorities when he expressed wishes to leave the house. The incident was reported on 5 Mar 2021 as one of many stability maintenance efforts during the annual Lianghui meetings.

On 2 March 2021, a dozen members of the Guizhou Human Rights Research Centre were collectively 'taken on mandatory vacation' by the Guizhou Public Security Bureau to the countryside of Guiyang prefecture (Guizhou) (coded to Guanshanhu). The 'vacation' is expected to last ten days. It was reported that GHKRC members were frequently arranged to leave for the countryside during 'politically sensitive' periods such as the Lianghui meetings and the June Fourth anniversaries. They were reported to have been gradually returned home during 11-12 Mar 2021.

On 2 March 2021, a member of the Guizhou Human Rights Research Centre was tortured at a detention centre after being arrested at his residence by six police officers and the Deputy Chief of Huaxi District State Security (Guiyang, Guizhou). He was tied to a long bench and subject to 30 hours of sleep deprivation. He was released on 13 Mar 2021 with police officers refusing to give evidence of an arrest warrant and charges.

On 21 February 2021, 11 rights defenders were visiting a rights defender - living under residential surveillance in a temporary unit in Sanxi village of Caijiagang residential district (Beibei, Chongqing) - due to Chinese New Year festivities, when they were followed by two unidentified personnel arranged by the government to guard the place. Bodily clashes between the two parties ensued when they tried to take a group photo before leaving the place.

On 8 February 2021, a rights defender was assaulted by two residential district and stability maintenance officials from Hongshan town while he was waiting to meet a high-level official at the Gulou District Government Offices (Fuzhou, Fujian), planning to follow up on his wife's complaint case about forced farmland evictions. He was hospitalised for his injuries.

On 8 February 2021, seven defendants (former and current LegCo and district councillors, CHRF, LJL, LSD) protested at the West Kowloon Magistrates Court' in Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Sham Shui Po) against political persecution for having a peaceful demonstration gathering in July 2020, which was unapproved due to severity of the pandemic. They held up a banner and chanted slogans.

On 1 January 2021, four CHRF and The Alliance members (including a former legislator) drove a truck from Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre to the Legislative Council in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western), passing through popular protest landmarks and calling for the release of all political prisoners. They displayed a banner that collected citizens' wishes and signatures, and advocated (held up the gesture) for the five demands. Outside the Court of Final Appeal, LSD members also demonstrated and called for the same cause. Similar demonstrations were held in multiple districts across Hong Kong.

On 17 December 2020, eight pro-democracy activists (CHRF convenor, former and current legislators and district councillors from DP, LSD, LJL) and other supporters demonstrated at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts in Cheung Sha Wan, Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Sham Shui Po) against political persecution, and called for the five demands. They held up a banner and shouted slogans.

On 4 December 2020, human rights activists gathered in the woods next to the Wuxi Maternity and Child Health Care Hospital in Chong'an (Liangxi) district (Wuxi, Jiangsu) to protest against police brutality and police-government collusion in enforcing stability maintenance operations against petitioners and activists. They held up placards.

Around 2 December 2020 (as reported), a petitioner was taken on mandatory vacation by public security officials in Beijing municipality after applying for permission to host two protests (including for The National Legal Awareness Day and Human Rights Day) within the month.

On 17 November 2020, dozens of citizens and two political group representatives (PP, CHRF) gathered at the Wanchai District Courts in Wanchai district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Wan Chai) to show solidarity with People Power Vice-Chair, who was being tried for incitement under the National Security Law. They shouted for the five demands, and wore t-shirts with slogans on them.

On 27 October 2020, a rights defender from Jing'an district, Shanghai was intercepted by local government personnel in Beijing municipality and brought back to Shanghai, after which he remained incommunicado at the time of reporting on 29 Oct 2020. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance in relation to the fifth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee that had commenced in Beijing.

Arrests: On 26 October 2020, close to 50 rights defenders and petitioners were taken away in Beijing Municipality and taken to Fuyou Street Police Station in Xicheng District (Beijing). They were later transferred by car to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail'. It was not reported how long they were there for.

On 25 October 2020, a rights defender from Minhang district, Shanghai was taken away by government personnel from the Beijing Office from Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' in Fengtai District (Beijing) and repatriated back to Shanghai. Upon arrival at Fucun Road station, Putuo district (Shanghai), he was taken away by government-hired security forces. He remained incommunicado at the time of reporting on 29 Oct 2020, and was suspected to be detained in a 'black jail'. Three other men were also taken away from Jiujingzhuang and repatriated to Shanghai on the same train. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance in relation to the fifth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee set to commence in Beijing.

On 12 October 2020, a rights activist and organiser from Nanchang prefecture (Jiangxi) (coded to Honggutan) was kidnapped and forcibly admitted to the Jiangxi Province Mental Hospital by the government's stability maintenance department, after authorities received information that he was planning a collective petition for psychological torture victims. He was held for more than two months until release on 16 Dec.

On 18 September 2020, several dozen pro-democracy supporters demonstrated as 14 pro-democracy activists arrived at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts in Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) to face charges of unauthorized assembly. The 14 activists in attendance (The Alliance, CHRF, DP, former LegCo members, LSD) joined in with banners and placards before the trial, and shouted slogans calling for the five demands. Two groups of eight pro-Beijing supporters ('Johnny Patriotic 1010') also demonstrated and called for the activists to be punished. They held up banners and shouted.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 6 September 2020, some demonstrators created roadblocks, and threw hard objects like cans, umbrellas and bottles at the police in Yau Tsim Mong district (Hong Kong). Police officers released pepper bombs, affecting nearby hawkers. On the same day, many demonstrations took place in the district against the enactment of the National Security Law, the implementation of 'health code' and the one-year delay of Legislative Council elections (supposed to take place that day). Some were also concerned with the 12 Hong Kong stowaways (some anti-ELAB activists) who were detained in Shenzhen after being caught on a boat to Taiwan in mainland Chinese waters. 289 people were arrested in total that day for participating in demonstrations.

On 1 September 2020, two human rights activists from Xiangyang, Hubei were intercepted by police officers at Xike station in Fengtai district (Beijing) and sent to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail.' The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance ahead of an international trade conference (CIFTIS 2020) held in Beijing from 4-9 Sep.

Arrests: Around 31 August 2020, over 100 ethnic Mongolian parents, teachers, herders, protest organisers, rights activists and other protest participants were arrested or placed in various forms of detention across Inner Mongolia [coded to Xincheng] since the spread of large-scale student boycotts, strikes and demonstrations against a national-level state policy to replace Mongolian with Mandarin Chinese as the medium of instruction. The first of these demonstrations started on 28 Aug. As of 7 September, a total of over 200 ethnic Mongolians had been arrested in Tongliao and Ordos prefectures.

On 1 August 2020, a human rights defender from Chongqing was strangled by the chief of Yuejin Village Police Station (Dadukou, Chongqing) during a black-jail detention at Yanzhao Hotel in Baoding prefecture (Hebei). Earlier in the day, he was intercepted by the chief and 12 of his subordinates at Shijiazhuang station while aboard train Z4 traveling to Beijing. Many rights defenders traveling to Beijing, specifically from Chongqing, had reportedly become government targets in the first week of August.

On 1 August 2020, a human rights defender and her son were stopped and assaulted in their local residential area in Yubei district (Chongqing) by a group of plainclothes officers from Huixing Police Station. While her son was hospitalised, the rights defender was taken away in a police car and placed under 10 days of administrative detention. She was preparing to submit an administrative complaint case in Beijing, and was amongst several rights defenders from Chongqing who had reportedly become government targets in the first week of August.

On 29 June 2020, more than 30 human rights activists gathered at Chongqing Yubei People's Court in Yubei District (Chongqing), in solidarity with two human rights defenders who were appearing in court for a case against the public security bureau for assaulting civilians on the grounds of maintaining stability. It was reported that the activists who gathered outside the court were intercepted and beaten by community security personnel.

Around 25 June 2020 (from 19 - 28 June), an academic scholar and lawyer - also founder of the New Citizens' Movement and Open Constitution Initiative, and human rights defender - was tortured with sleep and food deprivation for ten days during Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) in Beijing after formal charges on 19 June for 'inciting subversion of state power.' He was first taken away on 15 Feb in Panyu district, Guangzhou city (Guangdong) by police officers who searched his friend's home in the name of a 'coronavirus check.' After the RSDL, he was transferred to the Linshu County Detention Centre (Linyi, Shandong) and was held there for over half a year at the time of reporting on 21 Jan 2021.

Around 21 June 2020 (between 21 - 22 June), a rights defender from Xuzhou, Jiangsu was taken away by public security officers in Fengtai district (Beijing) and escorted back to Dandong, Liaoning, where he was quarantined in a hotel for 14 days on the grounds of 'preventive/quarantine measures in relation to the coronavirus.' He was tied up with metal wires during the detention, and was reportedly incommunicado for 20 days.

On 19 June 2020, a human rights activist and his wife were taken away from a railway station in Xi County (Xinyang City, Henan Province) by the county's party committee secretary, deputy mayor and director of the public security bureau. They were then detained in a 'black jail'. They were released 13 hours after they were first intercepted at the railway station. It was reported that they had been intercepted by the government officials while making their way to Xinyang Intermediate People's Court to hear a court case.

On 3 June 2020, a political prisoner-cum-human rights defender from Yichang, Hubei was taken away from his temporary residence in Yichang City, Hubei Province by public security personnel. His wife later confirmed that he had been taken on a 'mandatory vacation', to prevent him from 'causing trouble' ahead of the 31st anniversary of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Protests. After he was taken away, all the posts on his Twitter account were erased. The public security personnel stated that they would send him back to his place of residence on 11 June 2020.

On 1 June 2020, a human rights activist from Zhuzhou City was taken away from Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province by public security personnel. He was then taken on a 'mandatory vacation' in Jiangxi and Anhui Province. During this period, he was placed under 24-hour surveillance by public security personnel and not allowed to post about the June 4th Tiananmen Square Protests on the internet. He was sent back home on 5 June 2020 after the anniversary of the June 4th Tiananmen Square Protests was over.

On 30 May 2020, a rights defender was taken by police officers from his home in Changsha prefecture (Hunan). It was later suspected that police officers from Yunnan province (specifically the Public Security Sub-Bureau of Yuelu district, Changsha prefecture) were responsible for the arrest, as a source close to the police informed that the rights defender was transferred to Yunnan the next day (31 May) under claims of involvement with 'an armed group.' As of 6 July 2020, his family had not received any official correspondences (verbal or written) from the police regarding his whereabouts or the charges brought against him.

On 20 May 2020, a human rights activist from Chongqing was arrested in Tiananmen, Dongcheng District (Beijing). He was then taken away to the police station for interrogation, before being transferred to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' to be detained for several hours. Staff members from the Chongqing Municipal People's Government Office in Beijing later arrived at Jiujingzhuang and escorted the activist back to Chongqing where he continued to be detained at an unreported location.

actor1: Police Forces of China (2012-) People's Armed Police
notes: On 8 April 2020, more than 1,000 special police officers, and an unreported number of government officials from the municipal offices and district office were mobilised to demolish a Qing Dynasty-era ancestral house of a human rights activist in Yaodu District (Linfen City, Shanxi Province). The demolition followed the arrest of the activist and his third sister the day before. It was reported that the authorities had attempted to suppress the family for many years through the departments of land planning, public security, fire protection, among many others. The activist had been a target of government suppression for his activism on mainstream media for vulnerable communities in Linfen City.

On 15 February 2020, a human rights defender was taken away by the police in Panyu District (Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province), on the grounds of subversion of state power. He was initially thought to be held incommunicado, but it was subsequently confirmed and reported on 7 March 2020 that he was held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL). His sister was told by Shandong police on 20 June 2020 that he has been officially arrested after being held in RSDL.

On 17 January 2020, more than 20 protesters from the Hong Kong Alliance, League of Social Democrats, and China Human Rights Lawyers Concern Group protested in front of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. This is in protest against the recent rounds of crackdown on human rights lawyers in Mainland China by the Chinese Communist Party.

On 6 January 2020, two petitioners were taken by police forces while shopping in Wangfujing, Beijing. They were later taken to Qiluqing hotel (Haidan, Beijing) and has since been detained in the hotel.

On 26 December 2019, a human rights lawyer from Yichang, Hubei was taken away by Shandong National Security Police from his friend's place in Beijing, and held incommunicado in state custody. Officials notified his lawyer on 10 Jan 2020 that he was taken into Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) for 'inciting subversion of state power.' The RSDL was later reported to have taken place in Yantai, Shandong, during which he was subjected to torture, including sleep and food deprivation. He was transferred to the Linshu County Detention Centre (Linyi, Shandong) at an unreported date. Three more human rights defenders from Fujian and Shandong were taken away by the Shandong police on 26 Dec, as part of their crackdown on a civic gathering in Xiamen on 13 Dec 2019.

On 26 December 2019, a human rights defender was taken away by Shandong National Security Police from his residence in Huli District (Xiamen City, Fujian Province). His family was informed by Huli police that he was held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location in relation to criminal charges. No legal document was provided by the police. His family was not sure if the arrest was related to his participation in the Xiamen meeting on 13 December. On the same day, three other people (including a human rights lawyer) were also taken away by Shandong police. The human rights defender has been set free on 19 June 2020.

On 26 December 2019, a human rights defender was taken away by Shandong National Security Police from his residence in Zhangzhou City, Fujian Province. He was held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location. No legal document was provided by the police. On the same day, three other people (including a human rights lawyer) were also taken away by Shandong police. Their arrests were part of the crackdown following the civic gathering in Xiamen on 13th December 2019. The human rights defender has been set free on 19 June 2020.

On 26 December 2019, a human rights defender was taken away by Shandong National Security Police from his residence in Yantai City, Shandong Province. His wife received a notice saying that he was being held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location and that their houses would be searched. She said the arrest was related to his participation in the Xiamen meeting on 13 December. On the same day, two Fujian residents and a human rights lawyer in Beijing were also taken away by Shandong police. The human rights defender has been set free on 19 June 2020.

On 28 November 2019, an activist from Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province was believed to have been taken away by the local police when he was visiting in Hunan Province and had since been held incommunado. The reasons for his detention were not known.

On 28 October 2019, three rights-defenders-cum-forced evictees from Pingnan county, Fujian were beaten by government-hired private security forces after a court hearing in Beijing, one of whom (the father) sustained six rib fractures. One of the female victims (the daughter) had been repeatedly targeted since winning multiple court cases against the government. After they were taken back to Pingnan, the daughter was charged with 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble,' and had since been detained at the Ningde City Detention Centre till the time of reporting on 14 Oct 2020.

On 19 September 2019, a dissident and human rights activist from Sichuan was taken away by the police in Sichuan province and was held incommunicado. The reason for the arrest was unclear, but it was suspected that it had to do with his plan to open an animal farm in Zhongnanhai.

Around 18 September 2019 (as reported), a human rights defender was taken from Beijing to Zhongshan (Guangdong province) on a 'forced vacation' due to the stability maintaince in Beijing before the National Day on 1 October.

On 16 September 2019, a human rights defender/petitioner from Shenyang went missing in Beijing when he was on his way to meet a friend at Xihongmen station. He was stopped by local stability maintenance officials and ordered to go back to Shenyang, after that he could no longer be contacted on phone.

Around 16 September 2019, a human rights activist was transferred from a detention centre in Peng'an County (Nanchong City, Sichuan Province) and detained at a psychiatric hospital for two months. During the detention, he was forcibly administered drugs every day, which he claimed would make him drowsy and nauseous. The activist had first been taken away by three police officers from Beijing on 12 August 2019, before he was repatriated to Nanchong City where he was first administratively detained for 15 days, before being transferred to criminal detention for a further 20 days. He suspected that he was detained for an extended period as the authorities were concerned that he would 'cause trouble' during the National Day Parade and the 2019 Military World Games held in October.

On 14 September 2019, a prominent 'barefoot lawyer' (a self-taught legal activist) who worked to defend human rights went missing in Changyuan, Henan and has not been heard from for at least a week. It is suspected that he has been kidnapped. He had reportedly been monitored by Guangzhou police all the way from Guangzhou to Henan after he was released from prison lately.

On 14 September 2019, a human rights activist from Shenyang, Liaoning went missing shortly after he forwarded a message supporting a female petitioner who were forcibly taken away from her home in Beijing. He was reportedly taken away by stability maintenance officials in the district where he resided in Shenyang.

On 3 September 2019, a human rights activist in Huishan District (Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province) was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) by the local court on charge of the 'crime of picking quarrels and provoking troubles'. The charge was based on some twitter posts in relation to Xinjiang and the Tian'anmen event of 1989 among the others. The person was also a petitioner and was called into the police station on 2 September to 'discuss' the petition case. The RSDL decision on 3 September was not related with the petition.

On 29 August 2019, a human rights lawyer was taken away by the police at Guangzhou South railway station in Panyu, Guangzhou, Guangdong province. The police said they were trying to prevent him from going abroad. He went missing for 10 days. On 8 September 2019, he returned home in Jingzhou.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 21 July 2019, around 430,000 anti-government demonstrators (police estimated the turnout to be 138,000) participated in a march organised by the Civil Human Rights Front from Wan Chai to Sai Wan to demand that their 'five demands' be met. Some demonstrators occupied roads outside the legislature and government headquarters in Admiralty as police retreated. They chanted slogans and created makeshift barricades, while some also spray painted over CCTV cameras and threw eggs at the Legislative Council building. Police dispersed the crowd with tear gas after dark. A man driving through the scene attempted to argue with the black-clad demonstrators blocking the roads, but was then beaten up.

Around 10 July 2019 (month of), a rights defender-cum-lawyer died at an intensive care unit ward in Xiangcheng Hospital in his hometown (Zhangzhou, Fujian) (coded to Gulou). He was first transferred to the hospital on 26 April 2019, after completing his jail sentence in a prison hospital (Jianxin Hospital) in Fuzhou. During his time in the ICU, he was constantly guarded by the police and was not allowed to communicate with others. His family's requests for transferal for better treatment were denied, and visits were prohibited or occasionally granted and limited to 15 minutes a week. He was effectively detained until his death on 10 July 2019.

On 1 July 2019, dozens of Shanghai activists gathered in Room 304, No. 15, Lane 99, Guilin East Street, Xuhui District, Shanghai to commemorate the 12th anniversary of the death of the human rights activist Chen Xiaoming, who died from torture by the Chinese government in 2007. They asked that the government revisited the case again.

On 15 June 2019, a human rights activist was beaten up by government personnel stationing outside his apartment in Huiyang district (Huizhou, Guangdong) after he questioned them why they were preventing him from leaving his home. He was injured in the neck, face, head, chest, legs and arms. His camera was damaged. He was initially refused to be treated at a hospital but he received treatment after filing a complaint to the hospital's vice president. He was then taken to a police station.

On 10 June 2019, a human rights defender was beaten while held in custody at a detention centre in Huai'an City (Jiangsu Province) . The person had been detained by police since 15 May 2019 and had yet to be released at the time of reporting on 19 October 2019.

On 3 June 2019, a human rights activist and his fiancee were taken away by police from their home in Qiaodong (Xingtai, Hebei) and put in 'black jail' for a few days before sending to a detention centre and detained for 15 days. The reason for the detention was that the activist had posted a photo of him wearing a T-shirt written 'June Fourth' on Twitter earlier on the same day.
On 24 May 2019, a human rights defender was taken on 'mandatory vacation' by the authorities in Sihui (Zhaoqing City, Guangdong Province) right after he was released from the Sihui city prison.

On 13 May 2019, a human rights defender who was going to attend an open court hearing concerning another human rights defender was beaten by the police in front of the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court in Gusu District (Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province). He was hit in his left eye and was consequently detained in a police station.

On 4 May 2019, around 300 protesters and pro-democratic groups, including CHRF, engaged in a demonstration in the demonstration area of the Legislative Council in the Central and Western District of Hong Kong, protesting against the changes to the extradition law. Meanwhile, around 40 people from two pro-Beijing groups protested in support of the changes to the extradition law outside the Legislative Council. They also had a verbal confrontation with anti-ELAB protesters, including a pro-democracy legislative councillor. No injuries were reported.

On 29 April 2019, a rights activist was taken away by authorities from the Lingyan Shan hillside cemetery in Wuzhong District (Suzhou, Jiangsu) after he tried to visit the grave of an executed political dissident. He was incommunicado thereafter and is believed to be detained in the Xukou Police Station.

On 26 April 2019, an activist was called in to the station by Zhuzhou City (Hunan) police before being brought to have drinks at a restaurant nearby. Around midnight, two police officers took him to a nearby hotel, where he was held incommunicado until the following evening. It was part of a campaign by the CCP to silence dissent before nad during the Golden Week.

On 25 April 2019, a Shanghai human rights activist, along with his wife and his friend, were dragged into a car by police and government officials near the Beijing South Railway Station (Fengtai District, Beijing) and were subsequently detained in the Shanghai Municipal People's Government Beijing Office. The activist's wife and the friend were released in Beijing the next day morning, whereas the activist was sent back to his home in Shanghai in the evening.

On 25 April 2019, a Shanghaiese rights defender-cum-forced evictee and his wife were taken from Beijing South Station in Fengtai district (Beijing) by police forces and government officials from Hongkou district of Shanghai. Albeit recovering from a stroke and physical disabilities, the rights defender was detained at the Shanghai Liaison Office, while his wife was escorted back to their hometown. The couple was in Beijing for a medical visit.

On 24 April 2019, a Shanghai human rights defender was taken away by the government officials of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government Beijing Office in a railway station in Shanghai, and consequently held incommunicado. It was part of a campaign by the CCP to silence dissent before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation which held in Beijing on April 25-27.

On 22 April 2019, a human rights defender-cum-retired teacher from Shanghai was taken away near Panjiayuan Tower in Chaoyang district (Beijing) by undercover police officers from the Shanghai Liaison Office and Beijing police officers. He was sent to a Relief Service Centre 'black jail' near Beijing South Station in Fengtai and Dongcheng districts. He arrived in Beijing with several Shanghaiese petitioners, but was caught on his way to purchase cigarettes near his hotel accommodation. He was detained as of 24 April.

On 12 April 2019, 12 rights activists gathered at Zhengzhou Railway Transport Intermediate Court in Erqi district (Zhengzhou, Henan) to submit a complaint about the Henan Housing and Urban-Rural Construction Department for not carrying out its legal responsibility. They requested an admistrative reconsideration by the Henan Provincial People's Government, after discovering in March that the no one was present at the Housing Department to receive or acknowledge letters and correspondences from the people.

On 26 March 2019, two human rights defenders from Tianning district, Changzhou, Jiangsu were abducted by liaison officers once their train reached the platform in Beijing. They were detained Yongdingmen Hotel for the night, then at another hotel until 15 Mar after they were driven back to Changzhou by hired thugs, subdistrict officers and policemen from Qinglong station.

On 14 March 2019, a human rights defender from Guangzhou was visiting a friend - 'founder' of un-recognised political party Zhongguo Minfudang, who was under illegal house arrest - in Jiangpu subdistrict of Pukou district (Nanjing, Jiangsu) when he was caught from behind by a few undercover police officers. They twisted his arm, and he expressed pain. The rights defender was driven to Zhujiang police station, and shut in a small, black room for eight hours without food or water. When he fainted from hunger, they called the ambulence for him, then took him to the train station and forced him to leave Nanjing.

On 14 March 2019, a human rights defender from Yangjian Township, Wuxi was detained by police at the Majialou 'black jail' in Fengtai District (Beijing) after submitting a letter to CPC Central Committee leaders. He was then forcibly sent back to Wuxi.

On 14 March 2019, two Shanghaiese human rights defenders were stopped on the streets in Beijing when the police pulled up records showing that they had 'picked quarrels and provoked trouble' in the past. They disappeared when multiple policemen kidnapped them to 'an illegal concentration camp' at Dongrongxian Hutong.

On 14 March 2019, 2 human rights defenders from Shanghai were walking about in Beijing when police officers sent them to an 'illegal concentration camp' located in Dongrongxian Hutong in Xicheng District (Beijing). They are suspected to have been forcibly disappeared for at least two days.
On 14 March 2019, a human rights defender petitioned at the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development in Haidian District (Beijing) and is suspected to have been kidnapped then.

On 13 March 2019, a human rights defender from Putuo District, Shanghai was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' backed by the Putuo District government while he was petitioning at the Ministry of Public Security in Dongcheng District (Beijing). He was taken into a car by more than 10 people and sent in the direction of Nantong, Jiangsu.

On 13 March 2019, a human rights defender was picked up by more than 20 people including police officers, personnel from the Putuo District Bureau for Letters and Calls, and private security personnel while he was at the Shanghai Hongqiao railway station in Minhang. He was then detained at a 'black jail' in Qingpu District (Shanghai).

On 13 March 2019, a human rights activist was assaulted by a group of several police and government employees while he was visiting and having lunch with a political dissident who was detained at his home in Xiangtang village (Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province). The security personnel had been stationed at the residence of the dissident for surveillance. It was reported that the human right activist suffered bruises to his face and severe pain in his waist and legs, while the dissident sustained some minor injuries.

On 13 March 2019, a human rights defender from Shanghai was kidnapped from the Shanghai Railway Station in Jing'an District (Shanghai) by 7-8 'stability manintenance agents' backed by the Shanghai government while he was en route to Beijing. He was incommunicado thereafter.

On 12 March 2019, a human rights defender from Daqing, Heiliongjiang was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents from the Dawing government while he was petitioning at the Ministry of Agriculture in Chaoyang (Beijing). He was then forced to board a train headed to Daqing.

On 11 March 2019, a human rights defender, who was also a petitioner-cum-forced evictee, from Changzhou, Jiangsu was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' from the Changzhou City Qinglong Subdistrict Office while he was at McDonald's in Guang'anmen, Xicheng District (Beijing). He was incommunicado thereafter for at least 11 days and was suspected to have been held in a 'black jail' in Tianning District, Changzhou. Police officers reportedly said that he would not be released until 'matters were settled' regarding the cremation of his wife, whose body remained unburied after she drank pesticide in protest of forced demolitions and died in Oct 2015.

On 11 March 2019, a human rights defender was forcibly sent back to Shanghai by 'stability maintenance agents' from the Shanghai Government Office in Beijing after he petitioned at the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng. He was then detained at a 'black jail' housed in a rural tourism centre at Changxing Island in Chongming District (Shanghai).

On 10 March 2019, a human rights defender from Jiamusi, Heilongjiang was kidnapped while petitioning in Beijing Municipality and was incommunicado thereafter. Officials said that he had been sent home.
On 9 March 2019, a human rights defender from Shanghai Municipality was intercepted by police officers and was incommunicado thereafter for at least 9 days.

On 9 March 2019, a rights defender from Shanghai was intercepted by liaison officers in Beijing and locked in a 'black jail' after returning to Shanghai. It was his fourth time being locked in a 'black jail,' and the incident is allegedly related to the approaching annual Lianghui conventions.

On 9 March 2019, a human rights defender from Huahuang Village, Liangzihu, Hubei was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' backed by the Huahuang Village government at the Shijiazhuang Railway Station in Qiaoxi District (Shijiazhuang, Hebei) while en route to Beijing. He was forced to get on the train to Hankou, Wuhan.

On 8 March 2019, a human rights defender in Beijing being monitored by Shanghai government officials was handed over to 'stability maintenance agents' from the Pudong New Area government and sent to Shanghai. He was incommunicado thereafter and is suspected to have been kidnapped.
On 8 March 2019, a human rights defender from Pudong New Area, Shanghai was intercepted by liaison officers in Beijing. He was incommunicado ever since he boarded a train back to Shanghai on 10 Mar.

On 8 March 2019, 4 human rights defenders were picked up from their rented home in Beijing Municipality by police officers from the Fangshan District Public Security Bureau. They were incommunicado for at least 48 hours thereafter.

On 7 March 2019, a human rights defender was forced to return to Shanghai by train after being apprehended by personnel from the Shanghai government while carrying out his activism in Beijing. He was disappeared thereafter for at least 5 days.

On 7 March 2019, a rights defender from Shanghai was forced to board train 1461 from Beijing back to Shanghai and disappeared for at least two days thereafter. He had first been intercepted on 5 March 2019 by liaison officers in Beijing. The incident is allegedly related to the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 6 March 2019, a human rights defender from Zoucheng, Shandong was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' backed by the Zoucheng government while he was in Beijing Municipality. He was sent in the direction of Shandong.

On 6 March 2019, a human rights defender from Dasheng Village, Douhudi, Hubei was kidnapped by 7-8 'stability maintenance agents' from the Douhudi government while he was at the Beijing Xinfadi Market in Fengtai (Beijing). He was pushed into a car and sent in the direction of Hubei.
Since 5 March 2019, a human rights defender from Xishan District (Wuxi, Jiangsu) has been incommunicado for at least 12 days and is suspected to have been kidnapped.

On 5 March 2019, two human rights defenders who had had their homes demolished by the government shouted slogans at the Zhongnanhai in Xicheng (Beijing) in protest of the govenrment's actions. They were abducted and incommunicado thereafter.
On 5 March 2019, two human rights defenders in Beijing were forced to return to Shanghai and were disappeared thereafter for at least 5 days.
On 5 March 2019, a human rights defender was disappeared after being forced to return to Shanghai while en route to petition in Bejing.

On 5 March 2019, a criminal justice rights defender from Hubei was locked up at Majialou 'black jail' in Fengtai district (Beijing). The incident is allegedly related to the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 4 March 2019, a human rights defender was picked up by 'interceptor thugs' from the Xiangtan and Xiangxiang city governments at the Wuchang Railway Station in Wuchang District (Wuhan, Hubei). He was first held at a hotel room near the railway station before being transferred to another hotel room in Xiangtan City.
Since 4 March 2019, two human rights defenders from Baoshan District (Shanghai) have been incommunicado for at least 13 days and are suspected to have been kidnapped.

On 3 March 2019, a human rights defender from Shanghai went to the Great Hall of the People in Xicheng (Beijing), the venue of the liang hui, to submit a letter of complaint and was apprehended by officers from Beijing's Xicheng Public Security Bureau. He was incommunicado thereafter for at least one week.
On 2 March 2019, a prominent human rights defender in Shanghai was not able to be contacted or located for at least one week and is suspected to have been kidnapped.

On 2 March 2019, a human rights defender was taken from his home in Beijing by police officers from Yiyang County, Luoyang, Henan and was brought first to the Majialou 'black jail' in Fengtai before being detained in the Taoran Gardan Hotel in Xicheng. Police officers threatened to send him back to his registered address in Henan and he was incommunicado thereafter for at least 10 hours.

On 1 March 2019, a human rights defender from Liaoning was taken away from his rented home in Fangshan District, Beijing by police officers from Fushun, Liaoning. He was then held incommunicado at a 'black jail' housed on the third floor of the Fushun Xinfu No.3 Hospital in Xinfu District (Fushun, Liaoning) for at least 22 days.

On 1 March 2019, a human rights defender from Dazhi, Hubei was intercepted by stability maintenance officers at Wuhan train station prior to his train ride to Beijing. They detained him at a hotel, and confiscated his phone, ID card and personal possessions. He was transferred to a detention centre for another fifteen days on 4 Mar.

On 28 February 2019, a detained human rights lawyer who was scheduled to be released on 28 Feb was said to have been 'taken away' by the Domestic Security Protection Bureau when his supporters went to receive him at the Henan's Xinxiang No. 2 Prison in Xinxiang City (Henan). He was held incommunicado at a hotel near Zhengzhou City until 2 March 2019 and returned to his parents' home in Xinyang (Henan) after he started a hunger strike. His father and sister, who were among the four people to receive him at the prison, were also held incommunicado since then.

On 26 February 2019, a human rights defender from Zhenjiang, Jiangsu was dragged, beaten and cuffed up by public security officers from his hometown during a lunch engagement with his wife and friends in Beijing. The couple was taken back to Zhenjiang prefecture. The rights defender was arrested and detained at the Zhenjiang police station, and his wife had some personal freedoms taken away from her. The incident is allegedly related to the approaching annual Lianghui conventions.

On 26 February 2019, two Shanghaiese human rights activists were intercepted by liaison officers while they were petitioning at Beijing public security office. After they boarded train G169 back to Shanghai, they continued to be incommunicado as of 3 Mar. The incident is allegedly related to the approaching annual Lianghui conventions.

On 25 February 2019, after a protest outside the National Health Commission in Beijing, the convener of the protest (who is also a rights defender-cum-parent affected by the Henan vaccine scandal) was taken away by stability maintenance personnel and disappeared thereafter.

On 20 February 2019, a human rights activist was beaten by five people (including a police officer, district security officers, and security personnel) for not complying with their demands, causing serious pain in his right chest, when they were taking him from a train station in Shanghai to a 'black jail' on Hengsha Island. The man was stopped by the police and sent back on the train to Shanghai while he was petitioning in Beijing on 18 February 2018. He was released after being held for 23 days, where he went to the hospital for a body check-up and found fractures in his ribs.

On 12 February 2019, an unreported number of human rights defenders were intercepted and summoned to a police station in Zaoyang City (Xiangyang City, Hubei Province) when they attended a dinner banquet organised by another human rights defender. 1 human rights defender was reportedly brutally beaten by the police at the police station during the detention the same day.
On 12 December 2018, a human rights defender and disabled Vietnam war veteran from Baoji City (Shaanxi) disappeared after calling his family and has been incommunicado for at least 3.5 months.

On 8 November 2018, the wife of a human rights lawyer who has been held incommunicado since 2015 together with some rights activists staged a protest at the Tianjin No.2 intermediate People's Court in Hexi district (Tianjin). They wore T-shirts printed with her husband's photo and the slogan to demand her husband to be released.

On 2 November 2018, five human rights defenders disappeared in Shanghai (Shanghai) during the massive arrest of petitioners and human rights defenders when China International Import Expo was held in Shanghai.

On 22 October 2018, Liu Xiao Li, the disqualified candidate in the Hong Kong Legislative Council Kowloon by-election, went to protest together with the Hong Kong Labour Party member Li Zhuo Ren and other protesters in the by-election candidate introduction meeting by-election in Kowloon Bay International trade and Exhibition Center in Kowloon city (Hong Kong). The security guards forced them to leave and Li Zhuo Ren was carried away by the security guards. Before the meeting, the Hong Kong Labour party, LSD, CHRF, and other organizations also protested against Carrie Lam, Lantau artificial island housing project, and the disqualification of Liu Xiao Li.

On 12 October 2018, a group of human rights defenders held placards and protested in the People's Park in Huangpu district (Shanghai) over their wrongful detention during the 2019 World A.I. Conference in Shanghai after they were released from the detention.

On 6 October 2018, several dozen activists, including members of CHRF and LSD, gathered in front of the Immigration Tower in Wan Chai, Hong Kong, to protest the government's decision of banning the renewal of visa of a Financial Times reporter.

On 1 October 2018, over 1,000 people attended demonstration organized by the Civil Human Rights Front outside Hong Kong government headquarters (Hong Kong) on National Day of China. They protested over the curbs on its traditional freedoms in Hong Kong, and the pro-independence protesters were denied entry by the police.
On 1 October 2018, local authorities took away a civil rights activist in Shunyi, Beijing and put him in illegal custody in a hotel where he was placed under 24-hour surveillance.

On 28 September 2018, 4 human rights activists representing 57 petitioners petitioned at the Legal Office of the State Council in Xicheng District, Beijing to demand for official responses to the case they requested. They held banners outside the office to demand for justice after receiving no meaningful responses.

On 26 September 2018, more than 10 human rights activists petitioned at National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration located in Xicheng, Beijing to protest Shanghai Municipal Government's inability to solve the forced demolition of their properties.

On 22 September 2018, some CHRF members, along with members of the Labour Party and the LSD, rushed into the West Kowloon Highspeed Railway Station located at Kowloon, Hong Kong to protest the Highspeed Railway program and Juxtaposed Control mechanism in the Railway Station.

On 19 September 2018, more than 10 members of the CHRF went to the headquarters building of DAB located at Eastern, Hong Kong to protest the party's refusal of investigation into Shatin to Central Link. The protesters were blocked by the security guards at the entrance of the building, and more than 20 plainclothes and armed police officers arrived at the scence to be on stand by.

Around 12 September 2018 (as reported), recently in September 2018 (as reported), some members of the Cao Shunli human rights group protested in Shanghai for the 15th time to call for the authorities to release all political prisoners and lift bans on political party formation and newspapers.

On 3 September 2018, a civil rights activist was forcibly taken away in Beijing and back to Shanghai by the authorities. As of the reporting on 17 September 2018, the activist's whereabouts remained unknown .

Around 30 August 2018 (as reported), 10 rights activists - nine of which are female - protested on the streets of Shanghai to raise awareness about a fellow female rights activist who had been in forced disappearance incommunicado since the 19th National Congress in September 2017.

On 17 August 2018, a female housing rights activist in Wuxi, Jiangsu was sent to a monitored temporary residence by the police, a day after 200-300 government personnel demolished the house belonging to her and a fellow housing rights activist, and had them subsequently arrested and detained at Chaqiao police station. The other housing rights activist was also sent away, and his location remained unknown.

On 3 August 2018, authorities demolished the studio of artist and political activist Ai Wei Wei in Caochangdi Art Park in Chaoyang district, Beijing. Part of a wider demolition and gentrification campaign in Beijing, Ai was originally notified to have two weeks until he was scheduled to move out, but mechanical diggers began the demolition work much earlier without prior notice.

On 25 July 2018, a rights activist cum parent was taken away by the police at Zhanjiang West Railway Station in Mazhang District (Zhanjiang, Guangdong) as he was about to petition in Beijing regarding the Changchun Changsheng vaccine scandal. He was forcibly detained at Royal International Hotel in Suixi county.

On 25 July 2018, almost 100 human rights activists protested in front of the courthouse in Pudong district, Shanghai during the trial of a human rights activist. Two protesters were arrested by the police, and three activists were kicked out of the courthouse during the hearing.

On 24 July 2018, at least 10 human rights activists marched on the streets with banners to support a fellow Shanghaiese human rights activist was set to attend his first court hearing in Pudong district, Shanghai.

Around 24 July 2018 (as reported), one of the organisers who initiated a rights-defending group for Changsheng vaccine victims in Chongqing was incommunicado, possibly in relation to another organiser who was detained by the police for 4 hours on 23 July for her plan to petition at the local public health bureau that same day.

On 21 July 2018, protesters, democratic parties, student unions and pro-independence groups, led by the Civil Human Rights Front, marched to the Wanchai police headquarters to protest against the government for proposing a ban on The Hong Kong National Party. While some supported the pro-independence fight against the Communist Party of China, others including the CHRF, rallied more broadly against diminished freedom of speech and association. Political parties who participated include Civic Party, Labour Party, People Power, Demosisto and the League of Social Democrats. Organisers estimate that 1200 people participated in the protest, while police put the number at 600.

Around 19 July 2018 (as reported), Mongolian Chinese herders and rights activists clashed with private security forces in Jalaid Banner, Inner Mongolia. The security forces were hired by a Chinese-owned company (name unknown) accused of polluting local grasslands through mining activities. Mining activities had been banned, but remained active due to public-private collusion between the company and corrupt officials at lower levels of government.

On 18 July 2018, a rights activist and organiser was taken away from a police station in Nanchang prefecture (Jiangxi) (coded to Honggutan) and forcibly admitted by ten police officers to the Jiangxi Province Mental Hospital. He was targeted after taking part in a collective petition in Beijing from 25-30 Jun with nearly 100 psychological torture victims.

On 16 July 2018, around 20 human rights activist gathered at the Hubei Letters and Visits (Petitioning) Bureau in Wuchang district of Wuhan to protest against the kidnapping and abuse of disappeared human rights activists. 8 people were escorted away by authorities.

On 9 July 2018, a dozen of lawyers and activists in the legal profession - from the China Human Rights Lawyers Concern Group, Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, League of Social Democrats and Progressive Lawyers Group - assembled in front of the Court of Final Appeal in Central, Hong Kong for a silent protest. They protested against the persecution of Chinese human rights lawyers, and marked the 3rd anniversary of the 709 crackdown, in which over 300 lawyers were arrested, and some subsequently suspended even upon release. They specifically highlighted the case of Wang Quanzhang, the only lawyer in the crackdown whose location was still unknown in the crackdown.

On 8 July 2018, the eve of the 3rd anniversary of the 709 crackdown, around 30 protesters from the China Human Rights Lawyers Concern Group, Civic Party, Democratic Party and the League of Social Democrats marched to the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in Sai Ying Pun.
Around 5 July 2018 (between 2 - 9 July), local police beat up and tortured a civil rights activist during his detention in the police station in Hepu (Beihai, Guangxi).

On 1 July 2018, teachers, university and primary school students, convened by the Civil Human Rights Front, marched from Victoria Park to Civic Square (at the Central Government Complex) in protest against the controversial rise of Mandarin in primary and secondary schools, replacing Cantonese as the primary language of Chinese instruction. A final gathering was held, officiating the event's conclusion at 6:42pm.

Around 30 June 2018 (as reported), some female human rights activists of the Cao Shunli human rights group held banners and protested in Shanghai Municipality for the 12th time to call for the authorities to release all political prisoners and lift bans on political party formation and newspapers. They also protested oppression and torture against human rights defenders.

On 27 June 2018, more than 10 human rights defenders carrying placards protested on the streets in Shanghai Municipality to show support for a human rights defender who finished a 9-month imprisonment on the day. The human rights defender was charged obstruction of official duties by the court in Shanghai.

On 24 June 2018, around 30 people from the newly formed United Front for Open Libraries gathered outside the Central Library in Causeway Bay in Wan Chai District of Hong Kong to protest the removal of 10 LGBTQ-themed children's books from library shelves. Members of BigLove Alliance, Amnesty International Hong Kong, LGBTQ rights group Nutong Xueshe, the Student Christian Movement of Hong Kong, the Concern Group for Children's Books and a PP lawmaker also attended the protest.

On 22 June 2018, more than 30 human rights defenders assembled in front of the Fuzhou Cangshan People's Court in Cangshan District (Fuzhou City, Fujian Province) in supporting a female petitioner who sued the local government for unlawful arrest.

On 20 June 2018, some human rights activists of the Cao Shunli human rights group held banners and protested in Shanghai for the 11th time to call for the authorities to release all political prisoners and lift bans on political party formation and newspapers. It was a female-majority group.

On 19 June 2018, more than 100 villagers and human rights defenders demonstrated outside a fenced site recently sold to a private developer by the government in Fengsha Village (Foshan City, Guangdong Province). The protesters protested forced land acquisition and collusion between government and the private property developers.

On 13 June 2018, 4 human rights defenders protested in Shanghai Municipality to show support for a petitioner-cum-activist who was charged obstruction of official duties by the court in Shanghai. They displayed placards on the street.

On 3 June 2018, a human rights defender was abused while in custody at the Xicheng detention centre in Beijing.
