Despite his medical history of high blood pressure and cardiovascular and neurological diseases, his arms and legs were chained with torture instruments that prevented him from standing upright. He suffered injuries and became ill after they confiscated all his medications, and denied him a blanket after adjusting the air-conditioner to freezing temperatures.

Around 16 May 2018 (month of), several officers from the security bureau took a human rights defender away from his home in Guangzhou. He has not been heard from for more than half a year since then and is suspected to have been disappeared.

On 15 May 2018, a citizen was arrested at home at Lixia District (Jinan, Shandong Province) by local police and has been detained since then without a trial for over 11 months. He was working as a rights defender.

On 11 May 2018, a Shanghai rights defender was beaten by private security forces at the Shanghai People's Government Office for Calls and Letters in Huangpu after he tried petitioning for rights protection. The defender was punched and kicked uninterruptedly while police officers present at the scene were indifferent to the beatings.

On 11 May 2018, a human rights activist and singer who had been detained in police custody for more than 7 months in at Nansha, Guangdong was sent to the hospital for emergency reasons. He is suspected to have been subjected to abuse and violence by the police during his detention.

On 4 May 2018, a rights defender with lung cancer was denied warm clothes to wear and was kept freezing until 3 am by police after he was called in for questioning at Dingshan Police Station in Yixing, Wuxi, Jiangsu. The maltreatment could be related to the defender's earlier refusal to be interrogated by inspectors without the necessary qualifications for the discussed subject. The event led to the worsening of the man's condition, and he had to be hospitalized the same day.

On 12 April 2018, around 50 people from the Hong Kong Campaign for the Advancement of Human Rights and Peace in the Philippines (HKCAHRPP) gathered near the hotel where Filipino president Rodrigo Duterte was staying at in Tsim Sha Tsui, Yau Tsim Mong District (Hong Kong) during a three-day visit. Protesters chanted anti-Duterte slogans and protested against Duterte's war on drugs, which they said was a sham used to target activists and opponents. On the same day, there were also migrant activists reported to be protesting near the hotel.

On 10 April 2018, about 20 members of LSD, CHRF and the Civic Party marched from the Western Police Station to the Liaison Office in Central and Western District (Hong Kong) to protest against the disappearance of human rights lawyer Wang Quanzhang. The protest came after police in Beijing stopped Wang's wife from finishing her planned 100-kilometre march from Beijing to Tianjin to highlight his disappearance. Protesters held banners and chanted slogans calling for Wang's immediate release.

On 27 March 2018, a rights defender was slapped by a national security officer on their way to the police station in Changyuan County (Xinxiang, Henan), physically abused, and ordered to kneel by the national security officers when he was in Changyuan County Police Department. The rights defender was summoned by the Changyuan County Police Department to interrogation over the participation in two rights-defender groups.

On 18 March 2018, a Shanghai rights defender went incommunicado after he was taken by a group of unidentified people at the Wuxi Railway Station in Liangxi District (Wuxi, Jiangsu). During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 16 March 2018, a rights defender went incommunicado after the Beijing police inspected his ID when he was changing underground at Beijing Hepingmen Underground Station, and sent him to the Fuyoujie Police Station in Xicheng District (Beijing). During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 14 March 2018, a rights defender and her brother were physically abused in Dengzhou (Nanyang, Henan) by the police when they were kept in the hotel after the police took them from their friends' home which they were visiting. Later they were sent to the Nanyang Guangwu Police Station and went incommunicado.

On 6 March 2018, during the Lianghui conventions, a rights defender from Liaoning was stopped and attacked by the police when he was on his way to visit his parents. Several rights defenders have been attacked by the law enforcement personnel during the Lianghui conventions.

On 6 March 2018, two rights defenders were taken by local village officials and police officers in Shanghai and were handed over to a group of unidentified people by them, after that two rights defenders went incommunicado. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 4 March 2018, a rights defender from Panjin, Liaoning was taken away from Beijing Huangcun Underground Station in Daxing District (Beijing) by stability maintenance agents from Panjin. He remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 6 March 2018.

On 2 March 2018, a rights defender went incommunicado after he was taken from Beijing back to Shanghai by interceptors from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 1 March 2018, a rights defender from Wuhan was taken by more than ten unidentified people and went incommunicado when he was waiting for the bus at a bus station of 485 bus line in Beijing. He was in Beijing to petition together with a group of petitioners from Wuhan during the Lianghui conventions.

On 1 March 2018, a rights defender went to attend a trial in Chongqing and had since remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 8 March 2018. It was suspected that he might have been suppressed due to the heightened security measures around the Lianghui conventions period. It was reported that the local government sent more people to guard his house, for which he and the local government had not reached an eviction agreement.

On 1 March 2018, a rights defender was taken from his home in Shanghai by the police officers from Pudong Police Department Sanlin Police Station and went incommunicado. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 27 February 2018, a human rights activist was sent back to Shanghai from Beijing by government interceptors and was handed over to 4-5 unknown individuals at an underground parking lot at the Shanghai railway station in Jing'an district. He was held in a villa in Changxing Island, Chongming District until being dropped on a road on 21 March 2018. He was forcibly searched, served tea that was drugged and made him unconscious for the first three days of going incommunicado, and had his mobile phone and belonging taken away.

Around 26 February 2018, a human rights activist was detained in a black prison in a hotel in Nangang District (Harbin, Heilongjiang) after having met with the head of the Harbin Xiangyang Public Security Branch on the night of 26th and agreeing to return to Harbin to be interviewed by the head of the Criminal Investigation Department of the Provincial Public Security Department. The activist has been petitioning for 10 years after the death of his son while at school and is a member of an anti-corruption and human rights alliance.

On 15 February 2018, about 70 petitioners and human rights defenders gathered at the Yangjiaping Pedestrian Street in Jiulongpo District (Chongqing) to protest against the authorities forcibly admitting people to and detaining them in mental hospitals in retaliation to their activism. Protesters had started a petition against this issue on 11 February 2018.

On 15 February 2018, an unknown number of human rights activists from the Cao Shunli Human Rights Association for the seventh time took to the streets in Shanghai Municipality to demand the CCP lift the ban on political parties, remove restrictions on the press and release political prisoners.

On 14 February 2018, a human rights activist was summoned to the police station in Zixi County (Fuzhou, Jiangxi) after having signed a petition in support of Sui Muqing, a human rights lawyer. After he refused to sign a statement saying he was forced to sign the petition by Sui Muqing, the activist was beaten.

On 11 February 2018, 1000 people participated in a march organised by CHRF in protest against the Secretary for Justice, Cheng Yeuk-wah, who has been accused of spreading false information regarding illegal construction projects and also carrying out political tasks for Beijing. Protesters marched from Southorn Stadium in Wan Chai to Justice Place in Central (Hong Kong), held banners, and demanded that Cheng Yeuk-wah step down immediately. CHRF estimated that 1000 people took part, but police put the number at 700.

On 11 February 2018, at least 5 human rights activists from the Cao Shunli Human Rights Association for the sixth time took to the streets in Shanghai to demand the CCP lift the ban on political parties, remove restrictions on the press and release political prisoners.

On 11 February 2018, around 40 people from the Defend Hong Kong Campaign gathered at Hennessy Road in Wan chai District (Hong Kong) to call for the Justice Secretary, Zheng Ruohua, to immediately enact Article 23 of the Basic Law to safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. The protesters met with another group of protesters from CHRF, who were marching to Justice Palace in Central district to call for Zheng Ruohua's resignation in response to her alleged involvement in illegal construction projects. Although violence was avoided, both sides yelled and jeered at each other.

On 10 February 2018, a human rights activist went missing after being taken away by police in Fangshang District (Beijing). The activist had reportedly been planning an event for the Spring Festival and had received phone calls from Beijing officials demanding that he abandon his efforts.

On 8 February 2018, a Fujianese woman was beaten up by community authorities as she was on her way to make photocopies of her land approval outsourcing documents in Changfen village, Gufeng township, Pingnan county of Ningde, Fujian. When she reported the incident, she was arrested and beaten up by the deputy head of the Pingnan county police, and detained for 10 days.

Around 8 February 2018 (as reported), some people from the China Cao Shunli Human Rights Team protested on the streets of Shanghai Municipality to urge authorities to ratify the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and demand that officials disclose their property holdings.

On 31 January 2018, at least 6 human rights activists protested on the streets of Shanghai to demand that the government imediately ratify the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, as well as that public officials disclose their property holdings.
On 30 January 2018, at least 6 human rights activists protested in Shanghai to demand the release of all political prisoners.

On 24 January 2018, a human rights activist currently being held in Shangbancheng Prison in Shangbancheng Town (Chengde, Hebei) was attacked by guards who, despite the prisoner's poor health did not allow him to rest, even physically beating him and pouring pepper spray on him.

On 12 January 2018, about six national security officers forcibly abducted a human rights activist to the local police station in Mudu Town (Suzhou, Jiangsu) without providing any legal official documents. She was also beaten by those officers during detention.

Around 8 January 2018, some members of the China Cao Shunli Human Rights Group protested on the streets of Shanghai Municipality to urge authorities to lift the ban on political parties, remove restrictions on the press and release political prisoners. This was their fourth street protest.
On 7 January 2018, some human right activists marched on streets in Shanghai, to call for the government to release political prisoners across the country.
On 3 January 2018, 50 human right activists protested in front of the court, while 11 human right activists were brought to trial in Fuqing, Fujian. They held placards during the demonstration.

On 2 January 2018, several civil rights activists protested in front of the court and demanded for justice for the 11 human right lawyers brought to trial in Fuqing (Fuzhou, Fujian). They held placards during the demonstration.

On 10 June 2021, two rights defenders from Chongqing went missing in Beijing municipality, and remained incommunicado by the time of reporting on 13 Jun 2021. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 15 June 2021, an imprisoned rights defender was rounded up and assaulted by four prisoners at the Xi County Detention Centre (Xinyang, Henan) while writing up a complaint accusing against law enforcement officials. The assault was allegedly arranged by the authorities as well.

On 10 June 2021, a rights defender from Dandong, Liaoning was held at a coronavirus quarantine facility in Yuanbao district after he was kidnapped from his rental accommodation in Beijing municipality by six officials from the Dandong Government, and the Public Security and Petitioning Bureaus. They disabled his cell phone and deactivated his social media accounts. He was moved to a detention facility on 26 Jun 2021 despite testing negative. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 23 June 2021, an environmental activist was 'taken on mandatory vacation' by the State Security Department of his hometown in Jiangsu province (coded to Xuanwu), to an unspecified village near Tai Lake in the Changsanjiao area (the 'Yangtze Delta city cluster'). The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 6 July 2021, members of six environmental groups (Conservancy Association, Green Power, Greenpeace, The Green Earth, Greeners Action and Green Sense) demonstrated with a banner and an artwork made of plastic bottles outside the Central Government Complex in Central District (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They claimed that a proposed rebate of 10 cents per plastic bottle was not enough to get Hongkongers recycling, while offering HK$1 per bottle would be a lot more effective.

Around 10 July 2021 (as reported), police transferred a detained rights defender from the Qidao Police Station in Yuanbao district (Dandong, Liaoning) to a budget hotel nearby for two-day detention on 'security maintenance' grounds. The police first intercepted him at Siping, Jilin, on 6 July 2021, while he was on his way to visit his family members before forcibly transferring back to Dandong.

On 13 July 2021, a disqualified human rights lawyer was beaten up by police at Qingyang People's Court in Qingyang district (Chengdu, Sichuan) while filing a litigation case about losing his practicing license to provide legal services. Soon after he had used his phone to record himself, four police forced him to delete the video by pinning him down on the ground. He had his video deleted by the officers before leaving the court with injuries on two arms.

On 12 August 2021, 4 Civil Human Rights Front members, including members of the League of Social Democrats and the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, carrying banners protested at the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Western district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They called for the release of political prisoners held in mainland China, including New Citizens' Movement leader Xu Zhiyong and rights attorney Ding Jiaxi.

On 16 August 2021, ten environmental groups (including Greenpeace and The Green Earth) and an assistant professor protested with a banner and held a press conference in Hong Kong, calling on the government to impose a total ban on single-use plastic tableware in restaurants by 2025.
Around 27 April 2021 (as reported), more than 100 taxi drivers petitioned and demonstrated in Yanji county (Yanbian, Jilin) to defend their rights, namely taxi operation and ownership rights.

On 9 September 2021, members of the League of Social Democrats rallied outside the District Court in Wan Chai, Hong Kong (coded as Hong Kong - Wan Chai), ahead of a court session where the later saw 12 democrats pleaded guilty to take part in or incite others to participate in a banned Tiananmen Massacre vigil in 2020. They carried a banner that read, 'Peaceful assemblies are not a crime, commemorating 4 June is conscience, human rights are bigger than the regime, shame to political prosecution.'

Around 31 August 2021 (as reported), a few members of Hong Kong Fishers Consortium and a legislator protested at the Hong Kong government headquarters and the Consulate-General of Japan in Hong Kong in Admiralty, Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against Japan's plans to release radioactive water from the destroyed Fukushima nuclear plant into the sea, concerning the impact on the ocean ecosystem, human's health and the future of the fishing industry.

On 23 August 2021, representatives from 10 environmental groups, including Greenpeace, WWF Hong Kong, and The Conservancy Association, protested and submitted a petition to the Environmental Protection Department at the Central Government Complex in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) ahead of a meeting of the Legislative Council's Panel on Environmental Affairs. They called on a ban on the use and sale of plastic tableware before 2025 rather than bringing in phased restrictions more slowly. They demonstrated a banner and a three-meter artwork to express their demands.

On 22 April 2021, a volunteer group ('Dong Fong Zi Zhu Volunteer Group') protested at the Japan Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to oppose the discharge of radioactive wastewater - resulting from the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident - into the sea, and urged the Japanese government to rescind their decision. They cited environmental concerns such as ecosystem destruction.

On 17 April 2021, a citizen group ('Tong Sum Wu Gong') protested at the Japan Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to oppose the discharge of radioactive wastewater - resulting from the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident - into the sea, and urged the Japanese government to rescind their decision. They cited environmental concerns such as radioactive pollution, and food and ecosystem destruction.

On 14 April 2021, Civil Force members and legislators demonstrated at the Japan Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to oppose the discharge of radioactive wastewater - resulting from the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident - into the sea, and urged the Japanese government to rescind their decision. They were concerned about the negative global impact of radioactive marine pollution. They held up placards and banners to express their demands.

On 13 April 2021, the HKFTU Social Affairs Committee demonstrated at the Japan Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to oppose the discharge of radioactive wastewater - resulting from the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident - into the sea, and urged the Japanese government to rescind their decision. They were concerned about negative consequences to food safety, human health and the marine ecosystem. They held up placards and banners to express their demands.

On 2 April 2021, a Tibetan writer and environmental activist was taken away by the police in Seda county (Ganzi, Sichuan) for unknown reasons. His whereabouts were still unknown at the time of reporting on 15 April 2021.

On 9 March 2021, district councillors petitioned and demonstrated at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded to Hong Kong - Central and Western) to oppose the establishment of a concrete manufacturing plant in Area 137 of Tseung Kwan O, citing pollution concerns. They held up a banner to express their demands.

On 23 February 2021, a group of Tseung Kwan O residents and a district councilor petitioned and demonstrated at the Sai Kung District Council (Hong Kong) (coded to Hong Kong - Sai Kung) to oppose the establishment of a concrete manufacturing plant in Area 137. They believed that as a desalination plant was already under construction, a new plant construction would bring about pollution issues to a primarily residential area. They held up placards to express their demands.

Around 15 February 2021 (as reported), district councilors (Neo Democrats, CP, Hong Kong Labour Party) and an environmental program representative ('Missing Link- Polyfoam Recycling Scheme') held up placards at the Yeung Uk Rd Street Market in Tsuen Wan district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Tsuen Wan) to protest against the accumulation of debris during the holiday season which created problems for traffic and hygiene. They urged the Environmental Protection Department and Food and Environmental Hygiene Department to take more action.

Around 31 January 2021 (between 26 January - 5 February), a man was beaten up by some people during a visit to a factory within 500m of Tuhe village, Gucheng village of Fugou county (Zhoukou, Henan). The victim had been invited to the factory by the person-in-charge, and was beaten up by several people (assumed to be hired by the factory) when he arrived. He was hospitalised after sustaining damages to his cranium, eyes and face. Previously, the victim had called the Environmental Bureau on 20 Jan to file an anonymous complaint against the factory for river contamination.

On 14 December 2020, 4 environmental groups (including Conservancy Association and Greenpeace) demonstrated at the Ma On Shan Country Park, Shatin district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Sha Tin) against the rezoning of green belt areas around the Park for private and public housing developments.

On 27 November 2020, pro-democracy district councilors and NGOs (environmental groups like 350.org, Hong Kong Dolphin Conservation Society) petitioned and demonstrated at the Hong Kong Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western) against the exorbitant costs and environmental impact of proposed development project Lantau Tomorrow Vision. They held up banners and shouted slogans.

On 26 November 2020, nine environmental groups (including Designing Hong Kong, The Green Earth and Greenpeace) protested at the Hong Kong Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western) against land reclamation and habitat destruction of the proposed development project Lantau Tomorrow Vision. They called on the government to withdraw the plan. They held up a banner and submitted a petition.

Around 15 November 2020 (month of), a Tibetan environmental activist originally from Chaktse village, Biru county was taken from prison to a hospital in Lhasa, where sources say he was suffering from a brain haemorrhage and paralysis following injuries reportedly sustained in prison or beatings by Chinese authorities on the way to the hospital. Authorities did not notify his family about the hospitalization. The victim died on 6 Feb 2021. He was detained on 8 Nov 2013 with no information about his whereabouts, tried in secret, and sentenced to 21 years for his involvement and media engagement in protests against a mining project at Naghla Dzambha Mountain in Biru.

On 14 October 2020, many citizen groups demonstrated at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) about the lack of environmental and public hygiene policies during the coronavirus pandemic, such as reducing road traffic. They held up banners.

On 9 October 2020, a number of Tsuen Wan district councillors and representatives of the Land Justice League petitioned before the start of a District Council meeting in Tsuen Wan district (Hong Kong) against developing two green belts into private residential property, and called for a new round of government-led public consultation, and for the development project to be halted for the time being. They held up placards to express their demands.

On 13 August 2020, 100-300 Mongolian herders staged a protest at the Dorbod Banner People's Government (Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia) against the construction of large-scale, government-backed pig farms where Mongolian locals were prohibited from grazing. They were also protesting against the pressure of increased agricultural activity on water sources, and ecological pollution due to waste discharge. Two people were arrested. A second protest involving more than 100 herders took place in the afternoon.

On 17 July 2020, four members of environmental organisation Greenpeace demonstrated and delivered a 100,000-signature petition at the Legislative Council in Central district (Hong Kong) against the 'Lantau Tomorrow Vision' development project ahead of a Financial Committee meeting on the budget for the project's man-made islands. Another four-person group of LSD, Labour Party and HKCTU representatives marched from Admiralty to Civic Square in Central to protest against the project as well.

On 28 June 2020, members of Extinction Rebellion Hong Kong staged a 'die-in' protest at Happy Valley Cemetery in Wan Chai District (Hong Kong), to raise awareness of the dangers of air pollution and the global climate crisis. They placed 35 shoes on the ground of the cemetery to represent the number of people killed each week due to air pollution in the city. This was the first of two demonstrations staged by the group on the same day.

On 28 June 2020, at least 4 members of Extinction Rebellion Hong Kong demonstrated in Mong Kok, Yau Tsim Mong District (Hong Kong), to raise awareness of the dangers of air pollution and the global climate crisis. They held two large banners highlighting that 35 people are killed each week in Hong Kong due to air pollution. This was the second of two demonstrations staged by the group on the same day.

On 13 March 2020, Yuen Long district councillors petitioned at the Town Planning Board in Eastern District (Hong Kong), against the redevelopment plans of Nam Sang Wai. They stated that the redevelopment plan would affect the ecology of the wetland area and endanger rare migratory birds.

On 24 September 2019, a few villagers protested at the government complex in North Point, Eastern district of Hong Kong to oppose an asphalt plant's application to prolong its operation for five years in Sheung Shui. A councillor helping the villagers said that the asphalt plant has caused air pollution in the Northern district of Hong Kong. Villagers submitted a petition letter to the Town Planning Board.

On 22 June 2019, nearly 20000 villagers marched in Mingtang Village (Yunfu, Guangdong) to oppose the construction of a garbage incineration power plant in the city. They demanded the government to withdraw the project due to health concerns. They blocked highways. Many police arrived on the scene and arrested several a few demonstrators after some shoving and pushing on both sides. Demonstrators also threw water bottles and watermelons at police.

On 26 May 2019, around 250 students marched from Wan Chai to the Government Headquarters in Admiralty in the Central and Western District of Hong Kong, as part of the global youth-led movement #FridaysForFuture. They called for a declaration of an environmental and climate emergency, and an increase the use of renewable energy sources.

On 4 May 2019, 9 activists from the Extinction Rebellion Hong Kong carrying signs demonstrated in front of a 7-metre wide globe installation outside the Citywalk mall in Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong, as part of a global movement to curb carbon emissions.

On 26 April 2019, around 10 members of a local environmental concern group submitted a petition letter and demonstrated at the Legal Assistance Department in Admiralty, Central District (Hong Kong) for a judicial review of the 'Subsidy and Arrangement Scheme of the Government Demolition Act' ('510 Plan') and its consequences for the appropriation of the North East New Territories New Development Areas Planning. The Ma Shi Po villagers claimed that 300,000 squatter inhabitants were not properly consulted, and were not pleased that farmland owners were not compensated, while brownfield owners were.

On 12 April 2019, more than 200 local residents of a Mongolian herding community gathered outside government offices in Darhan-uul Sum of Heshigten Banner (Inner Mongolia) to protest over changes in management of grazing lands on nearby Dalainuur National Nature Reserve. Local authorities imposed a grazing ban on herding communities despite local herders saying they could use their indigenous knowledge to protect the land.

On 8 January 2019, more than 20 members of NTAS protested at the Environment Bureau in Central, Hong Kong to criticize the Bureau's inability to solve the problem of illegal dumping. They criticised the weak law enforcement of the Bureau, which hindered residents' access and affected the environmental health of the community.

On 8 November 2018, around 200 protesters staged a protest in front of Huanggang city government in Huangzhou district (Huanggang, Hubei) over governmental project of building an incineration plant. The protesters held banners and expressed their environmental concerns brought by the project.

On 6 November 2018, up to 100 protesters staged a protest in Bahe Town (Huanggang, Hubei) over governmental project of building an incineration plant. The residents held banners and marched around the town to express their environmental concerns brought by the project, and during the protest, they met the intervention from the local police and some protesters were taken to the police cars.

Around 10 October 2018 (as reported), eight representatives of environmental groups - including Greenpeace and WWF - demonstrated and petitioned outside Legislative Council of Hong Kong in Central District (Hong Kong) and demanded for the government to plan land use properly, prioritize the usage of brownfield land, as well as criticize the government for building up artificial islands and developing country parks. Protesters held banners and placards.

Around 9 October 2018 (as reported), Save Lantau Alliance petitioned at the Office of the Chief Executive in Central District (Hong Kong) over the Lantau artificial island housing project. The group held placards and handed a petition letter to the Chief Executive Carrie Lam and believed that the project violated the principle of sustainable development. 11 people also marched from the Cheung Kong Center to the Government House in the same district.
On 7 September 2018, members of Greenpeace protested outside the shareholders' meeting of a fast food restaurant chain in Hong Kong to call for the firm's focus on the plastic reduction plan.

On 21 August 2018, many environmental groups - The Green Earth, Green Sense, The Conservancy Association, Friends of the Earth HK and Greenpeace HK - led by Greeners Action protested at Tamar Park in Hong Kong in the format of a relay, criticizing the government for its 14-year delay in implementing a city-wide rubbish collection fee. Afterwards, 11 members walked to the government headquarters to present a banner with nearly 1000 citizen signatures to a representative of the Environment Bureau.

On 30 June 2018, more than 1000 residents affected by severe air and water pollution staged a demonstration at a waste treatment plant in Xiangyang town, Xiangfeng district (Harbin, Heilongjiang), against untreated wastewater discharge and groundwater contamination. The demonstration ended on 30 June when 40 residents were arrested by the local police, during which clashes were reported between demonstrators and the police. 20-30 people were still not released at the time of reporting on 7 July 2018, and some residents were also injured and hospitalized. They had been on site since 26 June, blocking the entrance and exit of the facility and assigning villagers to stay on guard 24 hours a day.

On 16 June 2018, dozens of animal activists, including members of Ocean Recovery Alliance, gathered at Maxim's Caterers' headquarters in Lai Chi Kok in the Sham Shui Po District of Hong Kong in protest of the continued use of shark fin at the restaurants.

On 10 June 2018, a Democratic Party lawmaker and members of Green Sense and Central and Western District Concern Group protested at the Hong Kong General Post Office in Central in the Central and Western District of Hong Kong against the demolition plan of the General Post Office. They held props, and claimed the plan would produce a large volume of construction waste.

On 5 June 2018, on the World Environment Day, more than 20 people from environmental groups, labour and business groups, including the Greeners Action and the Hong Kong Wastes and Recyclables Operators Network, carried banners and staged a petition at the government headquarters in the Central and Western of Hong Kong. The protesters demanded that the government submitted the bills of solid waste charging and introduced the levy on domestic waste.

notes: On 23 May 2018, hundreds of residents gathered at a mining site in Mapeng Village (Yulin City, Guangxi Province), holding banners and chanting slogans in opposition to the potential environmental and health issues caused by the mining operations. It was reported that the local village committee had approved the mining operation without consultation with the villagers. The special and anti-riot police were at the scene during the demonstration and clashed with the villagers. The police reportedly used their shields and batons to beat up villagers, causing some of the villagers to bleed in their heads. 16 villagers were arrested.

On 20 May 2018, nearly 10 people (including the head of an environmental group called Green Sense) and 2 legislative councillors demonstrated in front of The University of Hong Kong Tang Chi Ngong Building in Central and Western District (Hong Kong), to oppose the chopping down of two old banyan trees. They held banners and chanted slogans calling to protect these trees and protect the history of the people of Hong Kong. The two trees were due to be chopped down in the morning on the same day, as authorities stated that the trees were in poor health, with a risk of them collapsing.

On 20 April 2018, about 40 members of the Protect Cha Kwo Ling Harbour Concern Group and residents of Laguna City gathered at the North Point Government Office (Eastern District, Hong Kong) and protested against the Town Planning Board's decision to build a vocational training school on the beachfront near Cha Kwo Ling in the district. Members of the Legislative Council and the Civic Party participated in the protest. Protesters held signs and banners and criticized the government for misusing East Kowloon seaside instead letting citizens enjoy the clean air and natural scenery, and demanded that the original plan for a seaside park should be executed instead.

Around 15 April 2018 (middle of month), thugs hired by the town authorities forcibly dispelled villagers defending their land and property rights in Wanzhai Village (Sanming, Fujian), injuring several women and seniors during the process. An elderly woman was dragged on the ground and fell unconscious while local police ignored the assault. The villagers had been defending their rights for years against the environmental pollution caused by a mining company.

On 14 April 2018, 3 members of an environmental organisation, the Wild Aid, staged a silent protest with placards at a restaurant in the IFC building in Central Hong Kong over their use of shark fin. They were confronted by the restaurant staff and removed by security. No violence was reported.

On 3 April 2018, at least a dozen environmentalists and Legislative Council members petitioned and demonstrated with placards and graphics at the Hong Kong Police Headquarter in Wan Chai District (Hong Kong) because they had reason to suspect that several recent fires at Nam Sang Wai conservation park were committed by people on purpose. Among them were groups such as Friends of the Earth (Hong Kong), Green Power, Green Sense, and Land Justice League founder-cum-community organiser Chu Hoi-Dick. They demanded the police to investigate and pursue the case.

On 26 March 2018, several groups and lawmakers, including Greenpeace, Concerning Grassroots' Housing Rights Alliance, Community March, Northeast Supporting Group, and League of Social Democrats, staged a protest at Civic Square in Central District (Hong Kong) over the government not using Fanling Golf Course to develop housing projects and the criticism of environmental groups from the Chief Executive of Hong Kong Carrie Lam. During the protest, the protesters chanted slogans.

Around 25 March 2018, several representatives of environmental groups held banners and read out declarations at the start of the Country Park Forum in Hong Kong hosted by 20 environmental groups and attended by around 200 people. They demanded for the Hong Kong government not to use country parks and land reclamation to develop housing projects.

On 25 March 2018, lawmakers from the Legislative Council and Yue Long District Council, together with around 100 citizens, staged a protest in Nam Sang Wai Wetland in Yuen Long District (Hong Kong) and demanded for the police to find out the perpetrators behind the arsons in the wetland as soon as possible and protect the wetland. The protesters were lying on the ground to protest.
On 10 February 2018, around 50 environmentalists gathered outside the Maxim restaurant at the University of Hong Kong in Southern District (Hong Kong) to protest the sale of shark fins.

Other: Around 22 September 2021 (between 21 - 24 September), the China Human Rights Lawyers Concern Group in Hong Kong announced on 21 September 2021 that it was in the process of disbanding after political denunciation and investigation by national security police amid a crackdown on public dissent and peaceful opposition in the city. The group, founded to support human rights lawyers on the mainland, had refused the data request by national security police on the deadline of data submission. On 24 September 2021, Student Politicism, a pro-democracy student group, announced its disbandment after four current and former members were arrested and charged under the national security law.

Around 30 September 2021 (as reported), 4 representatives from the World Wildlife Fund and Hong Kong Federation of Trade Unions carried placards and held a press conference in Hong Kong to highlight that the 50-cent plastic bag levy had stagnated for years and no longer deterred plastic waste. They urged the government to step up the implementation of the waste reduction blueprint and increase the plastic charge as an economic incentive to reduce waste.

On 22 October 2020, a human rights lawyer (whose license was revoked since his last RSDL) was taken away from his residence in Fengxiang county (Baoji, Shaanxi) by the Hi-Tech Development Zone Branch of Baoji Public Security Bureau. He was then placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) in a hostel, where he was fixed onto a tiger chair from 22 October 2020 to 27 October 2020 and experienced prolonged interrogation, sleep, and water deprivation for more than five months. The arrest came six days after the victim posted a video on YouTube, sharing details about the torture he experienced during his first RSDL detention (10 days in the month of January). On 7 April 2021, the victim had been transferred to the Feng County Detention Centre in the Qinling (Qin Mountain) regions.

On 26 October 2021, members of the League of Social Democrats protested at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against the Chief Executive's policy address delivered on 6 October 2021. They argued that the massive plan for a northern metropolis and the Lantau Tomorrow Vision plan was a waste of resources and a cause of environmental damage.

On 13 January 2019, a human rights defender being detained at the Hunnan District Police Station in Shenyang (Liaoning) since 29 Oct 2018 was rushed to the hospital but did not survive. His son, who was monitored by almost 20 government officials during his meeting with the doctor, was told that his father died from a heart attack.

On 5 November 2021, a rights defender from Dandong, Liaoning, was kidnapped from his rental accommodation in Beijing municipality by officials from the Dandong Government and sent back to his hometown. Upon arrival, he was held at a budget hotel under the surveillance of the police. The incident was a case of stability maintenance ahead of the sixth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee set to commence in Beijing.

On 23 November 2021, fifteen Hong Kong green groups held a press conference and demonstrated in Hong Kong, urging the Environmental Protection Department to reject three project profiles relating to the Lantau Tomorrow Vision submitted by the government. They accused the government of jumping to the environmental impact assessment stage by ignoring an important environmental report, skipping a strategic environmental assessment, and failing to examine other land supply alternatives. Participating groups (including The Green Earth, Hong Kong Dolphin Conservation Society, and Greenpeace) held placards to express their demands.

On 2 November 2021, four people, including Professional Power representatives and Saigon district councilors, staged a protest and submitted petitions at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) as the government is studying the relocation of the Yau Tong Concrete Plant to Area 137 in Tseung Kwan O. Concerning environmental damage, they opposed the proposal and urged the authorities to develop a cement plant in a sealed cavern scheme to reduce environmental pollution.

On 22 October 2021, a female rights defender-cum-forced evicted was beaten up by Xinjiekou Residential District officials at her residential area in Maqun Sub-district of Qixia district (Nanjing, Jiangsu) when she tried to stop them from monitoring her by taking videos. She suffered neck injuries and needed to be hospitalized. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance in relation to the sixth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee set to commence in Beijing.

On 16 July 2021, a female human rights defender from Yuzhong district, Chongqing was intercepted by petition interceptors in the Beijing municipality and sent to a 'black jail' in Beijing where she was detained until her release on 2 August 2021. Upon her release, she was repatriated to Chongqing but was forcibly taken to a hotel in Chongqing for COVID-19 quarantine. This followed another incident on 8 June where she was taken away by petition interceptors in Beijing.

On 26 June 2021, a female rights defender from Wuhan was abducted by some people of unknown identity outside her apartment in Gangsi village, Fangshan district (Beijing) in a black car. Officials from Hubei Province Government Beijing Office and street subdistrict office were also present at the scene of the abduction. She was transferred to a room in Wuhan for a so-called 28-day 'coronavirus pandemic quarantine study class', where she was stripped naked, attacked in her genitals using electric batons, and placed under continual torture and ill-treatment. On 23 July 2021, she was finally sent back to her home in Wenjiawan Community after she deleted all of her photo records and social media content and signing a consent.

On 19 June 2021, a rights defending petitioner was kidnapped and assaulted by four unidentified men in their car when she stepped out of a police station at the train station in Chengdu prefecture (Sichuan) (coded to Wuhou). She was receiving assistance for being followed and restrained by those same men, who were trying to prevent her from boarding a train. Her trousers were taken off, as the men wanted to retrieve the cellphone she had hidden in her underwear. The men dropped her back at her home after knocking her unconscious.

On 8 June 2021, a female human rights defender from Yuzhong district, Chongqing was intercepted by petition interceptors in the Beijing municipality. She was sent to a 'black jail' in Chongqing where she was held until her release on 5 July 2021.

On 31 May 2021, a female rights defender residing in Binjiang district was kidnapped by a district officer in Xiaoshan district (Hangzhou, Zhejiang) after she was deceived into riding on his car. She was held captive at an elderly home until 2 July 2021. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 14 April 2021, a female rights defender was beaten with a baton by a staff during her visit to the Gulou District Housing Authority Bureau (Fuzhou, Fujian), by way of threatening her from submitting an application for the renovation of dilapidated houses. Her house was destroyed during a forced demolition operation led by the Gulou District Urban Enforcement Department.

On 30 March 2021, a female rights defender was beaten to the ground by a public security officer (from Nanjie Police Station) while visiting a conservation and development company office in Fuzhou prefecture (Fujian) (coded to Gulou). She was visiting to inquire about the situation with her dilapidated house, but was targeted as the situation resulted from a forced demolition operation led by the Gulou District Urban Enforcement Department. She was punched again in the police car, and detained at the police station despite suffering from rib fractures and soft tissue damage.

On 9 March 2021, a rights defender-cum-forced evictee was hospitalised in grave condition after being forced to take sleeping pills during her enforced disappearance at Nanyuan village, Fengtai district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Fengtai). The victim went into hiding on 26 Feb after anticipating being 'taken on mandatory vacation,' but was located by stability maintenance officers two days later and 'disappeared.' The incident was reported as one of multiple stability maintenance efforts carried out against petitioners nationwide during the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 18 February 2021, a rights defender from Putuo district, Shanghai was injected with poison and tortured during detention at a 'black jail' in Xinbei village, Huangshadaogang town of Chongming district (Shanghai). She was abducted earlier that day by officials of the Wanli Residential District Government Committee while petitioning in Beijing about an assault case involving her mother. When she was finally released home on 10 Mar, she was in poor health and unable to stand, before eventually passing away on 11 Apr 2021.

On 25 January 2021, a female human rights defender from Pingxiang, Jiangxi was intercepted at the National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration in Xicheng district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Xicheng) by interceptors from Xiangdong district, Pingxiang, and had since remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 27 Jan 2021.

Around 19 December 2020 (from 18 - 20 December), a female rights defender was kicked and punched by stability maintenance officers at the Canglang Sub-District Office in Gusu county (Suzhou, Jiangsu) due to arguments during an inquiry about forced eviction compensation. Later, when she was hospitalised, they tried to intervene and prevent doctors from providing her with medical inspection and treatment.

On 9 December 2020, a female rights defender and petitioner was kidnapped by the Shimahe sub-district chief at the Chongqing West railway station in Shapingba district (Chongqing) (coded as Chongqing-Shapingba) after returning from a trip. She remained incommunicado at the time of reporting on 22 Dec 2020.

On 26 October 2020, a female rights defender from Chongqing was beaten at 46-3 Gaojiachang, Yuquanying in Fengtai district (Beijing), after the police brought her into Fuyoumen Street police station earlier that day. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance in relation to the fifth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee that had commenced in Beijing.

Around 25 October 2020 (between 21-29 October), a female rights defender-cum-forced evictee from Nanjing was kidnapped by over 10 local government personnel of Xuanwu district (including interceptors, public security officers and Xinjiekou residential district's judicial officers) in front of the liaison office at Su 8 Hotel, Xiluoyuan residential district, Fengtai district (Beijing). She was confined to a room at an unknown location for nine days, and was beaten by police officers during her detention. Her release coincided with the end of the fifth plenary session of the 19th CPC Central Committee held in Beijing (location coded as Beijing-Fengtai).

On 28 September 2020, a female rights-defending petitioner was reportedly assaulted by on-duty police officers at the reception hall of the Hubei Letters and Visits Bureau in Wuchang district (Wuhan, Hubei), as witnessed by another female petitioner who was at the Bureau at the same time. She was then taken by the police to the police room, but it was not reported how long she was in the police room for.

On 31 August 2020, a female human rights defender from Yuzhong district, Chongqing had her ID checked and was then sent to Qinglonghu police station in Fangshan district (Beijing), and transferred to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail.' She was incommunicado as of 3 Sep after being escorted away on 1 Sep by a liaison officer from Chongqing. The incident was reported as a case of stability maintenance ahead of an international trade conference (CIFTIS 2020) held in Beijing from 4-9 Sep.

On 20 August 2020, a female rights defender was kidnapped and beaten up by a group of unidentified people outside the Jiangbei Huayuan Police Station in Jiangbei district (Chongqing) upon her release. She was intercepted while petitioning in Beijing and brought to the station earlier the same day. The kidnappers removed her trousers then punched and kicked her again after arriving at Beihai Shanzhuang (villa) in Tieshanping (Liangping, Chongqing). The police alluded that the group was sent by subdistrict level government officials. She was admitted to a hospital, and suffered toe fracture, bruises and soft tissue damage.

On 2 August 2020, a female rights defender-cum-forced evictee from Nan'an district, Chongqing was taken from Shijiazhuang prefecture (Hebei) by an unidentified group of people while aboard train Z4 traveling to Beijing. She was held at Yanzhao Hotel in Baoding prefecture (Hebei) as of 4 Aug under the order of Shijiazhuang government orders, and was one of several Chongqing petitioners who were intercepted on the train that day. Many rights defenders traveling to Beijing, specifically from Chongqing, had reportedly become government targets in the first week of August.

On 2 August 2020, a female rights defender-cum-forced evictee from Rugao, Jiangsu was intercepted by the police at Beidaihe Train Station in Beidaihe district (Qinhuangdao, Hebei), and transferred to two hotels (Yarun Hotel then Hairi Jingguan Hotel) where she was finally restricted in a form of 'black jail.' She had been intercepted and attacked multiple times in the past 6 years, and was one of several civilians prevented from entering the Baidaihe district during an annual summer high-level CPC conference (the 'Beidaihe conference').

On 7 June 2020, a female human rights defender was placed in heavy handcuffs and foot cuffs while being detained at the Qingyuan Detention Centre in Qingyuan prefecture (Guangdong). The two cuffs were chained to one another, forcing her into a curled position for a period of six days. She was also beaten up by other detainees who were held in her cell, though the reasons for the assault were not reported.

On 22 May 2020, a female human rights activist was taken away by the police in Beijing and forcibly repatriated to Chongqing on 23 May 2020. She was then detained in a farmhouse in Nan'an District (Chongqing), on the grounds of being quarantined as part of the COVID-19 prevention measures. This was likely part of the intensified security measures during the annual parliamentary sessions which started on 21 May 2020, to prevent people from travelling to Beijing to petition.

On 13 April 2020, a female human rights activist was taken away from her place of residence in Yubei District (Chongqing) by the police to the police station in the same district. During her detention which lasted more than 20 hours, she was handcuffed and shackled on a 'tiger bench' (a type of bench used to torture people). The activist had been arrested or harassed by the authorities several times on the grounds of 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble', for petitioning after her house had been forcibly demolished.

On 12 January 2020, a human rights activist from Hebei Province was forcibly dragged into a car by unidentified persons near the Beijing South Railway Station (Fengtai District, Beijing). The activist was subsequently detained for 15 days in her hometown of Julu County, before being transferred to a small hotel guarded by two people. It was also reported that on 4 February 2020, she was transferred and detained in a mental hospital. The activist had previously filed a petition for illegal land occupation.

On 9 January 2020, an activist was taken to Daxigou police station in (Yuzhong District, Chongqing) after stopping three unidentified men from kidnapping a lady (whom was later found to be another activist). When she requested for lunch at the police station, the police officers declined her request. She was subsequently violently dragged and detained in an iron cage for 7 hours.

On 11 October 2019, a female rights-defenders-cum-forced evictees from Pingnan county, Fujian, and her father were transferred by Beijing police in Beijing municipality to the hands of Pingnan government officers after they reported a case to the police. The officers beat the father, causing him to sustain six rib fractures during the ride back to Pingnan (Ningde City, Fujian Province). The daughter was charged with 'using other people's ID cards' and placed in administrative detention upon arrival.

On 29 August 2019, a human rights lawyer from Guangzhou who was just released from prison four months ago went missing after arriving at Guangzhou South railway station in Panyu, Guangzhou, Guangdong province. She has not been able to be contacted for at least 24 hours and is suspected to have been kidnapped.

On 19 August 2019, a female rights defender-cum-petitioner from Fujian was forcibly admitted to Kangning Psychiatric Hospital in Luohu district (Shenzhen, Guangzhou) (coded as Shenzhen-Luohu), and was reportedly forcibly medicated during her stay. The victim was a retired migrant worker and was known to be staying in Shenzhen since Sep 2018. She visied the law courts and Human Resources and Social Security Bureau until she lost contact with her family on 19 Aug. She was released in early 2020.

On 2 July 2019, a human rights activist from Chongqing was arrested by the police in Xicheng, Beijing when she was on her way to petitioning in Beijing. She was beaten up during more than 20 hours of detention and was sent back to Chongqing. She arrived in Chongqing on 4 July.

On 21 May 2019, a female human rights defender was taken on 'mandatory vacation' by the authorities in Foshan City of Guangdong Province, to prevent her from having a reunion with another human rights defender who would be released from the prison on 24 May 2019.
On 17 May 2019, a female human rights defender from Pingnan County of Fujian Province was arrested and held incommunicado by Beijing police in the Beijing Municipality.

On 17 May 2019, a female human rights defender was incommunicado after being kidnapped by the officers of Shanghai's Letters and Calls Bureau in Hongqiao railway station in Minhang District of Shanghai City. Her friend reported that she was likely to be detained in a 'black jail' in Chongming Island of Shanghai, where she had been detained several times before. She had petitioned for many years over the demolition of her husband's house by the government.

On 7 May 2019, the police forbade a female human rights defender from leaving the police station in Yan Village (Fangshan District, Beijing City) after she assisted a case on the ground that she was on a monitoring list. She was consequently detained in a black jail for 5 hours before sending back to her home town in Heilongjiang by some government personnel. She was released on the next day.

On 26 April 2019, a Shanghai human rights defender who had been detained with her husband at the Shanghai Municipal People's Government Beijing Office the night before was taken by government officials to the Beijing South Railway Station (Fengtai District, Beijing) and forced to return to Shanghai. When she resisted boarding the train, she was beaten by Shanghai officials. She was then detained in a black jail housed in a hotel in Hongkou District, Shanghai and released on 30 April 2019. She was diagnosed with a brain concussion after being released. It was part of a campaign by the CCP to silence dissent before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation which held in Beijing on April 25-27.

On 26 April 2019, a Shanghai human rights defender was taken away by the government officials in Beijing. She was detained in a black jail in Songjiang District, Shanghai before being released on 30 April 2019. It was part of a campaign by the CCP to silence dissent before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation which held in Beijing on April 25-27.

On 25 April 2019, a Shanghai human rights defender was taken away by the Fengxian government officials when she was petitioning in front of Beijing Municipal High People's Court (Chaoyang district, Beijing). She was forced to return to Shanghai was subsequently detained by authorities in a compound in Fengxian District, Shanghai for 5 days. On 29 April 2019, she was transferred to a hotel, before being released on 30 April 2019. It was part of a campaign by the CCP to silence dissent before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation which held in Beijing on April 25-27.

On 22 April 2019, a female Liaoning human rights defender was detained by public security officers at a hotel in Shenyang (Liaoning), following a series of investigations for a case of 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble.' She had first been released on 17 Apr after a month-long detention, then immediately brought to Beijing for further identification at the crime scene. After the investigation team escorted her back to Shenyang on 22 Apr, she was detained at the hotel for the night before being allowed to return home on 23 Apr.

Around 14 April 2019 (between 13-16 April 2019), a female rights activist was beaten up once by 'stability maintenance' officials from the neighbourhood committee in her village in Chongqing and held under house arrest for four days. She was among several hundred civilians - petitioners, rights defenders and dissidents - held incommunicado or subjected to house confinement due to President Xi's visit to Chongqing on 15 Apr.

On 27 March 2019, a human rights defender from Shenbei New Area, Shenyang was taken away by Dongcheng District police while she was waiting for her train home at Beijing railway station in Dongcheng District (Beijing). The Dongcheng police said that they were going to hand her over to local police in Shenyang and the human rights defender has been incommunicado for at least 14 days.

On 14 March 2019, a female Chongqing human rights defender was transferred to Majialou 'black jail' in Fengtai district from the Fuyoujie police station in Xicheng district (Beijing), where she had been held since 12 Mar after the police stopped her near Xi'anmen to checked her identity. She was later transferred to 602 Wangjingyuan in Chaoyang district.

On 13 March 2019, five female Shanghaiese human rights defenders were detained at Youwai police station in Fengtai district (Beijing) after being intercepted by the police as they were boarding the 102 bus at Beijing South station in Fengtai District. They were then sent back to Shanghai by train, one of them was locked up in a 'black jail' in Qingpu district by five police men and more than 20 'black security guards.' Three others experienced forced disappearance, and the remaining rights defender was sent home with a 'black security guard' guarding at her door.

On 13 March 2019, a female Shanghaiese human rights defender was intercepted by the police while traveling on the bus down 102 Road in Beijing. They confiscated her ID card and sent her back to Shanghai the same night. She had been incommunicado since for at least two days as of 15 Mar.

On 12 March 2019, a dozen people from the subdistrict office broke into the home of a female human rights defender in Dianjiang county (Chongqing), and took her forcefully to a mental hospital for a determination of mental illness. The incident was allegedly related to the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 12 March 2019, a female human rights defender from Pudong New Area, Shanghai was arrested at Meilia Hotel in Fengxian district (Shanghai) then locked up in Majialou 'black jail' in Fengtai district, Beijing. Her situation remained unknown. The incident was allegedly related to the annual Lianghui conventions.

On 12 March 2019, a female human rights defender was taken from her apartment in Shanghai by the superintendent of Zhijiang West Road police station and his men. They brought her to a 'black jail' in Suzhou.

On 11 March 2019, a female human rights defender from Luwan district, Shanghai was intercepted at Hongqiao train station in Minhang district as she was boarding a train to Beijing. Unknown men and a policemen from Zhunhai police station locked her up at Yirenyuan elderly apartment in Qingpu district, then transferred her to Taohua village in Nanhui district in Pudong New Area.
On 9 March 2019, a female human rights defender from Shanghai was intercepted by liaison officers on Chang'an Avenue, Beijing and has been incommunicado since.
On 8 March 2019, a female human rights defender was kidnapped at Wangzhuang of Fengtai district (Beijing) by the court police from her hometown.

On 5 March 2019, a human rights activist was intercepted by staff members from the Jiangsu Office in Beijing. She was then escorted to Jinjiang Inn 'black jail' in Baoshan District, Shanghai, where she was illegally detained. She escaped from the 'black jail' on 8 March 2019 and returned to Beijing by train on 12 March 2019 to further defend her rights. At Beijing South Railway Station, she was once again stopped by staff members of the Beijing Office and sent back to Shanghai on the same day by train.

On 4 March 2019, the 'police' arrested a rights-defender-cum-parent while she was fundraising in Beijing for disabled children. They did not produce official identification before arresting her, and the documents later produced were not stamped. She was then locked up in Majialou 'black jail' in Fengtai district for a day, and sent back to Hui county (Henan). Her husband disappeared after convening a protest with her on 25 Feb.

On 3 March 2019, a female human rights defender was detained at the Sheshan Forest Hotel in Sheshan National Forest Park in Shanghai. She was taken away by stability maintenance officers and policemen from Huaihai road in Shanghai just after she boarded high speed rail 108 earlier that day. She was held incommunicado for at least 15 days. The incident is allegedly related to the approaching annual Lianghui conventions.

On 24 February 2019, a human rights defender was kidnapped by 10 unidentified people at a bus stop in Qingyundianzhen, Daxing (Beijing) while on her way to seek medical treatment in Beijing. The assailants forced the human rights defender into a car without a license plate and drove to Hejia Hotel Yangqiao branch in Fengtai district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing-Fengtai) where they beat her up. The following day, they drove her back to Kunshan, Suzhou in another vehicle. She was detained for more than 20 days, during which she was also beaten up by officials and sustained head injuries. Upon her release, she sought medical consultation and was diagnosed with sensorineural hearing loss in her left ear and headache disorders. Previously, she had been monitoring the case of a disappeared person and had a court case scheduled for 4 March.

On 22 February 2019, a female human rights defender from Shanghai was 'taken on mandatory vacation' by ten stability maintenance officers, and brought to a farm villa in the Shanghai suburbs. She escaped on 26 Feb in an attempt to catch the train to Beijing from Hongqiao Train Station, but was intercepted by national security officers and police officers who presented no identification. She was placed under criminal detention afterwards.

On 25 October 2018, a human rights defender who had been held in a black jail in Beijing two days ago was sent back to Shanghai and taken from the Shanghai railway station in Jing'an District (Shanghai) to be held in black jail at 500 Fucun road in Putuo District. She was and later taken away by the police and sub-district officers from Changning District and has been missing since. She had gone to Beijing to submit a proposal to the NPC standing Committee on 23 October 2018.

On 23 October 2018, a human rights defender was arrested at the Jingxi Hotel in Haidian District (Beijing) while she was submitting a proposal to the NPC standing Committee. She was first brought to the Yangfangdian police station before being transferred to a black jail housed in the Relief Administration Service Center in Dongcheng District. The next day, she was sent back to Shanghai by train, after which she was detained in another black jail.

On 10 August 2018, a woman human rights activist who was being detained in her home in Kunshan, Jiangsu by stability maintenance agents was violently prevented from leaving her home when she attempted to leave and seek medical treatment in Beijing for her chronic illness. When she tried to call the police, the stability maintenance agents snatched away her phone and violently pushed her back inside her home and continued to detain her. She had been detained since 2 Aug after the agents forcibly took her back to Kunshan while she was on vacation in Beidaihe, Beijing.

On 30 July 2018, a female human rights activist was attacked by an unidentified laser weapon while attending a court hearing in Fuzhou city (Cangshan district), Fujian as a member of the public. After experiencing immediate symptoms included pain in her head, chest, neck and spine, as well as nausea and inability to speak, she was hospitalized and underwent cranial surgery.

On 27 June 2018, a human rights defender was beaten up by a police officer in front of the Shanghai Police Station in Huangpu District (Shanghai) while she was crying out her grievances. She sustained four fractures in her left ribs.

On 27 June 2018, a policeman beat up of a female Shanghaiese rights activist after she shouted outside the Municipal Public Security Bureau in Shanghai (Jing'an district), airing her grievances about the processing delay of her hukou migration documents. She was hurt so hard that her ribs broke, and she had wounds on her forehead and arms.

On 7 May 2018, a Xi'an woman rights defender was forcible taken and attacked by 5-6 police officers from Beijing Public Security Fengtai Branch at a motel in Fengtai District, Beijing. The defender was forcibly taken to the police station in her pajamas, and she was interrogated and beaten for three hours. The reason for the attack is unknown. After three hours, the defender was returned to the motel. In the past, the defender had been sent to a labour camp.

On 6 May 2018, a female labour rights activist visiting from Shanxi was beaten up by uniform-identified police troops at her room in Motai 168 Hotel near Beijing South station (Fengtai district). Although her visit was acknowledged by law enforcement officials from her hometown, they handcuffed her before taking her to You'anmen police station and hurt her violently. Hospital examination showed that she suffered from soft tissue damage.

On 4 May 2018, two human rights activists were taken away by police at Ping'anli West Street in Xicheng District, Beijing. Activists were taken to Gaojiachang black prison No. 46-3 after a group Chongqing activists had their identity documents checked and were intercepted on their way to petition. One activist was taken into a police car that had another Chongqing activist in it already, and the two were later transferred to another vehicle by a different group of people in uniforms.

On 16 March 2018, a female rights defender went incommunicado in Shanghai after she went to petition at the liaison office of the National People's Congress in Beijing (location not known) but was stopped by the police, sent to Yangfangdian Police Station in Haidian district, and escorted back to Shanghai via train G133 that same day. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 12 March 2018, a female rights defender who was a former victim of Liaoning Masanjia Female Labour Camp was taken by the local interceptors from Beijing Tianqiao in Xicheng District (Beijing) to the Xidan Street Police Station, handed over to the local government by the Beijing police, forced to return to Benxi Liaoning, and went incommunicado later. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 12 March 2018, a female rights defender from Banan Chongqing was taken by people from the Beijing-based office of the Chongqing Government while she was in Beijing to petition and sent back to Chongqing by the local government. After that, she was sent to the Yudong Yunzhuan Mountain Qingfeng Gorge Hotel in Banan District, Chongqing, got her ID confiscated by the local police, and went incommunicado. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 9 March 2018, a female rights defender were taken away from her home in Shanghai by nearly 20 people from the sub-district office and detained in a rural tourist resort in the suburbs of Shanghai. She had just been released from a detention centre where she was detained since 27 February 2018. She was previously held under soft detention in a rural tourist resort from 22 February but managed to escape on 26 February. She was taken into custody again by 20 to 30 police officers and personnel from the Public Complaints and Proposals Bureau when she was taking a train to Beijing on 27 February.

On 6 March 2018, a Shanghai human rights activist was beaten by 6 men from the Beijing-based Shanghai government while being held in a black prison set up by the Shanghai Municipal Government in Fengtai District (Beijing). She was beaten after refusing to go back to Shanghai with people she did not recognise but who claimed to be from the city's Jing'an District government. She was previously the victim of the forced demolition of her house and had not yet received compensation.

On 5 March 2018, a Shanghai human rights activist was abducted in Tiananmen Square in Dongcheng District (Beijing - Dongcheng) and taken to a black prison in Beijing Jiujingzhuang Jieji Service Centre by Tiananmen Public Security Bureau police. Afterwards, she was transferred to a black prison set up by the Shanghai Municipal Government in Fengtai District (Beijing).

On 4 March 2018, a female rights defender from Hangzhou Zhejiang was taken by the interceptors from the Hangzhou local government around the Beijing South Railway Station in Fengtai District (Beijing) and went incommunicado. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 1 March 2018, two female rights defenders from Jiangsu were taken in Beijing by the Beijing police when they were staying at their friend's place and petitioning in Beijing. They remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 7 March 2018.

Around 1 March 2018 (beginning of month), before the Lianghui conventions started, a female rights defender in Guangzhou (Guangdong) was sent to take on mandatory vacation by the local state security police. She was followed by stability maintenance personnel everyday and deprived of the freedom to go out, have contact with other people, and post comments on the Internet.

On 27 February 2018, a female rights defender went missing when she was at home in Jinyang Road Sub-district in Pudong New Area (Shanghai), and it was suspected that she was taken by the stability maintenance officers. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 25 February 2018, a female rights defender was taken by unknown people when she was walking in the residential area where she lived in Shanghai and went incommunicado. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 25 February 2018, a female rights defender was taken back to Chongqing when she was taking a train in Guang'an District (Guang'an, Sichuan) by stability maintenance personnel, and her situation was unknown afterwards. It was later reported that she was illegally detained for more than 20 days, due to heightened security measures around the Lianghui conventions period.

On 24 February 2018, a female rights defender was taken by a government official from the Shanghai House Expropriation Department in Shanghai and detained in Houniao Resort in Shanghai Chongmin District Chenjia Town Qianyugong Road No. 888. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 7 December 2021, four environmental groups (Green Power, Greenpeace, The Green Earth, Greeners Action) demonstrated and held a press conference in Hong Kong to demand effective public participation and timetables for the plastic reduction plan. They held signs to express their demands.

On 22 October 2021, Xinjiekou Residential District Stability Maintenance Office officers raided the house of a female human rights activist in Xuanwu district (Nanjing, Jiangsu) and beat her up, forcing her not to follow up her case of illegal demolition. She sustained six rib fractures and injuries over the body, resulting in hospitalization for half a month.

On 13 January 2022, a female human rights lawyer was assaulted from the back by a group of people at Suzhou Gusu District People's Court in Gusu (Suzhou, Jiangsu). She was injured after being dumped at the entrance of the court. It was not known if the attack was related to her case.

On 5 December 2021, a human rights activist from Tianhe district (Guangzhou, Guangdong) went missing and became incommunicado for the second time this year after sending a message signaling his arrest. He was officially arrested for 'inciting subversion of state power' and held in custody by Guangzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau on 12 January 2022.

On 11 January 2022, a human rights lawyer became incommunicado after being arrested by national security officers at his home in Dongkou county (Shaoyang, Hunan). His family received a notice of criminal detention on 17 January 2022, stating that on the same day he was arrested on suspicion of inciting subversion of state power, picking quarrels and provoking trouble, and currently detained in Changsha City No. 1 Detention Center, Hunan Province. His forced disappearance might be related to his efforts to pressure the government to release a teacher, Li Tian Tian, from a psychiatric hospital in late December 2021.

Other: On 5 July 2021, three human rights and civic groups - Civil Rights Observer, Progressive Lawyers Group and Progressive Teachers' Alliance - announced cease of operations and disbandment in Hong Kong while some cited a lack of resources and the 'current climate' in the wake of the national security law imposed by Beijing last year. The Progressive Lawyers Group announced its disbandment, although the group's convenor refused to disclose more details about the reason. It was reported that at least 13 civil society and professional organizations had disbanded within the last two weeks.

On 28 January 2021, a human rights activist was intercepted at Pudong International Airport in Pudong New Area (Shanghai) by customs officers, who was stopped from boarding a flight to visit his wife in the United States for 'national security reasons.' He announced that he would go on a hunger strike at the airport to protest against the travel ban, but had since become uncontactable at the time of reporting.

On 16 October 2019, the convenor of the Civil Human Rights Front was attacked by 4-5 unknown individuals with hammers at Arran Lane, Mong Kok, Yau Tsim Mong District (Kowloon City, Hong Kong) when he was en route to a CHRF meeting. He was injured in his head and arms and was sent to the hospital.

On 1 April 2021, supporters (citizens and groups including CHRF, DP, HKCTU, Labour Party, LSD) gathered at the West Kowloon Law Courts in Sham Shui Po district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Sham Shui Po) to support seven veteran pro-democracy activists on trial for illegal assembly in connection with a mass march in 2019 (the '8.18 case'), chanting slogans of support. Some defendants (former legislators affiliated with The Alliance, DP, Labour Party) also demonstrated ahead of the hearing, holding up placards and banners in protest against 'political suppression' and calling for the five demands.
