The pro-Beijing group Politihk Social Strategic also protested, calling for 'heavy sentence and imprisonment.'

Property destruction: On 20 March 2019, several dozens of people demolished the ancestral home of a human rights artist in Shangzhai village of Pingdu district (Beijing). They did not present any documentation or follow any official procedures, but claimed the house had to be demolished to build a road to fulfill President Xi Jinping's political vision of the 'new village.'

On 13 May 2019, a Hubei human rights defender was kidnapped by 5 masked men during lunch with a friend in Fangshan District of Beijing City. As of the reporting on 15 May, he still had not been heard from and could not be contacted. It was reported that he had been under surveillance and demanded to leave the city by the Beijing police recently.

On 18 May 2020, a female human rights activist was beaten by a group of unidentified black-clad people at one of the Beijing representative offices in Beijing. She was forcibly taken away by the group and remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 21 May 2020. She was likely to have been taken away as part of the intensified security measures ahead of the annual parliamentary sessions scheduled to start on 21 May 2020 to prevent people from travelling to Beijing to petition.

On 17 May 2020, three human rights activists (including two women) from Chongqing were taken away by unidentified persons in Chaoyang District (Beijing), and remained uncontactable at the time of reporting on 21 May 2020. They were likely to have been taken away as part of the intensified security measures ahead of the annual parliamentary sessions scheduled to start on 21 May 2020 to prevent people from travelling to Beijing to petition.

On 8 November 2018, two human rights defenders went to the black jail in Zhongxin road 1039 in Jing'an district (Shanghai) to visit their friend who was prisioned there. During the visit, they were attacked by the head of guards of the black jail and a young man.

On 7 March 2019, two human rights defenders were kidnapped by unidentified persons in Beijing and were incommunicado thereafter. This was reportedly related to the stability maintenance around and during the Lianghui sessions.

Around 27 September 2021 (week of), before the National Day on 1 October, a human rights defender went missing and became incommunicado in Jian city, Jiangxi (coded as Jizhou). On 9 November 2021, his family was informed that the Ji'an Public Security Bureau officially arrested the human rights defender on suspicion of picking quarrels and provoking trouble. He remained uncontactable, as reported on 28 January 2022.

On 15 August 2018, a retired professor-cum-human rights activist was taken away by national security officers and police from Shandong University dormitory in Licheng district (Jinan, Shandong) after being interviewed by the U.S. government-funded media, Voice of America. He had been forced disappearance for four years, as reported on 29 January 2022.

On 9 February 2020, a citizen journalist-cum-human rights defender was arrested by police from his residence in Wuhan city, Hubei (coded to Jiang'an), and became incommunicado for almost 2 years. The victim had been subjected to police violence and oppression since the 1990s due to his practice of Falun Gong. As reported on 4 February 2022, his family had finally found out that he was held at Jiang'An District detention facility but remained incommunicado.

On 1 July 2018, citizens, convened by the Civil Human Rights Front, marched from Victoria Park to Civic Square (at the Central Government Complex) in protest against encroaching authoritarianism, including controversies such as the juxtaposed border arrangement at the West Kowloon express rail station. Police forces were present to maintain order, especially when protesters diverted beyond pre-approved protest routes or joined midway. No clashes reported. A final gathering was held, officiating the event's conclusion at 6:42pm.

On 28 June 2019, between as many as 1000 to 10000 people took to the streets in Xinzhou district (Wuhan, Hubei) demonstrating against the construction of a waste incineration power plant. They shouted slogans and held banners to express concerns regarding environmental pollution. It was reported that more than 1000 police were deployed, and there were clashes between demonstrators and the police. Some demonstrators were beaten up, resulting in one man being hospitalised. Some of them threw water bottles at police.

On 12 September 2018, a female human rights activist was taken away from a bus station on Yongdingmen West in Beijing - Dongcheng by a staff member from the Jiangyin City representative office in Beijing and three 'thugs.' While arriving in a hotel in Fengtai District where she would be detained, she was violently dragged out of the car, causing her to collapse onto the ground due to her pre-existing injuries. She began to feel tightness in her chest and stomach cramps, and repeatedly vomited. She was repatriated to Jiangyin City later in the evening on the same day.

On 3 August 2020, a female rights defender from Jiangbei, Chongqing was assaulted by government-hired personnel during a black-jail detention at Shijiazhuang Hotel in Shijiazhuang prefecture, Hebei (coded to Chang'an). Many rights defenders traveling to Beijing, specifically from Chongqing, had reportedly become government targets in the first week of August.

On 26 October 2020, two rights defenders from Chongqing were beaten by their captors while being held at a 'black jail,' room 46-3 Gaojiachang in Fengtai district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Fengtai), one of whom vomited afterwards. The rights defenders had been intercepted by the police in Beijing earlier that day, and temporarily detained in Fuyou Street Police Station and Jiujingzhuang 'black jail,' before being transferred to Gaojiachang. Both were escorted back to the Liangjiang New Area (Chongqing) by seven people the following night, and left on the roadside (location coded as Beijing-Fengtai).

On 28 May 2021, seven female rights defending petitioners went missing after they last communicated that over 20 interceptors from Inner Mongolia province had surrounded their apartment on Fenghai South St in Fengtai district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Fengtai). They continued to be not contactable four days later on 1 Jun 2021. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.

On 4 March 2019, four human rights defenders were forcibly detained within one of their homes in Huangxiang subdistrict of Liangxi district (Wuxi, Jiangsu) by 'thugs' hired by the local government. While being detained, 7 'thugs' beat up at least 3 of them while police stood by without intervening. The victims sustained minor injuries, and were released afterwards.

On 2 March 2021, a female rights defender from Chongqing was beaten by three government-hired men in a car parked outside of Huazhong Hotel in Baoding prefecture (Hebei) (coded to Jingxiu), where they reportedly tried to escort her to a hotel room. Earlier that day, she was on her way to Beijing via train when police officers from the Xi'an North Railway Station Police Station tried to prevent her from boarding under a request for investigation from the Rongchang District Public Security Bureau (Chongqing). She boarded the train, but was robbed and escorted away via car upon her arrival at Gaobeidian East Railway Station in Gaobeidian (Baoding, Hebei).

On 18 March 2018, a female rights defender was physically assaulted and injured by the government-appointed 'thugs' at the Jinghua Hotel in Beijing - Fengtai where the Beijing-based Office of the Wuxi Government was. She was taken to the hotel by a group of unidentified people at the Fuyou Street Post Office when she finished sending her petition letter.

On 21 March 2018, a human rights activist was beaten by 6-7 government hired 'thugs' (which the government called 'temporary workers') at a commune petition office in Hongkou District (Shanghai). He went to the commune petition office earlier on the day to report his recent abduction by government employed personnel but was not accepted by the staff there. After being beaten, he also called the police to the scene, but the police refused to intervene.

On 10 January 2022, a rights defender from Dandong, Liaoning, was kidnapped by 6 government officers and police from his hometown outside the Ministry of National Security in Dongcheng district, Beijing (coded as Beijing - Dongcheng) after submitting petitions. He was repatriated to Yuanbao District of Dandong city, and held at a COVID-19 quarantine facility and a hotel under surveillance by three people. The interception was part of the campaign to suppress dissentients before the Winter Olympics Games in Beijing.

On 26 April 2018, a petitioner-cum-human rights defender was beaten by 3 'ruffians' employed by local 'stability maintenance' authority near his home in Wanzhou district (Chongqing) reportedly because he posted some comments to support the march of the wife of the '709 lawyer.' He was beaten for almost half an hour. Police was called to the scene but accused everyone at the scene of 'picking quarrels.' He went to the hospital on the day after and suffered from headache and nausea.

Around 15 March 2018 (between 9 March - 21 March), a human rights activist was violently slapped by local 'ruffians' hired by the local government during his detention in the 'black jail' in Qingpu District (Shanghai). He was forcibly intercepted by officials from the Shanghai Municipal Office when he was filing a complaint at the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng District (Beijing) on 9 March 2018. He was then forcibly repatriated to Shanghai where he was illegally detained in a 'black jail' until his release on 21 March 2018.

On 3 July 2018, a female civil rights activist was attacked and injured by several people in Runzhou District (Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province) when she demanded to see the doctors. She was also monitored by interceptors while in hospital.

On 16 February 2020, a female social justice activist from Beijing was taken into custody by the Beijing authorities. She was held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL). The arrest was likely prompted by a tweet sent out by the activist on 24 January 2020, which was critical of the Chinese authorities' attempted coverup of the coronavirus outbreak. Some international media had also reported that her enforced disappearance might be related to the recent arbitrary detention of her partner, who is a prominent human rights lawyer. She confirmed on Twitter herself that she has been set free on 19 June 2020.

On 24 April 2019, two human rights defenders, a mother and her daughter, were taken away by government officials at the Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport in Yubei city (Chongqing) before they boarded their flight to Beijing, where they planned to petitioned. One of them was beaten while being taken away and also had her mobile phone confiscated.

On 27 April 2019, a female petitioner-cum-rights defender from Huishan district, Wuxi was transferred by Wuxi government officials to the first floor of Jinghua Hotel from Fuyou Street police station in Beijing - Xicheng and escorted back to Wuxi that evening by a policemen, a government official and a government-hired security guard. Her mailing documents were stolen when she arrived in Beijing on 26 Apr with letters and complaints to send to central authorities.

On 7 March 2018, a female rights defender was taken from her home in Shanghai by a group of unidentified people and sent to a 'black jail' inside Chongming Houniao Resort. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 14 November 2021, a captured female human rights defender, who was also a petitioner-cum-forced evictee, was attacked by a government-hired security guard at Room 8313 of Shanghai Pattaya Holiday Inn in Yangpu district (Yangpu, Shanghai) after concerns over her health and hygiene. She was slapped in the face and nipped on her wrist. She was intercepted by police in Beijing on 29 September 2021 and finally released on 18 November 2021 after detaining in two Shanghai hotels.

On 13 March 2019, 3 women human rights defenders were detained by police at the You'anmen District Police Station in Fengtai while en route to petition. They were then forced to board a train back to Shanghai Municipality by a police officer and are suspected to have been kidnapped thereafter.

On 8 March 2018, a female rights defender was taken in Beijing and sent to Jiujingzhuang, a 'black jail,' by the Beijing police when she intended to petition to National People's Congress, and later she was sent back to Shanghai by the government officials from Huangpu District. On the next day, she was sent to a 'black jail' inside the Qingpu Jingui Island Fishing Resort.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 6 September 2020, citizens (including LegCo member, district councillors, several LJL, CHRF, Demosisto and LSD representatives) held several demonstrations throughout the day in Yau Tsim Mong district (Hong Kong) against the enactment of the National Security Law, the implementation of 'health code', and the one-year delay of Legislative Council elections (supposed to take place that day). Some were also concerned with the 12 Hong Kong stowaways (some anti-ELAB activists) who were detained in Shenzhen after being caught on a boat to Taiwan in mainland Chinese waters. They shouted anti-ELAB and pro-independence slogans, songs and hand signs. Police officers released pepper bombs at various points. 289 people were arrested in total that day for participating in demonstrations. A demonstrator and a person wearing a reporter's vest were escorted to the hospital (due to conditions not explicitly reported as related to the demonstrations).

On 31 December 2020, a dozen citizens hiked to the peak of Lion Rock Mountain in Wong Tai Sin district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Wong Tai Sin) to show support for social movements, demonstrators and activists in the fight for democracy, freedom, human rights, rule of law and justice. They held up a neon sign that spelt out 'FAITH' as part of the demonstration.

On 2 December 2020, a female rights defender from Fuzhou, Fujian was kidnapped by authorities in Beijing municipality after petitioning at the State Bureau for Letters and Calls in Xicheng district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Xicheng). She was subsequently detained at Jiujingzhuang 'black jail.' Government-hired 'black' security forces escorted her back to her hometown, and continued to hold her incommunicado at Xinfengyangshanzhuang 'black jail' in Guling, Fuzhou with at least two more women. She was released on 23 Dec 2020.

On 25 November 2020, LSD, HKFTU, the Hong Kong Manufacturing Industry Employees General Union (HKMEU) and former legislators protested ahead of the 2020 Policy Address at the Hong Kong Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong-Central and Western), with the LSD against political oppression and 'ineffective coronavirus mitigation measures,' and proposed development project Lantau Tomorrow Vision. The LSD, HKFTU and the HKMEU also protested about labour issues, including the setup of a coronavirus unemployment relief fund, increase of statutory holidays and Mandatory Provident Funds for low-salary employees.

Around 22 November 2020 (between 12 Nov - 3 Dec), a female rights defender from Guangxi was arrested in Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture (Yunnan) (coded to Jinghong City) by officers from the Guangzhou Bureau of State Security, possibly in connection with the '11.12 Guangzhou Arrests' crackdown on dissidents. Her family was notified on 3 Dec that she was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) on suspicion of subversion.

On 3 November 2020, a female rights defender was beaten by a CPC Committee official at the Longhe Town Government in Longhe town of Fengdu county (Chongqing). She was recently released after being intercepted in Beijing, then kidnapped and held in a 'black jail' from 23 Oct to 29 Oct.

On 24 October 2020, a female rights defender detained by police was made to sit in a torture chair at the Fengdu County Public Security Bureau in Fengdu county (Chongqing) for around 30 minutes. She was first kidnapped near Kaiyang Lane, Fengtai district (Beijing) by police and government officials on 23 Oct and taken to a 'black jail' room 46-3 Gaojiachang in the same district. On 26 Oct, a Longhe town official and four police officers kidnapped her to Tianhai Shangwu Hostel in Longhe town of Fengdu county (Chongqing). On 27 Oct, a town official confiscated her phone and pressed her against the bed in order to stop her from reporting the incident to the police. She was released on 30 Oct (location coded as Beijing-Fengtai).

On 26 December 2018, journalists and rights defenders gathered outside the Tianjin No.2 Intermediate People's Court in Hexi district (Tianjin) to show support for a human rights lawyer on trial as part of the '709 crackdown'. Police forced most protesters to go home and plainclothes police took away at least 8 protesters who shouted slogans and carried signs. One of them was released the same day while others have been out of contact for at least several days since.

On 26 December 2018, around 30 members of The Alliance, China Human Rights Lawyers Concern Group, League of Social Democrats and Civic Party, marched from Western Police Station and staged a protest in front of Hong Kong Liaison Office in Western District (Hong Kong). The protesters demanded for the release of a human rights lawyer who was arrested in the '709 Crackdown', and his wife was held under soft detention. They chanted slogans, stuck portraits of the couple and letters of protest outside the Liaison Office, as well as threw props into the Liaison Office.

On 18 October 2018, a civil rights activist from Yanshou County, Heilongjiang was taken away by the police at a metro station in Fangshan, Beijing and forcibly repatriated to Yanshou County. He had since been uncontactable. At the time of reporting on 19 October 2018, it was reported that he was likely detained in a 'black jail'.

On 18 October 2018, around 5 human rights defenders held banners in the 'Cuiyongyuan Noodle House' of the Communication University of China Canteen in Chaoyang district (Beijing) to support the talk show host Cuiyongyuan for exposing the corruptions in the Chinese police forces.

On 30 September 2018, before the Chinese National Day on 1 October, at least two members of the Guizhou Human Rights Commission were taken away by the authorities, likely from Guizhou Province, and 'taken on mandatory vacation' or placed under 'soft detention' in hotels in Guiyang City. It was reported that more than ten members of the Guizhou Human Rights Commission had been 'taken on mandatory vacation' or placed under 'soft detention' in hotels in Guiyang City before 1 October. This was to prevent them from participating in the ' National Day Take to the Street Together' activity, which intended to protest against the Chinese Communist Party.

On 29 September 2018, a member of the Guizhou Human Rights Commission was taken away by the authorities, likely from Guizhou Province, and 'taken on mandatory vacation' to an agritainment resort around Guiyang City (Guizhou). He was guarded by four people at the resort until 7 October. Before the Chinese National Day on 1 October, more than ten members of the Guizhou Human Rights Commission were 'taken on mandatory vacation' or placed under 'soft detention' to prevent them from participating in the 'National Day Take to the Street Together' activity, which was intended to protest against the Chinese Communist Party.

On 5 September 2018, more than 30 people from the police and urban management bureau forcibly demolished a shop owned by a human rights activist located in Yangpu District, Shanghai. The authorities claimed that the shop was 'illegal'.

On 31 August 2018, police forces stopped 14 Shanghaiese human rights activists at Ping'anli metro station (Xicheng district of Beijing), and sent them to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' once they were identified as petitioners. They were on their way to the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection office to report a complaint about the Shanghai local government. The petitioners reportedly learnt that they will be sent back to their hometown the next day, and continue to be detained or in a 'black jail' due to an upcoming international expo.

Around 29 August 2018 (as reported), a rights activist was made to leave Beijing a few days ahead of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation to be 'taken on mandatory vacation.' A few weeks ago, government officials accompanied his travels to Yunnan, then monitored and restricted him after he returned to Beijing.

On 28 August 2018, an arrested democracy rights activist was placed under 'Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location' by the police at the Pudong district station of the Shanghai Municipal Public Security Bureau. Days prior, the police had informed his family that he would be released from criminal detention within the week.

On 25 August 2018, many environmental activist groups - including the Society for Community Organisation, Land Justice League - grassroots citizen groups, and former Chief of the Hong Kong Observatory protested outside the last round of 2018 Land Supply Public Engagement meetings at EDB Kowloon Tong Education Services Center in Hong Kong. They called for the conservation of public parks, increase of the ratio of public housing, and against land reclamation and 'unfair media narratives for pitting conservation against livelihoods.' The environmental groups submitted a petition to the chairman of the Task Force on Land Supply, and protests continued inside the meeting venue as well.

On 2 August 2018, a retired professor-cum-human rights activist was removed by police from Shandong University dormitory in Licheng district (Jinan, Shandong) during a live interview with the U.S. government-funded media, Voice of America. He was taken on a 'mandatory vacation' for 10-12 days before being kept under tight surveillance at his home.

Around 25 July 2018, a Shanghaiese human rights defender residing in Pudong New District (Shanghai) was suspected to be missing after his friends found that he had not been online. They also failed to reach him at his residence in Pudong New District, Shanghai. The rights defender had been involved in the 'Toilet Revolution', and was suspected to have been kidnapped around 25 July 2018 and had been incommunicado for at least 17 days at the time of reporting on 11 August.

On 2 July 2018, two rights defenders from Xingtai City, Hebei were taken by the local national security agents on a 'mandatory vacation' to a rural farmhouse and detained there for the reason that they were planning to hold their wedding on the anniversary of the 709 crackdown. Several people who were related to 709 crackdown had been 'taken on mandatory vacation' due to the upcoming anniversary of the incident.

On 28 June 2018, 4 human rights defenders carrying placards protested on the streets in Shanghai Municipality to call for the release of Ding Deyuan, a christian petitioner-cum-activist, who was charged 'obstructing official business' by the court in Shanghai.

On 24 June 2018, around 20 and 30 environmental activists protested against 'excessive' plastic packaging at a supermarket in LOHAS Park in Sai Kung District of Hong Kong by unwrapping produce at checkout.

On 24 June 2018, around 15 environmental activists protested against 'excessive' plastic packaging at CitySuper's Times Square branch in Causeway Bay in Wan Chai District of Hong Kong. The activists unwrapped plastic packaging at the checkout, leaving a pile of plastic packaging in a box for staff to collect.

On 24 June 2018, around 20 and 30 environmental activists protested against 'excessive' plastic packaging at a supermarket in Mui Wo and North Discovery Bay in Islands District of Hong Kong by unwrapping produce at checkout.

On 21 June 2018, almost 50 petitioners and human rights defenders assembled in front of the Chongqing Jiulongpo People's Court in Jiulongpo District of Chongqing in support of 2 evicted farmers who were charged with 'inciting public nuisance'. The police intervened by holding 6 protesters incommunicado inside the court before releasing them at night. More than 10 people were detained in a psychiatric hospital and other premises. Some people were sent to the police station.

Around 9 June 2018, during the 2018 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Qingdao, Shandong a human rights activist begging in the area was forcibly sent back to Shanghai by people from the Shanghai Government. He was first held at the Meiyuan police station in Shanghai, before being handed over to triad members who kept him in a 'black jail' in Changxing Island, Shanghai. He was beaten violently during his three-day detention.

Around 9 June 2018 (between 7 - 11 June), a female human rights defender (who had reportedly petitioned before) was beaten up and had her right eye injured during the 5-day detention at a 'black jail' in Shanghai.

On 8 June 2018, more than 10 civilians from Shanghai, including one female rights defender from Changning district, travelled to Qingdao city (Shandong Province) and were subsequently held incommunicado by the Qingdao police at the Qingdao Youth Training Center 'black jail' in Shinan District, Qingdao City. This was part of a campaign by the CCP to silence dissent before and during the 2018 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Qingdao on June 9-10. The group was allegedly travelling for leisure.

On 5 June 2018, a Shanghai female human rights defender was intercepted by officials of the Shanghai Government Office in Beijing, then escorted back to Shanghai and detained in a 'black jail' in Putuo District for a short detention. After that, she was sent to Jinyang Xincun Police Station and officially arrested.

On 30 May 2018, more than 10 human rights defenders held placards and chanted slogans outside the Shanghai Pudong Huinan People's Court in Pudong New Area, Shanghai City in support for petitioner Ding Deyuan who was detained and accused of 'obstructing official business'. During the protest, Ding's lawyer arrived at the legal court and viewed the case documentation.

On 25 May 2018, a number of groups (including the CHRF, LSD, HKCTU, Labour Party, Justice and Peace Commission of the Hong Kong Catholic Diocese, and foreign domestic workers' groups) held a press conference in Hong Kong, demanding an apology from a New People's Party lawmaker for the remark she made earlier that week, claiming that gatherings of domestic workers in public spaces caused 'hygiene issues'. They also urged the government to enact reforms to improve the standards of accommodation, allow live-out arrangements, and regulate working hours for domestic workers. They held placards during the press conference.

On 1 May 2018, seven rights activists from Chongqing went missing for three days after participating in the 'National Resonance' event and having a meal together. Two of the activists were freed on 4 May but not allowed to communicate online or be interviewed by foreign media. By the time of report on 5 May 2018, there was still one person's whereabouts remaining unknown.

On 1 May 2018, a Green Leaf Initiative advocate disappeared at Jiefangbei Square in Yuzhong, Chongqing, after walking about wearing a green leaf on his shirt as part of the 'National Resonance' event. There was no further news about his whereabouts by the time of report on 5 May 2018.

On 29 April 2018, four human rights defenders gathered on streets in urban Shanghai with a banner that read 'commemorate the 50th anniversary of Lin Zhao's death'. Lin Zhao was executed by the government in 1968 for the crime of 'anti-revolution'.

On 21 April 2018, more than 10 petitioners and a human rights defender gathered outside of the Fuzhou International Conference and Exhibition Centre in Gulou District (Fuzhou, Fujian) to petition against the forced demolition of their homes. Protesters held placards that read 'return my home' and 'help us, Chairman Xi'. It was reported that 3 of them were taken by government personnel, and 1 of the arrested protesters was sent to a 'black jail'.

On 9 April 2018, a Shanghai female human rights activist was taken by police from Fuyou Street in Xicheng District (Beijing), sent to a 'black jail' in Fengtai District (Beijing) set up by the Shanghai Municipal Government and lost contact thereafter. She was in Beijing to petition for her forcibly demolished house. She had been harassed and detained several times by authorities in the past.

On 5 April 2018, dozens of members and lawmakers from LSD, Demosisto, and the China Human Rights Lawyers Concern Group marched to the Hong Kong Liaison Office in Wan Chai District (Hong Kong) to demand Beijing to release political prisoners, especially the last missing '709 lawyer'. They used large banners and shouted 'end the one party rule'.

On 16 March 2018, a rights defender was taken to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' by the Beijing police when he was begging around Tiananmen Square in Dongcheng District (Beijing), sent to Relief Administration Service Center of Beijing by the personnel from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government, and went incommunicado after he was sent back to Shanghai on 17 March 2018. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 16 March 2018, a female rights defender was sent to a 'black jail' in the Relief Administration Service Center of Beijing by the plainclothes police officers following her when she was petitioning at the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau in Dongcheng District (Beijing) about the inaction of the Shanghai Police Department, and later the interceptors from Changshou Sub-district sent her back to Shanghai and to the 'back jail' in No. 678 Anyuan Road. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 15 March 2018, four rights defenders, including two women, were intercepted by the Shanghai government personnel at the Shanghai Railway Station in Jing'an District (Shanghai). One of them was then handed over to some unidentified security guards hired by the Gaoqiao Town Government and taken to Changxin Island Guangrong Village 'black jail'. Another rights defender was detained in Changxin Island Guangrong Village 'black jail'. Both were detained until the end of the Lianghui annual sessions. The whereabouts of the two other female rights defenders were not reported.

On 13 March 2018, during the Lianghui conventions, a rights defender were forced to take 'mandatory vacation' in Hainan Island by three police after he was taken from Suixi County (Zhanjiang, Guangdong) and got his phone, as well as ID, confiscated. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 11 March 2018, four rights defenders were taken from their rented flat in Beijing by interceptors from the Shanghai liaison office. Two of them were escorted back to Shanghai and sent to a 'black jail', while the remaining two defenders were taken to a Relief Service Centre 'black jail' in Fengtai District (Beijing), forced returned to Shanghai afterwards, and went incommunicado when they were back in Shanghai. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 11 March 2018, a female human rights activist from Shanghai was picked up by Beijing police from Fuyou street near the Zhongnanhai in Xicheng District (Beijing). She was then detained in two separate 'black jails' until 12 March before being transferred to the underground criminal detention centre in Huayang police station in Changning District, Shanghai, where she was held incommunicado until her release on 12 April 2018.

On 11 March 2018, during the Lianghui conventions, a female rights defender were taken by the local stability maintenance officer when she was attending her cousin's wedding in Sichuan and kept in Xingyuan Hotel, while on 15 March 2018, she was taken to Nanchong Huicheng Mental Hospital and forced to be admitted, but she managed to avoid it. The rights defender was charged 'inciting subversion' because she posted on Twitter.

On 11 March 2018, a human rights defender was taken away by state security forces and held incommunicado in a 'black jail' for 10 days as part of the security crackdown during the annual meetings of the National People's Congress (NPC) and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPC). She resisted authorities' attempts to admit her to a mental hospital in Nanchong City (Sichuan) during these 10 days.

On 9 March 2018, a human rights activist was abducted by a local public security officer in Beijing and has since been missing. The activist was able to send a message saying that the door of the rental house in which she was staying was being broken down before the phone was disconnected. In the past, the activist suffered the illegal demolition of their house and had gone to Beijing while the 'two sessions' was being held to petition against illegal squatters on their land.

On 9 March 2018, a female rights defender was intercepted by Shanghai liaison officers when she was about to petition at the National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration in Xicheng district (Beijing), and went incommunicado after they escorted her back to Shanghai. It was later revealed that she was sent to Qingpu Qingcheng 'black jail' and guarded by 'special security personnel' at least till 18 Mar.

On 8 March 2018, a female rights defender was taken in Beijing and sent to Jiujingzhuang, a 'black jail,' by the Beijing police when she intended to petition to National People's Congress, and on the next day, she was sent to a 'black jail' inside Chongming Houniao resort. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 5 March 2018, a rights defender was intercepted by the interceptors from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government when he was taking the underground in Beijing to petition over the inaction of the government when he didn't get his pension. After that, he was taken back to Shanghai, sent to detention in Shanghai Hongzhi Company in Jing'an District (Shanghai) by the Lujiazui Sub-district office, and taken to a 'black jail' in Jiangxi.

On 5 March 2018, a rights defender was taken at Tiananmen Square in Dongcheng District to Jiujingzhuang, a 'black jail' in Beijing, by the Beijing police after checking his ID, when he was on his way to petition to the representatives of National People's Congress, and he was sent back and detained in Shanghai afterwards. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 5 March 2018, a female rights defender was taken at a bus station in Beijing by the personnel in charge of stopping petitioners from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government to the Relief Administration Service Center of Beijing, and she was detained in a 'black jail' inside the Hensha Island Beach Tianshi Resort after she was taken back to Shanghai by the local town government. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 5 March 2018, two female rights defender were taken from around Zhugangzi Village (Fangshan, Beijing) by the personnel in charge of stopping petitioners from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government. One of them was sent to a 'black jail' in Shanghai while the other went incommunicado after she was taken back to Shanghai. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 3 March 2018, a rights defender from Hubei was taken from his home in Jingshan County (Jingmen, Hubei) and sent on 'mandatory vacation' in Luoyang, Henan by the national security officers from Jingshan County, Hubei. This was part of the stability maintenance measures during the annual Lianghui conventions period.

On 3 March 2018, a human rights activist was preparing to travel to Harbin to aid a friend when they were intercepted by local police in Lutun Town (Yingkou, Liaoning) and taken to a black prison in a hotel where a team of special task forces kept guard. The task force was set up by the Liaoning government to maintain stability around and during the 'two sessions'. The activist and the friend are both members of an anti-corruption and human rights alliance.

On 3 March 2018, a Beijing rights defender was beaten and injured by a police at a hotel in Jiupu Town (Hangzhou, Zhejiang) while he was travelling there. The police and 3 other 'auxiliary police' arrived at the hotel and knocked at the defender's door to carry out an 'inspection' at night. When he requested that they produce a summons, he was beaten up and then handcuffed and taken to Jiupu Police Station for a few hours for getting his footprints and ID checked.

On 3 March 2018, a rights defender was taken in Linxiang County (Yueyang, Hunan) and kept in a 'black jail' behind Linxiang City Chang'an Street Sub-district Office by the personnel from the government, due to convening of the Lianghui Conventions. The rights defender escaped the 'black jail' on 13 March 2018 after being kept for ten days, but he was captured by five unidentified people, sent to the police station, taken away by the personnel from Chang'an Street Nanhua Sub-district office, and returned home on 22 March 2018.

On 3 March 2018, more than a hundred policemen took away 11 individuals, mostly previous petitioners, who were gathering for dinner at a human rights defender's home in Dongchangfu District (Liaocheng, Shandong). Three of the arrested people were detained in 'black jails'/hotels by their home district officials. Four were detained for criminal investigations and one was charged later on.

On 1 March 2018, a rights defender was physically abused by security personnel appointed by the government when they were taking him from Beijing back to Shanghai, after that he was detained in a 'black jail' inside the Chongming Hengsha Island Fishing Resort. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 28 February 2018, a rights defender was physically assaulted in a police car in Beijing by a police officer, and the other two were holding him when he was picked up by four Shanghai Changning District police officers from the police station where he was held after the Beijing police broke into his hotel room and taken him to a police station nearby. He was later sent to the Beijing Taoranting Garden Hotel where Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government is, and on 1 March 2018, he was sent back to Shanghai and the Shanghai Chongming Island Fishing Vacation Center 'black jail'.

On 28 February 2018, a female human rights defender - on a medical visit from Kunshan, Jiangsu - was kidnapped by five unidentifiable persons (likely hired by the government) near the Kaiyangli Post Office in Beijing (Fengtai district) and sent back to her hometown, after which she was held in a 'black jail' until 21 March 2018 when she was released. When she was freed and visited Beijing to report her case, You'anmen police station recorded her witness account but refused to file it, effectively denying her due process.

On 27 February 2018, a rights defender was taken to Nanxiang Mahjong and Chess Room by a group of people hired by the Nanxiang Town Government in front of a residential area in Baoshan District (Shanghai), and later he was detained in a 'black jail'. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 27 February 2018, two rights defenders were taken from their home in Shanghai by the police officers from Jing'an Police Department Baoshan Road Office, and kept in a 'black jail' on the opposite side of the Shanghai Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 26 February 2018, two rights defenders were taken to the Relief Administration Service Center of Beijing by the plain-clothes police officers in charge of stopping petitioners from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government at the Beijing South Railway Station in Fengtai District (Beijing), and on 27 February 2018, they were sent back to Shanghai, one detained in a 'black jail', and the other becoming incommunicado. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders were their targets.

On 26 February 2018, a female rights defender was taken by interceptors from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government at the Supreme People's Court of China in Dongcheng District (Beijing), and later she was detained in a 'black jail' in Shanghai from 27 February 2018. During the Lianghui conventions, the Shanghai Government and the police department had a nationwide stability maintenance operation, and the rights defenders are their targets.

On 4 February 2018, a female human rights activist from Guangdong and two of her family members were forcibly taken away from a hotel in Guangzhou, Guangdong by the police and sent on a 'mandatory vacation' to Huizhou, Guangdong. It was reported that the activist went to the Guangdong Provincial Department of Justice the day before to apply to audit the hearing for the proposed suspension of the license of a human rights lawyer. The activist believed that she was taken away to prevent her from gathering with her friends.

On 27 January 2018, five petitioners from Pingnan County were taken away from the entrance of a hotel at Gulou District (Fuzhou, Fujian) by the police. They were then taken to the nearby Huada Police Station, before local government officials from their county took them away and detained them in a hotel (a 'black jail') in the same district. It was reported that the local officials told the petitioners that they would be detained at the hotel for a few days until the 'two sessions' had concluded.

On 27 January 2018, a human rights lawyer who was responsible for defending the human rights lawyers in the 709 crackdown was transferred from a detention centre in Shijingshan District (Beijing - Shijingshan) and held under 'Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location' in Xuzhou, Jiangsu by the police. He was first taken away by the authorities in Beijing on 19 January and criminally detained. He was later charged with 'inciting subversion of state power'.

On 24 January 2018, a few hundred human rights defenders from all over Shanghai were forced onto a bus by plain clothes police in Pudong, Shanghai. They were then detained in a government-established 'black jail' at Fucun street/Fu Cun Lu in Putuo District (Shanghai). Police detained these petitioners to prevent them from protesting during a municipal meeting which was going to be held in Shanghai.

On 17 January 2018, many people - including high-profile journalists, human rights defenders and citizens - gathered to pay tribute to Former Premier of the PRC Zhao Ziyang at his former residence in Dongcheng district (Beijing) to commemorate his death. People delivered flowers and notes throughout the day, and held a banner saying 'do not forget Zi Yang' at some point. The government had still not allowed for Zhao to be properly buried next to his wife, so his family advocated for that, and called for a redress of Zhao's role in the '89 Democracy Movement. A large number of police forces were deployed at the scene to check people's IDs.

On 1 January 2018, CHRF organized a march from Wan Chai to the East Wing Forecourt of the government headquarters in Admiralty, Central and Western District (Hong Kong) in opposition to last week's formal endorsement by the government of a 'co-location' plan to set up a joint checkpoint at the West Kowloon station, which demonstrators felt would reduce Hong Kong's from Beijing. Towards the end of the demonstration, demonstrators from several groups, including People Power, broke into the East Wing Forecourt and attempted to rush onto the flag platform. They clashed with security personnel of the Government Headquarters, resulting in the injury of two demonstrators and one security personnel. Organisers said 10000 people participated but police put the turnout at 6200.

Property destruction: On 18 March 2022, during a forced demolition operation, over 10 urban law enforcement officers led by a demolition office team destroyed the house of a 'Rose group' human rights activist in Xuzhou city, Jiangsu (coded to Yunlong) without the activist's permission and attendance. The activist and the authorities had yet to settle a compensation agreement.

Property destruction: On 19 March 2022, on the second day of a forced demolition operation, urban law enforcement officers led by a demolition office team destroyed the house of a 'Rose group' human rights activist in Xuzhou city, Jiangsu (coded to Yunlong). The activist called the police for help.

On 21 March 2022, protesters from 12 different environmental groups including Greenpeace, the Conservancy Association, the Hong Kong Dolphin Conservation Society, and the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society held a press conference and demonstrated with banners in Hong Kong. They protested against the Development Bureau's plan to streamline procedures related to land development, which includes limiting who is allowed to submit a rezoning application and not consulting the public on those applications.

On 28 February 2019, a human rights defender from Huanggu District, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province was tricked and kidnapped by personnel from the Shenyang City government in Beijing. He was forcibly sent back to Shenyang City.

On 27 February 2019, two human rights defenders went to discuss matters at the Ministry of Public Security in Beijing and were subsequently sent to a 'black jail' in Qingpu District (Shanghai) and a 'black jail' housed at the the Dongtan Migratory Bird Resort in Chongming District (Shanghai) respectively.

On 27 February 2019, two human rights defenders went to discuss matters at the Ministry of Public Security in Beijing and were subsequently sent to a 'black jail' in Qingpu District (Shanghai) and a 'black jail' housed at the the Dongtan Migratory Bird Resort in Chongming District (Shanghai) respectively.

On 27 February 2019, a human rights defender who had been under 24-hour house arrest in Huishan District (Wuxi, Jiangsu) since 27 Feb 2018 was severely beaten up by officers from the Security Bureau when he tried to leave home to go to the temple. He was bedridden the next day.

On 26 February 2019, a human rights defender from Zhenjiang, Jiangsu was kidnapped by people allegedly from the Zhenjiang Police Department while having lunch near Beijing Normal University in Haidian (Beijing). He was held incommunicado for at least one day, and while being roughly carried away, his head hit the concrete floor heavily. No injuries were reported.

On 25 February 2019, more than 10 parents - from rights group 'Home of Yimiaobaobao' - whose children were victims of defective vaccines staged a protest outside the National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China in Xicheng (Beijing) to raise their concerns with officials attending the National Health Committee meeting. Protesters carried banners and were dispersed by police.

On 24 February 2019, a human rights defender was picked up from his home in Jing'an District and detained in a 'black jail' housed at the the Dongtan Migratory Bird Resort in Chongming District (Shanghai).

On 24 February 2019, a human rights defender from Chenzhou, Hunan was kidnapped by 'stability maintenance agents' from the Chenshou government while he was not far from the Beijing Institute of Technology in Haidian (Beijing).

On 15 February 2019, someone from the Gong County Government sent a human rights defender in Beijing back to Gongxian by plane. The human rights defender was not able to be contacted or located after returning to Gongxian County (Yibin, Sichuan).

On 20 February 2019, a human rights defender was was kidnapped in Shanghai while en route to Beijing to carry out his activism. He was held incommunicado for at least one week. The previous day, police had framed him and detained him for 17 hours.

On 19 February 2019, a human rights defender was beaten up by several security personnel at the Shanghai No.2 Intermediate People's Court in Jinag'an (Shanghai). He was then detained for 17 hours by the police after they framed him for beating up the security personnel.

On 6 May 2022, at night, a large group of residents carrying banners gathered outside the BYD Auto manufacturing factory in Yuhua district (Changsha, Hunan), accusing the company of releasing harmful emissions. They held pictures of children suffering nosebleeds alongside banners, protesting that the factory emitted a strong smell of paint which caused respiratory problems.

On 7 May 2022, a large group of residents carrying banners gathered outside the BYD Auto manufacturing factory in Yuhua district (Changsha, Hunan) for the second demonstration in two days, accusing the company of releasing harmful emissions. They held pictures of children suffering nosebleeds alongside banners, protesting that the factory emitted a strong smell of paint which caused respiratory problems.

On 14 May 2021, a human rights defender residing in Kunshan county (Suzhou, Jiangsu) was abducted for planning an opening ceremony for her tea shop, which was deemed by local police authorities as illegal assembly due to the expected attendance of rights defenders from around the country. It was reported on 13 Jun 2021 that she was being held at a hotel 'black jail' under the custody of the Kunshan State Security Bureau. On 26 October 2021, she was released and able to return home.

Around 12 May 2022 (as reported), a human rights defender and his wife were forced to disappear and became incommunicado in Guilin city, Guangxi (coded to Lingui) after being taken away by the police. They had recently been repatriated from Hebei province by the police a few days ago.

On 10 December 2021, a human rights lawyer went missing in Beijing two hours before attending an event linked to Human Rights Day at the EU representative office. As reported on 16 December 2021, he had become incommunicado since sending messages to his friends saying that he was 'not safe' to attend the event. He was suspected of being detained or forced disappearance. It was reported on 24 May 2022 that the lawyer was initially held by the Beijing and later transferred to the Jilin Yanji Public Security Bureau where his household is registered, remaining incommunicado.

On 11 March 2018, a female human rights activist was transferred out of Yangzhou City Detention Centre, Jiangsu (coded to Guangling) and placed under 'residential surveillance at a designated location' based on the charge of 'inciting subversion of state power.' She was initially arrested on 9 February 2018 while she was visiting her hometown in Yangzhou, and would be released on bail on 2 September 2018. Her arrest was part of the CPC's crackdown on an influential internet group, the 'Rose group', that was used to advocate for human rights. As reported on 24 May 2022, the courts have postponed her trial 6 times and continued to detain her past the most recent trial date of 24 April 2022.
