notes: On 13 May 2022, a female human rights petitioner went to the Yunyang District Government in Yunyang district (Shiyan, Hubei) to make an inquiry and was severely beaten by SWAT police at the gate. The SWAT police broke her leg, dragged her to lie immobile in a car, and then abandoned her on the street hours later.

On 1 June 2022, representatives from ten environmental groups (including Greenpeace, Hong Kong Bird Watching Society and the Conservancy Association) protested and held a press conference in Hong Kong coinciding with a month-long public consultant on 'Enhancing the Procedures of the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Ordinance' launched by the Environmental Protection Department. The group protested the government for 'seeking speed rather than quality' for various development proposals, urging the government to 'optimize' the EIA process based on environmental concerns and not sacrifice the environment for greed. They held a banner to express their demands.

Around 1 June 2022 (as reported), a rights lawyer and his wife were taken on a 'mandatory vacation' by the authorities from Beijing city and held in Pinggu District, Beijing. The move was part of a nationwide coordinated effort by police to silence dissent and prevent any form of public commemoration of the 33rd anniversary of the Tiananmen Square protests on 4 June.

Around 3 June 2022 (as reported), over 10 members of the Guizhou Human Rights Seminar were taken on 'mandatory vacation' by the police in Guizhou province (coded to Guanshanhu) to a rural area in Guiyang ahead of the 33rd anniversary of the Tiananmen Square protests on 4 June. Police said the move was a coordinated effort to silence dissent coinciding with the 'sensitive period' and the 20th congress of the ruling Chinese Communist Party (CCP) later this year.

On 25 August 2018, a human rights activist was placed under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL) by police in Pudong New Area district (Pudong, Shanghai) and held at an unreported location. He was formally arrested on 30 September 2018 and sentenced for 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' on 14 January 2019. He was released on 9 February 2022 upon completing his sentence.

On 26 May 2022, a member of the Guizhou Human Rights Research Seminar was taken on 'mandatory vacation' by the police in Guizhou province (coded to Guanshanhu) and held at a hotel ahead of the 33rd anniversary of the Tiananmen Square protests on 4 June. He returned home safe on 8 June.

Around 15 October 2021 (month of), a Tibetan language rights activist was arrested from Shiqu county (Ganzi, Sichuan) for an unknown reason by provincial authorities. As reported on 16 June 2022, the activist is still being held incommunicado in an undisclosed location. On 13 June 2022, he was formally sentenced for 'inciting separatism' and 'picking quarrels and provoking troubles' for four years and five months at an unknown prison.

Around 4 April 2020 (between 1 April - 8 April), an academic scholar and lawyer - also founder of the New Citizens' Movement and Open Constitution Initiative, and human rights defender - was subjected for eight days to sleep deprivation, limited food and water, and sitting in a tiger chair after being taken away on 15 February from Panyu district, Guangzhou city (Guangdong) by police officers who searched his friend's home in the name of a 'coronavirus check.'

On 3 June 2022, a rights activist was detained and held incommunicado by police in Hebei district, Tianjin City, a day before the 33rd anniversary of the Tiananmen Square protests on 4 June. Police installed security cameras near his home on 28 May 2022. As reported on 25 June 2022, he was detained at the Hebei District Detention Center in Tianjin but remains uncontactable. He was previously arrested in 2019 for 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' by posting comments critical of the government.

On 18 May 2020, unidentified people placed a female rights activist in incommunicado detention in an unknown place in Beijing. Since 2018, she has pushed the government for adequate compensation and vaccine laws after a vaccine paralyzed her daughter.

On 21 July 2022, government officials of the Suzhou government office in Beijing intercepted a female human rights defender from Suzhou when she was boarding a train in Beijing - Fengtai. She has since become uncontactable as reported on 22 July.

On 2 August 2022, unidentified men hired by the Fuzhou government rammed two cars into two human rights defenders from Fuzhou, one of them a woman and another a 91-year-old man, when they were travelling in Tianjin city (coded to Tianjin) with three other friends. Hit by the car, the elderly man fell to the ground. The two victims were then brought into the car by the attackers. The day after, the woman was found lying on the side of a road in Fuzhou, and the elderly man's whereabouts remain unknown.

On 29 June 2022, a human rights activist, who previously displayed placards regarding coronavirus vaccines at the village committee, was taken away by stability maintenance personnel in his hometown of Qidong county (Hengyang, Hunan) and held incommunicado for 3 days. On 1 July 2022, he was taken to the police station of his hometown for detention on charges of picking quarrels and provoking trouble.

Around 3 August 2022 (week of), the police placed a woman human rights defender from Fuzhou in incommunicado detention, after she was sent to a hospital in Jin'an district (Fuzhou, Fujian) by her ex-husband, who found her on a roadside after she was abducted by unidentified men hired by the Fuzhou government. On 2 August 2022, unidentified men rammed two cars into her and her 91-year-old companion, when they were travelling in Tianjin. The day after, the woman was found lying on the side of a road in Fuzhou, and the elderly man's whereabouts remain unknown.

On 3 June 2018, 2 human rights defenders were held incommunicado and placed under house arrest in a hotel by the Liwan District (Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province) police. They were transferred to Guangzhou Liwan Detention House around 15 June. It was reported that their arrests were due to the stability maintenance before the anniversary of the Tiananmen demonstrations on 4 June 1989.

On 25 October 2019, a woman human rights defender was taken by the police at the Liwan District Court (Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province) after she quarrelled with the security personnel while entering the court. She was held incommunicado for a week after getting into a physical confrontation with the police during security check before attending a trial. She was later confirmed to be arrested and would be probably charged later because she had bitten one of the policemen while she was taken.

On 9 September 2022, stability maintenance officers abducted a female human rights defender in a mountain in Beijing and detained her in a hotel in Shiyan, Hubei. She had been staying in the mountain for seven days to hide from people who raided her apartment on the police's orders. Over the years she fought for her rights because the local government refused to enforce the court's judgment in favour of her land dispute.

On 24 September 2022, local police placed a human rights defender under incommunicado detention in a hotel after taking him away in Hunan (coded to Yuelu, Changsha). Two days after, he was transferred to a police station, where he would be administratively detained for 15 days. Right before his two-day disappearance, he tweeted about the sudden death of a Chinese man in prison, and how police forced his family to cremate him as soon as possible. The man's daughter had been forcibly admitted to a psychiatric ward three times after she splashed ink on a public portrait of President Xi Jinping in July 2018.

On 2 October 2022, interception officers from Shandong detained a human rights defender from Shandong in a vehicle in Beijing (coded to Beijing), leaving the victim became incommunicado. He was traveling to Beijing to petition for his rights. The measure was part of the central government's campaign to stifle dissent before the 20th National Congress of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 16 October 2022.

Around 15 March 2022 (month of), Fuzhou police tortured a female human rights petitioner from Fuzhou in a 'black jail' in Fuzhou, Fujian (coded to Gulou), where she was detained because she went to Beijing to petition for her rights in a land dispute with the local government. She escaped afterwards. The footage of her escape went viral on the Internet, leading to her arrest for ''picking quarrels and provoking trouble'.

On 25 September 2022, local police took away a human rights defender from Shenyang city in Yanjiao town (Langfang, Hebei), which is near Beijing, where many human rights defenders file petitions against their local government. Upon arriving in Shenyang, he was taken to a hostel and later detained in mental health hospital on 30 September 2022. The measures were part of local officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the 20th National Congress of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 16 October 2022.

On 23 January 2020, a female rights defender-cum-petitioner was abducted by 6-7 men onto a vehicle at Fuzhou South Railway Station Square in Cangshan district (Fuzhou, Fujian) when she was traveling to Beijing to submit a petition. After two months, her family learned that she was admitted to a psychiatric hospital, but they were forbidden to visit her.

On 27 June 2018, a Shanghai female human rights defender, who was also a petitioner-cum-forced evictee, was attacked by a Public Security Bureau police officer in front of the Shanghai Municipal Public Security Bureau in Jing'an district (Jingan, Shanghai), causing her to suffer from rib fractures.

Other: On 12 February 2019, some ethnic Uyghurs launched a global social media campaign under the hashtag #MeTooUyghur to press China for video proof that their missing relatives are alive, after China released a video of a Uyghur man saying he was alive and well (Location coded as Beijing).

On 28 August 2019, an anti-ELAB #MeToo sit-in protest was held in Chater Garden in Central (Hong Kong - Central and Western) to protest sex white terror brought by alleged police misconduct during a strip-search of a female arrestee. Organiser said over 30,000 people attended the gathering while the police put the number at 11,500. The woman involved in the incident appeared on stage to address the crowd.

On 2 November 2021, a high-ranked female tennis player Peng Shuai, who was a doubles champion at Wimbledon and the French Open, went missing and became incommunicado in Beijing municipality after she accused former vice-premier Zhang Gaoli of pressuring her into a sexual relationship in a social media post. It was the first time that the #MeToo movement had reached the highest echelons of the ruling CCP. The tennis players' disappearance raised international concerns about her personal safety and whereabouts.

On 14 September 2021, supporters of a former CCTV intern who filed a sexual harassment case against her boss carrying placards stood behind the victim outside Haidian District People's Court in Haidian district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Haidian) to protest against sexual harassment. The court had ruled against the complainant in the landmark #MeToo sexual harassment case, saying there was insufficient evidence to support the victim's claims against state broadcaster CCTV anchor.

On 10 August 2022, people gathered outside the court in Beijing - Shijingshan to display placards and flowers in support of Zhou Xiaoxuan, a plaintiff in a #MeToo trial, where she accused a high-profile TV presenter of sexual assault back in 2014. The court rejected her claims, saying there was no sufficient evidence.

On 15 October 2022, police detained a human rights activist in a hostel, right after he was released from prison in Shayang county (Jingmen, Hubei). The detention was part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the 20th National Congress of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 16 October 2022. The activist had been in jail for 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' since 2021.

actor2: Police Forces of China (2017-) Hong Kong Police Force
notes: On 24 March 2022, 5 Ukraine nationals carrying Ukraine flag gathered in Hong Kong - Central and Western to protest in opposition to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Two protesters were arrested for failing to present their identity documents. The other three protesters were issued a penalty notice as they violated a prohibited group gathering amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

On 1 March 2022, restaurant workers and members of the Ukrainian community holding 'stop the war' posters gathered at a Ukrainian restaurant in Hong Kong - Central and Western in protest against the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

On 2 December 2020, around 100 supporters and women's rights activists protested at the Beijing Haidian People's Court in Haidian district (Beijing) (coded as Beijing - Haidian) in solidarity with a female sexual assault victim, who had filed charges against a state television anchor for sexual harassment. They held up placards and banners with slogans. Public security dispersed the protesters, and took foreign correspondents in for questioning. This sexual harassment incident has generated momentum for the #MeToo movement in China.

On 9 November 2022, police and quarantine officers quarantined a former human rights lawyer in a hotel for 7 days, even though he was tested negative for coronavirus or was not a close contact, after intercepting him in a railway station in Hanbin district (Ankang, Shaanxi). They also forced him to shoulder the costs of the quarantine. The lawyer had lost his license in 2018, having represented clients in human rights cases.

Around 26 June 2021, the AMCB - and many foreign domestic workers organisations - held a press conference and demonstrated in Hong Kong against the government's coronavirus lockdown advice, which had resulted in several issues including workers being denied of legally entitled rest days, enduring food shortages, and physical and sexual abuse. They held up placards to express their demands.

On 21 October 2021, Hong Kong Federation of Trade Unions representatives carrying placards and banners protested at Government Complex in Central district (Hong Kong) (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to demand resumption of full-day in-person class arrangements, although schools did not reach the required 70 percent threshold of vaccinated students and teachers against coronavirus. They argued that students learn better at full-day classes while parents spend less on child care.

On 16 October 2021, representatives of the Third Side and travel industry protested and submitted petitions to the Office of the Chief Executive in Admiralty, Western district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They demanded the resumption of customs clearance for vaccinated travelers commuting between Hong Kong and the Mainland to accelerate the recovery of the tourism sector after the coronavirus outbreak. Members of the Hong Kong Travel Agent Owners Association and Hong Kong Tourism Association joined the protest.

On 27 October 2021, a coalition of various tourism industry associations protested at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western), demanding a restoration of cross-border travel with the mainland and Macau as a way to boost tourism. The city's borders largely closed to pursue a zero-coronavirus strategy.

On 15 November 2021, 6 DAB legislative councilors held a press conference and demonstrated in Hong Kong, demanding the government block loopholes in coronavirus pandemic prevention and reopen the city's land border with mainland China as soon as possible. They held placards to express their demands.

On 26 November 2021, a few DAB members protested and submitted petitions at the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western), calling for reopening the border with mainland China as the border is currently closed due to coronavirus restrictions. They demonstrated over 20 placards on the ground to express their demands.

On 22 November 2021, representatives from 'Hong Kong Non-franchised Buses Association,' Hong Kong Tourism Association, and a private bus company protested and submitted petitions at the Government Headquarters in Central district, Hong Kong (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They called for reopening the border with mainland China this year as the border is currently closed due to coronavirus restrictions. They also demanded an extension of the Pre-approved Principal Payment Holiday Scheme to support the enterprises to face cash-flow pressure.

On 22 November 2021, HKFTU representatives and parents held a press conference and demonstrated in Hong Kong, calling for reopening the border with mainland China as the border is currently closed due to coronavirus restrictions. They demanded the prioritization of travel quota to four groups of travelers, including medical professionals, cross-boundary families, cross-boundary workers, and cross-boundary students. They carried placards to express their demands

On 12 December 2021, over 50 people in cross-border families accompanied by Society for Community Organization representatives held a press conference and demonstrated in Hong Kong for the government to reopen cross-border travels so that they could be reunited with family members in mainland China. The Hong Kong-mainland China border had been closed for two years amid the coronavirus pandemic. They held up placards to express their demands.

On 17 December 2021, HKFTU representatives demonstrated and held a press conference in Hong Kong, calling for reopening the border with mainland China as the border is currently closed due to coronavirus restrictions. They demanded that over half of the travel quota would be assigned for four groups of travelers, including medical professionals, cross-boundary families, cross-boundary workers, and cross-boundary students. They carried placards to express their demands

On 17 January 2022, a large group of migrant workers from other cities demonstrated and clashed with police in Dasi township (Xiqing, Tianjin) in opposition to a strict lockdown after Omicron (a new variant of coronavirus) was found, with people complaining of difficulties finding food. Many riot police officers were deployed to the scene and arrested a man who led the demonstration.

On 20 January 2022, residents demonstrated and clashed with police officers in Sungang Residential District of Luohu District (Shenzhen, Guangdong) in opposition to a strict coronavirus lockdown. Police arrested a few demonstrators.

On 9 February 2022, HKFTU lawmaker and the Hair And Make-Up Stylish Image Designers General Union (associated with HKFTU) members protested outside the Government Headquarters in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They opposed the latest coronavirus restrictions, which required salons to close from 10 February until at least 24 February, when a 'vaccine pass' will be rolled out that permits only vaccinated people to visit venues such as shopping malls and salons. They worried workers would suffer severe financial strain because of closures.

On 15 February 2022, members of the League of Social Democrats protested outside the Government Headquarters in Admiralty, Hong Kong - Central and Western against the government's 'dynamic zero Covid' approach to curbing the spread of coronavirus, claiming that achieving zero infections was not practical. They criticized that the government's relief measures were 'saving the market instead of saving the people.'
On 21 March 2022, residents chanted 'release lockdown' in Shenzhen city (Guangdong) to protest against the coronavirus lockdown, which the government sought to halt a growing coronavirus outbreak.

On 30 March 2022, in the evening, residents rallied in Pudong New Area (Pudong, Shanghai) to protest the difficulty of obtaining food and increased food prices amid coronavirus lockdown. The government had implemented stay-at-home orders in the district since 28 March 2022. The police arrested at least one person who called for the rally.

On 29 March 2022, residents gathered in Pudong New Area (Pudong, Shanghai) to protest the difficulty of obtaining food and increased food prices amid the coronavirus lockdown. The government had implemented stay-at-home orders in the district since 28 March 2022.

Around 28 March 2022 (as reported), dozens of residents protested at the entrance of their residential compound, shouting at the police in Minhang district (Minhang, Shanghai) to protest the difficulty of obtaining food and household items amid localized coronavirus lockdown. Some of the protesters said they held been in isolation for 26 days.
On 14 April 2022, residents demonstrated on the streets in Xin county (Xinyang, Henan) to protest the lack of food supplies amid the coronavirus lockdown.

On 11 April 2022, during coronavirus lockdown, residents protested at their residential compound in Minhang district (Minhang, Shanghai) because they were frustrated being confined to their homes and struggling to get government food supplies. People were knocking on cooking pots and chanting, 'hand out the supplies.'

On 8 April 2022, late at night, residents confronted security guards at the entrance to a residential compound in the Jiuting area in Songjiang district (Songjiang, Shanghai), demanding daily supplies amid coronavirus lockdown. People shouted, 'I'm starving to death!', 'hand out the supplies' to the epidemic prevention staff guarding the confined residential area.

On 8 May 2022, faculty and students at Beijing International Studies University protested at their campus in Beijing - Chaoyang against the university's arbitrary decision to erect an isolation fence as part of coronavirus restrictions. Protesters dispersed peacefully under the police's order.

On 15 May 2022, hundreds of students at Peking University gathered and shouted slogans at Wanliu campus in Beijing - Haidian (Beijing) against the university's attempt to set up an isolation fence as part of coronavirus restrictions. During the demonstration, some students attempted to remove the installed fence, but no other destructive behaviour occurred. Students heckled school administrators as they ordered the students to leave. The demonstration ended peacefully when the school eased its measures and agreed to remove the fence.

On 24 May 2022, several hundred Beijing Normal University students marched on campus in Beijing - Haidian (Beijing) shouting slogans and playing the school song on their phones to protest against the school's coronavirus prevention policies. Demonstrators called for exams to be postponed or moved online and for the right to return to their hometowns.

On 23 May 2022, students at China University of Political Science and Law gathered on campus in Beijing - Haidian (Beijing) to flash their cellphone lights and play the song 'Do You Hear the People Sing?' to protest against the school's coronavirus prevention policies. Demonstrators called for exams to be postponed or moved online and for the right to return to their hometowns.

On 26 May 2022, a large number of Tianjin University students rallied at Beiyang Garden on campus in Nankai district, Tianjin shouting slogans and playing the school song on their phone to protest against the school's coronavirus prevention policies. Demonstrators called upon school administrators to clarify on final exam protocol and time frames.

On 1 June 2022, between 2,000 to 3,000 residents gathered at Baimiao Inspection Checkpoint in Yanjiao township (Langfang, Hebei), demonstrating against strict coronavirus restrictions that made people difficult to make the daily commute into the capital. They chanted 'we need to commute; we need to eat,' demanding to be allowed back to work in Beijing. The demonstrators were suppressed by the police, during which there were violent clashes between the police and the demonstrators.

On 21 May 2022, from the evening until the next morning, over 100 workers rioted over coronavirus restrictions in a Taiwanese-owned Apple supplier industrial compound in Songjiang district (Songjiang, Shanghai). Rioters chanted, threw rocks at their Taiwanese managers' dormitory windows, and demonstrated against being confined and working overtime in the factory during coronavirus lockdown. The riot came after some employees were diagnosed with coronavirus because of inadequate pandemic prevention measures in the compound. Some police attended to the scene but no arrest were made.
On 14 June 2022, locals displayed banners and shouted slogans throughout Dandong city, Liaoning (coded to Zhenxing) to protest against strict coronavirus prevention policies.

On 18 June 2022, a large number of people protested in Kunshan city (Suzhou, Jiangsu) to call for the resumption of commuting between Kunshan and Shanghai and easing the coronavirus restrictions. Police on site took many people away. Following the protest, authorities eased its measures and allowed commuting to reopen.

On 5 July 2022, a large group of students and staff from Beijing Institute of Technology gathered on campus in Beijing - Haidian district to protest against the school for implementing stricter coronavirus prevention policies which demonstrators believed to be unreasonable. Police were on site to monitor the situation.

On 3 September 2022, residents chanted slogans in multiple residential areas in Huangpi district (Wuhan, Hebei) to demand that the government stop coronavirus lockdowns, which had already lasted for ten days. Some residents kicked the barriers blocking their doors to protest in the streets. A lot of police were present at the scene.

On 2 September 2022, residents chanted slogans in Huangpi district (Wuhan, Hubei) to demand that the government stop coronavirus lockdowns, which had already lasted for nine days. 20 to 30 police cars were present at the scene.

On 15 August 2022, a group of Guangxi residents protested against coronavirus lockdowns in Yinhai district (Beihai, Guangxi). They were dissatisfied that the government has not opened up the city even though they promised they would.

On 27 June 2022, a few hundred people gathered in Shapingba district (Shapingba, Chongqing) to protest against the local government's coronavirus restrictions. They were dissatisfied that they were not allowed to be out even though they were tested negative. The local government subsequently eased its measures.

On 10 August 2022, local residents chanted slogans and attempted to push through the localized lockdown iron barriers in Futian district (Shenzhen, Guangdong), in protest against coronavirus lockdowns in their district.

On 19 September 2022, a few hundred students marched towards the gate from their dorms and chanted the national anthem on their university campus in Jiangxia district (Wuhan, Hubei) to protest against the school's coronavirus lockdown policy because it could not provide them with electricity.

On 26 September 2022, up to a thousand residents chanted slogans and hurled water bottles at the police in Shawei Village in Futian district (Shenzhen, Guangdong), demanding that the government lifts local coronavirus lockdowns. Several hundred police formed human chains to block the protesters from barging out of the barricades of the neighborhood. Some police officers beat up and arrested protesters. The neighborhood had been locked down 5 times before, and residents, mostly from the working class, had difficulties making a living due to lockdowns.

Around 26 September 2022 (as reported), shopowners chanted slogans in a mall in Futian district (Shenzhen, Guangdong), demanding that the government lifts local coronavirus lockdowns. Police were on the scene. The area around the mall has been locked down many times, causing shops in the mall, once a hub for electronics in Asia, to incur losses.

On 26 September 2022, residents chanted slogans in Xinzhou village in Futian district (Shenzhen, Guangdong), demanding that the government lifts local coronavirus lockdowns. Lockdowns in the neighborhood have caused difficulties to residents, mostly from the working class, in making a living.

On 28 September 2022, students of multiple universities gathered and chanted slogans on their respective campuses in Zhengzhou, Henan (coded to Zhongyuan), demanding that campus coronavirus lockdowns be lifted. Police arrested students on some campuses, with online sources saying that students who led the protests were detained on the grounds of 'foreign infiltration.' Some institutions warned their students not to initiate any protests, while some stopped implementing lockdown measures.

On 4 October 2022, police beat up and arrested protesters, who gathered, chanted slogans and sang the national anthem at the airport in Gasa town (Xishuangbanna, Yunnan). They are tourists in protest against the local government's sudden coronavirus lockdowns, which had caused some of them to be forcibly taken to quarantine and others to be stranded in the airport. Police officers dressed in white protective gear and armed with guns were present, causing the protesters to panic. As the protest continued into the night, numerous police officers were sent to surround the protesters and arrest them.

On 6 October 2022, a few hundred tourists marched to the government office in Yongding district (Zhangjiajie, Hunan) to protest against its sudden coronavirus lockdowns. They were dissatisfied that they were mandated to quarantine for two weeks without prior notice and that some of them had their ID cards confiscated by health officials.

On 11 October 2022, four representatives of the League of Social Democrats held banners and chanted slogans outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western, demanding that the government repeal all coronavirus quarantine and social-gathering restrictions. The police fined them for obstructing the streets.

Around 26 October 2022 (as reported), hundreds of local residents gathered in Chengguan district (Lhasa, Tibet) to protest coronavirus restrictions. Most of the protesters were Han Chinese migrant workers, who could not make a living nor return home due to the coronavirus lockdown in Lhasa, which have been imposed for 80 days. The last recorded large-scale protest in the city was in 2008, when Tibetans protested against how the government treated and prosecuted them.

Around 26 October 2022 (as reported), local residents gathered in multiple districts (except from Chengguan district) in Lhasa, Tibet (coded to Lhasa, Chengguan) to protest coronavirus restrictions. Protesters were seen in online footages blocking streets, chanting slogans, pushing away iron gates, and engaging in verbal and physical scuffles with the police. Most of the protesters were Han Chinese migrant workers, who could not make a living nor return home due to the coronavirus lockdown in Lhasa, which have been imposed for 80 days. The last recorded large-scale protest in the city was in 2008, when Tibetans protested against how the government treated and prosecuted them.

On 14 November 2022, hundreds of residents gathered to demonstrate against coronavirus restrictions in multiple villages in Haizhu district (Guangzhou, Guangdong). Demonstrators chanted slogans, threw objects at officials in hazmat suits, pushed through quarantine cordons and barriers, and attempted to overturn a police car. Police officers used water cannons to disperse the crowds and arrested some residents. Many of the residents were originally from Hubei, and they felt that the stringent coronavirus restrictions against them were discriminatory.

On 16 November 2022, university students gathered and chanted their demands on their campus in Zhongyuan district (Zhengzhou, Henan). The students were dissatisfied with the school's month long coronavirus lockdown policy, without regard to their needs to get food or see their families.

On 22 November 2022, at least a few hundred factory workers demonstrated overnight against local coronavirus restrictions in their plant in Xinzheng (Zhengzhou, Henan). Some workers smashed up the front gate of the plant, windows, CCTV cameras and coronavirus testing booths; while some overturned a police vehicle. The police, including the People's Armed Police, dispersed the crowds with tear gas and water cannons. Health officials in hazmat suits beat up workers who were trying to escape the plant. Meanwhile, the workers threw stones and sprayed fire extinguishers at the police. There were injuries on both sides. Around 40 people were arrested. In compliance with local coronavirus rules, the factory had been keeping workers on-site, where they were subject to poor living conditions and social distancing measures, leaving them feeling misrepresented by their employment contracts.

On 26 November 2022, students gathered and held white papers to oppose censorship in China at Communication University of China in Jiangning district (Nanjing, Jiangsu). Police arrested around 60 students afterwards. The demonstration came in the wake of a residential fire in Urumqi, Xinjiang that killed 10 on 24 November 2022, as the Chinese public attributed the deaths to local coronavirus lockdowns, which had made evacuation difficult. The incident was later censored by the Chinese government.

On 5 December 2022, students gathered, chanted slogans and argued with university representatives at Nanjing Tech University in Gulou (Nanjing, Jiangsu) to demonstrate against coronavirus lockdowns on campus, even though only one coronavirus case was identified. The demonstration came in the wake of a residential fire in Urumqi, Xinjiang that killed 10 on 24 November 2022, as the Chinese public attributed the deaths to local lockdowns, which had made evacuation difficult. The incident was later censored by the Chinese government.

On 4 December 2022, around 1,000 students gathered and chanted slogans at Wuhan University in Wuchang district (Wuhan, Hubei) to demonstrate against poor living conditions during coronavirus lockdowns on campus.

Around 3 December 2022, residents gathered, chanted slogans and tore down barriers meant to quarantine them by hitting them with a car in a residential estate in Liangxi district (Wuxi, Jiangsu). They demanded that the local government lifts local coronavirus lockdowns.

On 11 March 2020, a large number of residents in Gangdu Park, Qingshan District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province) met with the management committee to oppose the use of garbage trucks for the transportion and distribution of meat to residents in the area. It was reported that scuffles broke out between the two parties. Due to the coronavirus outbreak, food for residents in Wuhan City had been purchased and distributed by the authorities.

On 12 March 2020, more than 1,000 residents demonstrated in Yingcheng City (Wuhan City, Hubei Province) against overpriced and poor quality food, which they had been forced to pay for following the coronavirus lockdown of the city. They surrounded police cars, and demanded for the release of a volunteer who had been arrested earlier for using his personal connections to purchase groceries at lower prices. They also shouted slogans, calling for the secretary of the community to step down.

On 17 March 2020, 377 workers demonstrated at a quarantine centre in Hongshan District (Wuhan City, Hubei Province), and demanded the government to either allow them to return to their hometowns to continue working and confirm exactly when they can return, or to continue subsidies to support them outside of the quarantine period. This was reported that these workers had completed their mandatory 14-day quarantine period following the completion of the two field hospitals in Wuhan in response to the coronavirus outbreak, but were not allowed to leave Wuhan.

On 30 April 2020, more than 10 members of the League of Social Democrats demonstrated outside the police headquarters in Hong Kong - Wan Chai, condemning the Hong Kong police for the use of 'epidemic prevention' as a pretext to prohibit the May Day march. They also criticised the police for curbing freedom of expression and 'trampling on the dignity of workers'. The chairperson of the LSD got into an altercation with the police, after the police asked the group to disperse on the grounds that they were violating the coronavirus restriction order. All of the demonstrators were issued a fixed penalty fine by the police.

On 2 July 2020, at least 6 members of the Performance Industry Association held a press conference in Hong Kong, urging the government to reopen performance venues such that the industry can return to work following the coronavirus pandemic. They stated that the number of performances had decreased to close to zero since February 2020, and urged the government to implement arrangements to waive rents as soon as possible and provide assistance fund to the industry. They held placards during the press conference.

On 29 July 2020, at least nine Democratic Party members, LegCo members and labour representatives held a press conference in Hong Kong to protest against coronavirus prevention measures and speak about challenges facing their respective industries (such as F&B, hospitality, entertainment venues and airports). They held up placards, urging the government for another round of financial aid eligible to all citizens and businesses amidst third wave of community outbreak.

On 19 August 2020, at least 10 people - citizen group Community Development Initiative, LegCo members, district councillors and medical workers - held a press conference in Hong Kong to express doubts about the government's coronavirus relief measures, including the effectiveness of comprehensive citywide testing and other potential privacy infringements. On 4 February 2023, seven people, including a journalist, held banners and marched in Hong Kong - Kwun Tong to demand that the government shuts down an illegally run concrete plant in their neighborhood, which they say has polluted the environment and disrupted daily life.

Around 4 February 2023 (as reported), up to a thousand residents chanted slogans and tried to go into the office of the economic development zone management committee in Jiangxia district (Wuhan, Hubei), in protest of the committee's to build a rubbish processing plant nearby, citing environmental concerns and disruptions to daily life. Private security officers and police officers pressed a demonstrator to the ground and wrapped their hands around his neck, before taking him away. Police also arrested around 20 people.

Around 13 September 2022 (as reported), more than 600 residents, mostly Uyghur, gathered and marched in the streets in a village in Yining City (Ili, Xinjiang) to demonstrate against local coronavirus lockdowns, as some of them were deprived of medical care and food. As a result, more than 600 Uighurs were detained.

On 27 November 2020, four police officers beat up a female human rights defender with disabilities, causing her right-hand finger to fracture, when she was in prison in Baiyun district (Guangzhou, Guangdong).

On 24 June 2021, police officers beat up a female human rights defender with disabilities, causing her to suffer from a coma, when she was in prison in Baiyun district (Guangzhou, Guangdong). They continued to hit her head against the wall and kick her in the legs when she was suffering from the coma.
On 3 August 2021, police officers beat up a female human rights defender with disabilities, causing her back to fracture, when she was in prison in Baiyun district (Guangzhou, Guangdong).
On 24 February 2023, six people chanted slogans in Hong Kong - Yau Tsim Mong to demand that Russia stops its invasion of Ukraine.

On 1 March 2023, a human rights lawyer became incommunicado, after he was stopped by police officers in a railway station in Nankang District (Ganzhou, Jiangxi), where he planned to board a train to Zhuhai for personal travel. The lawyer had represented Ai Wei Wei before. The measure was part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 4 March 2023.

On 16 June 2021, an elderly rights defender was beaten up by triad members at his rental accommodation in Beijing municipality while a police officer looked on without intervening. The measures were part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 4 March 2023.

They were held for over 30 hours in the basement of Meicun Police Station without any of their belongings, five of whom were held in 'unofficial criminal detention with no legal paperwork' for 30 more days.

On 26 March 2023, around 80 property owners held banners and marched to a public square in Hong Kong - Sai Kung to protest against land reclamation plans for District 132, citing disruptions to their neighborhood and environmental concerns. As a condition for the authorization, participants were capped at 100 and had to wear number tags around their necks, and police were to examine banners and placards for 'politically sensitive and seditious words' prior to the protests.

Around 20 February 2023 (as reported), a man became incommunicado after being taken presumably from his home in Jinan city, Shandong (coded to Lixia). The forced disappearance was part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions of the CCP in Beijing, scheduled to start on 4 March 2023.

On 26 February 2023, around ten triad members detained a Fuzhou-based petitioner in a hotel in Fuzhou for 17 days, after taking him away in Tongzhou district (Tongzhou, Beijing). He travelled to Beijing to get medical advice for his ill wife.

On 5 April 2023, ten government-hired triad members beat up a Changzhou-based petitioner and her mother when they were seeking medical help at Peking University First Hospital in Beijing - Xicheng. The attackers then detained them in a black car for 10 hours, and did not allow them access to the toilet or food, before escorting back to Changzhou.

On 19 February 2023, a man became incommunicado after police took him away for 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' in Wuhan city, Hubei (coded to Jiang'an). He had been one of the hundreds of retired persons who protested against the government lowering the amount of monthly medical benefits in Wuhan on 15 February 2023 (separately coded). The protest resulted in at least five demonstrators being arrested in the days that followed.

On 14 April 2023, six construction workers demonstrated in Hong Kong - Wan Chai to demand wage arrears. One of them sat on the edge of the fence on the rooftop to demonstrate, whilst others gathered on their scaffolding and held a banner.

On 17 December 2018, 4 women family members of human rights lawyers detained as part of the '709 crackdown' shaved their heads in protest of the lack of rule of law in the handling of these cases. While shaving their heads, the women and journalists were harassed and dispersed by police. After that, the women petitioned at the Supreme People's Court in Dongcheng District (Beijing - Dongcheng), but were prevented from doing so by over a hundred people who gathered there to intercept them.

On 24 December 2020, a female petitioner-cum-forced evictee from Qingyang district, Chengdu was beaten in the head and waist by unknown individuals on the N90E92 night train from Beijing to her hometown. She had visited the capital to inquire about her past interceptions and detentions at various police stations. After her visit to the Fuyoujie Police Station in Xicheng district (Beijing), she was transferred her to a 'relief centre' (for petitioners), after which she was escorted to the night train by government officials from Qingyang and government-hired triad members. She was held at a farmhouse in Chaoyang Lake, Pujiang county on 25 Dec, then transferred to Dekang Psychiatric Hospital in Chengdu on 20 Jan 2021.

On 20 April 2023, a journalist became incommunicado, presumably after being taken away from his home in Wuhan, Hubei (coded to Jiang'an). He was known for his investigative pieces on corruptive acts of local government officials.

On 21 April 2023, subdivided flat tenants and concern groups held placards and banners outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western to demand that the government enacts laws to regulate subdivided unit rent levels and restrict landlords' abilities to overcharge for utilities.

On 18 April 2023, members of the Hong Kong Federation of Trade Unions, including two lawmakers, held placards and banners outside the legislative council in Hong Kong - Central and Western to demand that the government increases the penalty that employers have to pay for neglecting their employees' safety.

On 10 April 2023, around 400 to 500 property owners and residents held placards, chanted slogans and marched from the local office of the Public Complaints and Proposals Administration to a park in Futian district (Shenzhen, Guangdong). They were dissatisfied that the school places allocation system was unfairly skewed in favour of the districts where government officials lived, in prejudice against their district. When the demonstrators arrived at Futian district, police surrounded the demonstrators and escorted them back to the petitions office.

On 18 April 2023, unidentified persons hired by the QIanjiang government beat up two QIanjiang-based female petitioners in Beijing - Fengtai, before taking them back to Qianjiang. One of the female petitioners was slapped in the mouth and attacked in the shoulder, and had to be hospitalised the day after. The petitioners had gone to Beijing with plans to file petitions against their local government.

On 21 April 2023, delivery workers gathered and went on a strike in Shanwei, Guangdong (coded to Chengqu). They were dissatisfied that the delivery platform that they worked at did not give them sufficient salary and subsidies.

On 28 April 2023, representatives of the Association for the Rights of Industrial Accident Victims held a banner and gave a petitioner letter to an official outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western to demand that the government designates 28 April as Workers' Memorial Day and sets up a monument to commemorate those who had died from industrial accidents.

On 23 August 2022, a few hundred investors gathered and chanted slogans outside a company building in Yangpu district, Shanghai to demand that the company pay back the interests it owed to them. The police forcibly dragged some of them into a bus. While doing so, minor scuffles between both sides occurred, causing some to be injured.

On 14 August 2022, a large group of tourists gathered and chanted slogans like 'I need to go home' and 'let us talk to the manager' at the doorway of a hotel in Jiyang district (Sanya, Hainan). They were dissatisfied about being stranded in Sanya due to its sudden coronavirus lockdown.

Around 7 July 2022 (as reported), 4 local police officers tortured a female Falun Gong practitioner by raping her, poking her nipples with a tool and shoving a lit cigarette into her nose when she was placed in incommunicado detention in an unknown location in Jilin city (coded to Chuanying, Jilin). Before being sent there, she was taken from her family on 12 June 2022, and was detained in room 102 at Shui Bu Hotel in Longtan district for a month. The police were trying to get a hard drive password from her.

On 10 September 2022, up to a thousand residents gathered and protested outside their residential blocks in Nanming district (Guiyang, Guizhou) to protest against coronavirus lockdowns, which had lasted for more than 10 days. 400 police officers were sent to the scene to maintain order. The management office of the property withheld fresh food and mooncakes from residents, instead selling them at a high price.

On 16 March 2021, police beat up a Falun Gong practitioner and pushed him off the window, causing his death, after they found Falun Gong materials when raiding his home in Yanji city (Yanbian, Jilin).

On 6 November 2019, two prisoners, on the orders of a correctional officer, beat a female Falun Gong practitioner to death in a prison in Xiangfang district, Haerbin, Heilongjiang. During the attack, the officer put his foot on her face to keep her in place. She had been sentenced to jail for four years in 2017, and three years in 2014, for practicing Falun Gong.

On 27 September 2022, residents gathered and protested in their neighborhood in Longgang district (Shenzhen, Guangdong), demanding that the government lifts local coronavirus lockdowns. The neighborhood had been locked down for a few days and the residents had trouble getting sufficient food.

On 6 September 2022, Gansu police detained a female petitioner from Gansu in a hostel in Gansu, after taking her away in Beijing (coded to Beijing). She frequents Beijing to file petitions against the local government.

She was on the way to leave the station after having been intercepted on her way to Beijing to file petitions and detained in a hostel since 6 September 2022 (coded separately).

Most of the protesters were Han Chinese migrant workers, who could not make a living nor return home due to lockdowns in Lhasa, which have been imposed for 80 days. The last recorded large-scale protest in the city was in 2008, when Tibetans protested against how the government treated and prosecuted them.

On 27 November 2022, people gathered and chanted slogans in Huangpu district (Huangpu, Shanghai). The police beat up some demonstrators. The demonstrators were calling for the Chinese authorities to investigate the residential fire in Urumqi, Xinjiang that killed 10 on 24 November 2022, and to release the people they arrested in the protests that followed the incident. The Chinese public attributed the deaths of the 10 victims to local coronavirus lockdowns, which had made evacuation difficult.

On 22 March 2022, people gathered and chanted slogans in Pingshan district (Shenzhen, Guangdong) to demonstrate against local coronavirus restrictions. On 12 June 2022, residents chanted slogans and held banners in multiple districts in Dandong city, Liaoning (coded to Zhenxing, Dandong) to demonstrate against the local coronavirus lockdown. Some of them tried to break through barriers meant to quarantine them.
