Around 7 March 2023 (as reported), factory workers gathered to demonstrate in Changzhou city, Jiangsu (coded to Xinbei) to demand wage arrears.
Around 7 March 2023 (as reported), factory workers gathered in their factories to demonstrate and went on a strike in Wuyi county (Jinhua, Zhejiang) to demand wage arrears.
Around 6 March 2023 (as reported), construction workers gathered to demonstrate in Dongwan city, Guangdong (coded to Nancheng) to demand wage arrears.
Around 6 March 2023 (as reported), workers hired by an employment agency held a banner in Tianjin city (coded to Hebei) to demand wage arrears.
Around 6 March 2023 (as reported), hotel employees gathered to demonstrate in Fuzhou city, Jiangxi (coded to Linchuan) to demand wage arrears
Around 5 March 2023 (as reported), construction workers held a banner in Guangzhou city, Guangdong (coded to Guangzhou) to demand wage arrears.
Around 4 March 2023 (as reported), construction workers held a banner in their construction site in Dongwan city, Guangdong (coded to Nancheng) to demand wage arrears.

Around 3 March 2023 (as reported), taxi drivers filed petitions to the local office of the Ministry of Transport and the Public Complaints and Proposals Administration in Pingdingshan city, Henan (coded to Xinhua) together. They were dissatisfied that the government mandated them to switch to electric vehicles, which they thought were more costly.

Around 3 March 2023 (as reported), factory workers gathered to demonstrate in Suzhou city, Jiangsu (coded to Gusu). They were dissatisfied that they lost their jobs, after hearing that their factory would be moved to elsewhere.
Around 3 March 2023 (as reported), construction workers gathered to demonstrate in Shenzhen city, Guangdong (coded to Shenzhen) to demand wage arrears.
Around 2 March 2023 (as reported), factory workers held a banner outside their factory in Xiangtan city, Hunan (coded to Yuetang) to demand severance pay and compensation for occupational accidents.
Around 2 March 2023 (as reported), factory workers gathered to demonstrate outside their factory in Dongwan city, Guangdong (coded to Nancheng) to demand severance pay.

Around 1 March 2023 (as reported), Foxconn factory workers gathered to demonstrate in their factory in Chongqing city (coded to Chongqing). They were dissatisfied that their factory changed their job positions and on-duty time slots.

Around 1 March 2023 (as reported), factory workers gathered to demonstrate in Shenzhen city, Guangdong (coded to Shenzhen). They were dissatisfied that they would lose their jobs, after hearing that their factory would be moved to elsewhere.
Around 1 March 2023 (as reported), construction workers gathered to demonstrate outside their construction site in Guangzhou city, Guangdong (coded to Guangzhou) to demand wage arrears.
Around 1 March 2023 (as reported), factory workers held a banner in Dongwan city, Guangdong (coded to Nancheng) to demand wage arrears.
Around 1 March 2023 (as reported), construction workers held a banner outside their construction site in Dongcheng district (Dongwan, Guangdong) to demand wage arrears.

Around 1 March 2023 (as reported), a few hundred employees of a property agency gathered to demonstrate outside their employer's headquarters in Minhang district (Minhang, Shanghai) to demand wage arrears.
Around 15 December 2022 (month of), employees of a property agency held a banner outside their employer's headquarters in Minhang district (Minhang, Shanghai) to demand wage arrears.

On 14 May 2023, around 100 bank depositors of rural banks held banners and chanted slogans near the People's Bank of China in Shanyang district (Jiaozuo, Henan) to demand their deposits be recovered after a freeze on bank withdrawals last year, as the government investigated the banks for involving financial crimes. Police dispersed the crowds with tear gas, causing many to be injured.
On 15 May 2023, construction workers held banners at their construction site in Hong Kong - Wong Tai Sin to demand wage arrears.

On 26 April 2023, a legislator from the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong and representatives of the Rural Committee held banners and placards outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They were dissatisfied that the government did not hold consultations before granting new ferries to ferry operators, which complained that the measure had increased their costs.

On 17 May 2023, people held the Chinese national flag, chanted slogans and handed a petition letter to the Consul General of the United States outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western. Later on the day, another group of people defaced, stepped on and tore apart the United States national flag at the same location. They were dissatisfied that a congressional committee in the United States urged the government to impose sanctions on judges in Hong Kong that were appointed by the government to adjudicate on cases relating to the National Security Law. They said the proposal signaled the United State's meddling of Hong Kong's affairs and an interference to Hong Kong's judicial interference.

On 12 May 2023, at least 70 employees of a bank gathered and went on strike outside their bank in Pudong New Area district (Pudong, Shanghai). They were dissatisfied that the bank reduced their salaries and benefits.

On 29 April 2023, 11 representatives of the Federation of Hong Kong and Kowloon Labour Unions held banners, chanted slogans and marched to the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the government enacts policies to promote the interests of local employees, in the eve of the Labor Day on May 1.

On 1 May 2023, five representatives of the League of Social Democrats and around 20 representatives of the Hong Kong Women Worker's Association held banners and placards outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They criticised the government for distributing free cinema tickets and air tickets, instead of using the resources to tackle problems commonly met by workers at the grassroots.

On 16 April 2019, a Falun Gong member from Datong, Shanxi was taken away and detained in Jinzhong Prison in Qi County (Jinzhong, Shanxi). He was violently beaten up by the prison personnel, and sustained broken ribs and had his teeth knocked out.

Around 18 April 2019 (week of), a Falun Gong member from Wanrong County, Shanxi, who was detained in Jinzhong Prison in Qi County (Jinzhong, Shanxi), was tortured for a week by a group of prison personnel. They used pen leads to pierce his nails, stomped his toes with their feet, stepped on his chest, stomach, ribs, and cervical vertebrae, causing him to bleed, vomit blood, and have blood in the stool. The Falun Gong member was first taken away on 15 October, where he was reportedly beaten up by the superintendent of the prison training unit on the same day.

On 4 September 2019, a female petitioner from Baoshan district, Shanghai was intercepted in Beijing Municipality and sent back to Shanghai on the same day. She was put in a 'black jail' in Chongming District, Shanghai. This was allegedly related to the upcoming rehearsal of the 1 Oct military parade in the coming weekend in Beijing, where petitioners had been travelling to Beijing in an attempt to express their grievances. This was part of a broader stability maintenance operations since 2 Sep, where petitioners had been intercepted or taken away being repatriated to their place of origin.

On 6 August 2019, around 200 demolition personnel (including special police officers and unidentified persons) beat up the legal representative, manager, and employees of a company in Dongsheng Town (Zhongshan, Guangdong). The legal representative suffered from broken bones and was hospitalised. The company had reportedly been harassed by demolition personnel to force them to relocate, after the landowner had leased the land to a new tenant.

On 13 July 2019, 50-60 people who had fallen victim to investment fraud protested at Xincheng Hotel (the office of the CPC Central Committee Supervision Group) in Xincheng district (Huhehaote, Inner Mongolia) against the fraud and to demand an explanation. Police intervened and prevented them from getting close to the hotel.

On 15 July 2019, 50-60 people who had fallen victim to investment fraud protested at Xincheng Hotel (the office of the CPC Central Committee Supervision Group) in Xincheng district (Huhehaote, Inner Mongolia) against the fraud and to demand an explanation. Police intervened and prevented them from getting close to the hotel.

On 1 October 2018, people who had fallen victim to investment fraud related to peer-to-peer lending protested in Wuhan in Hubei province (coded as Jiang'an) against the fraud. It was reported that undercover special agents who were pretending to be demonstrators reported to the police, and arrests were made by the police during the demonstration.

On 5 October 2018, at least 100 people who had fallen victim to investment fraud relating to peer-to-peer lending marched along Hanjiang Road in Jianghan district (Wuhan, Hubei) to protest the fraud. They held placards and shouted slogans, demanding to see the city governor. Police broke up the protest and took away more than 100 people with two coaches, during which a female protester was beaten up by police. Those who did not get detained continued their protest.

On 6 October 2018, an unknown number of people who had fallen victim to investment fraud relating to peer-to-peer lending protested at Jiefang Park in Jiang'an district (Wuhan, Hubei) against the fraud. They shouted slogans. Police broke up the protest around half an hour after it began. A few protesters were taken away.

On 26 January 2018, during the 'two sessions' of Jiangsu Province, a female petitioner was taken in Kunshan (Suzhou, Jiangsu) and detained in a 'black jail' until the end of the 'two sessions' of Jiangsu Province on 31 January 2018.

On 17 March 2018, some tenants from Langji and Jinyuan residential districts staged a protest in front of the sales department in the Hi-tech Industrial Development Zone in Wuhou, Chengdu, Sichuan, for the reason that the quality of the interior design of the sample apartments was lower than that stipulated in the contract. During the protest, police officers demanded protesters put down the banners, but did not otherwise intervene.

On 9 November 2018, 119 Falun Gong members were arrested by the police in Harbin and Daxing cities of Heilongjiang Province. This is believed to be a massive police operation cracking down on Falun Gong's influence. During the operation, four Falun Gong members were taken away by police from their respective homes in Nangang district (Harbin, Heilongjiang), where police also confiscated computers, Falun Gong books and printers from their homes. Location coded as Songbei.

On 11 November 2018, more than 150 homeowners of a residential estate took to the streets in Liangqing district (Nanning, Guangxi) to protest that the real estate company had not fulfilled its promise of greening construction. They chanted slogans and displayed several banners. The real estate company hired private security personnel to disperse the protesters.

On 16 November 2018, many veterans petitioned at the Civil Affairs Bureau of Xiangtan in Yuhu district (Xiangtan, Hunan) against the pension system. They had a negotiation with government officials but the negotiation eventually failed and the veterans destroyed the properties of the conference room.

On 2 December 2018, 200-300 people (all of them were reportedly women) marched in Yuhuazhai village (residential district), Yanta district (Xi'an, Shaanxi) to protest against forced demolition of their village. A few hundred police officers were deployed, pepper-spraying protesters and beating some up. At night, many private security personnel hired by the real estate developer broke into the house of a villager and beat him up. The security personnel were armed with knives. Private security personnel who were surrounded by villagers called the police to the scene. The police took away eight villagers.

On 3 December 2018, an estimated 10,000 people marched in Leshan City (Sichuan) (coded as Shizhong) to protest the newly-legislated differentiated parking fee regulation splitting Leshan city into two zones with different per hour parking fee. Protesters chanted slogans.

On 5 January 2018, a large number of villagers gathered around the local village committee office of Xinji Village, Machong Town (Dongwan, Guangdong) to protest against the committee's intentional cover-up of land renting revenue. It was reported that the villagers continued protesting for several days.

On 24 January 2018, more than 2000 villagers from Oroqen Autonomous Banner staged a protest in front of Bila River Forestry Bureau in Nuomin Town (Hulunbeier, Inner Mongolia) against the defarming-and-reafforestation agreement between the local government and the forestry bureau, and to demand the government to return their land. During the protest, the protesters chanted slogans and broke through the police cordon to advance to the front of the government building. It was reported that two representatives of the villagers were arrested during the protest.

On 13 December 2018, an unknown number of villagers of the Shunhe community in Taohua Town, Feixi County protested at the Provincial government in Luyang district (Hefei, Anhui) to demand compensation for land acquisition. Many protesters were arrested.

On 26 December 2018, more than 100 people who had fallen victim to investment fraud protested at the Tonglu county government in Tonglu county (Hangzhou, Zhejiang) against the fraud. They held banners. Three people were arrested and released later in the day.

On 5 January 2019, more than 150 workers of a digital company protested at the rooftop of the company in Weihai city in Shandong province (coded as Huancui) to condemn the company for forcing workers to resign. Protesters shouted slogans. It was reported that the workers continued to remain at the rooftop until the morning of 6 January, although only more than 20 people remained, as most workers had been invited to leave the rooftop to negotiate with the company and subsequently prevented from returning to the rooftop.

On 10 January 2019, a female Falun Gong member was hurt during interrogation in a police station in Shenzhou city (Hengshui, Hebei) as police pulled her hair and smashed her forehead with a phone. She was taken away by police from her home in Shenzhou city a day earlier.

On 11 January 2019, a 82-year-old Falun Gong member was taken away by police in Zhaoyuan City (Yantai, Shandong) while she was distributing Falun Gong leaflets on the streets. After a few hours, she was declared dead and her body was escorted by police to a funeral parlor. While the police stated that she died of illness, her family said that she was healthy. There was no direct report as to whether she was tortured to death during interrogation.

On 6 March 2018, a female Falun Gong group member was taken at her home in Changji City (Changji, Xinjiang) by unidentified people to 'brainwashing class' (reportedly used by the authorities to force practitioners to renounce the practice) after she was released from a female prison in Xinjiang where she was detained for three years.

Around 11 March 2018 (between 3 - 20 March), during the Lianghui annual sessions, a female rights defender was taken by the personnel from the Beijing-based Office of the Shanghai Government in Beijing Municipality when she was taking a bus to the Great Hall of the People to state the injustice she suffered. She was then detained in a 'black jail' for 15 days.

On 3 April 2018, 200-300 villagers gathered at the entrance of 207 National Highway in Hedongcun village (Maoming, Guangdong) to demonstrate against the planned construction of a waste incineration power plant in their village. They rejected the project because of concerns for pollution from the plant, and also because the government was allegedly using the development project as a pretext for land acquisition. Demonstrators held banners and chanted slogans. 100-200 police arrived at the scene and clashed with the villagers. 3 villagers were injured, and among them, two were seriously injured and sent to the hospital. Tear gas was used during the clash. The demonstrations had lasted for around a week as reported on 5 April by RFA. Police arrested dozens and injured at least 10 villagers between 2-4 April, resulting in two hospitalisations.

On 4 April 2018, villagers gathered in Hedongcun village (Maoming, Guangdong) to protest against the planned construction of a waste incineration power plant in their village. Protesters rejected the project because of concerns for pollution from the plant, and also because the government was allegedly using the development project as a pretext for land acquisition. During the protest, the local government deployed police to block the roads and take away all banners held by protesters. Protesters continued chanting slogans, and the police used pepper spray, as well as beat and arrested protesters. Several villagers were injured, and two were arrested.

On 20 February 2019, a female petitioner was intercepted by police in Wangyedian Inspection Station in Wangyedian Village in Harqin Banner (Chifeng, Inner Mongolia) and dragged off the coach and locked up in a hotel in Hexigten Banner. She was making her way to Beijing to take care of her son, and the incident was allegedly related to the upcoming Lianghui annual sessions. It was not reported how long they were detained for.

On 20 February 2019, more than 100 villagers demonstrated in Genbao (Genpu) Village in Jinhe Town, Saihan district (Huhehaote, Inner Mongolia) to prevent urban management personnel, police officers and local officers from demolishing the storage house of the village. They held banners and placards. Around 50 to 60 government personnel and officers entered the village, beating protesters up and injuring 8-9 of them. One woman was beaten unconscious. Many were sent to the hospital.

On 11 March 2019, two female Falun Gong members were taken away by police in Jinsha New District in Xinxing district (Qitaihe City, Heilongjiang) when they were distributing leaflets. They were beaten up and it was found that there were hard knots in their muscles, making it difficult for them to sit down. It was suspected they had been tortured.

On 15 March 2019, around 1,000 parents of students who got food poisoning after being fed bad food by their school marched at the Chengdu Qizhong Experimental School in Wenjiang District (Chengdu, Sichuan) to demand for an explanation and an investigation into the issue. One protester was taken away by two plainclothes officers for shouting slogans at the front gate of the school.

Property destruction: Around 19 March 2019 (between 19 - 20 March), the gate and a building connected to a mosque in Yutian County (Hotan, Xinjiang) was reportedly demolished by the authorities, as shown from a satellite image captured by a Chinese student abroad. This was a broader campaign to suppress Uyghur influence.

On 8 May 2018, two Falun Gong members (a married couple) were transferred from the Wuhan No. 1 Detention Center and Wuhan No. 2 Detention Center in Wuhan City, Hubei Province to Jianghan District Legal Education Centre, a 'black jail' used for the persecution of Falun Gong members. They had been administratively detained for 15 days, after they were first taken into custody by the police on 23 April 2018.

On 9 May 2018, more than 100 triad members led by urban management personnel attacked several villagers with knives and sticks in a forced eviction in Hanxiaodian Village in Luyang District (Hefei, Anhui), and two villagers were severely injured. Several villagers were also taken into custody and detained in a hotel 'black jail'.

On 1 June 2018, retired soldiers from all over the country gathered at in Luohe City (Henan Province) (coded as Yancheng) to protest against the arrest of retired soldiers on 27 May 2018 and the wife of a fellow veteran after she submitted a petition to the authority in Beijing. They continued to gather until 3 June 2018.

On 25 April 2019, a female petitioner from Yangpu district, Shanghai was intercepted in Beijing Municipality by government personnel from the Shanghai People's Government Office in Beijing, when she was on her way to the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development to petition against forced demolition of her house. She was beaten up during the process, sustaining injuries in her right arm and elbow. It was part of a campaign by the local police to prevent petitioners from petitioning before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation.

On 27 April 2019, a female petitioner from Wujiaochang residential district in Yangpu District, Shanghai was taken away by social security personnel from a detention centre in Beijing Municipality and sent to a holiday resort in Chongming, Shanghai. It was part of a campaign by the local police to prevent petitioners from petitioning before and during the second Belt and Road Forum on International Cooperation.

On 28 April 2019, more than 300 workers of the Mianduhe Forestry Bureau protested at the local government in Mianduhe Town in Yakeshi City (Hulunbeier, Inner Mongolia) to demand to be recognized as official staff, so that they would receive higher salaries and promotion opportunities. More than 100 special police were deployed. One worker was hit by an officer with a baton and bled in the head and was sent to a hospital. Four other workers were arrested.

On 12 May 2019, a female Falun Gong member was attacked by a person of unknown identity in Wanquan Town in Wanquan County (Zhangjiakou, Hebei). The attacker pushed her to the ground and violently hit her head. Four of her teeth came off and she also had a broken nose and fainted. Police then arrived but instead of arresting the attacker, they took away the female Falun Gong member as well as her companion, who was also a Falun Gong member.

On 19 May 2019, a female petitioner from Putuo district, Shanghai was intercepted in Beijing. She was sent back to Shanghai after agreeing to be placed under RSDL. Upon arriving at Shanghai Railway Station, she was forcibly taken away by police and unidentified private security personnel to a black jail in Qingpu district, Shanghai.

On 26 May 2019, 500 to 600 drivers went on strike and staged a sit-in protest at the Dongguan Bus Terminal in Wanjiang subdistrict (Dongwan, Guangdong) to demand compensation after the transport company had been acquired by another company. They continued to express their demands the next day.

On 18 July 2019, 300-400 drivers protested at the Dongguan office of an online delivery services platform in Dongwan city, Guangdong province (coded as Nancheng) against a reduction in prices. They demanded the price to be restored to the price set in 2018.

On 9 July 2018, around 200 veterans from Inner Mongolia staged a protest outside the municipal government building in Xincheng District (Huhehaote, Inner Mongolia) to defend their rights and demand better welfare from the government. During the protest, the protesters held banners.

Property destruction: On 21 March 2019, the United Front Work Department of Shan County, Heze City forcibly removed a plaque of a Buddhist temple in Shan County (Heze, Shandong), converted two buildings of the temple into government offices, and concealed all statues with cloth written with core socialist slogans. This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CPC to crack down on religious activities.

On 14 May 2019, a female Falun Gong member was transferred from a detention center in Wuhan City, Hubei province to a 'brainwashing class' in South Lake (Nanhu), Wuhan to be detained. This took place 10 days after she first got arrested by police on 4 May when talking to people about Falun Gong beliefs in Huangpi district, Wuhan. This was related to the upcoming Military World Games. Location coded as Jiang'an.

Property destruction: Around 15 June 2019 (month of), a Guanyin statue from a Buddhist temple in Songyuan City, Jilin province was removed by government-hired personnel. This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CPC to crack down on religious activities. Location coded as Ningjiang.

Property destruction: Around 30 June 2019 (end of month), government-hired personnel demolished all Buddhist statues of a pagoda inside a temple in Zhaocun Town, Xingping City (Xianyang, Shaanxi). This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CPC to crack down on religious activities.

Around 16 August 2019 (as reported), a female petitioner was taken away from Beijing Municipality by personnel from the Beijing Office. She was then repatriated to her hometown in Fuxin City, Liaoning province and detained in a hotel for a month. She was officially arrested on 12 Sep 2019.

Property destruction: Around 16 August 2019 (month of), a Buddhist temple in Yuhang district (Hangzhou, Zhejiang) was converted by the government into a cultural centre. The Guanyin statue inside the temple was covered up. This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CPC to crack down on religious activities.

On 4 September 2019, a female petitioner from Yangpu district, Shanghai was taken away by stability maintenance agents from her rental house in Beijing Municipality to a 'black jail' in Majialou. She was detained there until the next day when she was repatriated to Shanghai by personnel from the Beijing Office of Shanghai People's Government. She was then locked up in another 'black jail' hotel in Yangpu district and was still held there by the time of reporting 30 September 2019.

On 5 September 2019, a female Falun Gong member got into an altercation with the police when police was ransacking her house in Mulin Town, Shunyi district (Beijing). Several police officers physically blocked her during the process, causing the back of her head to hit a chair. She had a medical examination afterwards, which found that she had a concussion. During the raid, the police also took away her computer, Falun Gong books and other personal belongings.

Around 16 September 2019 (between 16 - 17 September), a Falun Gong member from Jianghan district, Wuhan city was arrested by police and locked up in a 'brainwashing centre' in Jianghan district, Hubei. It was reported that he would be released after the Military World Games. Coded as Jiang'an.

On 17 September 2019, a female Falun Gong member from Xiong County, Hebei province was dragged off her motorbike by a police officer in Xiong County (Baoding, Hebei), causing her to fall head first onto the ground. She fainted immediately. It was reported that she was not able to raise her arms after being dragged off the motorbike.

Around 25 September 2019 (as reported), a retired teacher (also a Falun Gong member) was transferred from Wuhan No. 1 Detention Centre in Dongxihu District (Wuhan, Hubei) and detained in a hospital in Jiang'an district (Wuhan, Hubei). This is related to the approaching Military World Games.
On 26 September 2019, the daughter of a Falun Gong member was taken away by police in Shayang County (Jingmen, Hubei). Her whereabouts remained unknown at the time of reporting 8 October 2019.

On 29 September 2019, a human rights lawyer from Shanghai was summoned to the Jing'an Branch of Shanghai Municipal Public Security Bureau in Jing'an District (Shanghai). He was then held incommunicado in a hotel. This incident was allegedly related to the upcoming National Day Celebration on 1 Oct.

On 16 August 2018, hundreds of victims of a financial fraud gathered in front of the municipal government of Wuhan City in Jiang'an District (Wuhan, Hubei) to demand the government to investigate the fraud and compensate them. The victims blocked the gate of the government. Special police and security guards surrounded the demonstrators. Clashes between the demonstrators and police were reported. Some demonstrators were taken into custody.

On 20 August 2018, more than 100 victims of a financial fraud staged a protest at the Hubei Provincial Government in Wuchang District (Wuhan, Hebei) to demand the government to investigate the fraud, arrest the chairperson of the company, and compensate the losses of investors.

On 21 August 2018, around 1000 victims of a financial fraud staged a protest in front of Wuhan Municipal Government in Jiang'an District (Wuhan, Hubei) to demand the government to investigate the fraud, arrest the chairperson of the company, and compensate their losses. Police forcibly took away protesters from the scene, and put protesters onto buses and sent to the complaint and proposal bureau.
Property destruction: On 25 August 2018, government officials demolished a house church in Xinye County (Nanyang, Henan) in a national campaign to suppress house churches and religious belief.

Property destruction: On 26 August 2018, the authorities tore down the cross of a house church in Housongmaying Town (Nanyang, Henan) in a national campaign to suppress house churches and religious belief.
Property destruction: On 26 August 2018, the authorities demolished the cross of a house church in Liaohe Town (Nanyang, Henan) in a national campaign to suppress house churches and religious belief.

Property destruction: On 26 August 2018, the authorities tore down the cross of a house church in Tanghe County (Nanyang, Henan) in a national campaign to suppress house churches and religious belief.

On 24 June 2018, an unknown number of petitioners (including one female) were beaten by security guards at the Shanghai People's Government Office for Calls and Letters in Huangpu District (Shanghai) when they were petitioning against the construction of an underground waste transfer station in their neighbourhood.

On 9 August 2019, a female petitioner from Hunan was arrested in Jiaomen North Road in Fengtai District (Beijing - Fengtai) by personnel from her local government's Beijing office, and locked up in a remote compound in Yuquanying. She was sent back to Xiangtan, Hunan by subdistrict office staff on 13 August.

On 2 September 2019, a female petitioner from Shanghai was intercepted by police in Dongtangzi Hutong in Dongcheng district (Beijing - Dongcheng) and sent back to Shanghai. Her whereabouts remained unknown at the time of reporting on 5 September. This was allegedly related to the upcoming rehearsal of the 1 Oct military parade in the coming weekend in Beijing.

On 1 November 2018, at least 12 petitioners staged a flash protest at the venue of the China International Import Expo in National Convention & Exhibition Center in Qingpu district (Shanghai). 12 people were detained, 8 among which remained uncontactable.

On 23 February 2019, two female petitioners on their way to Beijing were intercepted by police at Hongqiao Railway Station in Minhang district (Shanghai). One of them was locked up in an elderly house and the other was locked up in a hotel. The incidents are allegedly related to the upcoming Lianghui annual sessions. It was not reported how long they were detained for.

On 29 April 2019, two students from the School of Pharmacy of Peking University were assaulted by police and security guards in the School of Medicine on campus in Haidian district (Beijing - Haidian). One of them, female, was assaulted when she was in the toilet and a few male police kicked her door and pulled her from the toilet, dragged on the floor and took her away for interrogation. She went missing thereafter. This incident is allegedly related to the approaching 100th anniversary of the May-Fouth Incident.

On 2 May 2019, an unknown number of people who had fallen victim to investment fraud protested at the hotel of a property management group in Futian district (Shenzhen, Guangdong) against the fraud. One protester was beaten up by private security personnel hired by the hotel. One protester was taken away by police. The protesters had protested in Futian police station and the Letters and Calls Bureau on the same day.

On 20 June 2019, a female petitioner from Yangpu district, Shanghai was pepper-sprayed by police in the eye near Sheshan underground station in Songjiang district (Shanghai) when she attempted to get on a bus without paying the fare (petitioners are entitled to free rides). Besides pepper-spraying her eyes, the police also grabbed her hair and dragged her to the ground. She was taken to the hospital after being held in a police station for 10 hours. She was found to have suffered from subcorneal skin defect and right shoulder injury.

On 24 February 2023, around 20 members of a coalition of domestic workers' unions held placards and banners in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They were dissatisfied that lawmakers of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong called for the government to restrict their ability to change employers. They also demanded that one of the lawmakers of the party apologise for saying that they did not match their 'product description'.

On 13 May 2023, a female petitioner became incommunicado after police took her away in Beijing (coded to Beijing). A day before, she had travelled to Beijing to file petitions against her local government.

Around 15 March 2022 (month of), police tortured five Tibetans in a detention centre in Tibet province (coded to Lhasa, Lhasa). During the detention, which lasted for more than 40 days, they were beaten up repeatedly and their private parts and legs were electrocuted. One of them suffered from injuries as a result and had to be hospitalized for 10 days after being released from prison. They were taken to detention between 3 and 5 March 2022, after they were found worshipping local deities on what they considered a sacred mountain.

Property destruction: On 21 May 2023, dozens of police and local government officials raided the Zhongxing Christian Church in Jinshui district (Zhengzhou, Henan). They damaged the church's facilities, including shattering the interior windows, and confiscated churchgoers' properties. The government had declared the family church, which is not a part of the state-controlled Three-Self Church, to be an 'illegal social organization'.
On 17 May 2023, around 30 factory workers gathered to demonstrate in Xiamen city, Fujian (coded to Siming) to demand wage arrears.
On 20 May 2023, parents and students held placards and banners outside a school in Hong Kong - Wong Tai Sin. They were dissatisfied that their school was not allowed to continue operating.

On 11 March 2018, a petitioner from Dongxiang Wuxi was sent to Jiujingzhuang 'black jail' after the police from Beijing Fuyou Street Police Station inspected her ID in Beijing, and since 12 March 2018, she went incommunicado after she was sent back to Dongxiang by an unidentified vehicle and detained in the Dongxiang Police Station. During the Lianghui conventions, the Chinese government had a nationwide stability maintenance operation in which the rights defenders and petitioners were their targets.

On 7 June 2018, a Uyghur businessman became incommunicado, after police took him away in Guangzhou, Guangdong (coded to Guangzhou) for being an 'untrustworthy person with relatives abroad'. He was subsequently taken to a re-education camp.

Property destruction: Around 30 May 2023 (as reported), police raided a house church in Zhongshan city, Guangdong (coded to Dongqu). They damaged all the facilities in the house church, including items used for worshipping. House churches in China are not a part of the state-controlled Three-Self Church.

Other: On 27 May 2023, the Civic Party, the second largest pro-democracy party mainly consisting of barristers, announced it was disbanding in Hong Kong in light of the increase in censorship, as a result of the enactment of the national security law in 2020.

On 2 June 2023, representatives of the Federation of Hong Kong and Kowloon Labour Unions held banners and placards outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They were dissatisfied that the government's plan to import foreign labor would reduce job opportunities for local workers.

Around 26 May 2023 (as reported), socially idle persons and triad members beat up 'numerous' property owners in Hongshan district (Wuhan, Hebei). In one of the instances, ten triad members dragged a landlord along the grass and attacked him. The attackers were sent by a private developer, which expressed interest in building a railway in the district. The owners had opposed the plan, citing economic concerns and impacts on daily life.

Around 22 May 2023 (as reported), 34 teachers held placards and went on a hunger strike at the Education Bureau office in Hubin district (Sanmenxia, Henan). They were dissatisfied that they worked at least 12 hours a day and never received any social welfare that they were entitled to.

Other: On 2 June 2023, the Macau Union for the Development of Democracy, founded to organize vigils to commemorate the victims of the June Fourth Incident, announced it was disbanding in Macao in light of the increase in censorship in Hong Kong, the pandemic and recent changes in the national security law. On May 18, the local legislation unanimously passed a bill that introduced tougher penalties for sedition, secession and subversion, and widened the scope of acts that could fall those offences.

On 28 May 2023, a human rights lawyer was injured by a landlord, when trying to stop the property owner from forcibly evicting his tenant, another human rights lawyer, by removing the door to his home in Songzhuang town (Tongzhou, Beijing). The two lawyers had been subject to the '709 crackdown', and had been forced to move homes and harassed by police multiple times ever since. It was alleged that the landlord had the police's approval and backing before he acted against the tenant.

On 31 May 2023, a political dissident blogger's wife went incommunicado for four days, after police took her away in Yangpu district (Yangpu, Shanghai) and confiscated her phone. The wife had been advocating for the blogger's release, after he had been sentenced to seven years in prison for 'Inciting subversion of state power'. The forced disappearance was ahead of the 34th anniversary of the June Fourth Incident.

On 29 May 2023, three police officers, including a police chief, beat up a journalist for a Mainland China-based media outlet, when he was on an investigative news assignment in Zhijin county (Bijie, Guizhou). He was reporting about two teachers who died from drowning in a river after a dam leakage upstream caused flooding. Online rumours allege they were assigned by their school to pick up rocks at the river for decorative purposes, which the school, the local government and the local party committee denied. At the time of the assault, the journalist was interviewing one of the teachers' family members. The attackers also followed him and broke his phone. Three days later, the local government announced that it detained them for the incident, and demoted the police chief who was involved.

On 27 May 2023, Hui Muslims pushed against the police and hurled objects at them, in opposition to the local government's forced demolition of the Najiaying Mosque in Tonghai county (Yuxi, Yunnan), which is the largest mosque in Yunnan and was declared officially to be a cultural heritage. The rioters also toppled the scaffolding that authorities put in place to raze the mosque. Dozens of police, including those from the armed police forces, were deployed, wielding truncheons, riot shields and pepper sprays against the crowd. As a result of the clash, some were injured and allegedly 30 were arrested.

On 26 May 2023, government officers beat up and injured a secondary school principal at the office of the Ministry of Education in Jintai district (Baoji, Shaanxi), after he had met with the ministry's local chief to discuss his dissatisfaction with its decision not to allow his school to recruit more students. The principal was hospitalized subsequently for his injuries.

On 7 February 2023, residents held banners and placards outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western to demand that the government withdraw its plans to build short-term public housing in their neighborhood, which they said would impact the area's status as a central business district and be done without due consultation.

On 20 February 2023, representatives of the Society for Community Organization held banners and placards outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western to demand that the government enhances the quality of life of the poor, including setting up unemployment benefits and subsidies for daily subsistence.

On 20 February 2023, five representatives of the Democratic Party held a banner and handed a petition letter with signatures of at least 1,500 Hong Kong residents to a government official outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the government hands out cash vouchers.

On 4 June 2023, 24 people, including a journalist and prominent activists like the chairperson of the League of Social Democrats and the former vice-chairman of the now-disbanded Confederation of Trade Unions, were taken away by police in Hong Kong - Wan Chai, on suspicion of breaching the peace. They were commemorating the victims of the June Fourth Incident in their own ways, such as turning on their phone's flashlight, donning t-shirts with news reports of the crackdown, lighting up candles and making Buddha prayers.

On 2 June 2023, parents chanted slogans outside their children's school in Hongshan district (Wuhan, Hubei), in protest of a local government's policy which resulted in their children being switched to another campus that is three kilometres away from them. Police blocked the school's entrance.

On 3 June 2023, around 2,000 parents chanted slogans and physically clashed with the police outside their children's school in Hongshan district (Wuhan, Hubei), in opposition to a local government's policy which resulted in their children being switched to another campus that is three kilometres away from them. Police pushed the demonstrators, beat some of them up and arrested five to six people.

On 6 June 2023, police, private security officers and other unidentified people beat up a lawyer and some Christians outside a residential estate in Shuangliu district (Chengdu, Sichuan). The attackers blocked the Christians from returning to their home in the estate, before pushing them and physically assaulting, at least, one of the women. A lawyer passing by tried to stop the aggression, and was beaten up as well. In the end, the lawyer escaped and the Christians were sent to the hospital to treat their minor injuries. The Christians were members of the Early Rain Covenant Church, a house church that had been raided and shut down by the government for not being part of the state-administered Three-Self Church.

On 11 April 2023, an Anhui-based pastor became incommunicado, after being taken away by Anhui police in Lijiang city, Yunnan (coded to Gucheng) for illegally operating an organization. He went to the city to spread the gospel for a local church. The pastor is a member of the Huo Shi Gui Zheng church, which is not part of the state-administered Three-Self Church.

Around 15 June 2023 (as reported), police beat up a human rights lawyer in a police station in Wutai county (Xinzhou, Shanxi). He had been detained there for 3 years without a court trial, after being charged with 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble'. It is unknown whether he had suffered injuries from the attack.

The forced disappearance was a week before the court's review on the government's decision to reduce pensions, which has been a subject of advocacy among local human rights defenders.

On 14 June 2023, around 20 construction workers held banners and went on a strike outside their construction site in Hong Kong - Kowloon City to demand wage arrears.

On 13 June 2023, many people surrounded vehicles belonging to the local Urban Administrative and Law Enforcement Bureau, argued with and physically attacked the officials working there in Dongxing district (Neijiang, Sichuan). They were dissatisfied that earlier in the day, some of the urban administrative officers had beaten up a hawker for illegally selling eggs (separately coded).

On 12 June 2023, representatives of the Hong Kong Federation of Trade Unions, including lawmakers, held a banner and chanted slogans outside the Consulate-General of Japan in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They were dissatisfied about the Japanese government's plan to release water from the Fukushima nuclear plant into the ocean, disregarding impacts to the environment.

On 12 June 2023, Mongolian nomads gathered to demonstrate in grassland in Jarud Banner (Tongliao, Inner Mongolia), after knowing that government officials had sold the land to a Han person without consulting them. In reaction, employees hired by the buyer drove a bulldozer towards the crowd, causing one of them to be severely injured. The nomadic farmers had used the grassland for thousands of years to graze cattle.

On 19 June 2021, a veteran and former deputy chief of the Urban Management Bureau in Wuxi prefecture (Jiangsu) (coded to Binhu) had lost contact. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party. He had been imprisoned twice for helping others in their rights defending efforts.

On 30 November 2021, an elected female village leader from Yangzhai village (Suzhou, Anhui) was intercepted by petition interceptors in Beijing municipality after submitting evidence of illegal and criminal activities against a village secretary to the National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration. She went incommunicado after being repatriated to her hometown, as reported on 2 December 2021.

The injured elderly man was taken to a hospital for treatment, before being detained by the town government. He was released the next day.

On 6 November 2019, a pro-Beijing Hong Kong lawmaker was attacked during a campaign trail in Tuen Mun District, Hong Kong by a man with knife. His assistant and himself were both injured and sent to the hospital. The attacker accused him of orchestrating the July 21 attacks on train passengers and others at the hands of white-clad thugs in Yuen Long district.

On 15 March 2019, a human rights defender and former chief of the district petitioning bureau from Qingyang district of Chengdu, Sichuan was stripped naked, had unknown items forced into his mouth, and allegedly poisoned at the Qingyang Public Security Case Handling Centre (Chengdu, Sichuan) after being arrested by public security personnel and police forces.

On 23 February 2019, a government official was stabbed to death by a villager in Linquan County (Fuyang, Anhui) while he was leading a team to demolish illegal buildings in the area. The assailant also attempted to attack the other officials but was restrained.

On 19 November 2019, the former chairman and lawmaker of the Democratic Party (Hong Kong) was followed by several unknown individuals in black clothes after he exited the Tin Hau MTR station in Wan Chai District (Hong Kong) at night and later attacked by those people in a nearby alley with rods. He suffered multiple injuries to his head, back and arms. The incident was reported to be among the several attacks against district councillor candidates and pro-democracy party members that happened in the context of the anti-ELAB movement in Hong Kong since June 2019.

On 15 May 2019, two Shanghai petitioners, including a retired local government official, were intercepted by police at the Ministry of Public Security in Dongcheng district (Beijing) and taken to a detention centre. The retired official was locked up in a farmhouse in Pudong (Shanghai) until at least 22 May. It was reported that 4 other petitioners were also detained in the same farmhouse starting from 16 May 2019, though the location of where they were first taken away from was not reported.

On 25 December 2018, a petitioner against forced demolitions killed two government officials with a knife in Xinluo, Longyan before hijacking a bus and driving it into a crowd of people, killing eight others and injuring 25.

On 6 November 2019, a district councillor from DAB's Yau Tsim Mong branch was attacked by an unidentified man with a wooden stick during the District Council election campaign in Yau Ma Tei, Yau Tsim Mong District (Hong Kong).

On 21 July 2019, hundreds of masked assailants dressed in white assaulted residents, protesters, journalists and a lawmaker in Yuen Long, presumably targeting anti-government protesters returning from HK Island to New Territories. These attackers used bamboo sticks and other weapons to attack people in the station, causing 45 injuries, including one Legislative Councillor. Police officers were not visibly present when the attack occurred. In a widely circulated online video, pro-Beijing lawmaker was seen applauding to people dressed in white.

On 5 January 2018, the Party Committee Secretary of Nantai village of Jinxian county (Nanchang, Jiangxi) was stabbed and killed in his office by a sanitation worker who had been laid off by the town government. The sanitation worker used a fruit knife, and was arrested afterwards. His motive was not revealed by enforcement authorities.
Around 26 November 2018 (as reported), a Han official in Gongliu county (Ili, Xinjiang) was sent to a re-education camp because he didn't reach the quota of arresting Muslims in the Aga'ersen Town.

On 18 March 2018, the head of Village Committee in Jingshan Village (Ji'an, Jiangxi) stabbed the Village Party Secretary and his father to death in the local village committee election because he believes that the election was manipulated, and two people died.

On 29 August 2018, a team of urban planning officials rounded up a local villager in Zhijin county of Bijie prefecture, Guizhou and beat him up during an unannounced demolition of 'illegal constructions.' Out of anger, the villager immediately retaliated by driving an off-road vehicle towards the officials, causing 3 deaths and wounding 10 people, of which three were civilians who happened to be observing the scene. A dozen villagers were arrested after the government blamed them for the deaths. A witness account claimed that both parties had attacked each other with metal tubes, stones and wooden sticks.

Around 13 May 2018, a government employee was transferred from his criminal detention at an unreported location in Shenzhen and held under Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL). He was arrested by the Shenzhen police on 13 April 2018, on the grounds of 'inciting subversion of state power'.

Around 16 October 2018 (month of), a Han CPC Chief of Shache (Yarkand) county (Kashi, Xinjiang) disappeared from the public and was reportedly held by the Xinjiang Discipline Inspection Commission at an unknown location. He was described as an official who 'failed to tow the party line during the round-up of Uyghurs in Shache county'. He ordered a release of 7,000 people from 'internment camps', and held the opinion that holding Uyghurs up in detention facilities or camps would not improve ethnic relations, and the lack of working-class men would cause his county to miss production targets.

On 5 April 2018, a Kazakh man (who was working as the governor of Toli County in the last 1-2 years) was taken away by the authorities likely from Toli County (Ili Kazak Autonomous, Xinjiang) and sent to a re-education camp, according to a testimony from his sister. It was reported he was likely detained for bribery and signing a contract to build a mosque, while the official investigation notice stated that he was being investigated for serious breach of the law and CCP's discipline. He was then reportedly sentenced to 4 years in prison and is currently detained in a prison, though it was unclear when he was transferred to the prison.

On 22 March 2021, a suicide bomber set off a homemade explosive device at a village government committee office in Mingjing village of Panyu district (Guangdong, Guangzhou), resulting in four injured and five dead. The bomber targeted the committee office, which decided on matters linked to land use, after alleged dissatisfaction about monetary compensation regarding a major property redevelopment that involved relocating locals. He was reported to have participated in a range of petitioning and rights defending activities in the past.

The researcher had published anti-government content on social media.

On 10 May 2018, the leader of the Pingtan County Urban Construction Office brought a group of people to tear apart the middle section of the remodelled shipping containers used as a gathering venue by a Three-Self Church in Aoqian town (Fuzhou City, Fujian Province). A week later, 20 workers from the Longtian Town Urban Construction Office returned to the site to completely tore down the containers on the grounds that it was an 'illegal structure'. It was reported that the local government had first tried to demolish the worship place on 17 April 2018.

Property destruction: On 16 June 2019, a Christian house church in Xiang'an (Xiamen, Fujian) was forcibly shut down by police and the sign of the church was destroyed. Police also took away the phones of the church-goers. This is part of a crackdown of house churches in China.

Property destruction: Around 15 November 2019 (month of), eight Three-Self Church venues were forcibly shut down by the Lanshan District government (Linyi, Shandong). Crosses and other Christian symbols were also removed from the venues. One of the venues was also repurposed into a warehouse.

Property destruction: Around 15 May 2019 (month of), a Taoist Sanguan Temple in Chahe town in Honghu City (Jingzhou City, Hubei Province) was rectified into a 'cultural activity centre' by the temple manager in order to save the temple. Signboards promoting the core socialist values were posted, with a large Xi Jinping banner posted in the middle of a hall. It was an attempt to save the temple from being demolished by the authorities, after it was sealed off and marked for demolition by the authorities in the previous month, as part of the CCP policy to demolish temples nationwide.

Property destruction: Around 15 October 2019 (month of), a temple in Yudan village (Baoji City, Shaanxi Province) was repurposed into an activity centre by the government, where chess and mahjong tables, and other entertainment items, were brought into the temples. Religious statues were also replaced with portraits of Xi Jinping, and slogans promoting the core socialist values. This was part of a broader campaign to crack down places of worship across China.

Property destruction: Around 15 August 2019 (month of), 40 out of 79 temples in Liuhe town, Qichun county (Huanggang City, Hubei Province) were sealed off following an order from the central government to crack down on Buddhist and folk religion places of worship. People guarding these temples were evicted, and some of them were transferred to nursing homes. These closed temples included Buddhist Kaishan Temple, Ciyundong Temple, Caogong Temple, and the Fulin Temple in Liuhe town's Zhonglu village.

Property destruction: Around 16 May 2018 (month of), the Buddhist Guanying Ancient Temple in Liangzihu District (Ezhou city, Hubei) was converted into a cultural activity centre by the local government referring to the CCP's policy banning the construction of temples. There was no compensation made to the donors. The owner of the temple and some believers that went on to petitions were detained by the police for 'disrupting social order'.

Property destruction: On 22 October 2018, four Buddhist temples in Guichi District (Chizhou City, Anhui Province) were shut down by the local government. All of the temples were also painted white, and a number of the temples had their Buddhist-related symbols and incense burners destroyed.

Property destruction: On 3 September 2020, an unregistered Catholic church in Youtong village of Luancheng district (Shijiazhuang, Hebei) was shut down by village officials for refusing to join the Patriotic Church. It was converted into a parking lot.

Looting: On 17 April 2018, the local authority closed down a gathering venue set up by Catholic 'Tong Chou Hui' of Mingonglu Catholic Church on Jiefang Road in Erqi District (Zhengzhou, Henan) and banned future gatherings at the venue. In the same Catholic Diocese of Zhengzhou, the local authorities also confiscated the religious books in Shuanghuaishu Catholic Church, Jiayu Catholic Church, and Youfangcun Church, and searched through the ledgers of Mingonglu Catholic Church and the Xiaodelan Nursing House for the Elderly, which were run by the church. It was a part of a governmental campaign to crack down on underground religious institutions in Henan Province.

Property destruction: Around 15 September 2018 (month of), two Catholic churches in Qishan County (Baoji City, Shaanxi Province) were repurposed into 'Cultural Activity Centres' by the county authorities. The authorities claimed that the church did not receive the formal approval from authorities and were 'illegal buildings'. Instead of being demolished, the crosses from the churches were removed and the words 'Catholic Church' were replaced with signs stating that it was a 'Cultural Activity Centre'.

Property destruction: Around 1 August 2018 (beginning of month), a Catholic church in Gujun Town (Baoji City, Shaanxi Province) was redecorated into a 'Cultural Activity Centre' by the authorities. As an alternative to being demolished, religious features of the building including the church's cross was forcibly dismantled. Believers were later informed that the building would serve as a 'community centre', instead of worship purposes.

Property destruction: Around 15 December 2019 (month of), a Catholic Church in Guchuan Village in Weibin District (Baoji City, Shaanxi Province) was shut down for refusing to register with the state. Prior to its closure, Chinese words for 'Catholic Church' were removed from its outer walls, and all three crosses were removed from the roof. This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CCP to crack down on religious activities.

Property destruction: Around 15 March 2019 (month of), a Catholic Church in Bixi Town, Taihe County (Ji'an City, Jiangxi Province) was taken over by the government and repurposed into a cultural activity centre. After the church was repurposed, government officials also visited the homes of congregations members to force them to sign statements renouncing their faith. The incident was part of a broader campaign to persecute congregations and churches that declined to join the Chinese Patriotic Catholic Association.

On 1 March 2024, a female petitioner became incommunicado for at least 3 days, after unknown people, in collaboration with police, took her away in Gulou district (Nanjing, Jiangsu). The detention is likely part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions, scheduled to be held on 5 March 2024.

On 2 March 2024, two petitioners became incommunicado, after people pretending to be police took them away in Santai county (Mianyang, Sichuan). The detention is likely part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions, scheduled to be held on 5 March 2024.

On 25 February 2024, many police officers hit the shoulders and kicked the heads of two men in a railway station in Zhengzhou city, Henan (coded to Zhongyuan). They were bank depositors, who had previously demonstrated repeatedly to demand their deposits be recovered after a freeze on bank withdrawals in 2022, as the government investigated the banks for involving financial crimes. It is unknown what happened to the two people afterwards.

On 8 March 2024, dozens of relatives of the passengers of MH370, the Malaysia Arlines plane that disappeared from radar in 2014, gathered to demonstrate outside the Embassy of Malaysia in Beijing - Chaoyang to demand more investigations on the incident.

On 2 March 2024, parents gathered to demonstrate outside a school in Xiangfu district (Kaifeng, Henan) to demand that the school pays its teachers, who had gone on strike and refused to teach their children.

On 5 March 2024, representatives of the Protect Hong Kong Alliance held banners outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the United States government stops interfering with Hong Kong's political affairs, after Matthew Miller, spokesperson for the Department of State, expressed concerns over the implications on freedom of speech as Hong Kong made plans to enact Article 23.

On 7 March 2024, representatives of the Hong Kong Women Workers' Association held banners and gathered to demonstrate outside the government headquarters in Hong Kong - Central and Western. As the International Women's Day approaches on the following day, the group demanded that the government increases maternity and paternity leave, reduces the burden of caregivers and closes gender pay gap.

On 25 March 2020, a female petitioner from Huangpu District, Shanghai was beaten by stability maintenance personnel at the Shanghai People's Government Office for Calls and Letters in Huangpu District (Shanghai). One of the personnel strangled the back of her neck, before dragging her towards a police car parked by the side of the road. The petitioner's head and face were slammed several times against the police car.
Around 26 May 2020 (as reported), up to 100 migrant workers demonstrated in Shanghai against wage arrears owed to them by a construction project.

On 21 May 2020, up to 100 employees demonstrated at a factory in Shanghai against wage arrears owed to them by the employer. Special police were dispatched to the scene and 1 female employee was arrested.

Around 21 June 2020 (as reported), up to 100 employees demonstrated in Shanghai against wage arrears owed to them by a manufacturing plant. It was reported that they had been owed wages for more than three months.

Around 22 June 2020 (as reported), up to 100 employees demonstrated in Shanghai against wage arrears owed to them by an automobile company. It was reported that they had not received their wages for the month of May, as well as social security conditions for January and February 2020.
Around 6 July 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers staged a protest against a branch of STO courier in Shanghai.

On 1 June 2020, more than 30 employees of a delivery company in Shanghai gathered at the company site to protest because the owner of the company became unreachable 2 days ago and he stopped paying these employees more than 3 months ago.
Around 26 August 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 migrant workers held a sit-in protest in Shanghai to demand for wage arrears owed by a state-owned construction project.

On 25 September 2020, a Friday, four climate activists held a silent protest on Nanjing Road, Huangpu district (Shanghai) on 'global climate strike day', as part of the international FridaysForFuture campaign. They were stopped by the police and taken back to the station for a two-hour interrogation.
Around 8 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Shanghai Municipality to demand for half year's worth of wage arrears owed by a medical beauty centre for 19 years.

Around 30 September 2020 (as reported), 101-1000 workers protested in Shanghai Municipality to demand for wage arrears following the closure of a catering management company. The company reportedly had 66 branches and around 1000 workers across the country.

On 19 October 2020, as many as 100 delivery workers protested in Shanghai municipality to demand for wage arrears following the closure of the Baoshan and Hongkou district branches of a courier company.

On 26 October 2020, a female petitioner was taken away by a group of Jiaxing sub-district workers and triad members outside Jiaxing Police Station in Hongkou district (Shanghai) (coded to Shanghai-Hongkou). Her fingers were reportedly bleeding after she was violently taken into the van. She was then locked up in Room 8601 'black jail' at Hanting Hotel, No.4, Long 1063, Zhoujiazui Road in the same district until her escape on 8 Nov 2020.
Around 25 November 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Shanghai Municipality to demand for wage arrears and social insurance owed by a furniture company.

On 29 November 2020, a resident ignited a liquefied petroleum gas canister in 3 Dongjiadu, Huangpu district (Shanghai) (coded as Shanghai-Huangpu), killing himself and causing severe burns to several demolition workers. It was an act of defiance against a forced land seizure and eviction operation implemented by authorities two decades ago, that escalated when the resident's son was kidnapped on the same morning.

On 25 October 2020, government-hired private security personnel abducted a petitioner while he was held in state custody at a detention centre for petitioners at 500 Fucun Rd, Putuo district (Shanghai) (coded as Shanghai-Putuo), and held him incommunicado at Meidu Hotel 'black jail' in Fengxian district for 18 days.
Around 14 October 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Shanghai Municipality to demand for three months of wage arrears owed by a food production company.

On 19 December 2020, over 1000 temporary workers protested at an electronics multinational company factory in Shanghai municipality against being deployed to a different province, and demanded for unpaid subsidies. Police and security guards were present at the scene, and a large number of police officers built a human wall to maintain order. Pushing and shoving broke out between both sides and some protesters were reportedly pushed to the floor.

On 5 January 2021, 19 petitioners demonstrated after visiting the home of a fellow petitioner in Shanghai municipality to commemorate the death of her mother, who was killed while petitioning 13 years ago. They held up a banner calling for the Public Security Bureau to investigate and set up a case for her murder.
Around 3 December 2020 (as reported), as many as 100 workers protested in Shanghai municipality to demand for wage arrears owed by a cake shop.

On 20 February 2021, a rights defender was taken away near his residence in Shanghai municipality by five police officers and two security guards as part of stability maintenance efforts before the annual Lianghui meetings. A warrant for criminal detention was already issued at the time, but it was reported that his location remained unknown at the time of reporting on 23 Feb 2021. Prior to the incident, on 19 Feb, local police officers had visited him and his wife, demanding to detain him at a 'vacation village' for one month.

On 18 February 2021, a petitioner from Dongxin district, Pudong New Area was taken away by government-hired security guards at a high-speed railway station in Shanghai municipality, after she had been intercepted at the Beijing train station by personnel from the Zhuqiao town government and escorted back overnight. She remained not contactable at the time of reporting on 22 Feb 2021.

On 3 March 2021, at least three petitioners demonstrated at an urban park in Shanghai municipality for the government to help with recovering their property, which was destroyed by the municipal government during the 2009 Shanghai World Expo. Three of them were arrested by the police.
Around 11 March 2021 (as reported), as many as 100 workers filed an appeal and protested in Shanghai municipality to demand for wage arrears following the closure of a technology company.

On 19 March 2021, as many as 70 petitioners, rights activists and citizens were rounded up into police cars at (and on their way to) the Shanghai No.1 Intermediate People's Court in Changning district (coded as Shanghai-Changning), and held at the Shanghai Stability Maintenance Center 'black jail' on 500 Fucun Rd in Putuo district. They were prevented from attending the public trial of a well-known female farmer and land rights activist, who was charged with 'inciting subversion of state power.' At least one of them was transferred to a detention centre in the evening.

On 5 March 2021, on the first day of the annual Lianghui conventions, a female petitioner living in Changning district (Shanghai) was invaded at their residence by an unreported party during her sleep, who attacked her with a knife and left her with a cut around her right ankle. Leading up to the incident, she had been in discussion with the Huayang Rd Sub-district's newly appointed Head of Petitions, who promised to resolve all her petitioning efforts and stability maintenance incidents locally. At the time of the attack, she already agreed - in good faith - to cancel her visit to the People's Supreme Court in Beijing, where she planned to report unlawful procedures and forgery of documents by local officials during a house expropriation case in 2016.

On 8 March 2021, on the first day of the annual Lianghui conventions, a female petitioner living in Changning district (Shanghai) was invaded at their residence by an unreported party during her sleep, who attacked her with a knife and left her with a gash around her neck. She was similarly attacked three days ago. Leading up to the incident, she had been in discussion with the Huayang Rd Sub-district's newly appointed Head of Petitions, who promised to resolve all her petitioning efforts and stability maintenance incidents locally. At the time of the attack, she already agreed - in good faith - to cancel her visit to the People's Supreme Court in Beijing, where she planned to report unlawful procedures and forgery of documents by local officials during a house expropriation case in 2016.

On 11 March 2021, a female petitioner was attacked in her sleep while being held under soft arrest ('black jail') at a room in Tingfeng Hotel in Changning district (Shanghai), sustaining a knife cut to her right arm. Earlier that day, she was intercepted at the Shanghai Pudong Airport - other petitioners were able to board their flight - under the orders of the Changning District Government, then escorted to her soft arrest location by officers from the Huayang Rd Police Station. They confiscated her belongings, identification and travel documents, and petition materials.
Around 27 May 2021 (as reported), 101-1000 workers filed for arbitration and protested in Shanghai municipality to demand for wage arrears owed by a game company.

On 17 January 2022, a petitioner from Fuzhou, Fujian, was abducted by local government personnel and over 10 'gangsters' at his house in Wuhou village in Fangshan district, Beijing, and escorted back to his hometown. Upon arrival, he was held at Room 1202 DoubleTree by Hilton for 20 days, where he was under tight surveillance by police and forced to take the COVID-19 test every day. The incident was a case of stability maintenance ahead of the Beijing Winter Olympics.

On 12 September 2018, in the morning, more than 30 rights protection-seeking citizens were arrested by the local police when they lit firecrackers to celebrate the release of a prisoner at the First Detention Center of Fuzhou located in Jin'an District (Fuzhou, Fujian). After a month, police released most of them from custody, except making charges for four people for 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble.'

On 22 February 2024, two petitioners were attacked and injured (details unknown), likely by the police, when they were in Chengdu city, Sichuan (coded to Wuhou) looking for a lawyer to file petitions against the local government. The attack is part of government officials' campaign to stifle dissent, as the Two Sessions meeting was scheduled to be held on 5 March 2024 in Beijing.
Around 21 October 2021 (as reported), workers protested in Huanghua city (Cangzhou, Hebei) to demand wage arrears owed by the construction company.
Around 20 October 2021 (as reported), workers protested in Huanghua city (Cangzhou, Hebei) to demand wage arrears owed by the construction company.
