Around 23 March 2023 (as reported), employees of a forestry company filed petitions to the local village committee together in Qingchuan county, Sichuan (coded to Qiaozhuang) to demand wage arrears.

Around 15 January 2022 (month of), a police officer beat up a human rights lawyer three times in two weeks, when he was interrogating him in Changsha City No. 1 Detention Center in Quantang town (Changsha, Hunan). He had been taken there on 11 January 2022, and had become incommunicado since then (separately coded). The attack and his forced disappearance might be related to his efforts to pressure the government to release a teacher, Li Tian Tian, from a psychiatric hospital in late December 2021.

On 16 December 2022, correctional officers chained together a human rights lawyer's handcuffs and legcuffs to restrain his body in a sitting position in Changsha City No. 1 Detention Center in Quantang town (Changsha, Hunan). The torture took place after he kicked the prison door in protest of the officers' reluctance to let his lawyer in. The detention might be related to his efforts to pressure the government to release a teacher, Li Tian Tian, from a psychiatric hospital in late December 2021. Whilst detained, he could not be contacted by the outside world and had been subject to attacks (separately coded).

On 31 May 2023, an elderly woman died, after being pushed to the floor by an officer at the local Urban Administrative and Law Enforcement Bureau in Tangdukou town (Shaoyang, Hunan). The officer and the woman had an argument, after he tried to stop the woman from selling eggs in a food market, which he said was illegal.

On 22 February 2024, a Fuzhou-based petitioner became incommunicado for around 20 days, after police took him away outside Tiananmen Square in Beijing - Dongcheng. He had travelled to Beijing to file petitions against the local government. The detention is likely part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions, scheduled to be held on 5 March 2024.

On 8 March 2024, police beat up a Jiangsu-based female petitioner, causing her to lose consciousness and be hospitalized, in Beijing city (coded to Beijing). She had travelled there to treat her illness. Two days later, her father was attacked (separately coded). The attacks are likely part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions, scheduled to be held on 5 March 2024.

On 10 March 2024, police and triad members beat up a female petitioner's father, causing his eyes to bleed, outside his home, which is likely located in Jintan district (Changzhou, Jiangsu), where the petitioner is based. Two days ago, the petitioner was attacked by police (separately coded). The attacks are likely part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions, scheduled to be held on 5 March 2024.

On 13 March 2024, stability maintenance officers strangled the neck of a Jiangsu-based petitioner's wife, causing her to be hospitalized, when she was getting out of her home in Binhu district (Wuxi, Jiangsu) to work. A few days ago, the petitioner had tried to travel to Beijing to petition against the local government, and was unsuccessful after being intercepted. The attack is likely part of officials' campaign to stifle dissent before the Two Sessions, scheduled to be held on 5 March 2024.

On 29 December 2023, police dragged and beat up a woman, causing injuries to her back and shoulders, when they pressed her into a police car outside a prison in Licheng district (Jinan, Shandong). The woman had just been released from prison for being an 'online fugitive'. Instead of letting her family pick her up, the prison insisted on escorting her home with a police car, which the woman refused as it was illegal.

On 10 March 2024, a woman became injured, after unidentified men's car crashed into hers, likely in Zhangqiu district (Jinan, Shandong). She was driving there to escort her parents home, after they told her on the phone that they were being surrounded by government officials and unknown men, and blocked from going to the court to sue against the local government.

On 10 March 2024, government officials and unknown men beat up a woman, causing bone fracture at her back, at a hospital in Zhangqiu district (Jinan, Shandong). She and her husband had gone there, after their daughter became injured after unidentified men's car crashed into hers. She was driving there to escort her parents home, after they told her on the phone that they were being surrounded by government officials, and blocked from going to the court to sue against the local government.

On 27 February 2021, a woman became incommunicado, after triad members sent by the government took her away, likely in Zibo city, Shandong (coded to Zhangdian). She was abducted for being an 'online fugitive'. It is later known that she was sentenced to jail for three years.

On 27 February 2024, parents marched and gathered to demonstrate outside a government office in Jiaojiang district (Taizhou, Zhejiang) to demand that the government withdraws its decision to shut down schools near to their homes.

On 13 June 2021, a rights defender went missing after he was taken into the custody of the Hongkou District Government (Shanghai) and handed over to the subdistrict officials. He had remained incommunicado at the time of reporting on 18 June 2021. The incident was reported as one of a series of 'stability maintenance incidents' to portray prosperity ahead of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the ruling Communist Party.
Around 27 September 2021 (as reported), over 100 taxi drivers went on strike in Pingjiang county (Yueyang, Hunan) to protest the surging insurance fee.

On 2 October 2021, a captured female human rights defender, who was also a petitioner-cum-forced evictee, was attacked by a government-hired security guard at Room 8603 of Hanting Hotel on Zhoujiazui Road, Hongkou district (Hongkou, Shanghai) after complaining about her extrajudicial detention. Her surveillant used knee-to-chest restraint to hold her down on the ground, causing her to suffer rib fractures. She was intercepted by police in Beijing on 29 September 2021 and repatriated to Shanghai by Shanghai Municipal People's Government Beijing Office officials and their people.

Around 18 November 2021 (week of), a petitioner from Hongkou district was detained at Room 8603 of Hanting Hotel on Zhoujiazui Road, Hongkou district (Hongkou, Shanghai) by a government-hired security guard for an unreported reason.

On 19 December 2021, a pregnant school teacher from Shaba township (Xiangxi, Hunan) was taken away by over ten police officers and Education Bureau officers from her house and committed for psychiatric care at Xiang Xi Zi Zhi Hou Jing Shen Bing Yi Yuan (a psychiatric hospital) in Lingxi township. She had been incommunicado until being released under surveillance somewhere in Yongshun county on 24 December 2021. The detention initially came after she had publicly sympathized with a Shanghai journalism lecturer who was fired after saying that there should be a more rigorous study of China's official death count for the Nanjing massacre in 1937.

On 26 December 2021, a rights activist, a lawyer, and a man were beaten by village officials (or 'thugs' according to another report) in Shaba township (Xiangxi, Hunan) when they tried to visit a recently released teacher. After leaving the village, they reported the assault to the police and became incommunicado.

On 25 December 2021, a veteran was abducted by 'gangsters' hired by the Beiwaitan police station in Hongkou district (Hongkou, Shanghai). He was guarded by over 10 people at Jiaming Hotel on 507 Liyang Road before being released on 5 January 2022. During the detention, he was incommunicado, not allowed to take medication, and subjected to violence and threats.

On 27 July 2018, over 10 police from Beiwaitan station raided the house of a veteran and beat him up in Hongkou district (Hongkou, Shanghai). He was then detained on Changxing Island and became incommunicado for over 20 days.
Around 27 January 2022 (as reported), workers protested in Luxi county (Xiangtan, Hunan) to demand around 2,000,000 RMB worth of wage arrears owed by a firework factory.
Around 3 March 2022 (as reported), 50 workers protested in Pingjiang city (Yueyang, Hunan) to demand 285,121 RMB worth of wage arrears owed by a construction company.

On 13 June 2022, hundreds of people working in apparel marched with umbrellas, displayed placards, and shouted slogans outside a shopping plaza in Hongkou district, Shanghai to demonstrate against the government's delay in relaxing coronavirus restrictions for businesses. Police clashed with some demonstrators, throwing them to the ground.

On 9 September 2021, people gathered to demonstrate outside Evergrande's office in Hongkou district (Hongkou, Shanghai). As bondholders, they were worried that Evergrande would not be able to repay them after the company ran into a liquidity crisis.

On 26 May 2020, many investors chanted slogans outside a police office in Hongkou district (Hongkou, Shanghai). Police dispersed the crowds, citing the 'illegality' of the demonstration. The investors were dissatisfied that the government did not take responsibility and that their investments were not returned after the company went bankrupt, as local government officials had heavily promoted them before they decided to invest.

Property destruction: Around 15 June 2019 (month of), Guanyin statues of two temples in Yongji County (Jilin City, Jilin Province) were destroyed by government-hired personnel. This was part of a broader campaign undertaken by the CPC to crack down on religious activities.
Around 12 June 2023 (as reported), employees of a mining company held a banner and gathered to demonstrate in their mining field in Luodian county (Qiannan, Guizhou) to demand wage arrears.

On 26 September 2023, police forced a female human rights defender, also a petitioner, to sit on a tiger chair for a day in a police station in Hongkou district (Hongkou, Shanghai). The defender was arrested because she was taking a photo of a fellow human rights defender, who was holding a placard in protest against a court judge for failing to fulfil his duties.

This has affected their livelihood and many had to resort to borrowing money to make ends meet.

Around 9 March 2018, a Uyghur woman from Xinyuan County (Ili Kazakh Autonomous, Xinjiang) was taken away by the authorities and sent to a re-education camp, where she was detained until her release on December 2018. She and her husband had returned to China on 13 November 2016 after living in Kazakhstan and had their passport confiscated. While her husband was able to get his passport four months later, she was left behind and later sent to a vocational school for around 20 days in April 2017. She was told by the authorities at the camp that she was detained for having lived in Kazakhstan for five years. She later gave an interview in June 2020, recounting that she received injections that made her period stop, and was also kicked in the stomach during interrogations.

Her disappearance came six days after her sister spoke publicly about the conditions inside the camps in Xinjiang, and was believed to be the key reason for her disappearance. Another testimony stated that her apartment was found to be sealed by the public security bureau in mid-September 2019.
